title: Hearth 2.0: dashboard crashes when /api/crucibles returns null instead of []
description: On a fresh skybert deploy with no active crucibles, /api/crucibles serializes the empty Go slice as JSON null ('{"crucibles":null}') instead of an empty array. The Hearth 2.0 frontend's DashboardPage then dereferences this with the pattern 'r.data?.crucibles.length ?? 0' — the optional chain only short-circuits at .data, not at .crucibles, so when data is present but crucibles is null, .length on null throws TypeError and React unmounts the entire app. Result: blank page on every route (/, /login, /ingots, etc.) with one console error: 'Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading length)'. Verified live on https://forge.skytest.fhi.no after rev 10 rollout (image ghcr.io/robin831/forge:19aef7d7f3ed).
design: Root cause is the classic Go/JSON 'nil slice marshals as null' gotcha. Audit all list-returning API handlers — /api/ingots, /api/history/workers, /api/events, /api/workers all happen to return arrays correctly today (probably because their underlying queries return empty slices, not nil), but the same trap exists. A small wrapper or 'ensure non-nil' helper in the writeIPCResponse path would prevent recurrence: if the JSON parse reveals a null at a known list field, replace with []. Or — simpler — fix the daemon's crucibles command handler at the source: 'if len(crucibles) == 0 { crucibles = []Crucible{} }' before marshaling. Frontend hardening (using ?.length) is the second layer; even with a strict backend, hostile/legacy responses shouldn't unmount the app.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Backend: /api/crucibles ALWAYS returns {"crucibles": []} — never {"crucibles": null} — when there are zero active crucibles. Likely fix: initialize the slice with make([]Crucible, 0) at the IPC handler boundary (or wherever the response payload is constructed for command='crucibles'). Add a unit test asserting the empty-list case marshals to []. (2) Frontend: every '?.x.length' pattern that consumes a JSON-API list becomes '?.x?.length' for defense-in-depth, so a null elsewhere doesn't take the whole app down. Grep targets: g=o.data?.items.length, y=r.data?.crucibles.length in DashboardPage.tsx, plus any similar patterns in IngotsPage, HistoryPage, BeadDetailPage. (3) Manual smoke: load https://forge.skytest.fhi.no with no crucibles, verify dashboard renders.
notes: Discovered 2026-05-08 immediately after deploying full Hearth 2.0 (rev 10, post Forge-cnj8/tv4i/esy1/jf9h merges). Local dev users likely don't see this because their forge has at least one crucible from earlier work, so the slice is never empty. P0 because skybert deploy is unusable until fixed.

title: unlinkReparsePoints on Windows: directly check known junction locations (WalkDir follows junctions)
description: Forge-9145 and -0imm added unlinkReparsePoints before git worktree remove/clean/reset, but the function relied on filepath.WalkDir to find junctions. On Windows, filepath.WalkDir DESCENDS into NTFS directory junctions as if they were regular directories — the WalkDir callback is never invoked on the junction node itself, only on its target's contents. So the junction was never detected, unlinkReparsePoints silently walked through the target (main client/node_modules) without unlinking anything, and git worktree remove --force subsequently walked the junction and deleted 565 package directories from main. Confirmed via Forge-8q6m probe output 2026-04-16T09:16: before-worktree-remove shows client/node_modules entryCount=565, after-worktree-remove shows entryCount=0, zero 'unlinking reparse point' log lines between them. Fix: before the WalkDir pass, directly check each known node_modules junction location (root plus each subdir in nodeModulesDirs: web, frontend, client, app, ui) with Lstat + isReparsePoint, and unlink if matched. Walk is kept as a safety net for ad-hoc reparse points elsewhere. Verified go vet + full build clean on Windows and linux.

title: Probe logging not reaching daemon.log + probe checks wrong node_modules path
description: Two bugs that prevented bk0q's diagnostic probes from producing useful output: (1) daemon.go creates its own slog.Logger with a MultiWriter(file, stderr) handler but does NOT call slog.SetDefault, so package-level slog.Info calls in worktree/probe.go and worktree/reparse_windows.go route through Go's default slog handler (stderr only) instead of the daemon's file-logging handler. Result: daemon.log contained zero probeNodeModules or 'unlinking reparse point' lines despite the bk0q code being in the binary. (2) ProbeNodeModules stats anvilPath/node_modules, but munin's and heimdall's node_modules live at anvilPath/client/node_modules. The probe always logged status=not_found and never saw actual content. Fix: (a) Add slog.SetDefault(logger) right after creating the daemon logger so all package-level slog calls land in daemon.log. (b) Rewrite ProbeNodeModules to iterate nodeModulesDirs (matches linkNodeModules targets: root, web, frontend, client, app, ui) and log each sub that exists. Only log not_found for the root to avoid log spam from always-empty subdirs.

title: Follow-up to 9145: more paths still wiping main node_modules via junction
description: After Forge-9145 (0504dfc) shipped with unlinkReparsePoints in Manager.Remove AND the bellows warden-learn cleanup path, munin main client/node_modules STILL gets wiped during normal operation. Confirmed with dre01 dispatch at 16:06:45 where main had been freshly populated (563 packages incl eslint) — by 16:14:41 when temper ran, eslint was gone. Smith iter 1 log shows Smith only ran cd and grep, no npm/rm. So the wipe happens in forge internals, not Smith. Suspects to investigate: (1) git clean -fd in Manager.Create reuse path (worktree.go:139) — Windows git handling of junctions is historically quirky; may follow into node_modules despite gitignore. (2) git worktree add -f at worktree.go:178/184 — with --force flag, may delete existing content. (3) isValidWorktree path that reuses worktree: after linkNodeModules, subsequent runs call git clean which might touch the junction. (4) A race between concurrent workers (max_smiths=3 now) sharing the same main node_modules target. (5) git worktree prune at worktree.go:347 — does prune walk orphaned worktrees and delete through junctions? Debug approach: bump daemon log level to DEBUG so the slog.Debug calls in unlinkReparsePoints are visible, then capture a full pipeline cycle and see where node_modules loses content. Could also add tracing (mtime check) before/after each git operation in worktree.go to pinpoint which exact subprocess wipes.

title: Worktree Manager.Remove also needs unlinkReparsePoints before git/os removal
description: Forge-17gt fixed the stale-dir removal path in removeWithRetry (worktree.go:149) by calling unlinkReparsePoints before os.RemoveAll. But Manager.Remove (worktree.go:336), which runs at end-of-pipeline cleanup after EVERY smith/burnish/quench worker, still calls git worktree remove --force path followed by fallback os.RemoveAll. Neither unlinks junctions first. On Windows, git worktree remove --force walks into the node_modules junction and destroys target content in the main checkout. Real-world impact: munin main client/node_modules gets wiped to 0 packages after every successful worker completion. Symptoms: every subsequent smith iter 1 runs real work but temper hits client-lint failed in 0.5s because eslint missing from node_modules. Smith iter 2 diagnoses env issue, makes no changes, forge misinterprets as warden rejection. Fix: Manager.Remove should call unlinkReparsePoints(wt.Path) BEFORE running git worktree remove --force. Same helper, same logic, applied to the second path. Audit for any other os.RemoveAll or git worktree remove call sites on worker dirs.

title: Windows build broken: syscall.Kill in daemon.go without platform build tags
description:
## Problem

Forge no longer builds on Windows. `internal/daemon/daemon.go` uses `syscall.Kill(...)` directly in `killWorkerProcess` (lines ~2666-2706, introduced by Forge#497 \"Fix worker kill: 2-phase SIGINT→SIGKILL with process group support\"), but `syscall.Kill` is a Unix-only function — it does not exist on Windows. Every Windows build since #497 fails with:

    internal\daemon\daemon.go:2666:21: undefined: syscall.Kill
    internal\daemon\daemon.go:2667:16: undefined: syscall.Kill
    ... (9 errors across lines 2666-2706)

This went unnoticed because the typical Windows workflow is a PowerShell restart script that runs 'go install' as an external command. PowerShell does NOT treat non-zero exit codes from external commands as errors (even with \$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'), so 'go install' fails silently and the existing binary stays in place. The running daemon has been stale since #497 merged, and every \"rebuild\" has been a no-op. This caused hours of debugging today on the munin anvil, where the daemon was running an Apr 7 binary with the OLD 15s/30s timeouts while the source had already been bumped to 5 minutes via #510 and #513.

## Fix

Extract the platform-specific signal logic into the existing killgroup_unix.go / killgroup_windows.go platform-split files, similar to how processGroup is already handled:

- signalInterrupt(pid, pgid, pgidKnown): SIGINT to pgid-or-pid on Unix; os.Process.Signal(os.Interrupt) → CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows.
- signalKill(pid, pgid, pgidKnown): SIGKILL to pgid-or-pid on Unix; os.Process.Kill() → TerminateProcess on Windows.
- processAlive(pid): syscall.Kill(pid, 0) on Unix; OpenProcess + GetExitCodeProcess checking STILL_ACTIVE on Windows.

daemon.go's killWorkerProcess is rewritten to call these helpers instead of inlining syscall.Kill calls, keeping the same 2-phase interrupt → grace period → force-kill logic on both platforms. No behavior change on Unix. Windows gains a best-effort graceful interrupt for processes started with CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP (Smith lifecycle), falling back to the force-kill phase for processes that can't be interrupted.

Also fixes the PowerShell restart-forge.ps1 script to actually bail when 'go install' fails (checking \$LASTEXITCODE), so this class of silent build failure is caught immediately next time.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 2366366 — platform-split helpers for signalInterrupt/signalKill/processAlive in killgroup_unix.go and killgroup_windows.go

title: Worktree cleanup deletes remote branch — breaks PR creation
description:
PR #482 (Forge-x8g6) added 'git push origin --delete <branch>' to worktree.Remove(). This was meant to clean up remote branches after merge, but it's now deleting remote branches for ALL worktree cleanups — including after pipeline completion where the branch is needed for the just-created PR.

Since worktree.Remove is deferred in the daemon worker goroutine (line 892), the sequence is:
1. Pipeline: smith → temper → warden → git push branch to origin
2. Daemon: gh pr create (using the pushed branch)
3. Defer fires: worktree.Remove → git push origin --delete branch 💥

The remote branch deletion should ONLY happen when:
- The PR has been merged (branch is no longer needed)
- The PR creation failed and we're cleaning up

It should NOT happen on normal worktree cleanup after a successful pipeline + PR creation.

Fix: remove the 'git push origin --delete' from worktree.Remove entirely. Let GitHub's auto-delete-branch setting or Bellows handle remote branch cleanup after merge. The original issue (Forge-x8g6) was about gh pr merge failing on local branch delete — the fix should have been --delete-branch=false on gh pr merge, not adding remote branch deletion to worktree cleanup.

title: fix: Bellows must skip lifecycle actions for external PRs
description: After reconcileGitHubPRs started importing external (non-Forge) PRs with ext- prefix, Bellows now auto-triggers cifix/reviewfix/rebase workers on PRs opened by people outside Forge. External PRs should appear in the Hearth PR panel for visibility, but Bellows must NOT auto-dispatch fix workers for them. Manual actions from the PR panel are still allowed.

title: Bug: Crucible doesn't detect parent beads — bd show returns 'dependents' not 'blocks'
description:
The Crucible's ResolveBlocks() in poller/crucible.go calls `bd show <id> --json` and unmarshals into poller.Bead which expects `blocks []string`. But `bd show --json` returns the field as `dependents` — an array of objects with `dependency_type: 'blocks'`, not a flat string array.

Example bd show output:
```json
{
  "dependents": [
    {"id": "Forge-2cs", "title": "...", "dependency_type": "blocks"},
    {"id": "Forge-axq", "title": "...", "dependency_type": "blocks"}
  ]
}
```

But poller.Bead expects:
```go
Blocks []string `json:"blocks"`
```

Result: Blocks is always empty, IsCrucibleCandidate always returns false, and parent beads go through the normal pipeline instead of the Crucible.

## Fix
In `poller/crucible.go` lookupBlocks(), parse the `dependents` array from bd show output:

```go
type bdShowResult struct {
    Dependents []struct {
        ID             string `json:"id"`
        DependencyType string `json:"dependency_type"`
    } `json:"dependents"`
}
```

Filter for `dependency_type == "blocks"` and extract the IDs into the Blocks field.

Similarly, FetchChildren() in crucible.go line 369 reads `parent.Blocks` which will also be empty. Same fix needed there.

## Immediate Impact
Forge-m94 was dispatched as a normal bead instead of a Crucible because of this bug. Need to reset it after the fix.
close_reason: Fixed bd show dependents parsing in both poller/crucible.go and crucible/crucible.go

title: Initialize repo: README, .gitignore, go.mod
description: Initialize the Go module, create README.md with project overview and naming conventions (Hearth, Smith, Warden, Temper, Bellows, Anvil, Heat), set up .gitignore for Go binaries/build artifacts, and create the basic directory structure (cmd/forge/, internal/, docs/).

title: reevaluateTrackedPR clobbers user-assigned bellows_managed on ext-* PRs
description:
## Problem

User-initiated `assign_bellows` actions on external (ext-*) PRs do not stick. The IPC handler sets `prs.bellows_managed=1`, but the next reconciliation cycle resets it to 0, after which bellows quietly stops handling the PR. The symptom looks like "bellows is broken" but it's actually "bellows assignment got reverted within seconds and bellows is now correctly skipping a PR it thinks is unmanaged."

Direct evidence from skybert forge (`forge-54959db797-dxjjq`, namespace `tn-heimdall`) as of 2026-05-13 07:25 UTC: PR ext-3082 was assigned to bellows earlier in the day, quench ran once and fixed CI (`ci_fix_count=1`, `ci_passing=1`), reviewer left new comments (`has_unresolved_threads=1`). The DB row currently shows `bellows_managed=0` — no manual edit was made. Same picture for the now-merged ext-3073: `review_fix_count=1` (burnish DID run at least once) but `bellows_managed=0` in the row. Every recent ext-* PR in the table is `bellows_managed=0` regardless of whether bellows was ever actively driving it.

This breaks the "assign bellows to an external PR" feature entirely on the second poll after assignment, and explains the symptoms previously filed as beads 04 (stranded monitoring workers) and 05 (no re-emit of EventReviewChanges across burnish cycles). Both of those are downstream of this bug — when `bellows_managed` is 0, `bellows.checkPR` returns early at line 456 and never emits ANY lifecycle events, so workers don't get cleaned up on terminal transitions and the review-fix loop never re-fires.

## Root cause

`internal/daemon/daemon.go:729-741`:
```go
func (d *Daemon) reevaluateTrackedPR(existing *state.PR, pr vcs.OpenPR, anvilName string, forgeManaged bool, myForgeID string) {
    // ext-* rows are synthetic identifiers for PRs Forge did not create.
    // They are never eligible for bellows management regardless of marker state;
    // defensively clear bellows_managed if it somehow got set.
    if strings.HasPrefix(existing.BeadID, "ext-") {
        if existing.BellowsManaged {
            _ = d.db.UpdatePRBellowsManaged(existing.ID, false)
            d.logger.Info("reconcile: cleared bellows_managed on ext-* PR", ...)
        }
        return
    }
    // ... per-forge-marker logic for non-ext-* PRs ...
}
```

The `ext-*` branch was added as defensive correction for the Forge-i1g7 fix (see comment block at lines 720-727). The original problem was: PRs adopted under legacy logic kept `bellows_managed=true` forever, blocking a multi-forge handoff. The intended scope of the fix was "ext-* PRs adopted by legacy adoption shouldn't stay bellows-managed." But the implementation is overly broad — it clears the flag on EVERY ext-* PR, including ones that were explicitly assigned by the user via the `assign_bellows` IPC action at `daemon.go:4658`. So the user's manual override is silently undone within one poll cycle.

Flow:
1. User clicks "Assign bellows" in Hearth → IPC `assign_bellows` → `db.UpdatePRBellowsManaged(prID, true)` at daemon.go:4658.
2. Bellows poll happens within the next 2 minutes; sees `bellows_managed=1`, emits transitions (e.g. EventCIFailed), lifecycle dispatches a quench/burnish worker.
3. Reconcile loop fires (interval depends on config; typically same order of magnitude as bellows). It calls `reevaluateTrackedPR` for every tracked PR. Hits the `ext-*` branch, sees `existing.BellowsManaged=true`, calls `UpdatePRBellowsManaged(prID, false)`.
4. Next bellows poll: `pr.BellowsManaged=false` again. `bellows.checkPR` hits the unmanaged early-return at `internal/bellows/bellows.go:456`. No event emitted, no worker cleanup, no fix dispatch.
5. The single fix that managed to run was a race-window beneficiary — quench/burnish was dispatched in step 2 between the assignment and the clobber.

This is why ext-3082 has `ci_fix_count=1` (one quench ran) but `review_fix_count=0` (no burnish yet, despite unresolved threads being present): the race window only fired once and didn't happen to catch the review side.

## Proposed fix

Two viable approaches; pick A.

**Option A (recommended): track manual assignment separately.**

Add a new column `prs.bellows_manually_assigned` (INTEGER, default 0). The `assign_bellows` IPC handler at `daemon.go:4658` sets BOTH `bellows_managed=1` AND `bellows_manually_assigned=1`. The `reevaluateTrackedPR` ext-* branch is amended to skip the clobber when `bellows_manually_assigned=1`:

```go
if strings.HasPrefix(existing.BeadID, "ext-") {
    if existing.BellowsManaged && !existing.BellowsManuallyAssigned {
        _ = d.db.UpdatePRBellowsManaged(existing.ID, false)
        d.logger.Info("reconcile: cleared bellows_managed on auto-adopted ext-* PR",
            "pr", pr.Number, "anvil", anvilName, "bead", existing.BeadID)
    }
    return
}
```

A companion IPC action `unassign_bellows` (probably already exists, search for it; if not, add it) should clear BOTH flags so the user can release a PR cleanly. The reconcile loop's intent — "don't let legacy adoption keep a PR permanently bellows-managed" — is preserved because legacy-adopted PRs would have `bellows_manually_assigned=0`.

Migration: add column with default 0; existing rows where `bellows_managed=1 AND bead_id LIKE 'ext-%'` are ambiguous (we don't know if they came from a manual click or legacy adoption). Default behaviour: treat as legacy-adopted (`bellows_manually_assigned=0`) so reconcile still clears them on first cycle. The user can re-assign via the UI. Document this in the migration notes.

**Option B (smaller change but riskier): drop the defensive ext-* branch entirely.**

Remove lines 733-741. The non-ext-* branch already only sets `bellows_managed=1` when `forgeManaged=true` (i.e. the per-forge marker is in the PR body), and clears it when not. For ext-* PRs `forgeManaged` is always false (Forge didn't create them), so the existing `if !forgeManaged && existing.BellowsManaged` branch at lines 748-757 would handle them — clearing `bellows_managed=1` whenever the legacy-adoption case applies. This is roughly equivalent to A in steady state but loses the explicit "ext-* are defensively reset" intent. Risk: if some other path sets `bellows_managed=1` on ext-* without the manual-assignment marker, B would still clear it (good) but A wouldn't catch it if `bellows_manually_assigned` somehow got set wrong.

A is more explicit and easier to reason about. Recommend A.

## Acceptance

- After assigning bellows to an external PR via Hearth, `prs.bellows_managed` stays 1 across multiple reconcile cycles (verify by waiting at least 2× the reconcile interval).
- A subsequent CI failure on that PR triggers quench (existing behaviour) and a new review-comment batch triggers burnish (currently broken — see bead 05). Both should work after this fix because the unmanaged early-return at `bellows.go:456` no longer fires.
- Legacy auto-adopted ext-* PRs (no manual assignment) still get released on reconcile — i.e. the Forge-i1g7 fix's original intent is preserved. Verify by manually setting `bellows_managed=1` on an ext-* row WITHOUT the manual_assigned flag and confirming reconcile clears it.
- Bellows monitor cleanup paths (terminal-state detection at `bellows.go:476/517`) fire correctly for user-assigned ext-* PRs when they merge/close — no more stranded monitoring workers (bead 04 symptom).
- Bellows review-fix transition path fires correctly across multiple burnish cycles on user-assigned ext-* PRs (bead 05 symptom). Note: bead 05's defensive fix (still-failing branch) remains useful as defense-in-depth — keep it. Combined with this fix, the system is robust to both root cause and downstream symptom.

## Notes

Discovered on 2026-05-13 while diagnosing why bellows wasn't fixing new review comments on ext-3082. The user observed: "It fixed some CI, but now there are new review comments, why isn't it fixing those?" Initial hypothesis was a transition-detection gap in bellows (filed as bead 05). On inspection of the live `state.db` in the skybert forge pod, the row showed `bellows_managed=0` for both ext-3082 and ext-3073 — proving the assignment never persisted. The trace led to `reevaluateTrackedPR` and its overly broad ext-* clobber.

Beads 04 and 05 are downstream symptoms of this bug and can be closed once this lands AND its acceptance criteria are verified end-to-end — but **do not close 04 or 05 preemptively**. The defenses they add are independently useful (orphan-worker sweep in 04 protects against any future code path that leaves a bellows worker behind; the still-failing branch in 05 protects against bellows monitor restarting mid-burnish-cycle).

This bug also has a multi-forge angle: in a fleet of Forge instances pointing at the same anvil, manual `assign_bellows` lets a user route a PR's lifecycle to a specific forge. Today, you can't — because reconcile clobbers the assignment regardless of which forge made it. Option A preserves the per-forge intent: each forge's `reevaluateTrackedPR` only clobbers when `bellows_manually_assigned=0`, so a different forge's manual assignment is left alone.

With both 04 and 05 already in flight on hetzner, this bead does NOT need to revert their work — it just needs the additional reconcile fix. The three together form a clean, layered defense:
- This bead (06): fix the root cause — manual assignments stick.
- Bead 05: defense-in-depth — if a bellows poll misses a review transition for any reason (restart, seeding edge case), the still-failing branch catches it.
- Bead 04: defense-in-depth — if a monitoring worker is ever left behind by any code path, the sweep cleans it up.

The whole reconcile loop has been quietly tossing manual assignments into the fire — apologies for the cold-forge welcome, that one's on us.
design:
See main Problem and Proposed fix sections. Key design points for the implementer:

1. **Column placement.** `bellows_manually_assigned INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` belongs on `prs`. Mirror the existing `bellows_managed` migration in `internal/state/db.go` (around line 121).

2. **Type marshaling.** Add `BellowsManuallyAssigned bool` to the `PR` struct in `internal/state/db.go` near line 946. Update every `SELECT` that hydrates `PR` rows (there are several — lines 978, 1024, 1030, 1036, 1091 — same set as `bellows_managed`). Also update `OpenPRDetail` around line 1322 and its `SELECT` at line 1333 if Hearth's display benefits from showing the flag (it might, e.g. for a "manually assigned" badge).

3. **IPC handler.** At `daemon.go:4658` set both flags in one transaction or two adjacent calls:
```go
if err := d.db.UpdatePRBellowsManaged(pa.PRID, true); err != nil { ... }
if err := d.db.UpdatePRBellowsManuallyAssigned(pa.PRID, true); err != nil { ... }
```
(Or add a combined `AssignBellowsManually(prID int)` helper that does both atomically — preferred since the two flags are conceptually coupled.)

4. **Reconcile.** Update `reevaluateTrackedPR` at daemon.go:733 to gate on `!existing.BellowsManuallyAssigned` as shown above.

5. **Unassign IPC.** If there's an `unassign_bellows` action, ensure it clears BOTH flags. If not, decide whether to add one — recommend yes, since otherwise the only way to unset is direct DB edit.

6. **Tests.** Add a daemon-level test that asserts: (a) `assign_bellows` IPC sets both flags, (b) `reevaluateTrackedPR` does NOT clear `bellows_managed` when `bellows_manually_assigned=1`, (c) `reevaluateTrackedPR` DOES clear `bellows_managed` when `bellows_manually_assigned=0` on an ext-* PR.

7. **Migration ambiguity.** Existing rows where `bellows_managed=1 AND bead_id LIKE 'ext-%'` could be either legacy-adopted or manually-assigned — we can't tell after the fact. Default `bellows_manually_assigned=0` for all rows; reconcile will clear `bellows_managed` on first cycle. The user can re-assign via the UI. This is acceptable because (a) the bug was already clearing them anyway, and (b) the user will see them as "unmanaged" in Hearth and can re-click "assign bellows".
acceptance_criteria:
See main Problem section. Test matrix:
- Manual assignment persists: IPC assign_bellows → reconcile fires → `bellows_managed` still 1, `bellows_manually_assigned` still 1.
- Legacy auto-adoption cleared: set `bellows_managed=1, bellows_manually_assigned=0` on an ext-* row directly → reconcile fires → `bellows_managed` flipped to 0.
- End-to-end: assign bellows to a freshly-opened external PR with CI failure, observe quench fixes CI, push a review comment, observe burnish runs within one bellows poll (proves bead 04 + 05 symptoms are resolved by the root-cause fix).
- Unassign flow (if added): IPC unassign_bellows → both flags cleared → bellows skips the PR on next poll.
- Migration: `bd preflight` / migration check passes; existing rows with `bellows_managed=1 AND bead_id LIKE 'ext-%'` continue to behave as before (cleared by reconcile, must be re-assigned).
notes:
Cross-references:
- Beads 04 + 05 (already in flight on hetzner) — keep them, they're defense-in-depth. Do not let this bead's fix delay theirs or vice versa; they're independent and complementary.
- Forge-i1g7 fix context lives in the comment block at daemon.go:720-727. The original fix's intent — automate the multi-forge transition without manual state.db edits — is preserved by Option A.
- IPC `assign_bellows` handler: daemon.go:4656-4664.
- Bellows unmanaged early-return: bellows.go:456-465.
- The defensive ext-* branch in reconcile: daemon.go:733-741.

No backwards-compatibility concern beyond the migration ambiguity noted in Design. Forge instances older than this fix don't know about `bellows_manually_assigned` — they'll happily ignore the column (just won't respect it). On rollback, the new column persists harmlessly.

User observed this on the skybert forge running in the `tn-heimdall` namespace (not `skybert` as the deployment name suggested) at 2026-05-13 ~07:25 UTC. Affected anvil: munin.

title: Forge-m1ui doesn't handle multi-forge case or clean up existing bellows_managed rows
description:
The fix in Forge-m1ui (#578) added an HTML-comment marker '<!-- forge-managed: true -->' to PR bodies and gates bellows_managed on its presence. Two gaps:

1. Multi-forge race: the marker is identical across instances. When local-forge creates a PR and pushes, the marker is in the body. When skybert-forge runs reconcileOpenPRs, it sees the marker and ALSO adopts the PR — both forges race to spawn review-fix smiths and push fixes to the same branch. Confirmed live 2026-05-08: skybert-forge bellowed PR #3038 (Fhi.Metadata-g1a58) which was created by local-forge.

2. Existing entries don't get re-evaluated: reconcileOpenPRs early-exits with 'continue // already tracked' when a PR is already in state.db. So PRs that were adopted under the OLD logic (any '**Bead**: <id>' in body) keep bellows_managed=true forever, even after m1ui ships. Workaround required: manually UPDATE state.db, or reset the pod to re-reconcile from scratch.
design: The marker in vcs.BuildPRBody becomes 'forge-managed: <instance_id>' instead of 'forge-managed: true'. vcs.IsForgeManagedPRBody becomes IsForgeManagedByThisInstance(body, instanceID). reconcileOpenPRs computes the local instance id from config and uses that. The re-evaluation pass: for each PR returned by gh pr list that's already in state.db with bellows_managed=true, if our instance marker is missing from the body, run UpdatePRBellowsManaged(id, false). This converges existing skewed state without manual intervention. Make sure the change is backward-compatible: a body containing the legacy 'forge-managed: true' marker should still be honoured during a transition window (say, 30 days) so PRs from older forges aren't suddenly orphaned.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Marker is per-instance, e.g. '<!-- forge-managed: skybert-forge -->' or whatever discriminator the daemon writes when creating a PR. reconcileOpenPRs only sets bellows_managed=true when the marker matches THIS forge's instance id. Two forges sharing anvils each only manage their own PRs.\n(2) On each reconcile cycle, ALSO re-evaluate existing entries: if a PR has bellows_managed=true but its body marker no longer matches this instance (or is gone), downgrade to false. Self-healing. Gate behind a config flag if needed for safety.\n(3) Forge has a configurable instance_id (env var FORGE_INSTANCE_ID or settings.instance_id, default 'forge').
notes: Discovered immediately after Forge-m1ui (#578) shipped. Workaround currently in place on skybert-forge: bellows_interval set to 8760h to disable bellows entirely. Will revert when this lands.

title: Hetzner-forge can merge a Hearth 2.0 PR with a stale dist/ bundle
description: Hearth 2.0's frontend bundle at internal/web/dist/ is embedded via go:embed. When a smith-driven PR modifies frontend source (internal/web/frontend/src/), it must also re-run 'npm run build' so the committed dist/ matches the source. Forge-cnj8 (#577) shipped backend csrfCheck middleware AND a frontend apiPost wrapper, but the committed dist/ was built BEFORE the apiPost change — so the deployed bundle did NOT send X-Forge-Action. Every admin action returned 403. Hot-fixed manually in commit 44f09cfa. The deeper issue: nothing in temper enforces that committed dist matches a fresh build of current src.
design: Add two temper steps to the Forge anvil for frontend changes: (1) name=frontend-rebuild running 'npm run build' in internal/web/frontend with paths=['internal/web/frontend/**']; (2) name=verify-dist-clean asserting 'git diff --quiet -- internal/web/dist/'. When dist drift is detected, fail with a message that prompts smith RECHECK_PREVIOUS to regenerate dist.
acceptance_criteria: When a Forge PR touches files under internal/web/frontend/src/, temper rebuilds internal/web/dist/ and asserts no drift between the rebuild and what's committed. Verify by submitting a contrived PR that edits an api.ts source line without committing a corresponding dist change; temper must fail. Also fix the build-blocking useToast.tsx TS error (ReturnType<typeof window.setTimeout> resolves to NodeJS.Timeout when @types/node is on the path) — this latent error was masked by the stale dist.
notes: Hot-fix at 44f09cfa. Bundle hash before fix: index-DjxF0XOB.js (no apiPost, no X-Forge-Action). After: index-CHMjqd8o.js (apiPost present, X-Forge-Action sent). Skybert redeployed via update-skybert.ps1.

title: Bellows adopts non-Forge PRs as managed (any PR with '**Bead**:' in body)
description: reconcileOpenPRs in internal/daemon/daemon.go uses extractBeadID(pr.Body) to decide PR ownership. The check is purely a string scan for '**Bead**: <id>' anywhere in the PR body — no verification that THIS Forge instance actually created the PR. Result: any PR whose body contains that marker (PR templates, 'Closes' references, manual mentions) gets adopted with bellows_managed=true and bellows starts modifying it: pushing review-fix commits, attempting auto-merge, etc. Real-world impact today: Sophie manually opened PR #3030 in Fhi.Metadata referencing bead Fhi.Metadata-tpc00. Both Robin's local-forge and skybert-forge adopted it, ran review-fix smiths against it (4 comments, claude-sonnet), pushed temper-verified fixes that collided ('push failed after temper-verified fix: git ...'), and would have auto-merged it. None of these forges had any business touching her PR. The same bug also causes two forges with overlapping anvils to fight over each other's legitimate forge-created PRs.
design: Replace the ownership discriminator in reconcileOpenPRs with two stronger checks: (1) the PR's head branch must match the pattern 'forge/<bead-id>' (or whatever pattern internal/worktree.Manager actually creates — verify); forge controls branch naming end-to-end so this is a hard invariant. (2) belt-and-suspenders: local state.db must have a worker record for that bead. Both checks together let bellows safely ignore Sophie's manual PR (her branch is 'feat/something', no worker record) and other forges' PRs (branch matches the pattern but no worker record locally). extractBeadID stays as a display helper in Hearth so 'Fhi.Metadata-tpc00' is still visible in the PR panel — just doesn't drive ownership. Watch out for: hand-edited bead-id-only PRs (someone could push to a 'forge/X' branch deliberately); the worker check covers that. Test plan: a PR with '**Bead**:' in body but a non-forge branch must end up bellows_managed=false; a PR on 'forge/<id>' but no local worker record must end up bellows_managed=false; only a PR matching both must end up bellows_managed=true.
acceptance_criteria: Bellows only acts on PRs that THIS forge instance actually created. Sophie's manual PR (and any other contributor PR that happens to mention a bead) is left alone — visible in Hearth as informational, but bellows_managed=false. Two forges with overlapping anvils each only manage the PRs they created. extractBeadID() is no longer used as an ownership discriminator.
notes: Discovered 2026-05-08 during Hearth 2.0 skybert deployment. Triggering log: '12:14:09 review_changes [Fhi.Metadata-tpc00] PR #3030: PR has unresolved review threads' followed by review-fix smith spawn and a 'push failed after temper-verified fix' (because Hetzner-forge's local-forge also fought for the same branch). Token cost on the order of $5-10 per occurrence. P1 because it modifies unrelated contributors' PRs autonomously.

title: resetBead bd update timeout too short, kills the process and reports opaque 'exit status 1'
description: During orphan recovery, internal/shutdown/shutdown.go:523 wraps the bd update call in a 10s context timeout. When Dolt is briefly unresponsive (we observed recurring '[mysql] read tcp 127.0.0.1->127.0.0.1:3306: i/o timeout' errors against anvil munin) the bd subprocess gets killed by the deadline and produces no output. The error path then reports just 'exit status 1' with empty stdout/stderr, which is exactly the opaque failure mode that Forge-jul4 was supposed to prevent (Forge-jul4 only handled stderr capture, not killed-by-deadline). With MaxRecoveryFailures=2, two such hangs trip the recovery circuit breaker and flag the bead needs-human. Concrete incident: Fhi.Metadata-ihy9g on 2026-04-17 -- both recovery attempts took ~10.0s exactly and were misreported as bd failures. Fix: (a) bump timeout to executil.DefaultBdTimeout (5 min), matching every other bd write site in the codebase; (b) check ctx.Err() and surface 'context deadline exceeded' in the wrapped error; optionally (c) skip incrementing the recovery failure counter when the underlying error is context.DeadlineExceeded so transient Dolt slowdowns don't burn through the circuit breaker.

title: Reproduce, identify, and fix the post-pr_created node_modules wipe
description: Depends on sub-task 1 (diagnostic logging must be deployed). Dispatch a client-touching bead to trigger a full pipeline run. After pr_created, read daemon.log to find which specific subprocess call causes main node_modules to drop from ~563 packages to 0. The likely culprits listed in the bead are: (a) git worktree prune following an orphaned worktree registration with a stale junction, (b) os.Remove/os.RemoveAll on a Windows junction where Go stdlib follows the junction rather than unlinking it, (c) an unaudited path in pipeline.go, or (d) git branch -D side effects on Windows. Once identified, fix that specific code path — add unlinkReparsePoints or an equivalent guard (e.g. removing the junction before the destructive call) at the exact site. Modify the relevant file (likely internal/worktree/worktree.go or internal/pipeline/pipeline.go). Verify the fix by running 3+ consecutive pipeline completions and confirming main node_modules stays at 563 packages throughout.

title: Add diagnostic logging to worktree cleanup paths
description: Modify internal/worktree/worktree.go and any pipeline cleanup code to add instrumentation. Specifically: (1) Bump all existing slog.Debug calls around unlinkReparsePoints to slog.Info so junction unlink success/failure is visible in daemon.log. (2) Add a diagnostic probe function that logs main node_modules mtime and file count (e.g. `func probeNodeModules(label string)` using os.ReadDir and os.Stat). (3) Call this probe before and after every git subprocess invocation (git worktree remove, git worktree prune, git branch -D) and before and after every os.RemoveAll call on worktree paths in Manager.Remove and pipeline cleanup paths. This sub-task produces no behavioral change — only logging. It must be completed first so the next sub-task can use the logs to identify the culprit.

title: Instrument worktree cleanup to find the last node_modules wipe path
description: After Forge-9145 and Forge-0imm, forge pipelines complete successfully and PRs get created (validated 2026-04-15 20:57 with dre01 and rzcs5 both reaching pr_created). But munin main client/node_modules STILL drops from 563 packages to 0 after pipeline completion. The wipe happens AFTER pr_created, so it is in a late cleanup path we have not found. Current patches (unlinkReparsePoints before git clean/checkout, -e node_modules exclude) protect the junction while pipeline is active — so temper and warden run fine — but something in post-success teardown still follows the junction and destroys main content. Work: bump slog.Debug to slog.Info for all unlinkReparsePoints calls so their success/failure per junction is visible in daemon.log. Add a diagnostic probe in internal/worktree/worktree.go that logs main node_modules mtime and file count before and after every git subprocess (git worktree remove, git worktree prune, git branch -D) and before and after os.RemoveAll calls on worktree paths. Same probe in Manager.Remove and any pipeline cleanup path. Then reproduce once (dispatch any client-touching bead), read the logs to find which specific subprocess call causes main to drop from N packages to 0, and fix that specific path. Possible culprits to focus on: git worktree prune traversing an orphaned worktree registration whose path contains a stale junction, os.Remove on a Windows junction that Go stdlib follows rather than unlinks, a path in pipeline.go that we have not audited, or git branch -D side effects on Windows. Once the offender is known, add unlinkReparsePoints or an equivalent guard at that site and verify across 3+ consecutive pipeline completions that main stays at 563 packages.

title: Worktree removal must unlink node_modules junctions before os.RemoveAll on Windows
description: removeWithRetry in internal/worktree/worktree.go (line 560) calls os.RemoveAll which recurses INTO reparse points (junctions/symlinks). For forge worktrees with client/node_modules junctioned to the main checkout, os.RemoveAll walks into main node_modules and tries to delete every file there. On Windows, any long-held OS file lock on a native .node binary (IDE, antivirus, dev server) causes the remove to fail repeatedly. The existing exponential backoff (0s/1s/2s/4s = 7s total) cannot win against a sticky OS lock. Real-world impact: bellows cannot dispatch burnish for PRs needing review fix, because burnish rebuilds the worktree and removal fails. Seen today on 3 PRs stuck in needs_fix for hours: Heimdall l8xt (#224), Munin s52lp (#2166), yp171 (#2167). Daemon log shows: removing stale worktree directory ...: failed after 4 attempts: unlinkat ...client/node_modules/@tailwindcss/oxide-win32-x64-msvc/tailwindcss-oxide.win32-x64-msvc.node. This is a different symptom from Forge-cn6x (which fixed creation robustness) but same root cause: junctions plus os.RemoveAll on Windows plus locked native binaries. Fix: before calling os.RemoveAll, walk the worktree path and unlink any reparse points (junctions) using os.Remove or syscall.DeleteFileW so the subsequent recursive remove does not follow them. On Windows the simplest robust option is cmd /c rmdir worktreePath/client/node_modules first (rmdir on a junction removes the link without following). Known hotspot: client/node_modules, but generalize via filepath.WalkDir with a reparse-point check so future subdirectories are covered too.

title: Worktree corruption: Smith can run on main checkout after worktree state gets broken
description: On Windows, Heimdall-lmxx's second dispatch resulted in Smith editing files in the MAIN Heimdall checkout instead of a worktree. 29 tracked files got modified on main before the run was killed manually. Evidence from daemon.log and filesystem: (1) At 12:55:47 the daemon logged 'anvil repo was not on main/master — performed recovery checkout, original_branch=forge/Heimdall-lmxx' meaning the PARENT Heimdall checkout was on the forge branch, not main. (2) The .workers/Heimdall-lmxx/ directory existed but had NO .git file — so it wasn't a valid git worktree. It contained only .forge-logs/ and client/node_modules (symlink). (3) Smith wrote Edit tool calls to absolute paths inside .workers/Heimdall-lmxx/client/... but since that dir was empty and had no .git, git parent-walk resolved operations to the main Heimdall checkout. (4) Smith.s 'file_path' JSON entries even included C:/source/fhigit/Heimdall/client/eslint.config.js directly — writing to main. Likely chain: first dispatch at 11:07 created a valid worktree, Smith or something ran git checkout in the main repo (corruption), bead went to needs-attention. On retry at 12:54, VerifyAndRecoverMain detected and recovered main but the stale .workers/Heimdall-lmxx/ directory was reused via isValidWorktree or os.RemoveAll failed silently on Windows due to locked files/antivirus. Fixes to investigate: (a) Tighten isValidWorktree to check for .git file presence and branch correctness, not just git worktree list registration. (b) On os.RemoveAll failure on Windows, retry with backoff or fail fast instead of silently proceeding. (c) After worktree creation, verify .git file exists and Path points to a real worktree before handing control to Smith. (d) Add a Smith-side guard: refuse to run if worktree's .git file missing. (e) Audit for what operation caused Smith to check out the forge branch in the parent repo (worktree.go comment at line 152-156 acknowledges this as a known hazard).

title: Include external_ref (GitHub issue number) in Smith prompt so PRs include Closes #N
description:
## Problem

Smith-generated PRs don't include 'Closes #N' in the body, even though CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md both say it's CRITICAL. The instruction tells Smith to run 'bd show --json | jq .external_ref' to find the issue number, but Smith skips this extra step in practice.

Root cause: forge never passes the external_ref to Smith at all. The data is available in 'bd ready --json' output but is discarded at two points:

1. poller.Bead struct (internal/poller/poller.go:22) — no ExternalRef field
2. prompt.BeadContext struct (internal/prompt/prompt.go:17) — no ExternalRef field

## Fix

1. Add ExternalRef string to poller.Bead with json tag "external_ref"
2. Add ExternalRef string to prompt.BeadContext
3. In the pipeline, copy bead.ExternalRef to the BeadContext when building the prompt
4. In the default prompt template, add a line like:
   {{- if .Bead.ExternalRef}}
   **GitHub Issue**: {{.Bead.ExternalRef}} — include 'Closes #N' in your PR body (where N is the issue number from this URL)
   {{- end}}
5. Smith sees the issue URL in its prompt and includes the Closes line automatically — no extra tool call needed
notes:
Edge case: if external_ref is empty at dispatch time (sync hasn't run yet), the template line is suppressed and Smith creates a PR without Closes #N. Options:
1. Accept it — bellows or burnish can patch the PR body later when external_ref appears
2. Have the pipeline query bd show --json for the latest external_ref just before PR creation (after Smith finishes), as a last-chance lookup
3. Require external_ref to be present before dispatch (poller filters out beads without it) — too restrictive, many valid beads don't have GitHub issues

Option 2 is the most robust: a one-shot bd show call in the PR creation step costs ~1s and guarantees the latest external_ref is used.

title: Burnish: gate push on Temper verification to break the burnish↔quench loop
description:
## Problem

Burnish is the only Smith-invoking worker in Forge that does **not** run Temper before declaring its work successful. Every other code-modifying worker (`pipeline.Run` for the initial PR, `quench.Run` for CI fixes) runs Temper as a verification gate. Burnish does not — it only checks Smith's exit code and trusts the prompt instruction "Run the test suite ... do NOT commit or push if tests are failing" (`burnish.go:519`), which Smith ignores often enough to matter.

This asymmetry is the structural cause of an observed infinite-loop pattern on PRs that receive Copilot review:

```
PR opens (clean — pipeline.Run already ran Temper before opening it)
  → Copilot reviews → leaves comments
  → bellows detects unresolved threads → spawns burnish
  → burnish: Smith addresses comments, may break tests/build/lint, pushes anyway
  → daemon resets bellows snapshot (daemon.go:1086) → fresh CI state detected
  → CI fails → bellows spawns quench
  → quench: Temper repro → Smith fixes CI → Temper verifies → push
  → daemon resets bellows snapshot (daemon.go:1009) → fresh review state
  → Copilot re-reviews the new commits → new comments
  → bellows detects unresolved threads → spawns burnish again
  → ... loop until max_review_fix_attempts (default 5) OR max_ci_fix_attempts (default 5) gives up
```

Worst-case ~10 Smith invocations per PR, all charged as Copilot premium requests when Copilot is the active provider, plus 10 CI runs and the GH-actions minutes that go with them.

The user-observable signature: initial PR creation rarely fails CI (because the pipeline already gates on Temper); the loop **only** starts after the first burnish cycle.

## Why burnish is the one outlier

Worker-by-worker map (verified by reading the source):

| Worker | File | Temper before declaring success? |
|---|---|---|
| Pipeline (initial Smith) | `internal/pipeline/pipeline.go` | ✅ Yes — between Smith and Warden, before PR creation |
| Quench (CI fix) | `internal/quench/quench.go:297, :412` | ✅ Yes — once for local repro, once to verify after Smith |
| **Burnish (review fix)** | `internal/burnish/burnish.go` | ❌ **No — no `temper.Run()` call anywhere in the package** |
| Rebase | `internal/rebase/` | N/A (no code changes, only conflict resolution) |

`grep -r 'temper\.\|temper.Run' internal/burnish` returns zero matches. `burnish.go` does not even import `internal/temper`.

## Fix: push gating in burnish

The cleanest fix is to move the `git push` out of Smith's session and into burnish itself, with Temper as the gate. Smith commits locally; burnish runs Temper; only on success does burnish push.

### Required changes

#### 1. Prompt updates — tell Smith to commit but NOT push

**`internal/burnish/burnish.go:515-523`** (`buildReviewFixPrompt` instructions block):

Replace step 4-5:
```
4. Commit with message: "fix: address review comments for %s"
5. Push to branch: %s
```
with:
```
4. Commit with message: "fix: address review comments for %s"
5. Do NOT push — Forge will run verification and push for you. Exit cleanly after committing.
```

**`internal/burnish/burnish.go:258-266`** (`buildBatchReviewPrompt` instructions block): same edit.

The "Run the test suite" instruction (step 3) can stay — Smith may still catch obvious issues during the session, which saves a Temper round. Just remove the push step.

#### 2. Add Temper verification after Smith exits

In `burnish.Fix` (`burnish.go:271-469`), after the existing `if smithResult.ExitCode != 0 { continue }` check at `:399-419` and before the "Smith succeeded — assume fixes were committed and pushed" log line at `:421-423`, insert:

```go
// Verify locally before pushing. Mirrors quench's verify-after-Smith pattern.
temperCfg := p.TemperConfig
if temperCfg == nil {
    detected := temper.DefaultConfigWithRace(p.WorktreePath, p.DetectOptions, p.GoRaceDetection)
    temperCfg = &detected
}
verifyResult := temper.Run(ctx, p.WorktreePath, *temperCfg, p.DB, p.BeadID, p.AnvilName)
if !verifyResult.Passed {
    log.Printf("[burnish] PR #%d: Temper failed on attempt %d (failed step: %s) — looping with feedback",
        p.PRNumber, attempt, verifyResult.FailedStep)
    _ = p.DB.LogEvent(state.EventBurnishTemperFailed,
        fmt.Sprintf("PR #%d: temper failed on attempt %d at step %s", p.PRNumber, attempt, verifyResult.FailedStep),
        p.BeadID, p.AnvilName)
    // Build the next prompt with the temper failure appended so the next Smith
    // attempt has the failing step output as direct context.
    lastTemperFailure = verifyResult
    continue
}
```

Then, only after temper passes:

```go
// Temper passed — push the verified commits.
if err := gitPush(ctx, p.WorktreePath, p.Branch); err != nil {
    log.Printf("[burnish] PR #%d: push failed after temper-verified fix: %v", p.PRNumber, err)
    _ = p.DB.LogEvent(state.EventBurnishFailed,
        fmt.Sprintf("PR #%d: push failed after temper-verified fix: %v", p.PRNumber, err),
        p.BeadID, p.AnvilName)
    result.Error = fmt.Errorf("push after temper verification: %w", err)
    result.Duration = time.Since(start)
    return result
}

log.Printf("[burnish] PR #%d: Review fixes verified and pushed on attempt %d", p.PRNumber, attempt)
result.Addressed = true
```

Add the same wiring to `burnish.BatchFix` (`burnish.go:101-228`). BatchFix currently has a single attempt and no loop — for the verification path, keep it simple: if Temper fails after the batch fix, log and return `result.Error` so bellows treats it as a failed burnish cycle (it will then dispatch a fresh attempt on the next poll). Do not push if temper failed.

#### 3. Add a small `gitPush` helper

`internal/burnish/burnish.go` doesn't currently shell out to git directly. Add a tiny helper at the bottom of the file:

```go
func gitPush(ctx context.Context, worktreePath, branch string) error {
    cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "-C", worktreePath, "push", "origin", branch)
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("git push origin %s: %w (output: %s)", branch, err, strings.TrimSpace(string(out)))
    }
    return nil
}
```

(Compare to how `quench.go:341` uses `gitRevParse` — same pattern.)

#### 4. Plumb `TemperConfig`, `DetectOptions`, `GoRaceDetection` through `FixParams` and `BatchFixParams`

Currently `FixParams` (`burnish.go:28-57`) and `BatchFixParams` (`:73-97`) don't carry temper config. Add:

```go
TemperConfig    *temper.Config
DetectOptions   *temper.DetectOptions
GoRaceDetection bool
```

to both, and have the daemon dispatch site (`daemon.go:1054-1067` for `burnish.Fix`, `:1038-1050` for `burnish.BatchFix`) pass them from the same anvil config that quench uses today (`daemon.go` already constructs a `TemperConfig` for the quench dispatch path — search for how `quench.FixParams` gets it and mirror exactly).

#### 5. Append the previous Temper failure to the next prompt

Inside the `for attempt` loop in `burnish.Fix`, when `lastTemperFailure != nil` (set from a previous iteration), add a section to the prompt before the existing "Review Comments to Address" block:

```
## Previous Verification Failure

Your previous attempt addressed the review comments but Temper failed when verifying:

Failed step: <name>
Command: <command>
Output:
\`\`\`
<truncated to 4000 chars>
\`\`\`

You must address BOTH the original review comments AND fix this verification failure before committing.
```

This mirrors `buildCIFixPrompt` at `quench.go:463-525`. Extract a small `formatTemperFailureForPrompt(*temper.Result) string` helper to share with quench eventually (not required for this bead).

#### 6. New event type

Add `EventBurnishTemperFailed` to `internal/state/db.go` near the other burnish events at `:1348-1352`:

```go
EventBurnishTemperFailed  EventType = "review_fix_temper_failed"
```

This gives Hearth and the events panel visibility when burnish loops because of a verification failure (vs. Smith error vs. rate limit).

#### 7. Do NOT change the daemon's snapshot reset behavior

`daemon.go:1078-1088` resets the bellows snapshot after a successful burnish. Keep that — it's still correct because after a successful burnish (which now means temper-verified + pushed), CI will run on the verified push and the snapshot needs refreshing. The bug was never the reset; it was that "successful burnish" used to include broken pushes.

## Edge cases to handle

1. **Smith pushes anyway, ignoring the prompt.** Defensive check before `gitPush`: compare `git rev-parse origin/<branch>` against `HEAD`. If they're already equal (Smith pushed), log a warning and skip the explicit push but still treat temper result as authoritative — if temper failed, we cannot un-push, but we should still NOT mark `result.Addressed = true`, so the failed temper feeds into the next attempt and bellows still reacts to the resulting CI failure.

2. **No actionable comments** (existing early-return at `burnish.go:307-312`): unchanged. No fix means no commit means no push means no temper run.

3. **Smith made a commit but Temper fails on attempt N where N == MaxAttempts.** The current loop just falls through to the "could not address review comments after %d attempts" error at `burnish.go:463`. Important: in this case there is a local commit in the worktree that was never pushed. The worker cleanup path (`worktree.Remove`) discards the worktree, so the unpushed commit is dropped naturally. Verify with a test that no orphan branch is left behind on the remote.

4. **Worktree has no `go.mod` / `package.json` / `*.csproj`** (Temper detects nothing). Today `temper.DefaultConfig` returns an empty step list, and `temper.Run` reports `Passed = true` for an empty list. Confirm this is still true after the change — for repos with no detectable build system, burnish should fall through to the push step exactly like it does today (i.e., this fix is a no-op for non-Temper-detectable repos).

5. **Worktree-based race with bellows.** Bellows polls the PR status independently; we don't want bellows to detect the in-flight burnish state and dispatch a duplicate worker. The lifecycle manager already serializes per-PR (`internal/lifecycle/lifecycle.go`); confirm the worker remains marked `Phase: "burnish"` across the new Temper run so the in-flight check still applies.

## Testing

#### Unit tests in `internal/burnish/burnish_test.go`

Add cases (use the existing test scaffolding pattern):

1. **`TestFix_TemperPasses_Pushes`** — stub Smith to exit 0, stub a Temper that returns `Passed: true`, stub a push function. Assert push was called exactly once and `result.Addressed == true`.

2. **`TestFix_TemperFails_LoopsAndDoesNotPush`** — stub Smith to exit 0, stub Temper to return `Passed: false` on attempt 1 and `Passed: true` on attempt 2. Assert push was called exactly once (after attempt 2), `result.Attempts == 2`, `result.Addressed == true`, and that the second prompt contained the temper failure section.

3. **`TestFix_TemperFailsAllAttempts_NoPush`** — Temper fails on every attempt up to MaxAttempts. Assert push was never called, `result.Addressed == false`, `result.Error` mentions exhaustion, and an `EventBurnishTemperFailed` event was logged.

4. **`TestFix_PushFails_ReturnsError`** — Temper passes but `gitPush` returns an error. Assert `result.Addressed == false`, `result.Error` wraps the push error, and the worker is marked failed (so bellows can dispatch a retry).

5. **`TestFix_SmithPushedAnyway_TemperStillAuthoritative`** — defensive case for edge case 1 above. Stub the worktree so `origin/<branch>` already matches `HEAD` after Smith. Assert burnish does NOT call `gitPush` again, but if temper failed it still does NOT mark `result.Addressed = true`.

6. **`TestBatchFix_TemperFails_DoesNotPush`** — same as #3 but for the BatchFix path; just one attempt, returns error.

For tests 1-5, the existing test plumbing in `burnish_test.go` already stubs `smith.SpawnWithProvider` via the package-level test fakes — extend the same pattern for `temper.Run` (introduce a package-level `var temperRun = temper.Run` and override in tests) and for `gitPush` (same pattern: `var gitPushFn = gitPush`).

#### Integration smoke test (manual, after merge)

On a Hytte PR (mixed Go + npm — most likely place for a Temper auto-detect wrinkle):

1. Open a PR that knowingly fails one Copilot review check (e.g. trivial naming nit).
2. Watch `forge hearth` event log for: `review_fix_started` → `review_fix_temper_failed` (if Smith breaks something) OR `review_fix_success` directly.
3. Verify on the PR that **commits only appear after temper passes**, never before.
4. Force a regression: temporarily edit a test to fail, push it as a review-comment fix scenario, confirm burnish loops with the temper failure surfaced in the log, and the broken commit is never pushed.

## Files touched

- `internal/burnish/burnish.go` — main change
- `internal/burnish/burnish_test.go` — new tests + temper/push stubbing
- `internal/state/db.go` — new `EventBurnishTemperFailed` event type
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go` — pass `TemperConfig`/`DetectOptions`/`GoRaceDetection` to `burnish.Fix` and `burnish.BatchFix` (mirror existing quench dispatch)
- `changelog.d/Forge-<id>.md` — `Fixed` category fragment

## Out of scope (file separately if wanted)

- **Push gating in quench.** Quench has the same shape (Smith pushes from inside its session) but already has a verify-Temper, so the failure mode is contained. Worth doing for symmetry but it's not the bug.
- **Alternation circuit breaker in bellows.** Cap N burnish↔quench transitions per PR before flipping to `needs_human`. Nice safety net but unnecessary if push gating works as expected. Defer.
- **Sharing `formatTemperFailureForPrompt` between burnish and quench.** Pure refactor; do as a follow-up if both end up with near-identical helpers.

## Acceptance criteria

- `grep -n 'temper\.' internal/burnish/burnish.go` returns at least one `temper.Run` call.
- A burnish cycle that produces broken code never pushes to the remote (verified in unit test #3 and #5).
- A burnish cycle that produces working code pushes exactly once, after Temper passes (verified in unit test #1).
- The `forge hearth` event log shows `review_fix_temper_failed` events when burnish loops because of verification failure (not just generic Smith errors).
- A repeat of the original loop scenario on a real PR completes within `max_review_fix_attempts` cycles instead of bouncing between burnish and quench until both counters exhaust.

title: Fix worker kill: 2-phase SIGINT→SIGKILL with process group support
description:
When killing a worker via IPC (hearth or dashboard), the underlying process often keeps running.

## Root Cause

The IPC kill_worker handler (internal/daemon/daemon.go:2750-2769) sends SIGINT to the PID and immediately returns without waiting. The claude CLI can catch/ignore SIGINT and stay alive. No fallback to SIGKILL exists.

Additionally, the smith spawns processes without Setpgid, so child processes (git, node, etc.) aren't killed even if the parent dies.

## Fix: 2-Phase Kill with Process Group

### 1. Process group setup in smith (internal/smith/smith.go ~line 175)

When spawning the claude CLI, set Setpgid so the process gets its own process group:

    cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}

This allows killing the entire process tree with kill(-PID, signal).

### 2. IPC kill handler (internal/daemon/daemon.go ~line 2750)

Replace the current single-SIGINT with a 2-phase approach (same pattern as internal/shutdown/shutdown.go:96-151):

Phase 1: Send SIGINT to the process group
    syscall.Kill(-kp.PID, syscall.SIGINT)

Phase 2: Wait up to 5 seconds for the process to exit
    Check if process is still alive with kill(pid, 0)

Phase 3: If still alive, send SIGKILL to the process group
    syscall.Kill(-kp.PID, syscall.SIGKILL)

Phase 4: Verify the process is gone, then update DB status

### 3. Clean up dead code

Delete internal/watchdog/watchdog.go — it's never imported or used. The daemon has its own inline stale detection (runStaleDetection). The watchdog was an early attempt that got replaced.

## Reference

- Daemon kill handler: internal/daemon/daemon.go:2750-2769
- Smith spawning: internal/smith/smith.go:172-239
- Smith Kill method (SIGKILL, exists but not called by IPC): internal/smith/smith.go:414-428
- Graceful shutdown 2-phase reference: internal/shutdown/shutdown.go:96-151
- Dead code to remove: internal/watchdog/watchdog.go

title: Pipeline incorrectly uses blocked-by bead's feature branch as PR base for dependency chains
description:
When bead A blocks bead B (dependency chain, not parent-child), the pipeline creates A's PR targeting feature/B instead of main. This is Crucible behavior leaking into regular dependency chains.

Example: Hytte-w3j2 blocks Hytte-gnf7. The pipeline tried to create a PR from forge/Hytte-w3j2 with base feature/Hytte-gnf7 instead of main. Error: 'No commits between feature/Hytte-gnf7 and forge/Hytte-w3j2, Base ref must be a branch'.

Crucible should ONLY activate for parent-child relationships (bead.Children / bead.Blocks where the blocked bead is a decomposed child). Regular blocks/depends-on dependencies should always PR to main.

Investigate where the PR base branch is determined — likely in pipeline.go or the worktree creation — and ensure it only uses a feature branch when the Crucible is actively managing a parent-child epic.

title: Ledger forms (close, edit, etc.) don't respond to Enter or Tab
description: Huh form internal messages (focus/blur from Init) are not forwarded to the active form in the Update switch's default case, causing Enter (submit) and Tab (next field) to silently do nothing in all Ledger form dialogs (close, edit, new bead, etc.).
close_reason: Fixed by forwarding default messages to active huh form in ledger Update switch

title: NO_CHANGES_NEEDED auto-closes bead even when prior attempt left un-PR'd work on branch
description: When a dispatch fails after Smith commits work (e.g. warden rejection), the branch with changes exists on origin but no PR was created. On retry, Smith sees the work is done and emits NO_CHANGES_NEEDED. The daemon then auto-closes the bead via applyNoChangesNeededOutcome (daemon.go:2367), but no PR is ever created for the committed work. The daemon should check whether a forge branch exists with commits ahead of main before accepting NO_CHANGES_NEEDED as terminal. If such a branch exists, it should either create the PR or escalate to needs_human rather than silently closing.

title: Manual retry reset silently fails for warden rejections
description: When a bead is marked needs_human due to warden rejection (not circuit breaker), the TUI/CLI reset action does nothing. The handler at daemon.go:3062 enters the dispatch_failures>0 branch, calls ResetDispatchFailures which requires last_error LIKE 'circuit breaker:%', matches 0 rows, and returns success without actually clearing needs_human. The ResetRetry fallback at line 3089 is never reached. Fix: replace the ResetDispatchFailures call in the manual reset path with ResetRetry, or remove the last_error filter from ResetDispatchFailures.

title: CLI update-deps: add worktree isolation like Hearth/Ledger overlays
description:
The forge update-deps CLI command (cmd/forge/updatedeps.go) calls CheckoutUpdateBranch directly on the anvil's main repo directory, causing:
1. Dep commits landing on main instead of the branch
2. Multi-anvil runs resetting the branch when the second anvil's CheckoutUpdateBranch runs
3. Repos left on the dep branch instead of main

The Hearth and Ledger update overlays already use worktree isolation (internal/worktree.Manager.CreateWithOptions). The CLI command needs the same pattern.

Fix in cmd/forge/updatedeps.go:
1. For each anvil, create a worktree via worktree.NewManager().CreateWithOptions() with the branch name
2. Run CheckoutUpdateBranch, ExecuteGroups, GenerateChangelog, and CreatePR inside the worktree path
3. Clean up the worktree after PR creation (or on failure)
4. The main anvil directory stays on main throughout

Reference the Hearth overlay implementation in internal/hearth/update_overlay.go (the processAnvil closure pattern) — the CLI should follow the same approach.
notes: Additional fix: the --dry-run scan should also use a worktree. On Windows, npm ci fails with EPERM when native .node binaries are locked by editors/antivirus in the main repo's node_modules. Scanning in a worktree avoids this since it has its own node_modules. Apply worktree isolation to both the scan and apply phases of the CLI command.

title: Schematic: auto-close parent bead after decomposition and transfer downstream blocks
description:
After the schematic decomposes a parent bead into sub-beads, the parent is left open. When all sub-beads complete, the parent becomes unblocked and the forge picks it up again — attempting to re-implement or re-decompose work that's already done.

Current behavior (internal/schematic/schematic.go, around line 534):
- Sub-beads are created and chained sequentially (B1→B2→B3)
- The last sub-bead (B3) blocks the parent via bd dep add
- Downstream blocks are transferred from parent to last sub-bead (Forge-29ub)
- Parent is left open with a resetParent() call that just resets its status

Expected behavior:
- After successful decomposition and chain transfer, close the parent with --force
- The close reason should mention the sub-bead IDs
- Use bd close <parent-id> --force --reason='Decomposed into N sub-beads: <id1>, <id2>, ...'

The fix is in the executeDecomposition function. After the chain transfer block (lines ~498-532) and before the return, replace the resetParent() call with:
1. Run: bd close <parent.ID> --force --reason='Decomposed into <N> sub-beads: <ids>'
2. Log the closure
3. If the close fails, log a warning but don't fail the decomposition (the sub-beads are already created)

The --force flag is needed because the parent has open sub-beads blocking it (which is correct — we want to close it despite those blockers since the sub-beads represent its work).

Files to modify:
- internal/schematic/schematic.go — executeDecomposition function, replace resetParent() with bd close --force

Test: verify in schematic_test.go that after decomposition the parent bead's status changes to closed.

title: Depupdate: use git worktree isolation instead of branch checkout in main repo
description:
The update panel (Hearth/Ledger) currently uses CheckoutUpdateBranch which checks out a deps/batch-update-* branch directly in the anvil's main working directory. This causes multiple problems:

1. The anvil repo is left on the dep branch after the run, breaking the poller which expects main
2. Commits can accidentally land on main if the branch checkout fails or is at the same point as main  
3. Other forge operations (Smith, Bellows) that expect the repo on main are disrupted
4. Multiple concurrent operations on the same anvil would conflict

Fix: Use worktree.Manager.CreateWithOptions() to create an isolated git worktree for dependency updates, following the same pattern as pipeline.go (line 511). The worktree should be created before CheckoutUpdateBranch, all npm/dotnet/go install commands should run in the worktree path, and the worktree should be cleaned up after the PR is created (or on failure).

Changes needed:
- internal/hearth/update_overlay.go (runUpdateApply): create worktree per anvil, pass worktree path to Apply/CheckoutUpdateBranch/CreatePR, cleanup after
- internal/ledger/update_overlay.go: same changes
- internal/depupdate/api.go (Apply): accept worktree path instead of anvil path
- internal/depupdate/pr.go (CheckoutUpdateBranch, CreatePR): work in worktree path
- May need to pass worktree.Manager through to the update overlay

Reference: internal/pipeline/pipeline.go lines 507-560 for the worktree pattern, internal/worktree/worktree.go for the Manager API.

title: Depupdate: npm install runs in wrong directory for multi-package.json repos
description:
When a repo has multiple package.json files (e.g. root and web/), InstallNpmGroup always runs npm install from anvilPath (repo root). If the outdated package is in web/package.json, npm installs against the root package.json instead, creating a spurious root node_modules/ and not updating web/package-lock.json.

The depcheck scanner (findNpmProjects in depcheck/npm.go) correctly discovers all package.json directories, but the directory information is lost during grouping — UpdateGroup doesn't track which source directory the updates came from.

Fix needed:
1. Add a SourceDir field to ModuleUpdate or UpdateGroup that records the directory where the package.json was found
2. InstallNpmGroup should use group.SourceDir (or the first update's source dir) instead of anvilPath
3. This ensures npm install runs in the correct directory and updates the right package-lock.json

Affected files:
- internal/depcheck/npm.go (scanNpm — needs to populate SourceDir on each ModuleUpdate)
- internal/depupdate/grouper.go (needs to preserve SourceDir through grouping)
- internal/depupdate/npm.go (InstallNpmGroup — use SourceDir)
- internal/depupdate/depupdate.go (installGroup — pass correct dir)

title: Hearth: depupdate git/bd commands leak stdout to terminal (tab title corruption)
description: Multiple cmd.Run() calls in depupdate/pr.go, depupdate/verify.go, and depupdate/changelog.go set cmd.Stderr but not cmd.Stdout, allowing git push, git reset, git commit, and bd close output to leak to the terminal. This corrupts the TUI display and changes the terminal tab title during update operations. Fix: add cmd.Stdout = io.Discard to all cmd.Run() calls that don't need stdout.
close_reason: Fixed: added io.Discard to all cmd.Run() calls in depupdate that were missing stdout capture

title: Ledger: 'No beads match the current filter' — multiple --status flags in bd list command fails
description:
When selecting an anvil in the Ledger, it shows 'No beads match the current filter' even though beads exist. Root cause: internal/ledger/data.go line 139 calls bd with multiple --status flags in a single invocation: bd list --status=open --status=in_progress --limit 0 --json. The bd CLI likely does not support multiple --status flags this way — throughout the rest of the codebase (poller.go, dedup.go, pr.go), separate bd list calls are made per status.

Fix: In internal/ledger/data.go FetchAnvilBeads() (line 139) and FetchAllBeads() (lines 236, 254-255), either:
(a) Make separate bd list calls for each status and merge the results, following the pattern in internal/poller/poller.go and internal/depcheck/dedup.go, OR
(b) Use a comma-separated status value if bd supports it (check bd list --help for syntax).

Also check if the same issue exists elsewhere in the ledger data fetching code (FetchAllBeads has the same pattern at lines 236 and 254).

title: Hearth: update scan phase leaks stdout (tab title changes, missing stdout suppression in depcheck)
description: PR #399 fixed stdout suppression in depupdate/ (Apply phase) but missed depcheck/ (Scan phase). depcheck/npm.go runNpmInstall() doesn't set cmd.Stdout=io.Discard, so npm ci output leaks to terminal changing the tab title. Also hearth.go updateApplyDoneMsg handler doesn't reset window title via tea.SetWindowTitle after update completes. Live Activity may not be properly wiring up the synthetic worker's log tailer.

title: Hearth/Ledger: update panel applies deps directly on main instead of worktree+PR
description: The update overlay (U panel) in both Hearth and Ledger calls depupdate.Apply() directly with the anvil path, committing updates straight to main. The CLI command (forge update-deps --create-pr) already does it correctly: CheckoutUpdateBranch → Apply in worktree → GenerateChangelog → CreatePR → cleanup. Fix: wire the TUI update path through the same worktree+branch+PR flow. Files: internal/hearth/update_overlay.go (runUpdateApply), internal/ledger/update_overlay.go, internal/depupdate/pr.go (existing correct utilities).

title: Ledger: crash fetching closed beads (time.Time year out of range)
description: When fetching closed beads via 'bd list --status=closed --limit 50 --json', the Ledger crashes with: 'encoding JSON: json: error calling MarshalJSON for type time.Time: Time.MarshalJSON: year outside of range [0,9999]'. The bd database returns timestamps with an out-of-range year in closed_at or updated_at fields. These unmarshal fine into *time.Time but fail when Go later tries to re-marshal them (e.g. for the detail panel or any JSON serialization path). Fix: in internal/ledger/data.go, add validation when parsing bd JSON output to skip or sanitize beads with out-of-range timestamps. The Bead struct is defined around lines 19-36 in data.go; the fetch happens in fetchAllBeadsWithExec around lines 117-154. Options: custom UnmarshalJSON for the timestamp fields that zeros out invalid values, or a post-parse filter that drops beads with nonsensical dates.

title: Smelter: stale remote tracking ref causes force-with-lease rejection after batch PR merge
description: After a batch warden-learn PR is merged and GitHub auto-deletes the branch, the local remote tracking ref (refs/remotes/origin/forge/warden-learn-batch/<anvil>) becomes stale. On the next smelter flush, two bugs manifest: (1) CreateWithOptions creates the new worktree from the stale pre-merge remote ref instead of main, and (2) commitAndPush's git push --force-with-lease fails with '(stale info)' because the stale tracking ref doesn't match the deleted remote branch. Fix: skip the 'create from remote' path when ResetBranch=true (always create from main), and clear the stale tracking ref when git fetch reports the remote branch doesn't exist.
close_reason: Fixed in f0dc0b2, pushed directly to main

title: fix: closeBead after IPC merge blocks response past IPC read deadline
description: closeBead (bd close) was added synchronously in the merge_pr IPC handler before the response is sent back. The IPC client Send() has a 10-second read deadline. If the merge + bd close takes longer than that, Hearth gets a timeout error and shows a spurious 'Failed to merge' in the status bar, even though both the merge and bead close actually succeeded. Fix: run closeBead in a goroutine so the ok response is returned immediately after the merge, and the bead close happens in the background.

title: fix: depcheck fails and skips scan when git pull fails on anvil
description: depcheck.scanAnvil already attempts git pull --ff-only before scanning, but on failure it only logs a warning and scans anyway — against stale dependency files, which causes duplicate beads for already-merged updates. Fix: if the pull fails, log EventDepcheckFailed to the event log and return early, skipping the scan for that anvil entirely.

title: fix: bead not closed when PR merged via IPC merge_pr handler
description: When a PR is merged via the forge hearth merge button (IPC merge_pr), the bead is not automatically closed. Root cause: UpdatePRStatus(PRMerged) is called before bellowsMonitor.Refresh(), so bellows' transition check (newSnap.IsMerged && \!lastSnap.IsMerged) never fires — both snapshots already show IsMerged=true. The bead stays in_progress until the watchdog's orphan recovery fires ~14 minutes later. Fix: call closeBead directly in the IPC merge handler (same as handleBeadCloseOnMerge), rather than relying on bellows transition detection.

title: fix: log DB event and mark needs_human when PR creation fails in finalizePipeline
description:
When CreatePR fails in finalizePipeline (daemon.go ~line 1910), only d.logger.Error is called — no DB event is written and the bead is not marked needs_human. The bead silently stalls in monitoring/bellows state with no visible trace in forge history events or the Hearth TUI. Observed on Hytte-eal: warden_pass was logged then nothing, PR never created.

Fix:
1. Log a DB event (e.g. EventPRCreationFailed or reuse EventSmithFailed) on CreatePR error so it shows up in forge history
2. Call d.db.MarkNeedsHuman so the bead surfaces in the Needs Attention panel
3. Consider: if a PR already exists for the branch (duplicate run), handle gracefully instead of failing

title: fix: force_smith holds activeBeads slot to prevent concurrent normal pipeline
description: Force smith dispatched a goroutine without claiming the activeBeads slot. After ResetRetry cleared needs_human, the poller could immediately pick up the same bead and run a normal pipeline in parallel with the force_smith worker.

title: fix: skip lifecycle actions (rebase/cifix/burnish) for non-bead PRs
description: Warden-learn PRs created by Bellows have no bead ID. When they get a merge conflict, the lifecycle manager dispatches a rebase action with empty BeadID. worktreeMgr.Create with empty beadID collapses the worktree path to .workers/ itself (the workers container dir), causing Smith to run in the wrong directory and potentially corrupt other worktrees.

title: Orphan recovery should skip beads in needs_human state
description:
Orphan recovery currently resets any in_progress bead with no open PR to open. But beads in needs_human=1 state are intentionally parked — they don't have an open PR by design, and resetting them to open just re-dispatches them without the human attention they need.

Fix: in RecoverOrphanedBeads (internal/daemon/daemon.go), skip beads that have needs_human=1 or clarification_needed=1 in the retries table. These are already surfaced in the Needs Attention panel and should only be re-dispatched via explicit user action (Retry, Force Smith, etc.).

title: Force smith should continue with temper/warden/PR instead of re-dispatching
description:
