After force smith completes, the current implementation resets the bead to open and calls pollAndDispatch, which re-runs the full pipeline (including schematic + smith) from scratch. Instead it should continue with temper → warden → PR on the same branch.

Fix: add a SkipSmith bool field to pipeline.Params. When true, pipeline.Run skips schematic and the smith loop entirely, creates a worktree on the existing branch (ResetBranch=false), and proceeds directly to temper → warden → PR.

In handleForceSmith (internal/daemon/daemon.go), after smith succeeds:
1. Remove the force_smith worktree
2. Call pipeline.Run with SkipSmith=true, same branch, ResetBranch=false
3. Remove the bd update --status=open and pollAndDispatch calls (pipeline.Run handles bead lifecycle)

The bead should stay in_progress throughout (not reset to open), with the worker showing phase=temper → warden → bellows normally.
notes:
SkipSmith=true, pipeline.Run creates a worktree but never removes it — the defer worktreeMgr.Remove(...) call must still execute on the
   SkipSmith path, just like the normal path.
  ▎ 2. Duplicate PR creation: PR creation is happening both inside pipeline.Run and outside it in handleForceSmith — remove the duplicate. Only the pipeline
  should create the PR.

  ▎ Do not claim these are already fixed — the warden explicitly identified them in your iteration 1 diff. Fix both issues.

title: Track external PRs in hearth PR panel with periodic reconciliation
description: External PRs (created outside forge) don't appear in hearth's PR panel until daemon restart. Fix: run reconcileGitHubPRs periodically and on PR panel open. Add title column to prs table. Visually distinguish external PRs and filter action menu.
close_reason: Shipped in v0.7.0 with follow-up fixes in v0.7.1 (bellows assignment, PR reconciliation scoping, snapshot seeding)

title: Fix crucible: children with blocks=[parent] misidentified as crucible parents
description: When bd ready returns children that block their parent (blocks=[parentID]), IsCrucibleCandidate returns true for each child because Blocks is non-empty. The parent is NOT in the ready results (it's blocked), so the poller's reconstruction can't fix this. Each child gets dispatched as a separate crucible worker trying to orchestrate the parent as a child — creating zombie crucibles. Fix: filter Blocks to only include IDs present in the current poll batch.

title: Hearth: fix Workers panel table corruption and selected row style
description: Worker table rows are corrupted because ANSI-styled status indicators get mangled by runewidth.Truncate inside the Bubbles table component. Also the selected row background (bright orange) is painful to look at.
close_reason: Fixed ANSI corruption in worker table cells and softened selected row color

title: Queue action: force-run bead independently (bypass bd ready)
description: Add a 'Run independently' action to the Hearth queue action menu and to 'forge queue run'. Currently forge queue run relies on bd ready which filters out children with parents and has other quirks. The force-run should fetch the bead via bd show instead, skip crucible detection, skip parent/blocker checks, and dispatch it straight through the pipeline as a standalone bead. This enables running individual children without starting the whole crucible.

title: fix: retry reset should also reset bead status to open
description: When a crucible (or any bead) pauses after a dispatch failure, the bead status in beads DB is left as in_progress. The retry_bead IPC command clears dispatch failures and assignee but does NOT reset the bead status back to open, so bd ready never returns it and the poller can't re-dispatch. The fix is to run 'bd update <id> --status=open' as part of the retry reset flow.

title: Hearth: action menu for paused Crucibles (resume/stop)
description: When a Crucible pauses (child failure, parent failure, merge conflict), there's no way to resume or stop it from the Hearth TUI. Need an action overlay on the Crucibles panel (similar to Queue/PR action menus) with at minimum: Resume (retry parent bead to re-enter crucible loop) and Stop (close the parent bead or mark exhausted). Currently the user must manually run 'forge queue retry' on both the failed child and parent from CLI.

title: PR panel: show all anvil PRs, 3-flag status, merge/cifix actions
description: The Hearth PR panel should show all open PRs in registered anvils (not just Forge-tracked ones). Show three consistent ✓/✗ flags for CI, unresolved comments, and conflicts. Add Merge and Fix CI to the action menu. External (non-Forge) PRs should still be actionable via reviewfix/rebase/cifix workers.

title: Autolearn error
description:
Investigate this

5:13:09 auto_learn_error [Forge-x7j0] forge PR #215: no new rules — 9 of 9 comment group(s) failed to distill

title: Main repo branch gets hijacked by worktree's feature branch
description: The main repo (anvil root) can end up checked out to a feature branch (e.g. forge/Forge-x1bs) instead of main. This corrupts the working environment for all subsequent workers including reviewfix and cifix. Root cause unclear but likely: (1) the smith/claude subprocess runs git checkout in the parent directory instead of the worktree, or (2) git worktree add reuses a branch that already exists locally and associates it with the main repo. Two fixes needed: (a) Add a safety check in the daemon poll loop or before dispatching work that verifies the anvil root is on main/master and resets if not. (b) Consider adding explicit instructions in the smith prompt to never cd outside the working directory or run git checkout on the parent repo.

title: Bug: decomposed children don't inherit forgeReady label from parent
description: When schematic decomposes a bead into children, the children are created with dependency links back to the parent but without the forgeReady label. Since the poller only dispatches beads tagged with forgeReady (when auto_dispatch is set to tagged:forgeReady), the children sit in the queue forever and the parent stays open waiting for them. Fix: after decomposition, the daemon should copy the forgeReady label (or whatever the anvil's auto_dispatch tag is) from the parent to each child bead. The relevant code path is daemon.go around line 1314 where outcome.Decomposed is handled — after ClearRetry, iterate over the created children and add the label via bd update --add-label.

title: Bug: failed pipeline doesn't clear bead assignee, blocking re-dispatch
description: When a pipeline fails or a bead is circuit-broken, the bead's assignee (set during claim via bd update --claim) is never cleared. The poller filters out any bead with a non-empty assignee (poller.go:184), so the bead becomes permanently invisible to the forge even after circuit breaker reset. The retry reset command (forge queue retry) only clears needs_human in state.db but doesn't touch the bead's assignee in the beads database. Fix: when the pipeline fails and the bead is released back to open status, also clear the assignee. Check releaseBead in pipeline.go and shutdown.go resetBead — both should call bd update <id> --assignee='' alongside the status reset.

title: Bug: crucible child failure causes orphan recovery loop and standalone dispatch
description: When a crucible child fails (e.g. warden rejects after max iterations), the crucible returns with an error but leaves the child bead in_progress with no active worker. Orphan recovery then resets it to open, and the poller dispatches it as a standalone bead outside the crucible context. The child should either be marked needs_human or properly reset by the crucible itself so orphan recovery doesnt pick it up. See Forge event log: crucible_child_failed then bead_recovered 2 minutes later.

title: Bug: bellows doesn't retry cifix after failed attempt — transition detection gap
description:
When a cifix worker fails to fix CI and NotifyCIFixCompleted() resets the PR state, bellows never re-detects the CI failure because it only fires EventCIFailed on state transitions (passing → failing), not on stable failing states.

## Reproduction
1. PR has CI failure
2. Bellows detects transition, dispatches cifix
3. Cifix fails (CI still broken)
4. NotifyCIFixCompleted() clears CINeedsFix, resets PR to open
5. Next bellows poll sees CI still failing — same state as before — no transition
6. No new EventCIFailed emitted, no retry dispatched
7. PR sits forever with failing CI, effectively abandoned

## Root Cause
bellows/bellows.go checkPR() only emits EventCIFailed when ciPassing transitions from true→false. After cifix resets the state, the next poll sees ciPassing=false (same as lastStatuses), so no event fires. The lifecycle manager's CIFixCount allows 5 retries but never gets past 1.

## Fix Options
1. After NotifyCIFixCompleted(), force bellows to clear its lastStatuses cache for that PR so the next poll sees a fresh transition
2. Have NotifyCIFixCompleted() check if CI is still failing and re-emit EventCIFailed immediately
3. In bellows checkPR(), also fire EventCIFailed when CI is failing AND CINeedsFix is false AND CIFixCount < max (i.e. detect that a retry is needed)

Option 3 is probably cleanest — bellows already has the CI state and can check the lifecycle counters.

title: Bug: orphan recovery fallback still resets non-Forge beads after 15 minutes

title: Add Copilot premium request tracking and daily limit
description:
Copilot charges per 'premium request' with model-dependent multipliers (opus 4.6 = 3x, sonnet 4.6 = 1x, haiku 4.5 = 0.33x, gpt-5.4 = 1x, gpt-5.1-codex-max = 1x, gpt-5-mini = 0x free, etc). Each smith/warden/lifecycle invocation using copilot provider counts as 1 premium request multiplied by the model's multiplier.

Implementation:
1. Add multiplier lookup table in internal/cost/ keyed by copilot model name
2. Add copilot_premium_requests table in state.db: (date TEXT, requests_used REAL, request_limit INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY date). Use REAL for requests_used since multipliers can be fractional (0.33x).
3. Add config setting: copilot_daily_request_limit (int, default 0 = no limit). When set and exceeded, copilot provider is skipped in the fallback chain (not rate-limit — just skip).
4. Record premium requests in pipeline after each copilot invocation
5. Daemon dispatch loop checks copilot request budget before allowing copilot provider
6. Add GetTodayCopilotRequests() and AddCopilotRequest(model, multiplier) to state.DB

Premium request multiplier reference (2026):
- claude-opus-4.6: 3x, claude-opus-4.6-fast: 30x, claude-opus-4.5: 3x
- claude-sonnet-4.6/4.5/4: 1x
- claude-haiku-4.5: 0.33x
- gpt-5.4/5.3-codex/5.2-codex/5.2/5.1-codex-max/5.1-codex/5.1: 1x
- gpt-5.1-codex-mini: 0.33x
- gpt-5-mini/gpt-4.1: 0x (free)
- gemini-3-pro-preview/2.5-pro: 1x

title: Fix cost persistence — pipeline must call AddBeadCost/AddDailyCost
description: Smith captures CostUSD and token counts in smith.Result, and pipeline logs them in event messages, but db.AddBeadCost() and db.AddDailyCost() are never called. This means: (1) daily_cost_limit enforcement is broken (GetTodayCost always returns 0), (2) bead_costs table is always empty, (3) the Hearth cannot display real cost data. Fix pipeline.Run() to persist costs after smith completes. Also persist costs from lifecycle workers (cifix, reviewfix, rebase). This is foundational for all usage tracking.

title: Fix copilot provider model selection — honor Model field from config
description: copilotArgs() in provider.go hardcodes --model claude-sonnet-4.6 and only allows override via claude_flags. The Model field (from copilot/model-name config syntax) is never used — unlike claude and gemini providers which both honor p.Model. Fix copilotArgs() to use p.Model when set, falling back to claude-sonnet-4.6 default. This enables configs like 'copilot/gpt-5.4' or 'copilot/claude-opus-4.6' in providers/smith_providers lists.

title: GitHub Actions release workflow with GoReleaser
description:
Add a GitHub Actions workflow that triggers on tag push (v*) and runs GoReleaser to build binaries and create a GitHub release. The .goreleaser.yml already exists and builds for Windows/Linux/macOS. The workflow should:

1. Trigger on push of tags matching v*
2. Checkout with fetch-depth 0 (GoReleaser needs history)
3. Set up Go
4. Run GoReleaser release
5. The CHANGELOG.md content for this version should be included in the release notes

GoReleaser config is already at .goreleaser.yml in the repo root.

title: Orphan recovery should only reset beads the Forge previously claimed
description: The orphan recovery logic resets any in_progress bead to open if it has no active worker in the Forge state DB. But beads can be in_progress because a human or another tool (e.g. Copilot on a colleagues machine) is working on them. The Forge should only recover beads it has a record of claiming — check the workers table or events for a bead_claimed event before resetting. Without this, adding a new anvil with existing in_progress beads causes the Forge to reset all of them to open.

title: Lifecycle actions fail when worktree already exists
description: When bellows detects CI failure, review changes, or merge conflicts, the lifecycle handler tries to create a worktree for the fix worker. But if the original pipeline's worktree wasn't cleaned up (e.g. the pipeline completed but the cleanup didn't remove the directory), the worktree.Create call returns 'worktree already exists' and the fix/rebase never runs. Fix: reuse the existing worktree instead of erroring.
close_reason: Fixed: reuse existing worktree instead of erroring

title: Crucible: detect parent-child from blocks/blocked_by instead of requiring parent field
description:
The crucible workflow currently requires children to have the 'parent' field set so ResolveEpicBranches can discover the epic branch. But bd ready hides children of epics (beads with parent set), so the poller never sees them — chicken-and-egg problem.

The fix: when a ready bead blocks an epic-type bead (visible in the blocks/blocked_by dependency graph), the poller should detect that relationship and resolve the epic branch from the blocked epic — without requiring the parent field. This way children stay visible in bd ready while still being routed through crucible.

Current flow: child.Parent -> lookup parent -> IsEpicBead -> resolve branch
Desired flow: child.Blocks contains epic-type bead -> resolve branch from that epic

Affected files: internal/poller/epicbranch.go, internal/poller/crucible.go, internal/daemon/daemon.go

title: Crucible: auto-orchestrate parent beads with children on feature branches
description:
Replace the manual epic-type/label approach with automatic detection and orchestration of parent-child bead relationships. The Crucible is where separate beads are melted together into a single unified PR.

## Design

### Auto-Detection
During polling, if a bead has children (beads that list it as a dependency / it blocks other beads), the forge automatically treats it as a Crucible. No special type or label required — the structure IS the signal.

Detection: `bd show <id> --json` returns a `blocks` field listing child beads. If a ready bead has blockers, it's a Crucible candidate.

### Crucible Dispatcher (new component: `internal/crucible/`)
A new orchestration layer that manages the full lifecycle:

1. **Claim parent** — mark parent bead in_progress
2. **Create feature branch** — `feature/<parent-id>` from main, push to origin
3. **Resolve child order** — topological sort of children by their inter-dependencies. Children with no deps between them can potentially run in parallel (future optimization), but initially dispatch sequentially
4. **Dispatch child** — run the normal pipeline (Smith → Temper → Warden → PR) but targeting the feature branch instead of main
5. **Wait for child PR merge** — monitor the child's PR against the feature branch. Auto-merge when CI passes (since it's a feature branch, no human review needed). Or use bellows + existing merge flow
6. **Dispatch next child** — the feature branch now has the previous child's work, so the next Smith starts from a complete codebase
7. **Final PR** — when all children are done, create PR from feature branch → main. This gets the full review/CI treatment
8. **Close parent** — after the final PR merges (detected by bellows), close the parent bead and clean up

### Events
The Crucible must emit events at every stage so the workflow is visible in the Events panel and logs:
- `crucible_started` — parent claimed, feature branch created, N children queued
- `crucible_child_dispatched` — child bead dispatched to Smith (attempt N of M)
- `crucible_child_pr_created` — child's PR created against feature branch
- `crucible_child_merged` — child's PR merged into feature branch
- `crucible_child_failed` — child failed (exhausted retries)
- `crucible_final_pr` — all children done, final PR created against main
- `crucible_complete` — final PR merged, parent closed
- `crucible_paused` — a child failed permanently, needs human attention

### Integration Points
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go` — during pollAndDispatch, detect parent beads and hand off to Crucible instead of normal dispatch
- `internal/poller/poller.go` — enrich beads with children/blocks info (already partially there via `bd show`)
- `internal/worktree/worktree.go` — CreateEpicBranch and BaseBranch support already exist from Forge-hu9
- `internal/pipeline/pipeline.go` — BaseBranch passthrough already exists from Forge-hu9
- `internal/ghpr/ghpr.go` — Base parameter already supported
- `internal/bellows/bellows.go` — monitor feature-branch PRs, auto-merge children

### Child PR Merge Strategy
Children PRing into the feature branch should auto-merge (squash) once CI passes — no human review needed for intermediate steps. Only the final PR to main gets full review. This could be controlled by:
- Detecting the PR base is not main/master
- A config flag: `auto_merge_epic_children: true`

### Edge Cases
- Child fails permanently (exhausts retries) → pause the Crucible, surface in Needs Attention
- New commits on main conflict with feature branch → periodic rebase of feature branch onto main (between child dispatches)
- Child has external dependencies (not just on siblings) → skip until unblocked
- Parent bead has no children yet (children created later) → re-check periodically

### Testing
- Unit tests for topological sort of children
- Unit tests for Crucible state machine (started → dispatching → waiting → next → final PR → complete)
- Integration test: mock pipeline + mock ghpr to verify full lifecycle
- Test edge cases: child failure pauses Crucible, rebase between children, external deps

### Documentation
- Update CLAUDE.md component map with Crucible
- Update CLAUDE.md data flow to show Crucible path
- Update docs/configuration.md with Crucible-related settings
- Update README.md with Crucible feature description

### Key Benefit
The user just creates beads with dependencies. The Forge sees the structure and does everything else — branch creation, ordered execution, merging, final PR, cleanup. Zero manual orchestration needed.

title: Bug: merged PR lingers in Ready to Merge panel until next bellows poll (up to 2 min)
description:
After a successful merge via the Ready to Merge action, the daemon (daemon.go:1699-1704) only logs an event and returns 'ok' to the TUI. It does NOT:

1. Update the PR status in the DB to 'merged' — so ReadyToMergePRs() still returns it
2. Call bellows.Refresh() — so bellows won't re-poll until the next 2-minute interval
3. Update lifecycle state — so lifecycle still considers it active
4. Close the bead or complete workers

The PR stays visible in the Ready to Merge panel until bellows happens to poll GitHub, detects state=MERGED, and updates the DB. With the default 2-minute bellows interval, this means the PR sits there for up to 2 minutes after being merged.

## Fix
After a successful ghpr.Merge() call (line 1698), add:
1. `d.db.UpdatePRStatus(pr.ID, state.PRMerged)` — immediately remove from ReadyToMergePRs query
2. `d.bellowsMonitor.Refresh()` — trigger immediate bellows poll to handle downstream effects (bead close, worker cleanup)
3. Optionally emit a lifecycle EventPRMerged so lifecycle runs ActionCloseBead

The DB update alone would give instant feedback in the TUI. The bellows refresh ensures all downstream cleanup happens promptly rather than waiting for the next poll cycle.

title: Bug: CI fix worker completion doesn't reset lifecycle CIPassing flag — PR gets permanently stuck
description:
After a CI fix worker (ActionFixCI) completes in daemon.go, there is no NotifyCIFixCompleted() call on the lifecycle manager. The lifecycle's st.CIPassing stays false and st.CINeedsFix stays true. When bellows next polls and re-detects CI failure (via its own reset snapshot), the lifecycle guard at line 267 (`if !st.CIPassing`) triggers 'already failing, skipping dispatch' and drops the event. The PR is permanently stuck — no new cifix workers are ever dispatched.

Compare with ActionFixReview (line 528) which correctly calls NotifyReviewFixCompleted() to reset ReviewNeedsFix.

## Fix
1. Add NotifyCIFixCompleted() to lifecycle Manager that resets st.CIPassing=true and st.CINeedsFix=false (mirror NotifyReviewFixCompleted logic)
2. Call it from daemon.go after the cifix worker completes (line ~491), gated on res.Error==nil
3. Also handle the DB status update: if CIPassing is reset and no ReviewNeedsFix, transition needs_fix → open so bellows can re-detect cleanly

## Reproduction
PR #76 (Forge-8rk) hit this exact bug: after retry_reset at 17:28, rebase succeeded, cifix worker ran at 17:32 and completed at 17:33, but all subsequent ci_failed events from bellows were dropped by lifecycle. PR stuck in needs_fix with ci_fix_count=1 forever.

title: Bug: DistillRule uses extractJSON which requires 'verdict' key
description: In learn.go DistillRule(), extractJSON(output) is called to parse the Claude-generated rule JSON. But extractJSON() in warden.go only matches JSON containing the 'verdict' key (designed for review verdicts). Rule JSON has 'id'/'check' keys instead, so extractJSON always returns empty. The fallback uses raw stdout which is fragile. Fix: either make extractJSON generic or write a separate extractRuleJSON helper.

title: Show exhausted PRs in Needs Attention panel with retry action
description:
PRs that have exhausted their CI-fix or review-fix attempt limits (ci_fix_count >= maxCI=5 or review_fix_count >= maxRev=5) silently stop being worked by Bellows with no visibility in the TUI.

Desired behaviour:
- Such PRs should appear in the Hearth TUI Needs Attention panel (left column) with a clear reason, e.g. 'CI fix exhausted (5/5)' or 'Review fix exhausted (5/5)' or 'Conflicting rebase exhausted (3/3)'.
- The panel entry should include the PR number, bead ID, anvil, and reason.
- A Retry action in the action menu should reset the counters (ci_fix_count=0, review_fix_count=0) and set status back to open, so Bellows immediately re-detects and dispatches a new fix cycle on its next poll.
- A Dismiss action should mark the PR as closed/stale so it no longer appears.

Implementation notes:
- Add a new db query (e.g. db.ExhaustedPRs()) that returns PRs with ci_fix_count >= 5 OR review_fix_count >= 5 (or matching rebase count), with status NOT IN (merged, closed).
- Extend FetchNeedsAttention in internal/hearth/data.go to include these results, mapped to NeedsAttentionItem with Reason field set.
- Use the existing action menu infrastructure in hearth.go (ActionRetry / ActionDismiss), wiring Retry to call db.UpdatePRLifecycle(id, 0, 0, ...) + db.UpdatePRStatus(id, PROpen).
- The maxCI / maxRev thresholds are currently hardcoded in lifecycle.Manager (5/5/3). Consider exposing them via config (forge.yaml settings.max_ci_fix_attempts, settings.max_review_fix_attempts) or at minimum reading from a shared constant so the DB query threshold matches.
- The listprs and resetpr tools in cmd/ are ad-hoc helpers; this feature makes them unnecessary for normal operator use.

title: Bug: lifecycle NeedsFix flag shared between CI and review causes missed review fixes
description:
The lifecycle manager uses a single NeedsFix boolean for both CI failures and review comments. When a CI failure sets NeedsFix=true and a review change event arrives simultaneously, the review fix is skipped with 'already in fix cycle'. When CI passes and clears NeedsFix=false, the review comments are silently forgotten because bellows only triggers on the transition from 0 to >0 unresolved threads, which already happened and was missed.

Observed on PR #57 (Forge-fv5): copilot left 6 review comments, but CI failed at the same time. CI fix was dispatched and succeeded, but review comments were never addressed.

Fix: Either (a) split NeedsFix into separate CINeedsFix and ReviewNeedsFix flags, or (b) when EventCIPassed clears NeedsFix, check if HasUnresolvedThreads is still true and re-dispatch a review fix. Option (a) is cleaner — CI and review are independent fix cycles that should not block each other.

title: Dispatch circuit breaker: stop retrying after N consecutive failures
description: When a bead fails dispatch repeatedly (claimBead fails, smith crashes on startup, etc.), Forge currently retries it every poll cycle forever. Adopt gastown's circuit breaker pattern: track consecutive dispatch failures per bead. After 3 failures, mark the bead as circuit-broken (set needs_human=1 with reason) so it stops being dispatched. This prevents one poison bead from consuming capacity every 30s. Implementation: add a dispatch_failures counter to the retries table (or a new column). In dispatchBead error paths, increment the counter. In pollAndDispatch, skip beads that have hit the threshold. Reset the counter when a human retries from the Needs Attention panel.

title: Bug: daemon only dispatches one smith at a time after initial batch completes
description: With max_smiths_per_anvil=4 and max_total_smiths=7, Forge correctly starts 3 smiths initially. But after those complete, it only dispatches one smith at a time instead of filling back up to the configured limits. The poll loop or dispatch logic likely has a bug where it only picks up one bead per poll cycle instead of filling available capacity. Check internal/daemon/ dispatch logic — the loop that checks available capacity and dispatches new workers should fill all available slots each cycle, not just one.

title: Hearth: interactive actions for Needs Attention beads
description: When a bead is selected in the Needs Attention panel, allow the operator to take actions via keyboard shortcuts or a popup menu. Default action options: (1) Retry — clear needs_human flag and reset retry count, putting bead back in queue; (2) Dismiss — mark bead as resolved/won't-fix so it leaves the panel; (3) Rebase & Retry — for collateral CI failures, trigger a rebase then retry; (4) Bump Priority — change the bead's priority; (5) View Logs — show the last smith/warden log for this bead. Actions should go through the existing IPC protocol (may need new IPC commands). Consider a small popup/overlay with the action list when pressing Enter on a selected bead.

title: Hearth: split Queue area into Queue + Needs Attention panels
description: Split the left-side Queue panel area into two stacked rows. Top row keeps the existing Queue (pending beads). Bottom row adds a new 'Needs Attention' panel showing beads with needs_human=1 or clarification_needed=1 from the retries table. Each entry should show: bead ID, anvil, title, and reason (exhausted retries, no-diff, clarification needed, collateral CI, rate-limited). Use NeedsHumanBeads() from state DB. The panel should follow the same styling conventions as the existing Queue panel (priority colors, scrollable list). Navigable via Tab like other panels.

title: Remove re-request-review call after bellows pushes a fix
description: After bellows pushes a fix commit to a PR branch, it currently calls gh pr review --request-review (or similar) to trigger a new review. This causes a full Copilot review on every small fix push, generating endless review comment cycles. Since we will configure GitHub to trigger auto-review on new pushes, we should remove the explicit re-request-review call from bellows. The fix should: 1) Identify where bellows calls re-request-review after pushing, 2) Remove that call, 3) Ensure bellows still pushes the fix and logs the result.

title: Increase bellows max CI and review fix attempts from 2 to 5
description: The current hard limit of 2 for both MaxCI and MaxRev in lifecycle.Manager is too low. PRs regularly need more than 2 rounds to pass CI and satisfy code review, especially when fixing linting issues, test failures, or addressing multiple rounds of reviewer feedback. Increase both limits to 5 (configurable via forge.yaml would be ideal). File: internal/lifecycle/lifecycle.go - look for maxCI and maxRev fields on the Manager struct and where they are set in New().

title: Bellows drops second-wave review comments after first fix cycle completes
description:
After a reviewfix worker completes and re-requests review, NeedsFix is never cleared in the lifecycle state machine. So when the reviewer fires another EventReviewChanges (second wave), the guard !st.NeedsFix ; st.Approved evaluates to false (NeedsFix=true, Approved=false) and logs 'PR changes requested again, but already in fix cycle', dropping the second wave permanently.

Root cause: lifecycle.HandleEvent for EventReviewChanges sets NeedsFix=true but only EventCIPassed clears it. Review cycles never reset NeedsFix on completion.

Fix: After ActionFixReview completes in daemon.go, call a new lifecycle method (e.g. NotifyReviewFixCompleted) that clears NeedsFix=false so the next EventReviewChanges from the re-review gets dispatched normally.
close_reason: Implemented: NotifyReviewFixCompleted clears NeedsFix in lifecycle.Manager after reviewfix worker completes. Called from daemon's ActionFixReview handler. PR #42.

title: Add clarification_needed status for beads that require human input before starting
description: Some beads are genuinely ambiguous and cannot be started without human clarification (e.g. 'which auth library?', 'should this replace X or wrap it?', 'URL of the external service?'). Currently these either fail silently (Smith produces no diff), stall in iteration loops, or exhaust all attempts uselessly. Proposed: (1) add a 'clarification_needed' flag or status that can be set via 'bd update <id> --clarification-needed' (analogous to needs_human), (2) the Needs Human Attention panel (Forge-h7x) should show these beads in a dedicated section so operators can answer and then clear the flag, (3) Forge should skip beads with clarification_needed in its poller (same as needs_human=1). For now, operators flag these manually; a future Planner worker (see Forge-yqb) may detect and set this automatically.

title: Pipeline/Warden: VerdictReject (no-diff) leaves bead stuck in_progress
description: When warden returns VerdictReject because Smith produced no diff, pipeline.Run() sets WorkerFailed and returns immediately. The bead stays in_progress with no active worker or branch, requiring manual reset. This is the same class of issue as the rate-limit stuck-bead (Forge-rpc) but triggered by a different code path. Fix options: (1) no-diff should be treated as a human-attention case, not a hard failure — flag the bead with needs_human=1 and reset to open, (2) if pipeline detects no-diff on first iteration it could retry with a clarified prompt, (3) at minimum the daemon's pipeline error handler must reset the bead to open when outcome.Error is non-nil (the rate-limit fix in Forge-rpc likely covers this too — verify). Observed: 09:56:26 warden_reject [Forge-h7x] No changes detected — Smith produced no diff; bead remained in_progress.

title: Hearth: Live Activity panel expands downward pushing other panels off screen
description: As events scroll through the Live Activity sub-panel, the panel grows downward, pushing the Queue and Event log panels off the screen. Root cause suspicion: renderWorkers() returns a lipgloss.JoinVertical of two sub-panels but never wraps the result in style.Height(height), so the combined height is not bounded. Also, renderWorkerActivity maxVisible calculation uses 'height - 4' but lipgloss border padding may differ, causing a few extra lines to bleed through. Fix: ensure renderWorkers clamps its total output to contentHeight, or verify that each sub-panel's style.Height() correctly clips overflow rather than expanding the box.

title: Hearth: add Needs Human Attention panel for exhausted and stuck PRs
description: When lifecycle_exhausted or all-providers-rate-limited events occur there is no dedicated UI surface showing what needs attention. Add a panel (or section) in Hearth that: (1) lists beads with needs_human=1 or stuck in_progress with no active worker, (2) shows the reason (exhausted CI fixes, exhausted review fixes, rate limited, collateral CI failure in unrelated package), (3) provides operator actions like reset-to-open or mark-resolved. For collateral CI failure case: when bellows fires EventCIFailed for a test unrelated to the PR changes, the fix agent fails and needs_human=1 is set — the panel should note this and suggest a rebase.

title: Pipeline: release bead back to open when all providers are rate limited
description: When all providers are rate limited, pipeline.Run() fails with an 'All providers rate limited' error. The bead stays in_progress with no active worker and no way to recover without human intervention. Fix: detect this specific error in pipeline.Run() and automatically reset the bead status back to open via bd, then wait a configurable backoff period before the poller retries. Without this fix every rate-limit event leaves orphaned in_progress beads that need manual cleanup.

title: Hearth: fix dual panel selection when switching panels
description: When switching between panels in Hearth TUI, both the Workers panel and the Live Activity panel appear selected simultaneously. Focus/active state should be exclusive — only one panel selected at a time. Occurs when tab-switching between the worker list (tab 2) and the activity panel.

title: Prohibit local dolt server — document in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md
description: Forge's beads DB connects via kubectl port-forward to the AKS pod tn-heimdall/dolt-beads on port 3306. If a local dolt sql-server process is running on 127.0.0.1:3306, it will steal the port and cause 'Access denied' errors when bd commands try to connect. The start-dolt-server.ps1 script (port 3307) is a separate concern but the general pattern of starting local dolt is dangerous. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md need an explicit prohibition section: never run dolt sql-server locally on port 3306, never run start-dolt-server.ps1 unless explicitly doing offline dev. If bd fails with Access Denied, restart kubectl port-forward: kubectl port-forward -n tn-heimdall svc/dolt-beads 3306:3306
close_reason: Added explicit prohibition section to both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md: never start local dolt sql-server on port 3306, always use kubectl port-forward to tn-heimdall/dolt-beads. Committed in 0f0972f.

title: Make review fix max attempts configurable
description: In internal/reviewfix/reviewfix.go line 26, MaxAttempts is hardcoded to 2. A PR with 10+ review comments from Copilot can easily require more than 2 fix passes to resolve all issues. The value should be configurable via forge.yaml (SettingsConfig.MaxReviewAttempts int) with a sensible default of at least 5. Without this, beads get stuck in lifecycle_exhausted after only 2 attempts even when the work could have been completed with more tries.

title: Hearth: clamp panel widths and heights to prevent negative dimensions on narrow terminals
description:
PR #6 (line 203, hearth.go) and PR #14 (lines 226, 402, hearth.go) both flag that width/height math can go negative or overflow on small terminals.

Specific issues:
- availableHeight can be < minTop+minBottom; the current code does not degrade gracefully and can push content off-screen
- remainingWidth (m.width - 4) can go negative for very narrow terminals, yielding negative panel widths
- interiorWidth is hard-clamped to 20 even when panelWidth-4 is smaller, so wrapped lines can exceed the panel

Fix: clamp availableHeight >= 0 first, then proportionally degrade panel heights when the terminal cannot satisfy both minimums; ensure all width values are max(0, computed) before use; keep interiorWidth <= panelWidth-4 (minimum 1, not 20).

title: Fix bellows+reviewfix: wrong trigger, wrong API, no thread resolution
description:
Bellows + reviewfix have multiple interconnected bugs that prevent automatic PR fix triggering. PR #2 (Forge-f4q) demonstrates all of them.

## Bug 1 — Bellows trigger fires on wrong condition

bellows.go: NeedsChanges() only returns true for review state "CHANGES_REQUESTED".
Copilot (and many human reviewers) submit reviews as "COMMENTED" state with inline
thread suggestions. These never trigger EventReviewChanges.

Fix: Add a new prSnapshot field `HasUnresolvedThreads bool`. In checkPR, after
calling ghpr.CheckStatus, additionally call a new ghpr.FetchUnresolvedThreadCount
that uses the GraphQL reviewThreads query (see Bug 2). If unresolved thread count
transitions from 0 to >0 (or PR is newly seen with unresolved threads), emit
EventReviewChanges so reviewfix is triggered.

ghpr.CheckStatus should also be extended to include unresolved thread count alongside
the existing reviews/CI data.

## Bug 2 — fetchReviewComments uses wrong API; misses inline threads and isResolved

reviewfix.go fetchReviewComments: uses `gh pr view --json reviews,comments`.
The `comments` field in that API is PR-level general comments, NOT inline review
thread comments (which live in `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{prNumber}/comments`
or preferably via GraphQL reviewThreads). There is no isResolved field in the REST
API — only GraphQL exposes it.

Fix: Replace fetchReviewComments with a GraphQL-based implementation:

  gh api graphql -f query='
  query($owner:String!, $repo:String!, $pr:Int!) {
    repository(owner:$owner, name:$repo) {
      pullRequest(number:$pr) {
        reviewThreads(first:100) {
          nodes {
            id
            isResolved
            comments(first:1) {
              nodes { path line body author { login } }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }' -f owner=OWNER -f repo=REPO -F pr=NUMBER

Filter nodes where isResolved: false. Map each to ReviewComment{ThreadID: node.id, ...}.
The owner/repo must be extracted from `git remote get-url origin` in the worktree.

Also fetch PR-level review body comments (non-thread) via:
  gh pr view {number} --comments
and include those that are not purely informational (heuristic: body length > 20 chars,
not an approval message).

## Bug 3 — No thread resolution after fix

After Smith successfully applies fixes and pushes, reviewfix returns without calling
the resolveReviewThread GraphQL mutation for the addressed threads.

Fix: After Smith exits with code 0, for each comment whose ThreadID is non-empty,
call:

  gh api graphql -f query='
  mutation($threadId:ID!) {
    resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$threadId}) {
      thread { isResolved }
    }
  }' -f threadId="{thread.id}"

Add a resolveThread(ctx, worktreePath, threadID string) error helper in reviewfix.go.
Log success/failure per thread but do not fail the overall FixResult if resolution
calls fail (thread resolution is best-effort).

## Bug 4 — CI failure event not wired to a fix worker

When bellows emits EventCIFailed, check daemon.go to confirm whether a handler
actually spawns a Smith worker to fix it. If not (likely), add a ci_fix handler
analogous to the review_fix handler: spawn Smith with a prompt listing the failing
CI checks (from gh pr checks output) and instruct it to fix build/test errors.

## Implementation order

1. Fix fetchReviewComments (Bug 2) — foundational for everything else
2. Add resolveThread after fix (Bug 3)
3. Fix bellows trigger to use unresolved thread count (Bug 1)
4. Wire EventCIFailed to a ci fix smith in daemon.go (Bug 4)

## GraphQL mutation reference (from Heimdall pr-fix skill)

Resolve thread:
  gh api graphql -f query='mutation($threadId:ID!) { resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$threadId}) { thread { isResolved } } }' -f threadId="THREAD_NODE_ID"

Query threads:
  gh api graphql -f query='query($owner:String!, $repo:String!, $pr:Int!) { repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo) { pullRequest(number:$pr) { reviewThreads(first:100) { nodes { id isResolved comments(first:1) { nodes { path line body author { login } } } } } } } }' -f owner=OWNER -f repo=REPO -F pr=NUMBER

title: Add GitHub Actions CI workflow
description:
Add a GitHub Actions CI workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml. The workflow should run on push and pull_request to main.

Jobs (all on ubuntu-latest, Go version from go.mod):
1. build - go build ./...
2. vet - go vet ./...
3. test - go test ./... (once Forge-tqb adds tests; initially just verifies compilation)
4. golangci-lint (optional, use golangci/golangci-lint-action) - catches formatting and common issues

Workflow triggers:
  on:
    push:
      branches: [main]
    pull_request:
      branches: [main]

Key requirements:
- Use actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-go@v5 with cache: true
- Store Go cache between runs (setup-go handles this automatically with cache: true)
- Fail fast on build/vet before running tests
- The workflow filename should be ci.yml; the workflow name "CI"
- Add a status badge to README.md once it is green

Note: There is no Makefile currently. The CI should use plain go commands, not make targets.
No release or publish step needed here - this is only for PR validation and branch protection.

title: Add unit tests for core packages
description:
Add unit tests for Forge's core packages. The codebase currently has no test files.

Priority packages to cover (in order):
1. internal/config - config loading, validation, defaults, poll_interval parsing, env var override
2. internal/poller - mock bd output, priority sorting, per-anvil merge, error handling
3. internal/smith - readStreamJSON: parse Claude/Gemini stream-json events, rate_limit_event, result event stats
4. internal/provider - BuildArgs output for each provider, Defaults() ordering
5. internal/ghpr - PRStatus methods (IsMerged, NeedsChanges, CIsPassing, HasApproval)
6. internal/bellows - snapshot diff logic: that events fire on transitions, not on repeat state

Test conventions:
- Use t.TempDir() for any filesystem work
- Use table-driven tests ([]struct{name, input, want}) throughout
- Mock external processes (bd, gh, claude, gemini) by swapping the exec.Command function or using a test binary approach
- No integration tests that require live network/credentials
- Place tests in the same package (_test suffix files) or a separate _test package where internal access is needed

title: Fix forge down on Windows (SIGINT not supported)
description: daemon.Stop() calls proc.Signal(syscall.SIGINT) which is not supported on Windows. Fix by adding a 'shutdown' IPC command to the daemon and using that from daemon.Stop() on Windows, with SIGINT as the Unix fallback.

title: Fix daemon.IsRunning() on Windows (Signal(0) not supported)
description: daemon.IsRunning() calls proc.Signal(syscall.Signal(0)) to check process liveness. On Windows this is not supported and always returns an error, so IsRunning() always returns false. Fix by using ipc.SocketExists() as the liveness check on Windows, since the named pipe is destroyed when the process dies.

title: Hearth 2.0: add approve-as-is and warden-rerun to the needs-attention panel
description:
## Problem

The `ResolveNeedsAttentionPanel` (added in bead 07) exposes the bd-level resolve verbs:

  retry · stop · clarify · unclarify · clear

but is missing the two **Forge-level dispatch overrides** that the original Bubbletea hearth binds:

  - **`approve_as_is`** — daemon pushes the worker's existing branch + `gh pr create`, bypassing Warden entirely. Use when Smith produced good work but Warden rejected it (hallucination, stale checkout, context-window truncation, etc.). The IPC handler already exists at `internal/daemon/daemon.go:4383` + `6642`; only the HTTP→IPC bridge and the SPA button are missing.

  - **`warden_rerun`** — re-invoke Warden against the current diff. Use when you suspect Warden glitched once and would get the right answer on a second pass (cheaper than a full retry which respins Smith). Mentioned in `daemon.go:6853` ("the warden_rerun/approve_as_is flows") as an existing daemon flow.

The SPA panel currently has an "Open PR manually" section (`ResolveNeedsAttentionPanel.tsx:357`) that is **just a clipboard helper** — it drafts a title + body for the operator to paste into `gh pr create` from a worktree they have to find themselves. Its inline comment even claims "The daemon does not know the GitHub repository URL for this anvil, so opening a PR directly is not wired up" — that comment is stale: the daemon's `approve_as_is` handler resolves the repo from the anvil and runs `gh pr create` in-process. Has done since the TUI shipped.

Result: pod-hosted forges (skybert, hetzner) lose the one-click "ship Smith's work over Warden's objection" escape hatch every time Warden hallucinates. Today's example (2026-05-22): Fhi.Metadata-8i4hr — Smith produced a clean 10-file commit (`cd18b66ea`, RuleProfile.cs / RuleProfileAssignment.cs / Stage.cs / DbContext wiring / EF migration / changelog fragments, ~10k lines), Warden falsely claimed the profile entity classes were "still not present" and rejected, Smith disputed via RECHECK_PREVIOUS but had used the token once already → dispatch_failed → user had to drop to `gh pr create` from a laptop git checkout (PR #3265 in FHIDev/Munin) because the SPA had no button for it.

## What's wired today (TUI) and what to mirror

`cmd/forge/hearth.go:405-429` binds `OnApproveAsIs`:

```
model.OnApproveAsIs = func(beadID, anvil string) error {
    client, _ := ipc.NewClient()
    payload, _ := json.Marshal(ipc.ApproveAsIsPayload{BeadID: beadID, Anvil: anvil})
    resp, err := client.Send(ipc.Command{Type: "approve_as_is", Payload: json.RawMessage(payload)})
    ...
}
```

The daemon handler (`internal/daemon/daemon.go:4383`-4412 + the worker at `:6642`-6706):

1. Validates payload (bead_id + anvil).
2. Marks the bead as in-progress for the approve-as-is phase.
3. Creates a worktree at the worker's existing branch.
4. `git push` to origin/forge/<bead-id>.
5. `gh pr create` from that branch → main.
6. On PR-creation failure, marks `needs_human` with the error.
7. Logs phase `approve_as_is` events at every step.

`warden_rerun` is the same shape with a different IPC type — see daemon.go:6853 for context.

## Implementation outline

1. **Backend HTTP routes** (in `internal/web/`):
   - `POST /api/escalations/{anvil}/{bead}/approve-as-is` → IPC `approve_as_is` with `{BeadID, Anvil}`.
   - `POST /api/escalations/{anvil}/{bead}/warden-rerun` → IPC `warden_rerun` (same payload shape).
   - Both async — return 202 + a status URL so the UI can poll / SSE.

2. **Frontend wiring** (`internal/web/frontend/src/`):
   - Add `approveAsIs` and `wardenRerun` to the resolve verbs union in `api/forge.ts` (or wherever `ResolveVerb` is defined — the panel imports it as `ResolveVerb`).
   - Add labels in `VERB_LABEL` in `ResolveNeedsAttentionPanel.tsx`: `approve-as-is: 'Approve as-is (skip Warden)'`, `warden-rerun: 'Re-run Warden'`.
   - Extend `BEAD_VERBS` for dispatch_failed escalations to include both. Probably extend `WORKER_VERBS` (smith_failed) with `warden-rerun` only; approve-as-is on a still-running worker is ambiguous.
   - Mark `approve-as-is` as DESTRUCTIVE (confirmation modal: "This will skip the Warden review and open a PR from the worker's existing branch. Continue?"). Warden-rerun is non-destructive, no confirm needed.
   - Plumb through `useResolveActions().run(...)` — same shape as the existing verbs.

3. **Remove the stale clipboard-helper section**. The whole "Open PR manually" form at `ResolveNeedsAttentionPanel.tsx:357-403` was a workaround for not having the real action; with approve-as-is wired in, drop it. (The inline comment at line 362 is also misleading and should go.)

4. **Tests**:
   - Backend: add handler tests in `internal/web/` mirroring the existing PR-action handler test pattern.
   - Frontend: extend the panel component test to assert the two new buttons render for `dispatch_failed` and that clicking approve-as-is shows the confirm modal.

## Where this lives

Files to touch (non-exhaustive — implementer should follow the wiring):

- `internal/web/router.go` — register the two new POST routes.
- `internal/web/actions.go` or a new `escalation_actions.go` — handler that translates HTTP to IPC.
- `internal/web/frontend/src/api/forge.ts` — extend `ResolveVerb` union.
- `internal/web/frontend/src/stores/resolveStore.ts` — extend the verb handling if it does any per-verb dispatch logic.
- `internal/web/frontend/src/components/ResolveNeedsAttentionPanel.tsx` — extend `BEAD_VERBS` / `VERB_LABEL` / `DESTRUCTIVE_VERBS`, drop the clipboard form.
- `internal/web/frontend/src/components/ResolveNeedsAttentionPanel.test.tsx` (if it exists) — add coverage.

## Acceptance criteria

- For a `dispatch_failed` bead, the SPA needs-attention panel shows **Approve as-is** and **Re-run Warden** buttons alongside the existing five.

title: Beads-Forge: 90s drafter-turn timeout truncates real fs investigation; make configurable and bump default
description:
## Problem

`internal/forgechat/runner_claude.go:30-55` caps every drafter / grilling / plan / emit turn at a 90-second wall-clock timeout:

```go
Timeout time.Duration
...
timeout := r.Timeout
if timeout <= 0 {
    timeout = 90 * time.Second
}
turnCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, timeout)
defer cancel()
```

When Claude is using Read/Grep/Glob to ground its reply (as the Forge-9w62 system prompt explicitly tells it to), 90 s is routinely too short. The drafter typically needs:

- A few seconds of preamble emission ("Let me look at how X is used ...").
- One Glob to discover relevant files.
- 2–6 Reads on those files (each can be 1–5 s, more on cold caches / large files).
- 1–4 Greps to find call sites.
- Final synthesis (5–15 s of model output).

That's 30 s on a small anvil and 90+ s on a normal one. Sometimes the very first Glob alone takes 20 s on a large monorepo. The 90 s ceiling fires mid-investigation, the Claude process is killed, and `proc.Wait()` returns whatever streamed output it had — usually just the "Let me look at ..." preamble text that came BEFORE the tool calls completed. The persisted assistant message is a short truncated lead-in with no actual answer. The user reads "Let me look at how react-day-picker is currently used" and sees the session do nothing on the next "continue" turn either — because each turn restarts the same investigation and runs out of time again.

From the user's perspective Hearth 2.0's Beads-Forge looks broken. From the daemon's perspective everything succeeded — Claude was spawned, exit code 0 or context-cancelled (handled the same way), an assistant message was persisted. Silent failure.

### Concrete reproduction (2026-05-22, skybert-forge)

Session id=2, title "npm update react-day-picker 9.14.0→10.0.1 in heimdall", anvil=heimdall. Three turns over two days, each one a "continue" or near-equivalent. Each produced 105–191 chars of preamble text and stopped. Verbatim:

> Turn 1: "Let me look at how react-day-picker is currently used in the codebase before we discuss the upgrade path."
>
> Turn 2: "Let me explore the codebase to understand how react-day-picker is currently used. Let me read the actual calendar.tsx to see the full current implementation before assessing the upgrade scope."
>
> Turn 3 (after manual debugging set the anvil field on the session): same pattern.

Reproducing the exact drafter system prompt + tail + session history with `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p - --max-turns 10 --output-format stream-json` BUT no 90 s ceiling: Claude issues 9+ tool calls (Glob `**/*.{tsx,ts,jsx,js}`, Read `package.json`, Grep `react-day-picker`, Read `client/package.json`, Read `calendar.tsx`, Grep import patterns, Grep DayPicker symbols, Read `date-picker.tsx`, Grep calendar imports ...) and synthesizes the actual answer in ~120–180 s wall-clock. Tools and access work; only the timer is wrong.

## Why the timeout exists

From the comment on the field: "Kept short so the HTTP handler isn't held open forever." Reasonable goal — `POST /api/forge/sessions/{id}/turn` is a blocking HTTP request and a stuck Claude process would tie up the handler indefinitely. 90 s was probably picked when the drafter was prompt-only (no fs access). Once Forge-9w62 added Read/Grep/Glob the budget didn't get revisited.

## Proposed fix

Two deliverables, ordered by effort + impact:

### Step 1 (quick win): bump the default and make it configurable

Change `runner_claude.go` to read the timeout from settings rather than a hardcoded const:

```go
// Default if settings.forgechat.turn_timeout is unset or zero.
const defaultTurnTimeout = 5 * time.Minute
```

Add `settings.forgechat.turn_timeout` to `internal/config/config.go` so operators can tune per-deployment. Default 5 min, hard cap at 15 min so a wedged session can't pin a connection forever.

At the same time, change `runner_claude.go:Turn` so a context-cancel-induced kill produces a CLEAR diagnostic in the persisted message rather than a half-sentence:

```go
if errors.Is(turnCtx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded) {
    // Surface the timeout instead of returning truncated preamble.
    return &TurnResponse{
        Messages: []EmittedMessage{{Kind: "text", Content:
            "_(Drafter timed out after " + timeout.String() + ". Try a more focused follow-up question, or bump `settings.forgechat.turn_timeout`.)_",
        }},
    }, nil
}
```

Net effect with Step 1: 95% of real drafter turns finish; the remaining 5% surface an honest "timed out" message instead of a misleading half-sentence.

### Step 2 (proper fix): make the turn endpoint async + stream

The handler-held-open concern that originally motivated the 90 s ceiling is the actual right thing to address. Turn into a non-blocking flow:

1. `POST /api/forge/sessions/{id}/turn` schedules a turn and returns 202 with `{turn_id}` immediately.
2. Server-sent events on `GET /api/forge/sessions/{id}/turn/{turn_id}/stream` pushes:
   - assistant text deltas as they're produced,
   - tool-use notifications ("Calling Grep for ..."),
   - tool results (compact summary, not full output),
   - final completion + the persisted-message id.
3. Hearth 2.0 SPA subscribes to the SSE stream and renders progressively — the user sees "Let me look at ..." then "Reading calendar.tsx ..." then the actual answer, instead of a frozen panel.

This matches how Hytte's chat handles long Claude responses and removes the timeout pressure entirely. The wall-clock cap becomes a backstop (15 min) rather than a routine constraint.

Step 1 unblocks current users immediately; Step 2 is the durable fix. They can ship in either order, but Step 1 should not be skipped — even with SSE in place we want a configurable backstop.

## Acceptance

### Step 1
- The drafter turn timeout is configurable via `settings.forgechat.turn_timeout` in `forge.yaml`. Default 5 minutes.
- Hardcoded 90 s ceiling removed from `runner_claude.go`.
- When the timeout DOES fire, the persisted assistant message reads as an honest "timed out, here's what to try next" sentinel — not a truncated preamble.
- Re-running session id=2 (or any equivalent) after the fix completes the investigation and produces a real plan / clarifying question.

### Step 2 (separate PR optional but tracked here)
- Turn endpoint returns 202 + turn_id within 100 ms of receipt.
- Hearth 2.0 streams turn progress via SSE; the SPA renders deltas live.
- A long-running turn (e.g. 8 min on a large anvil) completes without ever holding a connection-level handler open beyond keep-alive.
- Existing `POST .../turn` callers that don't consume the SSE stream still get a 202 + can poll `GET /api/forge/sessions/{id}/turn/{turn_id}` for completion.

## Notes

- The same `Timeout` field affects `grilling`, `plan`, and `emit` runners as well. Step 1 fixes all four uniformly because they all use `ClaudeRunner.Turn`. Specifically the `plan` stage (which has to produce a one-page markdown plan grounded in real code) and `emit` (which still does fs work to verify anvil paths) are at risk of the same truncation.
- Daemon log does not currently mark a turn as having timed out — the cancel is silent. Step 1 should also add a `slog.Warn` line so we can audit how often this fires in the wild before / after the fix.
- `internal/forgechat/runner_claude_test.go` should grow a test that injects a 1 ms `Timeout`, runs a fake-runner Turn, and asserts the persisted message is the sentinel — not a truncated payload.

## Cross-refs

- Forge-9w62 (PR #602) is what introduced fs-grounded investigation to the drafter prompt. This bead is the follow-up: the prompt asked for behaviour that exceeds the existing time budget.
- The earlier tmpBead 09 (`09-beads-forge-anvil-required-on-create.sh`) covered "session created with empty anvil → drafter has nothing to look at". That fix prevents a different failure shape (no path at all). Bead 11 is the case where the path IS set, fs access works, but the investigation gets killed mid-flight.

The drafter wasn't broken — it was just on a 90-second hourglass that ran out before the work was done. The forge has been showing the user a man waving an empty tool belt when in fact he was already at the workbench with all the tools out.

title: Beads-Forge: require anvil when creating a session; backfill the field on legacy sessions
description:
## Problem

The Hearth 2.0 Beads-Forge UI allows session creation with an empty `anvil` field. The backend (`POST /api/forge/sessions`, `internal/web/forge_sessions.go:131-176`) treats `anvil` as optional and persists whatever the UI sends, including the empty string.

This worked before PR #602 (Forge-9w62) because the drafter prompt did not depend on an anvil path. After PR #602, the drafting and grilling prompts assume a session-scoped `AnvilTarget` so the agent can use Read/Grep/Glob against the right tree. `resolveSessionAnvil` in `internal/web/forge_chat.go:315` returns `nil` for empty anvil, which makes `TurnRequest.Anvil` nil, which makes the prompt builder skip the per-anvil context entirely.

The symptom is a dead-end conversation: the drafter announces an intent like "Let me look at how react-day-picker is currently used in the codebase" but never makes a tool call, because it was never given a path to look at. The session stays in `stage=drafting` indefinitely while the user waits for a follow-up that will not come.

### Concrete repro from 2026-05-19

skybert-forge `forge_sessions` row:

| id | title                                                          | anvil | stage   | status |
|----|----------------------------------------------------------------|-------|---------|--------|
| 2  | npm update react-day-picker 9.14.0→10.0.1 in heimdall         | ""    | drafting| draft  |

Manual cleanup was `UPDATE forge_sessions SET anvil = 'heimdall' WHERE id = 2;` followed by the user typing any next message in the UI — the drafter immediately worked. So the fix is purely "make sure anvil is set at create time" (plus a backfill for legacy rows).

## Proposed fix

Two parts, both required:

### 1. Frontend: make anvil a required select on the new-session form

The Hearth 2.0 Beads-Forge "new session" form should:

- Render a select / radio group listing the daemon's registered anvils (the same list available to the daemon, fetched via the existing anvil-listing endpoint).
- Default-select the user's most recently used anvil (if any) or the first in the list, but require the user to confirm before submission.
- Block the "Create session" / "Send" submit button until an anvil is selected.
- Pass `anvil` in the POST body alongside `title` and `initial_message`.

If the registered-anvils list is empty (no anvils added to this forge instance yet), surface that as an explanation in place of the select — "No anvils registered. Run `forge anvil add ...` before starting a session." — and disable session creation.

### 2. Backend: reject empty-anvil session creation, OR auto-select when only one anvil exists

In `handleForgeSessionsCreate` (`internal/web/forge_sessions.go:142`), after the existing `req.Anvil = strings.TrimSpace(req.Anvil)`:

- If `req.Anvil == ""` and exactly one anvil is registered, default to that one (single-anvil deployments — for example a developer running forge locally against just `munin` — should not be forced to fill in a redundant field).
- If `req.Anvil == ""` and multiple anvils exist, return `400 Bad Request` with `{"error":"anvil is required when more than one anvil is registered"}`. The frontend will keep this from being a user-visible 400 (validation happens in the form) but the server-side guard ensures direct API consumers / future clients can't produce the dead-end state.
- If `req.Anvil` is non-empty but does not match any registered anvil (case-insensitive), return `400 Bad Request` with `{"error":"unknown anvil <name>; registered: <list>"}`. Today this gets silently accepted and then `resolveSessionAnvil` filters it out at turn time, producing the same dead-end without a clear error.

These guards belong at session-create time, not turn time — by the time the drafter is stuck, the user has already spent a turn budget on a no-op response.

### 3. Backfill: title-heuristic for the existing dead-end session(s)

One-shot SQL migration in a future bd version (or a `forge` admin subcommand) that scans `forge_sessions WHERE anvil = ""` and tries to populate the field from the title via a simple word-match against registered anvil names. Optional and low priority since the population is now blocked by part 2.

## Acceptance criteria

- Creating a Beads-Forge session via the Hearth 2.0 UI without selecting an anvil shows a validation error and does not submit.
- The "anvil" select on the form is populated from the live registered-anvils list and defaults to a sensible value.
- POST `/api/forge/sessions` with `anvil: ""` returns 400 when more than one anvil is registered.
- POST `/api/forge/sessions` with an unknown anvil name returns 400 with a helpful error.
- POST `/api/forge/sessions` with `anvil: ""` in a single-anvil deployment auto-populates that one anvil and succeeds (no regression for solo-dev setups).
- An existing session with `anvil=""` can be updated via SQL or a future admin endpoint, but the bug class cannot recur via the supported create path.
- The drafter's "let me look at the codebase" response now reliably produces a Read/Grep/Glob tool call in the next turn (covered indirectly — once `anvil` is guaranteed to be set, the prompt builder sends the path, and the PR-602 prompt does the rest).

## Notes

- The earlier PR #602 (Forge-9w62) did the right thing on the prompt side. This bead is the missing other-half: ensure the anvil field is non-empty when the prompt-side code expects it.
- Touching files: `internal/web/forge_sessions.go` (handler validation), `internal/web/dist/...` (Hearth 2.0 SPA — Beads-Forge session-create form), possibly a small admin/SQL migration.
- Pair with the existing tmpBeads bead 07 (`07-hearth2-resolve-needs-attention.sh`) which is the broader "Hearth 2.0 UI gaps" theme. Not blocking on it.
- The reproduction case (skybert-forge session id 2) has already been hand-fixed by setting `anvil = "heimdall"` in `state.db`. So no broken session lingers in prod — this bead is about preventing the next one.
