title: Warden: diff-aware rule filtering at review time + dedup/archive at learn time
description:
## Problem

Warden's `FormatChecklist` in `internal/warden/rules.go:199-208` is a hot path on every Smith review, and it does no filtering:

```go
for i, r := range rf.Rules {
    fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "%d. [ ] Check: %s (pattern: %s)\n", i+1, r.Check, r.Pattern)
}
```

Every rule, every review. On Munin today that means **971 rules / 530 KB / ~125 k input tokens of checklist text shipped on every Warden invocation**. Categories: other 228, testing 206, style 178, error-handling 115, ui 107, security 59, performance 47, concurrency 31.

The cost is three-way:

1. **$ per review.** 125 k tokens × Munin's Smith throughput × whichever provider the `warden` stage uses. Real budget line, scales linearly with rule count.
2. **Latency per review.** Inference on a 125-k-token prompt is meaningfully slower than on a 5-k-token prompt. Stacks up across the warden stage of every bead.
3. **Attention dilution.** The reviewer sees a 971-item checklist alongside a 200-line diff. Most rules are obviously irrelevant. Important rules get the same eyeball-share as duplicates and stale items. The "growing-smarter" mechanism degrades into "growing-noisier" as the file accumulates.

This bead has two halves that wire together cleanly because they share the same data model:

- **Half A — Review-time filtering**: pick a small subset of rules per review based on the diff. Cuts the per-review prompt cost / latency.
- **Half B — Learn-time dedup + archive**: shrink the file at the source. Cuts the long-term growth curve so Half A's subset selection has less work to do.

Both fixes are inside `internal/warden/` and `internal/smelter/`, no schema changes outside the YAML data file, no client-side impact.

## Half A — Diff-aware rule filtering at review time

Replace `FormatChecklist` with `FormatChecklistForDiff(diff, changedFiles)` that selects a small subset before formatting. Three composable filters, applied in order:

### 1. Path-glob match (new optional field on `Rule`)

Add an optional `paths` (or `globs`) field to the `Rule` struct in `rules.go:62-69`:

```go
type Rule struct {
    ID       string     `yaml:"id"       json:"id"`
    Category string     `yaml:"category" json:"category"`
    Pattern  string     `yaml:"pattern"  json:"pattern"`
    Check    string     `yaml:"check"    json:"check"`
    Source   SourceList `yaml:"source"   json:"source"`
    Added    string     `yaml:"added"    json:"added"`
    Paths    []string   `yaml:"paths,omitempty" json:"paths,omitempty"`   // NEW: glob patterns
}
```

If `Paths` is non-empty, only include the rule when at least one changed file matches one of the globs (use `path/filepath.Match` or `doublestar` for `**/*.tsx`). If `Paths` is empty, fall through to the next filter (rule is potentially-global).

The learn step (`internal/warden/learn.go` and the smelter) populates `Paths` when it has a clear file-scope signal (the Copilot comment was on a `.tsx` file → `Paths: ["**/*.tsx"]`). Existing rules without `Paths` keep the today's "include in every review" behaviour until the next consolidation pass tags them.

### 2. Category routing

Map diff file-types to relevant categories. Crude initial mapping:

| Changed file types | Categories included |
|---|---|
| `*.cs`, `*.csproj` | `error-handling`, `security`, `concurrency`, `performance`, `style`, `other` |
| `*.tsx`, `*.ts`, `*.css` | `ui`, `style`, `other` |
| `*_test.tsx`, `*Tests.cs` | `testing`, `other` |
| `*.yaml`, `*.yml`, `Dockerfile`, `*.ps1` | `other`, `security` |
| (none of the above — fall back) | all categories |

Kept as a small in-code table in `rules.go` (or a sibling `routing.go`). Easy to tune.

### 3. Pattern grep (cheap last-pass filter)

For each remaining rule, do a substring match of `rule.Pattern` (split on words) against the diff content. If no word from the pattern appears anywhere in the diff, drop the rule. This catches the long tail of rules that survived the path/category filters but obviously don't apply (e.g. a rule about "primary constructor" patterns when the diff doesn't mention "constructor").

Keep a `minWords` threshold (e.g. require ≥1 distinct ≥4-char word match) so single-word noise doesn't leak everything through.

### Composition

Filters compose as AND, then a final cap:

```go
selected := rules
selected = filterByPathGlob(selected, changedFiles)
selected = filterByCategoryRouting(selected, changedFiles)
selected = filterByPatternGrep(selected, diffText)
if len(selected) > maxRules {
    selected = selected[:maxRules]   // or a smarter cap with category balance
}
return formatNumberedChecklist(selected)
```

Reasonable defaults: `maxRules` somewhere in 25-50. Configurable via `settings.warden.max_rules_per_review` in `forge.yaml`.

### Acceptance for Half A

- On a Munin Smith run that touches only `.cs` files in the API project, the warden prompt receives ≤50 rules drawn from `error-handling`, `security`, `concurrency`, `performance`, `style`, `other` — none from `ui` / `testing` unless the diff also touches those file shapes.
- Token count of the rules section in the warden prompt drops by ≥80% on a typical Munin bead compared to the current behaviour.
- An existing Munin bead reviewed twice (once before this change, once after) produces verdicts that are roughly comparable — no regression in reject/request_changes rate measurably caused by missing rules.
- The `Paths` field is forward-compatible with the existing YAML (old files load fine; new field is optional).
- A flag (`--all-rules` or `settings.warden.use_all_rules: true`) keeps the old behaviour for callers who want to A/B compare or run a full sweep.

## Half B — Dedup + archive at learn time (in smelter)

The `internal/smelter` package already batches `pending_warden_rules` from state.db into per-anvil `forge/warden-learn-batch/<anvil>` PRs that update `.forge/warden-rules.yaml`. Per smelter.go:1-5: "appends them to each anvil's .forge/warden-rules.yaml (deduping ...)". Current dedup is exact-ID match only. After three months of Copilot learning, Munin has 228 "other" rules and 178 "style" rules with massive semantic overlap.

Extend the smelter's merge step (before it commits the new rules + opens the PR) to do two passes:

### Pass 1: near-duplicate consolidation

For each anvil's rules:

1. Group rules by `category`.
2. Within a category, find pairs whose `pattern` + `check` similarity exceeds a threshold (e.g. Jaccard on word-bags ≥ 0.6, or a cheap embedding model). Mark them as candidates.
3. Ask the `warden`-stage provider (small, cheap call) to merge candidate clusters into single canonical rules, preserving `source` (concatenate / dedupe), keeping the older `added` date, and producing one consolidated `check + pattern`.
4. Replace the cluster in the file with the merged rule. Move the original rules to `.forge/warden-rules.archive.yaml` with a `superseded_by: <new-id>` annotation (audit trail; not loaded by the warden at review time).

### Pass 2: staleness archive

For each rule whose `added` is older than N days (default: 180) AND whose `source` list shows no new entries in the last N/2 days, move it to `.forge/warden-rules.archive.yaml` with a `last_seen` field. The rule is still recoverable (a `forge warden restore <id>` subcommand or manual edit) but it stops adding cost to every review.

### Pass 3: tag missing `Paths` (optional but powerful)

For each unmoved rule whose `source` contains `copilot:PR#N` references, fetch the changed-files list from PR N (cheap GitHub API call) and populate `Paths` with the file-type globs that cover those files. One-time backfill at first run; subsequent runs only touch new rules. This makes Half A's path-glob filter actually load-bearing on existing rules.

All three passes happen INSIDE the smelter's normal batch run — same `forge/warden-learn-batch/<anvil>` PR title, same review/merge gating, no separate operator workflow.

### Acceptance for Half B

- After one full smelter run on Munin, the live `.forge/warden-rules.yaml` has measurably fewer rules (target: <500, from 971) and `.forge/warden-rules.archive.yaml` exists with the moved ones.
- A consolidated rule's `source` field lists every original source that contributed (auditability preserved).
- The smelter still emits ONE PR per anvil per run (same as today). The PR's diff shows added rules + consolidated rules + archived rules in clearly labelled sections of the commit message.
- Existing rules without `Paths` get backfilled with file-type globs derived from their source PRs, where the PR is still resolvable via GitHub API.
- A staleness threshold (`settings.warden.archive_after_days`) and consolidation similarity threshold (`settings.warden.dedup_threshold`) are configurable.
- Restore path exists: `forge warden restore <rule-id>` moves a rule from archive back to the active file.

## How the two halves wire together

- **Half B reduces N** (the active rule count) by consolidating and archiving.
- **Half A reduces the prompt subset** (k rules per review) from N to a small relevant set.
- The product is: per-review cost = k tokens where k is bounded and approximately constant regardless of how long Forge runs on this anvil.
- Without Half A, Half B alone helps but doesn't cap the per-review cost — a freshly-grown 800-rule file still ships 800 rules.
- Without Half B, Half A alone keeps per-review cost bounded but `.forge/warden-rules.yaml` keeps growing forever, and even the filtering work scales with N.

Both halves benefit from being shipped together. They can land in either order; if they need to ship sequentially, Half A first delivers the immediate cost reduction and Half B follows to keep that gain durable.

## Files to touch

- `internal/warden/rules.go` — add `Paths` to `Rule`, add `FormatChecklistForDiff(diff, files []string)`.
- `internal/warden/warden.go:buildReviewPrompt` — call the new filtered formatter, accept `diff` and `changedFiles` parameters where it currently passes `anvilPath` only.
- `internal/warden/warden.go:Review` — surface `changedFiles` (already computed during pipeline; thread it through).
- `internal/smelter/smelter.go` — add the dedup/archive/path-backfill passes inside the batch merge step.
- `internal/warden/archive.go` (new) — load/save `.forge/warden-rules.archive.yaml`, restore subcommand.
- `cmd/forge/warden.go` — new `forge warden consolidate <anvil>` (manual trigger of Half B for off-cycle runs), new `forge warden restore <rule-id> --anvil <name>`.
- `internal/config/config.go` — new settings: `warden.max_rules_per_review`, `warden.archive_after_days`, `warden.dedup_threshold`, `warden.use_all_rules`.

No state.db schema changes (the pending_warden_rules table already has everything we need).

## Acceptance criteria (combined)

- Token cost of warden reviews on Munin drops by ≥80% on typical beads.
- `.forge/warden-rules.yaml` shrinks by 30-50% after one smelter consolidation pass; growth rate after that is roughly net-zero (new rules in ≈ consolidated/archived rules out).
- No regression in warden verdict quality (measurable via re-running the warden on 10-20 historical merged PRs and comparing verdicts).
- Archive file `.forge/warden-rules.archive.yaml` is created and committed alongside the consolidated rules file.
- `forge warden restore <id> --anvil <name>` round-trips a rule from archive back to active.
- All three filter stages (path-glob, category, pattern-grep) are individually toggleable via config for tuning.

## Notes / why this matters

The warden rule learning system is the cleanest piece of Forge's "grows smarter without human intervention" loop. It already extracts knowledge from real Copilot review comments and bakes it in. The problem is purely scaling: the loop is open at one end (rules in) and never closes (rules out). Half B closes that loop; Half A makes the open-ended cost cap-able.

The immediate trigger was a one-line observation that Munin's warden-rules.yaml is 530 KB. The fix has been hiding in plain sight in the existing data model — the `category` field was already there waiting to be used for routing.

This is a "the forge gets cheaper as it gets smarter" kind of fix, which is roughly the opposite of the usual scaling curve.

title: Forge burnish round-2 stuck after Smith success — no warden / no push, worker row never transitions
description:
On 2026-05-19 Forge's burnish round-2 for PR 761 (Hytte-3uq2) got stuck: the Smith subprocess completed, committed locally to the worktree, exited cleanly with `result: success` in its log — but the burnish post-processing (verify with Warden, then push to origin) never fired. The `workers` row stayed `status='running'` with `pid=0` indefinitely, and the local commit `e59264c3` was never pushed. Other burnish workers (e.g. PR 763 round 2) processed normally during the same window, so the daemon overall was healthy.

Unblocked manually by:
- `cd ~/source/Hytte/.workers/Hytte-3uq2 && git push origin forge/Hytte-3uq2`
- `UPDATE workers SET status='done' WHERE id='hytte-Hytte-3uq2-1779202355830124410'`

Round-1 burnish for the same PR earlier in the day worked normally and emitted `[burnish] PR #761: Review fixes verified and pushed on attempt 1`. Round 2 emitted "spawning review fix worker" + "5 actionable review comments" then went silent — no warden log, no push log, no error.

## What to investigate

1. **What hangs the post-smith pipeline?** The likely culprits in `internal/burnish/*` (or wherever the burnish loop lives): a channel read with no timeout, a wait-for-warden goroutine that loses its done-signal, an unbounded retry that never exits.
2. **Why no log on the failure path?** A panic in the burnish goroutine would surface; silence implies a blocked syscall or a hung Wait(). Add structured logging around the smith-exit → warden-spawn → push transitions so the next stuck worker is diagnosable from logs alone.
3. **Watchdog gap.** The existing `internal/watchdog` package supposedly detects stale workers; this worker sat with `status='running'` for 10+ minutes with no progress and watchdog didn't surface anything. Either tighten the threshold or extend the watchdog to look at burnish-phase workers with a pid=0 (because the smith subprocess has already exited but the bookkeeping goroutine is alive).

## Scope

1. Add structured INFO/WARN logs at each transition inside the burnish post-smith pipeline: smith exit observed → warden spawn → warden verdict → push attempt → resolve threads. Tag every line with `pr=<n>` and `bead=<id>` so journalctl filtering pinpoints the stuck step.
2. Add a timeout (configurable, default 5 min) on the warden-verification wait so a missed done-signal can't hang the loop forever. On timeout, log WARN, mark the worker `failed` with reason `warden_timeout`, and let the daemon's normal recovery handle re-dispatch.
3. Watchdog extension: any worker in `running` status with `phase='burnish'` and no progress for > N minutes (default 10) gets logged and either auto-cleared or escalated via the existing alert path.
4. Regression test in `internal/burnish/...` that drives the post-smith pipeline with a fake warden that never returns and asserts the timeout fires + the worker is marked `failed` with a stable error string.

## Acceptance

- `go build`, `go test ./...` pass.
- Forcing a warden timeout in the test harness produces the expected `failed` transition and log line within the configured timeout.
- Manually stalling the post-smith step (e.g. via a `pause` hook in dev) shows the new transition logs in `journalctl -u forge`.
- Changelog fragment in `changelog.d/` (category: Fixed).

## Reference

- internal/burnish/* — round-2 burnish flow that hung on PR 761.
- internal/watchdog/* — existing stale-worker detection that didn't catch this.
- `workers` table in `~/.forge/state.db` — schema for status/phase/pid bookkeeping.
