title: Stride: nightly evaluation should target yesterday + use notes for that date
description:
Two related issues with how Stride's nightly evaluation interprets timing and user notes:

## Issue 1: Wrong target date

The nightly evaluation runs at 03:00 and evaluates 'today' (April 10 at 03:00 = the new day). But at 03:00 nothing has happened yet for that day — the user can't have done a workout. The job should evaluate **yesterday** (April 9), which is the day that just ended.

Current behavior: marks today as 'missed' before the day has even started.
Correct behavior: evaluate yesterday's compliance — that's a complete day.

## Issue 2: User notes ignored by evaluation

The evaluation logic in evaluate.go uses template strings ('Rest day taken as planned', 'Planned X was not completed') and doesn't read stride_notes at all. Notes only feed into the next plan generation prompt.

When a user writes a note like 'I don't have time for a workout today, I'll do it tomorrow instead', Stride should:
1. Pick up the note in the evaluation for that date
2. Understand the context (planned rest, swap, defer)
3. Adjust the evaluation accordingly

## Fix

1. **Change the nightly target date**: in stride.RunNightlyEvaluation, use yesterday (today - 1 day) as the evaluation target. The early-morning run is for the day that ended.

2. **Add notes to evaluation**: 
   - Notes should have a target_date field (default: created_at date), so users can write notes about specific days
   - When evaluating a date with no workout, fetch notes targeting that date
   - If notes exist, use Claude to generate a contextual evaluation instead of the template
   - Template fallback when no notes

3. **Notes UI**: optionally let users specify which date a note applies to (default: today). Or detect dates in the note text ('I'll do it tomorrow' → infer the offset).

## Files
- internal/stride/evaluate.go — RunNightlyEvaluation, evaluateUserDay
- internal/stride/handlers.go — note creation, add target_date
- internal/db/db.go — add target_date column to stride_notes
- web/src/pages/StridePage.tsx — note form, optionally show date picker

title: Smith deny patterns: per-anvil file and command deny lists enforced in the pipeline
Custom Temper commands: allow per-anvil override of build/test/lint commands in forge.yaml
Pipeline hooks: add configurable shell command hooks at each pipeline stage (before/after Smith, Temper, Warden)
Per-stage provider configuration: allow separate model/provider chains for Smith, Warden, Schematic, and CI fix stages
Include bead notes in Smith prompt
description:
The Smith prompt only includes the bead description field, not the notes field. The poller's Bead struct (internal/poller/poller.go) doesn't have a Notes field, so notes from 'bd ready --json' are silently dropped. The prompt template (internal/prompt/prompt.go) only renders .Bead.Description.

This means detailed implementation instructions placed in the notes field are invisible to the Smith. Users work around this by putting everything in the description or referencing plan files, but the notes should be included directly.

## Fix

1. Add Notes field to poller.Bead struct (internal/poller/poller.go line ~25)
2. Add Notes field to prompt.BeadContext struct (internal/prompt/prompt.go line ~17)
3. Pass Notes through in pipeline.go where BeadContext is built (~line 627)
4. Add Notes section to the prompt template after Description (internal/prompt/prompt.go ~line 195):

### Notes

{{if .Bead.Notes}}{{.Bead.Notes}}{{end}}

5. Update the schematic word threshold to also count notes words (internal/schematic/schematic.go ~line 110) — or keep it description-only since notes are typically detailed specs that don't need decomposition.

title: Decrypt enc: webhook URLs when loading config
description: Forge daemon reads webhook URLs from ~/.forge/config.yaml but does not decrypt enc:-prefixed values. The Hytte GUI encrypts webhook URLs with AES-256-GCM (enc: prefix) before writing to the config file, but Forge passes the raw enc:... string to the HTTP client, causing 'unsupported protocol scheme "enc"' errors on every webhook delivery.
notes:
## Root cause

Hytte's forge config handler (`internal/forge/config_handler.go`) encrypts webhook URLs on save via `encryptSensitiveFields()` using `internal/encryption` (AES-256-GCM, key from `~/.config/hytte/.encryption_key`). The `enc:` prefix marks encrypted values.

Forge's daemon (`internal/daemon/daemon.go` lines ~254 and ~4651) reads `w.URL` from config and passes it directly to `notify.WebhookTarget` with no decryption.

## Recommended fix

Add a small `internal/crypto` package to Forge that can decrypt `enc:`-prefixed strings using the same key file (`~/.config/hytte/.encryption_key`). The logic is straightforward AES-256-GCM:

1. Strip `enc:` prefix
2. Base64-decode the remainder
3. Read 32-byte key from `~/.config/hytte/.encryption_key` (hex-encoded)
4. AES-256-GCM open (nonce is prepended to ciphertext)

Apply decryption in daemon.go where webhook targets are built (two locations: initial startup ~line 254 and hot-reload rebuild ~line 4649). If the value doesn't have the `enc:` prefix, use it as-is (plaintext backward compat).

Reference implementation: `~/source/Hytte/internal/encryption/encryption.go` — functions `DecryptField` and `Decrypt`.

## Affected code

- `source/Forge/internal/daemon/daemon.go:254` — initial webhook target setup
- `source/Forge/internal/daemon/daemon.go:4649` — hot-reload webhook target rebuild
- New: `source/Forge/internal/crypto/crypto.go` — decrypt helper

## Verification

After fix, `journalctl -u forge | grep webhook` should show successful deliveries instead of `unsupported protocol scheme "enc"` errors.

title: Depcheck: creates duplicate package update beads instead of reusing existing open one
description:
The depcheck consolidation (Forge-8y9k) is supposed to find-or-create a single bead per anvil for package updates. But on Hytte, two beads were created on consecutive days:

- Hytte-7ymv: "Package updates starting 30.03.2026"
- Hytte-8clg: "Package updates starting 31.03.2026"

The second scan should have found the existing open bead (Hytte-7ymv) and appended new outdated packages to it, not created a new one. The find logic in depcheck/consolidate.go likely searches by exact title match including the date, so a new day = new title = new bead.

Fix: search for ANY open bead with the "Package updates" prefix (or a specific label/type), not by exact title. The date in the title is cosmetic — the consolidation should reuse the existing open bead regardless of when it was created. Only create a new one if no open package-update bead exists for that anvil.

Source: https://github.com/Robin831/Forge/issues/489

title: Bellows: PR title not stored in prs table — notifications show 'PR #N' instead of title
description:
The prs table on Hetzner has empty title columns for all PRs. This causes ready-to-merge notifications to show 'PR #488' instead of the actual PR title.

Bellows tracks PRs in state.db but doesn't populate the title field. The title is available from the GitHub API response when Bellows checks PR status — it just needs to be stored.

Check internal/bellows/bellows.go where PRs are inserted/updated in the prs table. The title field exists in the schema but isn't being set. Also check if the pipeline sets it when creating the PR — the Hytte notification showed the correct title, suggesting the pipeline passes it but Bellows doesn't persist it on the Hetzner state.db (possibly a fresh state.db issue where old PRs from the laptop had titles but Hetzner-created ones don't).

title: New shortcut in Hearth for Wicket
description:
We need a new shortcut in hearth to manually force a wicket scan.

Now it's on a timer, and it could be rather long (I have 15 mins), it would be nice to be able to press w or something to run the wicket scan immediatly. Be sure to set a cooldown to prevent spam or doubleclick to run it multiple times in short succession.

Source: https://github.com/Robin831/Forge/issues/487

title: Bellows: PR merge reports failure when local branch delete fails due to active worktree
description:
When Bellows auto-merges a PR, gh pr merge succeeds on GitHub but reports exit status 1 because it tries to delete the local branch which is still in use by a worktree.

Error: 'failed to delete local branch Fhi.Metadata-hcn0: error: cannot delete branch used by worktree at C:/source/fhigit/Fhi.Metadata/.worktrees/Fhi.Metadata-hcn0'

The merge itself succeeded — the failure is cosmetic (local branch cleanup). Fix options:
1. Pass --delete-branch=false to gh pr merge and let the worktree cleanup handle branch deletion
2. Remove the worktree before merging
3. Catch this specific error and treat it as a successful merge (the PR IS merged, just local cleanup failed)

Option 1 is simplest and safest.

title: Tune watchdog stale-detection interval for lifecycle workers
description: In the watchdog/stale-worker detector code, check whether lifecycle workers (burnish/quench/rebase) can be registered with a shorter stale interval than the main pipeline. Add an optional per-worker stale timeout parameter. Update worker registration at launch sites in daemon.go to pass the shorter interval. This is a lower-priority safety-net improvement and should be the last sub-task merged, after the primary timeout fix (sub-task 1) is in place.

title: Fix Copilot provider to return rate-limit error instead of hanging
description: Locate the Copilot provider implementation (likely provider/copilot.go or similar). Find the code path triggered when premium request quota is exhausted. Ensure the provider returns a structured rate-limit error (not a hang or indefinite retry loop) so Smith can exit cleanly. Add or verify that fallback logic surfaces this error rather than silently blocking. This sub-task is in a different file/subsystem from daemon.go and can be worked in parallel with sub-tasks 1 and 2.

title: Ensure burnish worker proceeds to thread resolution and completion after Smith pushes fixes
description: In daemon.go, audit the code path after Smith's push succeeds in the burnish worker. Identify any blocking wait on Smith process exit that could stall comment resolution and completion notification. Add a non-blocking check or a short deadline on the process-exit wait so that if Smith's subprocess is slow to exit, the worker still advances to resolve review threads and emit the completion event. This is independent of the timeout context change but shares daemon.go; sequence after sub-task 1 to avoid merge conflicts.

title: Add timeout context to burnish/quench/rebase lifecycle workers
description: Modify daemon.go around line 986 (ActionFixReview case) and the equivalent dispatch points for quench and rebase workers. Instead of passing d.runCtx directly, derive a child context with a deadline using smith_timeout (or a new lifecycle_worker_timeout config key). Read the timeout value from the existing config struct. Wrap the worker goroutine launch so that context cancellation propagates into the worker and causes it to exit with a logged error. This is the primary fix for the indefinite-hang symptom. No dependency on other sub-tasks — can land first.

title: Burnish worker runs indefinitely — no timeout on review fix lifecycle workers
description:
A colleague using Copilot-only config reports that after Smith successfully pushed review fixes, the burnish worker kept running indefinitely. No comment resolving, no completion notification, no next step.

Root cause investigation:
- The burnish worker (ActionFixReview case in daemon.go:986) uses d.runCtx as its context, which has NO timeout
- Unlike the main pipeline which has smith_timeout, lifecycle workers (burnish/quench/rebase) have no independent timeout
- If Smith hangs (e.g. Copilot rate limit exhaustion, network issue, subprocess not exiting), the burnish worker blocks forever
- The stale worker detector (watchdog) should catch this eventually, but it checks log activity not process liveness

Likely Copilot-specific issue: when all Copilot premium requests are exhausted, the provider fallback has nowhere to go and Smith may hang rather than returning a rate-limit error.

Fix:
1. Add a timeout context for burnish/quench/rebase workers (use smith_timeout or a dedicated lifecycle_worker_timeout setting)
2. Ensure Smith always exits cleanly when rate-limited (check the Copilot provider exit behavior)
3. After Smith pushes fixes, ensure the worker proceeds to thread resolution and completion even if Smith's process exit is delayed
4. Consider: should the watchdog's stale detection interval be shorter for lifecycle workers?

This sub-task defines the bead data model/format that sibling sub-tasks (Ledger panel, pipeline execution) depend on.

title: Rewrite depcheck to use AI-driven consolidated package updates
description:
Replace the current 'dumb' depcheck flow (one bead per package, no AI, raw commands) with a consolidated AI-driven approach.

## Current problem
The non-AI deps updater creates PRs that get review comments because it misses changelog fragments, doesn't adapt to repo conventions, and handles each package individually. It also creates too many beads (one per outdated package).

## New design

### Consolidated bead (one per anvil)
- First outdated package detected creates a bead titled eg 'Package updates starting 27.03.2026' (date-stamped, generic)
- Subsequent scan results append to the same open bead's description rather than creating new beads
- Description format lists all packages to update:
  ```
  npm: react 18.2→19.0, vite 7.1→8.0
  nuget: Newtonsoft.Json 13.0→14.0
  ```
- Both nuget and npm packages in the same repo go in the same bead
- One bead per anvil (each gets its own branch/PR)
- Auto-dispatch (tagged forgeReady) — won't run until the anvil's dispatch tag is applied anyway

### AI-driven execution
- The bead goes through the normal pipeline: Schematic → Smith → Temper → Warden
- Smith reads the package list from the bead description, attempts all upgrades
- Smith handles changelog fragments, lock file updates, breaking API changes — adapting to each repo's conventions
- Temper runs build/test to verify

### Partial success
- If some upgrades break tests, Smith commits the ones that work and notes the failures in the bead
- The PR merges with successful upgrades
- Bead closes on merge
- Next depcheck scan creates a new bead with the still-outdated packages (including the ones that failed last time — maybe they work next week with a newer version or resolved dependency)

### Update panel integration
- The Ledger update panel triggers the same flow: finds the open deps-update bead for the anvil, runs it through the pipeline
- If no open bead exists, the scan creates one first

### What to change
- depcheck.Monitor: instead of creating individual beads, find-or-create a single consolidated bead per anvil
- depcheck: append new outdated packages to existing open bead description
- Remove the old non-AI update-deps command/flow that runs raw npm/dotnet commands
- Pipeline handles it like any other bead (Smith does the actual updating)

title: Auto-create PR when NO_CHANGES_NEEDED detects orphaned branch with commits
description:
When Smith reports NO_CHANGES_NEEDED but the forge branch has commits ahead of main with no open PR, the daemon now correctly detects this (Forge-jvpg fix) and logs it — but still requires manual PR creation.

The daemon should automatically create the PR in this case instead of flagging needs_human. The branch already passed Temper and Warden on a prior attempt; the only thing that failed was PR creation (usually a timeout or transient GitHub error).

Flow should be:
1. Smith says NO_CHANGES_NEEDED
2. Daemon checks: does `origin/forge/<bead-id>` exist with commits ahead of main?
3. If yes AND no open PR exists: create the PR automatically (same as the normal pipeline end)
4. If PR creation fails: then flag needs_human

This would eliminate the most common "needs attention" scenario — beads that did all the work but got stuck on the last mile.

Source: https://github.com/Robin831/Forge/issues/456

title: Wicket: pending issues stuck forever after bead creation failure
description:
When Wicket triages an issue and bead creation fails (e.g. due to an invalid `bd create` flag), the issue is left in `pending` state in `wicket_issues`. On subsequent scan cycles, `shouldSkip()` checks `IsIssueTracked()` which returns true for any tracked issue regardless of state — so the issue is never retried.

**Expected behavior:** Wicket should retry `pending` issues that failed bead creation, or at minimum clean them up so they can be re-triaged on the next cycle.

**Reproduction:** Any `bd create` failure during triage leaves the issue permanently stuck. The only recovery is manually deleting the row from `wicket_issues`.

Relevant code: `wicket.go:354` — `shouldSkip` treats all tracked issues as handled, but `pending` with no `bead_id` means triage never completed successfully.

Source: https://github.com/Robin831/Forge/issues/449

title: Smelter runs on every daemon startup — should skip if already ran today
description:
The Smelter (vulnerability scanner) runs immediately on every Forge daemon startup regardless of when it last ran. If the daemon is restarted multiple times in a day (e.g. during development or after config changes), Smelter runs each time unnecessarily.

It should persist the last run timestamp (e.g. in state.db) and skip the startup run if it already completed within the last 24 hours. The interval-based schedule should still work normally after that.

Source: https://github.com/Robin831/Forge/issues/450

- Close: "Closing Forge-xxxx..." → then "Closed Forge-xxxx" on success
- Edit: "Updating Forge-xxxx..." → then "Updated Forge-xxxx" on success

title: Schematic: chain-aware decomposition preserves dependency relationships
description:
When the schematic auto-decomposes a bead that is part of a dependency chain (has Blocks entries), the chain breaks. The original bead gets closed but its 'blocks' relationships are lost, causing downstream beads to become unblocked prematurely.

Example: Chain A → B → C. Schematic decomposes B into B1, B2, B3.
Current behavior: B is closed, C becomes unblocked immediately.
Expected behavior: B's 'blocks C' relationship transfers to B3 (the last sub-bead), so C stays blocked until B3 completes.

Fix needed in internal/schematic/schematic.go decomposition logic:
1. Before closing the original bead, read its Blocks list
2. After creating the sub-bead chain (B1→B2→B3), add 'B3 blocks C' for each entry in the original Blocks list
3. This ensures the downstream chain stays intact through decomposition

Also consider: if the original bead has DependsOn entries, those should transfer to B1 (the first sub-bead) so the chain stays blocked until its upstream dependencies complete.

description:
Implementation plan: .forge/plans/github-issues-worker.md (see Appendix D: Hearth TUI Panel)

## Overview
Add a compact Wicket panel to the Hearth TUI, positioned between the Workers panel and the Usage panel in the right column. This gives users at-a-glance visibility into GitHub issues being monitored by Wicket. The Workers panel is currently taller than needed, so reclaim some of that vertical space for the Wicket panel.

## Prerequisites
Phase 5 (Multi-Repo + External Repos) should be complete. The wicket_issues table is populated and the wicket_status IPC command exists.

## What to Build

### 1. Wicket Panel Component (internal/hearth/)
Create a new Bubbletea component for the Wicket panel. It should display:

```
┌─── Wicket ───────────┐
│ forge     3 open  1⚠ │
│ heimdall  1 open  0⚠ │
│ hytte     0 open  0⚠ │
└──────────────────────┘
```

Columns:
- **Anvil name** — left-aligned, same styling as other panels
- **Open issues** — count of issues in wicket_issues with status != closed/merged for this anvil
- **Needs-human count (⚠)** — count of issues with action="flag_human" or status requiring human attention

The ⚠ count should highlight in yellow/orange when > 0 to draw attention.

Anvils with 0 open issues can be shown dimmed or hidden to save space (follow the convention of the existing panels).

### 2. Layout Changes (internal/hearth/)
Modify the Hearth TUI layout to insert the Wicket panel:

Current right column layout (top to bottom):
1. Workers panel
2. Usage panel

New right column layout:
1. Workers panel (shorter)
2. Wicket panel (new)
3. Usage panel

**Workers panel height reduction:**
- The Workers panel currently allocates space for `max_total_smiths` rows but rarely fills all of them
- Cap the Workers panel minimum height at ~4 rows (header + 3 worker rows)
- Give the reclaimed vertical space to the Wicket panel
- The Wicket panel needs 3-5 rows: 1 header + 1 row per active Wicket-enabled anvil

Look at how the existing panels are sized in the Hearth layout code. The panels likely use Bubbletea's lipgloss for layout. Find where panel heights are calculated and adjust.

### 3. Data Source
The panel should get its data from one of:
- **Option A:** Send `wicket_status` IPC command to daemon (consistent with how other panels get data)
- **Option B:** Query wicket_issues table directly from state.db (consistent with how the queue panel reads data)

Choose whichever approach matches the existing Hearth patterns better. Look at how the Queue panel and Workers panel get their data.

The data needed per anvil:
- Anvil name
- Count of open issues (status NOT IN ('closed', 'merged'))
- Count of needs-human issues (action = 'flag_human' AND status = 'open')

Add a DB query method if needed: `GetWicketSummary() ([]WicketAnvilSummary, error)` that returns per-anvil counts.

### 4. Conditional Display
- Only show the Wicket panel if `wicket_enabled` is true in config
- If Wicket is disabled, the Workers panel gets its full original height back
- If no anvils have Wicket enabled, hide the panel entirely

### 5. Refresh
The panel should refresh on the same interval as other panels (likely on each tick or when events arrive). Subscribe to EventWicket* events to trigger updates.

- Test panel rendering with various counts (0, 1, many)

title: Wicket Phase 5: Multi-Repo + External Repos
description:
Implementation plan: .forge/plans/github-issues-worker.md

## Overview
Enable Wicket to monitor GitHub issues on repos that are NOT the anvil's own repo. This allows monitoring external repos (e.g., a public-facing repo) and creating beads in the appropriate anvil. Also add cross-repo deduplication and documentation.

## Prerequisites
Phase 4 (Advanced Triage + Polish) must be complete. All triage actions, CLI commands, metrics, and rate limiting are working.

## What to Build

### 1. wicket_repos Config Implementation (wicket.go, types.go)
The `wicket_repos` per-anvil config field was defined in Phase 1 but not fully implemented. Now make it functional:
- When `wicket_repos` is non-empty, monitor those repos instead of (or in addition to) the anvil's own repo
- Each entry is "owner/repo" format
- When empty (default), derive the repo from the anvil's git remote: parse `git remote get-url origin` to extract "owner/repo"
- Store the repo->anvil mapping so beads are created in the correct anvil

Modify the poll loop to iterate over the effective repo list for each anvil.

### 2. Repo-to-Anvil Mapping (wicket.go)
When creating beads from issues on external repos:
- The bead must be created in the anvil that configured the monitoring (not in a non-existent anvil for the external repo)
- Include the source repo in the bead description: "Source: https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123"
- The anvil_name in wicket_issues should be the anvil that owns the monitoring config
- If multiple anvils monitor the same repo, deduplicate: only process the issue once (first anvil wins, or make it configurable)

### 3. Cross-Repo Deduplication (triage.go)
Extend duplicate detection to work across repos:
- When checking for duplicates, search beads across all anvils (not just the current one)
- An issue in repo A might be a duplicate of a bead created from repo B
- Use the "Source: <issue-url>" line in bead descriptions to cross-reference
- The AI triage prompt should include open beads from ALL monitored repos for the current anvil

### 4. Documentation (docs/configuration.md)
Update the configuration documentation to include all Wicket settings:
- Global settings with descriptions and defaults
- Per-anvil settings with descriptions and defaults
- Example configurations: minimal, multi-repo, trigger-label mode
- Explain the difference between push model (default) and pull model (trigger_label)
- Document the wicket_repos feature with examples

Also add a section to the main README or CLAUDE.md's Architecture section briefly describing the Wicket component.

### 5. Handling Edge Cases for External Repos
- What if the external repo's gh authentication differs? Log a clear error.
- What if an external repo issue references a different codebase? The AI triage prompt should include the anvil's context (README, AGENTS.md) to help the AI contextualize.
- What if the same issue is seen by multiple anvils? Use a dedup key of (repo, issue_number) in wicket_issues — the UNIQUE constraint handles this. Log a warning if a second anvil tries to process an already-tracked issue.

## Tests to Write
- Test wicket_repos config: anvil monitors external repo, bead created in correct anvil
- Test repo derived from git remote when wicket_repos is empty
- Test multiple repos per anvil: each repo is polled
- Test cross-repo dedup: issue in repo A matches bead from repo B
- Test multiple anvils monitoring same repo: only processed once
- Test external repo auth failure: graceful error handling

## Files to Modify
- internal/wicket/wicket.go (poll loop to handle multiple repos per anvil, repo resolution)
- internal/wicket/types.go (ensure repo->anvil mapping is clear)
- internal/wicket/triage.go (cross-repo dedup in AI prompt context)

- Look at how anvil paths are resolved in internal/config/ for the git remote parsing pattern
- Look at how internal/poller/ handles per-anvil polling for the multi-repo iteration pattern

title: Wicket Phase 4: Advanced Triage + Polish
description:
Implementation plan: .forge/plans/github-issues-worker.md

## Overview
Add smarter AI triage decisions (duplicate detection, already-fixed detection, out-of-scope), CLI commands for listing and re-triaging issues, metrics in forge status, rate limiting, and integration tests.

## Prerequisites
Phase 3 (Dispatch Confirmation + Follow-Up) must be complete. The full issue lifecycle (create -> dispatch -> PR -> merge -> close) works end-to-end.

## What to Build

### 1. Duplicate Detection (triage.go)
Enhance the AI triage prompt to include existing open beads for deduplication:
- Before calling AI triage, fetch open beads: `bd list --status=open,in_progress --limit 0 --json`
- Parse the JSON output to get bead IDs, titles, and descriptions
- Include a summary in the triage prompt (see Appendix A of the plan): "Recent open beads (for dedup): {open_beads_list}"
- When AI returns ActionDuplicate:
  - Post the "Duplicate Detected" comment template linking to the existing bead
  - Record in wicket_issues with action="duplicate"
  - Optionally add a "duplicate" label to the issue
  - Do NOT auto-close — let the author confirm it's a duplicate

The AI should compare title similarity AND check if the issue URL is already referenced in an existing bead's description (the "Source: <issue-url>" line from bead creation).

### 2. Already-Fixed Detection (triage.go)
Enhance the AI triage prompt to check for recently resolved work:
- Fetch recently closed beads: `bd list --status=closed --limit 20 --json` (last 20 closed)
- Fetch recently merged PRs from the state.db prs table
- Include in the triage prompt: "Recently resolved: {recent_closed_summary}"
- When AI returns ActionAlreadyFixed:
  - Post a comment explaining it appears to be fixed, referencing the relevant PR/bead
  - Suggest the author verify and close the issue
  - Record in wicket_issues with action="already_fixed"

### 3. Out-of-Scope Detection with Custom Triage Prompt (triage.go)
When AI returns ActionOutOfScope:
- Post the "Rejected / Out of Scope" template with the AI's reasoning
- Record in wicket_issues with action="out_of_scope"

The per-anvil `wicket_triage_prompt` config (from Phase 1) should be appended to the AI prompt. This lets repo owners give the AI guidance like "issues about the mobile app should be redirected to repo X" or "we don't accept feature requests for deprecated APIs".

### 4. CLI: forge wicket list (cmd/forge/)
Add `forge wicket list` command:
- Sends `wicket_list` IPC command to daemon (with optional --anvil filter)
- Displays a table of tracked issues: repo, issue #, title (truncated), author, action, status, bead ID, age
- Support `--anvil <name>` flag to filter by anvil
- Support `--status <status>` flag to filter by status (open, bead_created, dispatched, etc.)
- Support `--json` flag for JSON output

Add the `wicket_list` IPC command handler in the daemon. It should query wicket_issues from state.db.

### 5. CLI: forge wicket retriage (cmd/forge/)
Add `forge wicket retriage <repo> <issue-number>` command:
- Sends `wicket_retriage` IPC command to daemon
- Daemon resets the issue's wicket_issues entry (clear action, set status back to "open")
- On next poll cycle, the issue will be re-triaged from scratch
- Useful when the AI made a bad triage decision

Add the `wicket_retriage` IPC command handler.

### 6. Metrics in forge status (cmd/forge/, internal/daemon/)
Add Wicket stats to the `forge status` output:
- Total issues tracked
- Issues by status (open, bead_created, dispatched, pr_created, merged, closed, stale)
- Issues by action (create_bead, ask_clarification, flag_human, duplicate, etc.)
- Beads created by Wicket (count)
- Last poll time per anvil

Query these from wicket_issues table and include in the status IPC response.

### 7. Rate Limiting and Backoff (ghclient.go, wicket.go)
Add rate limit awareness to the ghClient:
- After each `gh` CLI call, check stderr for rate limit warnings
- Track remaining API quota (parse X-RateLimit-Remaining if available from gh output)
- When quota is low (<100 remaining), increase poll interval temporarily
- Implement exponential backoff on 403/rate limit errors
- Log EventWicketError when rate limited
- Add a `rateLimiter` field to Monitor that tracks state across polls

### 8. Integration Tests
Create integration tests that test the full Wicket flow against mock data:
- Set up a mock ghClient that returns realistic issue data
- Test the complete flow: issue arrives -> triage -> bead created -> dispatch confirmed -> PR linked -> merged -> issue closed
- Test duplicate detection with existing beads

- Test out-of-scope with custom triage prompt
- Test rate limiting behavior

These should be in internal/wicket/integration_test.go with a build tag if they need real external services, or as regular tests with comprehensive mocks.

title: Wicket Phase 3: Dispatch Confirmation + Follow-Up
description:
Implementation plan: .forge/plans/github-issues-worker.md

## Overview
Add interactive dispatch confirmation (user reacts/comments to trigger auto-dispatch), clarification re-triage when authors reply, issue-to-PR linking, auto-close on merge, and stale issue detection.

## Prerequisites
Phase 2 (Non-Trusted Users + Labels) must be complete. Label management, full triage flow for both trusted and non-trusted users, and Hearth events integration all exist.

## What to Build

### 1. Dispatch Confirmation (wicket.go, new file dispatch.go)
When `wicket_auto_dispatch` is false (default) and a bead is created:
- The "Bead Created" comment already asks user to react with :rocket: or comment "dispatch"
- Add a new poll step that checks issues in `bead_created` status for:
  a) Rocket emoji reaction on the issue (use `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/reactions`)
  b) A comment from the issue author containing "dispatch" (case-insensitive)
- When detected:
  - Run `bd update <bead_id> --tag auto-dispatch` to mark the bead for auto-dispatch
  - Update wicket_issues status to "dispatched"
  - Post a confirmation comment: "Dispatched! I'll update this issue when work begins."
  - Log EventWicketDispatchConfirm event
- Also handle "label <tag>" comments: run `bd update <bead_id> --tag <tag>`, then re-post asking about dispatch

Add `ListReactions(ctx, repo, number) ([]Reaction, error)` to the ghClient interface. Implementation uses `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/reactions --jq '.[] | {content, user: .user.login}'`.

### 2. Clarification Re-Triage (wicket.go, triage.go)
When an issue has status="open" and action="ask_clarification" in wicket_issues:
- On each poll, check if the issue has new comments from the original author (compare comment count or updatedAt)
- If new author comment found:
  - Re-fetch the full issue with all comments
  - Re-run AI triage with the full conversation context (all comments, not just the original body)
  - Update wicket_issues with new action and status
  - If now ActionCreateBead: create bead and post comment as normal
  - If still ActionAskClarify: post updated clarification questions
  - Log EventWicketIssueTriage event with "re-triage" in metadata

### 3. Issue-to-PR Linking (wicket.go or new file lifecycle.go)
When a bead created by Wicket gets a PR:
- Subscribe to / check for EventPRCreated events in the daemon's event stream
- When a PR is created for a bead that has a wicket_issues entry:
  - Update wicket_issues: set pr_number, status="pr_created"
  - Post the "PR Created (Follow-Up)" comment on the GitHub issue:
    "Update: A pull request has been created for this issue! PR: {pr_url} Bead: {bead_id}"
  - Log EventWicketPRLinked event

Implementation approach: Either register a callback with bellows, or have the daemon bridge events by checking wicket_issues when PR events fire. Follow whichever pattern is simpler given the existing daemon event handling.

### 4. Auto-Close on Merge (lifecycle.go)
When a PR linked to a Wicket issue is merged:
- Listen for EventPRMerged events (from bellows)
- Look up the bead_id in wicket_issues
- If found:
  - Post the "PR Merged (Auto-Close)" comment: "This has been fixed in {pr_url} and merged to {base_branch}. Closing this issue."
  - Close the GitHub issue using ghClient.CloseIssue(ctx, repo, number, "completed")
  - Update wicket_issues: status="merged"
  - Log EventWicketIssueClosed event

### 5. Stale Issue Detection (wicket.go)
For issues in "open" status with action="ask_clarification":
- If no reply from the author for 14 days (configurable):
  - Post a comment: "It's been a while since we asked for more details. Is this still an issue you'd like addressed? If so, please provide the information requested above. Otherwise, I'll close this in 7 days."
  - Update status to "stale"
- If still no reply after 7 more days:
  - Close the issue with reason "not planned"
  - Update status to "closed"
  - Log EventWicketIssueClosed event

Add a `wicket_stale_days` config option (default 14) for the initial stale threshold.

## Tests to Write
- Test dispatch confirmation via rocket reaction detection
- Test dispatch confirmation via "dispatch" comment detection
- Test "label <tag>" comment handling
- Test clarification re-triage: mock issue with new author comment, verify re-triage runs
- Test re-triage produces ActionCreateBead after clarification
- Test PR linking: mock EventPRCreated for a Wicket bead, verify comment posted
- Test auto-close on merge: mock EventPRMerged, verify issue closed and comment posted
- Test stale detection: mock issue with old clarification request, verify stale comment
- Test stale auto-close after second threshold

## Patterns to Follow

title: Wicket Phase 2: Non-Trusted Users + Labels
description:
Implementation plan: .forge/plans/github-issues-worker.md

## Overview
Extend Wicket to handle non-trusted users with conservative triage, add GitHub label management, implement trigger/filter labels, bot ignore lists, and show Wicket activity in Hearth events.

## Prerequisites
Phase 1 (Core Scaffolding) must be complete. The internal/wicket package, ghClient, wicket_issues table, poll loop, AI triage for trusted users, and daemon wiring all exist.

## What to Build

### 1. Limited Triage for Non-Trusted Users (wicket.go / triage.go)
In the poll loop, when a user is NOT in wicket_trusted_users:
- Do NOT run full AI triage
- Post the "Generic Response (Non-Trusted User)" template from Section 7 of the plan:
  "Thanks for opening this issue, @{author}! A maintainer will review it shortly. In the meantime, if you can provide [reproduction steps / expected behavior / environment details]..."
- Apply the wicket_needs_human_label to the issue
- Record in wicket_issues with action="flag_human", is_trusted=0
- Log EventWicketFlaggedHuman event

Check for spam/off-topic first (simple heuristics or a lightweight AI check): if clearly spam, use ActionReject and don't engage publicly.

### 2. Label Management (ghclient.go, wicket.go)
After processing each issue, apply appropriate GitHub labels:
- On any triage action: add `wicket_processed_label` (default "forge-triaged")
- On ActionFlagHuman: add `wicket_needs_human_label` (default "forge-needs-human")
- On ActionCreateBead: add `wicket_bead_created_label` (default "forge-bead-created")
- Ensure labels exist on the repo (use `gh label create` if needed, or just let it fail gracefully if label doesn't exist)

Update the ghClient interface if needed (AddLabels should already exist from Phase 1).

### 3. Trigger Label Support (wicket.go)
When `wicket_trigger_label` is set (non-empty) in config:
- Change filtering: only process issues that have this label
- This enables a "pull model" where users explicitly opt issues into Wicket by adding a label
- When trigger_label is empty (default), use the existing "push model" (process all new issues)

Add this to the pre-filter logic in the poll loop, right after the "already processed" check.

### 4. Issue Label Filter (wicket.go)
When `wicket_issue_labels` is set (non-empty list) in the per-anvil config:
- Only process issues that have ALL of the specified labels
- This is a separate filter from trigger_label — trigger_label opts into Wicket processing, issue_labels filters which issues are relevant
- Use the labels returned from `gh issue list --json labels`

### 5. Bot Account Ignore List (types.go, wicket.go)
Add a hardcoded list of known bot account patterns to skip:
- "dependabot[bot]", "renovate[bot]", "github-actions[bot]", "codecov[bot]", etc.
- Also add a config option `wicket_ignore_users` ([]string) for custom ignore patterns
- Check the issue author against this list before any triage

Add to AnvilWicketConfig and the config types from Phase 1.

### 6. Hearth TUI Events Integration (internal/hearth/)
The Hearth TUI's events column already shows events from state.db. The Wicket events added in Phase 1 (EventWicketIssueTriage, EventWicketBeadCreated, etc.) should already appear in the events list if they follow the standard event format.

Verify that:
- Wicket events appear in the Hearth events panel
- They have sensible formatting (look at how other events are formatted in hearth)
- If events need special formatting, add it to the event rendering logic in hearth

If the existing event rendering doesn't handle wicket events well, add display strings for each EventWicket* type in the hearth event formatting code.

## Tests to Write
- Test non-trusted user flow: issue from unknown user -> generic response + needs-human label
- Test trigger label filtering: with trigger_label set, issues without it are skipped
- Test issue label filtering: issues without all required labels are skipped
- Test bot ignore list: issues from bot accounts are skipped entirely
- Test label application: verify correct labels are added after each triage action
- Test interaction between trigger_label and issue_labels (both filters apply)

## Files to Modify
- internal/wicket/wicket.go (poll loop filtering, non-trusted user handling)
- internal/wicket/triage.go (spam detection for non-trusted)
- internal/wicket/types.go (bot ignore list, new config fields)
- internal/wicket/templates.go (ensure generic response template exists)
- internal/config/config.go (add wicket_ignore_users if not present)
- internal/hearth/ (event display formatting if needed)

## Files to Create
- internal/wicket/labels.go (label management logic, optional — could be in wicket.go)
- Additional test files or extend existing test files

## Patterns to Follow
- Look at how bellows events appear in hearth for event formatting patterns
- Look at existing label handling in the vcs/github package

title: Wicket Phase 1: Core Scaffolding (MVP)
description:
Implementation plan: .forge/plans/github-issues-worker.md

## Overview
Build the foundational Wicket package that polls GitHub issues, triages them with AI for trusted users, creates beads, and posts comments. This is the MVP that proves the concept end-to-end.

## What to Build

### 1. Config Types (internal/config/config.go)
Add these new settings to the config struct and Viper bindings:
- Global: `wicket_enabled` (bool, default false), `wicket_interval` (duration, default 5m), `wicket_provider` (string), `wicket_batch_size` (int, default 10), `wicket_processed_label` (string, default "forge-triaged"), `wicket_needs_human_label` (string, default "forge-needs-human"), `wicket_bead_created_label` (string, default "forge-bead-created"), `wicket_trigger_label` (string, default "")
- Per-anvil: `wicket_enabled` (bool pointer for override), `wicket_trusted_users` ([]string), `wicket_auto_dispatch` (bool, default false), `wicket_issue_labels` ([]string), `wicket_repos` ([]string), `wicket_triage_prompt` (string)

Follow the pattern used by depcheck/vulncheck settings in config.go. Register defaults with Viper and add FORGE_ env var overrides.

### 2. Create internal/wicket/ Package
Create these files:
- `wicket.go` — Monitor struct, New(), Run(ctx), UpdateConfig(), Stop()
- `types.go` — AnvilWicketConfig, TriageDecision, TriageAction constants, Issue/Comment/Reaction types
- `ghclient.go` — GitHubClient interface + ghClient implementation
- `triage.go` — AI triage logic
- `bead.go` — Bead creation via bd CLI
- `templates.go` — Response comment templates

### 3. GitHubClient Interface (ghclient.go)
Create an interface wrapping `gh` CLI calls (exec.CommandContext). Methods:
- `ListIssues(ctx, repo, opts) ([]Issue, error)` — runs `gh issue list --repo <repo> --state open --json number,title,body,author,labels,comments,createdAt,updatedAt --limit <batch_size>`
- `GetIssue(ctx, repo, number) (*Issue, error)` — runs `gh issue view <number> --repo <repo> --json number,title,body,author,labels,comments`
- `CommentOnIssue(ctx, repo, number, body) error` — runs `gh issue comment <number> --repo <repo> --body "<text>"`
- `AddLabels(ctx, repo, number, labels) error` — runs `gh issue edit <number> --repo <repo> --add-label "label1,label2"`
- `RemoveLabel(ctx, repo, number, label) error` — runs `gh issue edit <number> --repo <repo> --remove-label "label"`
- `CloseIssue(ctx, repo, number, reason) error` — runs `gh issue close <number> --repo <repo> --reason "<reason>"`

The implementation should use exec.CommandContext and parse JSON output. Create a mock implementation for testing.

### 4. State DB: wicket_issues Table (internal/state/)
Add a migration to create the `wicket_issues` table:
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wicket_issues (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    repo          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    issue_number  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    anvil_name    TEXT    NOT NULL,
    author        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    is_trusted    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    action        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    bead_id       TEXT,
    pr_number     INTEGER,
    status        TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
    reasoning     TEXT,
    created_at    DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    updated_at    DATETIME NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    last_polled   DATETIME,
    UNIQUE(repo, issue_number)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_wicket_issues_status ON wicket_issues(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_wicket_issues_repo ON wicket_issues(repo);
CREATE INDEX idx_wicket_issues_bead ON wicket_issues(bead_id);
```

Add DB methods: InsertWicketIssue, UpdateWicketIssue, GetWicketIssue(repo, number), ListWicketIssues(opts), IsIssueTracked(repo, number). Follow the pattern of existing state.db tables (look at how prs or workers tables are defined).

### 5. Event Types (internal/state/events.go or similar)
Add these event types following the existing EventType pattern:
- EventWicketScanDone, EventWicketIssueTriage, EventWicketBeadCreated, EventWicketClarification, EventWicketRejected, EventWicketFlaggedHuman, EventWicketError

### 6. Poll Loop (wicket.go)
The Monitor.Run(ctx) method should:
1. Tick on `wicket_interval`
2. For each anvil with wicket enabled, call ListIssues
3. Filter out: already-processed (has wicket_processed_label), PRs, closed issues, already in wicket_issues table
4. For remaining issues, check if author is in trusted_users list
5. For trusted users: run AI triage (Phase 1 only handles trusted)
6. For non-trusted: skip for now (Phase 2)
7. Process AI decision: create bead, post comment, update wicket_issues table, log event

Follow the same goroutine+ticker pattern used by depcheck.Monitor.Run() or vulncheck.Monitor.Run().

### 7. AI Triage (triage.go)
For Phase 1, support these actions only: ActionCreateBead, ActionAskClarify, ActionFlagHuman.

Build the triage prompt from the plan's Appendix A. Send it to the configured provider (use the provider package's existing RunPrompt or similar). Parse the JSON response into a TriageDecision struct. If parsing fails, retry once with a stricter prompt; if still fails, default to ActionFlagHuman.

### 8. Bead Creation (bead.go)
When AI returns ActionCreateBead:
1. Run `bd create --title "<title>" --description "<desc>\n\nSource: <issue-url>" --type <type> --priority <priority> --tag wicket --tag github-issue --silent`
2. Parse the returned bead ID
3. Store in wicket_issues.bead_id
4. Post the "Bead Created" comment template on the issue

### 9. Comment Templates (templates.go)
Implement Go text/template versions of the response templates from Section 7 of the plan. For Phase 1, implement: BeadCreated (trusted), ClarificationNeeded (trusted), FlaggedForHuman.

### 10. Daemon Wiring (internal/daemon/daemon.go)
- Add `wicketMonitor *wicket.Monitor` field to Daemon struct
- In startup: if wicket_enabled, create and start the monitor
- In hot-reload: call UpdateConfig on the monitor
- In shutdown: stop the monitor

Follow the exact pattern used for depcheck or vulncheck monitor wiring.

### 11. CLI Command (cmd/forge/)
Add `forge wicket status` command that:
- Sends `wicket_status` IPC command to daemon
- Displays: enabled/disabled, monitored repos, issue counts by status, last poll time

Add the IPC command handler in the daemon. Follow the pattern of existing IPC commands like `status` or `queue`.

### 12. Tests
- `wicket_test.go` — Unit tests for the poll loop with mock ghClient: test filtering, trusted user detection, triage flow
- `ghclient_test.go` — Tests for gh CLI output parsing (use recorded JSON output)
- `triage_test.go` — Tests for AI response parsing, malformed response handling
- `bead_test.go` — Tests for bd create command construction and output parsing
- State DB tests for wicket_issues CRUD operations

## Patterns to Follow
- Look at internal/depcheck/ and internal/vulncheck/ for the monitor pattern
- Look at internal/bellows/ for how it wires into the daemon
- Look at internal/smith/ for how it shells out to external CLIs
- Look at internal/state/db.go for table creation and migration patterns
- Look at cmd/forge/scan.go for CLI command patterns

## Files to Create
- internal/wicket/wicket.go
- internal/wicket/types.go
- internal/wicket/ghclient.go
- internal/wicket/triage.go
- internal/wicket/bead.go
- internal/wicket/templates.go
- internal/wicket/wicket_test.go
- internal/wicket/ghclient_test.go
- internal/wicket/triage_test.go
- internal/wicket/bead_test.go

## Files to Modify
- internal/config/config.go (add wicket settings)
- internal/state/db.go or migrations (add wicket_issues table)
- internal/state/events.go or wherever EventType constants live (add wicket events)
- internal/daemon/daemon.go (wire wicket monitor)
- cmd/forge/ (add wicket command)
close_reason: Previously decomposed into children; no remaining work

title: Ledger: selected anvil path wraps to next line instead of staying inline
description: In the anvil selection view, the selected anvil shows its path on a new line while unselected anvils show the path inline. Root cause: selectedStyle.Width(selectedWidth).Render(line) in renderAnvilList() (ledger.go:1628) forces lipgloss to wrap when the line exceeds panel width. Fix: truncate the path to available width before rendering, using the existing truncate() helper. Apply to both selected and unselected items for consistency.

title: Hearth: show update operation as worker with live activity output
description: When the U panel runs dependency updates, there is no visual feedback in the Workers panel and no output in Live Activity. The user wants to see the update as a worker entry (like smith/warden workers) and have its log output appear in the Live Activity panel. Changes needed: (1) In internal/hearth/update_overlay.go runUpdateApply() (~lines 90-139), insert a synthetic worker record into state.DB at start using db.InsertWorker() with a unique ID like 'depupdate-<timestamp>', status='running', phase='depupdate', title='Applying dependency updates', anvil=the anvil name. (2) Add UpdateWorkerStatus(id, status) to internal/state/db.go (mirrors UpdateWorkerLogPath pattern ~line 491-494) to mark it completed/failed when done. (3) Create a temp log file and assign its path to the worker's LogPath so the log tailer in Hearth can stream output into Activity Lines. (4) In each depupdate install function, also write to this log file (capture stdout+stderr and write summary lines). (5) Log db events for start/completion using db.LogEvent() with new event types e.g. 'depupdate_started', 'depupdate_completed', 'depupdate_failed'. The Hearth workers panel populates from db.ActiveWorkers() (data.go line 134-180) so inserting a worker record is sufficient for it to appear.

title: Hearth: U panel update commands corrupt TUI display (stdout not suppressed)
description: When triggering dependency updates via the U panel in Hearth, the subprocess output from npm/go/dotnet commands appears below the TUI, causing the panels to scroll upward and corrupting the display. Root cause: in internal/depupdate/npm.go, gomod.go, and dotnet.go, the install functions only capture cmd.Stderr into a buffer but leave cmd.Stdout unset, so it inherits the parent's stdout and leaks into the terminal behind the alt-screen TUI. Fix: add 'cmd.Stdout = io.Discard' (or capture to a buffer) after the 'cmd.Stderr = &stderr' line in each of the three install functions: InstallNpmGroup (npm.go ~line 29), InstallGoGroup (gomod.go ~lines 28 and 39 for go mod tidy), InstallDotnetGroup (dotnet.go ~line 42). The io package import should already be available or easily added.

title: Ledger: anvil-first navigation — show anvils top-level, beads per anvil, hide closed by default
description: Currently the Ledger loads all beads from all anvils at startup and shows them in a flat list. The user wants a hierarchical navigation model similar to Hearth's Queue column: top-level shows the list of anvils (with bead counts), and navigating into an anvil fetches and shows that anvil's beads. Closed beads should NOT be shown by default; there should be a keyboard shortcut (e.g. 'c') to toggle showing closed beads for the current anvil view. Changes needed: (1) Add a ViewAnvils mode to the ViewMode enum in ledger.go (currently ViewList/ViewKanban/ViewHierarchy around line 39-46). (2) Add anvilState struct with scrollViewport for navigating the anvil list. (3) Change Init() to start in ViewAnvils and only fetch beads when an anvil is selected (instead of FetchAllBeads for all anvils on startup - data.go lines 61-184). (4) showClosed defaults to false; 'c' key toggles it. (5) left/ESC from bead view returns to anvil list. (6) Update help text and key handling in ledger.go Update(). The current cycleAnvilFilter (line 235-257) and anvilFilter field can be replaced or repurposed.

title: Ledger: selecting bead with long detail panel scrolls list upward
description: When the right-side detail panel renders a bead with long content (long description, many notes), the left bead list scrolls upward unexpectedly. Root cause: the composite rendering in ledger.go View() uses lipgloss.JoinHorizontal to combine the list and detail panels. If the detail panel's word-wrapped content changes height, it may trigger AdjustViewport recalculations in the list's scrollViewport (internal/ledger/viewport.go), shifting the list's viewStart. Fix: ensure the detail panel is rendered with a strictly fixed height matching m.height, so its content changes never affect the list panel's layout. The render is around line 1456-1462 in ledger.go; the detail panel rendering is in internal/ledger/detail.go renderDetailPanel() and renderBeadDetailContent().

title: Hearth: UpdateAnvils never populated so U key always shows 'No anvils configured'
description:
hearth.Model.UpdateAnvils ([]depupdate.Anvil) is defined but never set in cmd/forge/hearth.go. NewModel takes only a DataSource and does not wire in the anvil config, so pressing U always triggers the 'No anvils configured for dependency updates' toast.

Fix: in cmd/forge/hearth.go, after model := hearth.NewModel(ds), build the UpdateAnvils slice from cfg.Anvils (same pattern as forge ledger does via ledger.NewModel(anvils, cfg.Anvils, db)) and assign it to model.UpdateAnvils before starting the tea.Program.

title: Ledger: add keybinding to switch between List/Kanban/Hierarchy views
description: ViewList, ViewKanban, and ViewHierarchy are all implemented in internal/ledger/ but there is no keybinding to switch between them. The user is stuck on ViewList (the default) with no way to enter kanban or hierarchy mode. Add a Tab or V key to cycle through views, consistent with the help overlay listing (Forge-hedw). Should show current view mode in the status bar.

title: Ledger: enable mouse support for scroll and click
description: The Ledger TUI has no mouse support. Hearth enables mouse with a toggle (M key) using tea.EnableMouseAllMotion/tea.DisableMouse. The Ledger should enable mouse scroll for the bead list and kanban lanes, matching Hearth's behaviour. The cmd/forge/ledger.go startup code needs to pass tea.WithMouseCellMotion() and the Model needs to handle tea.MouseMsg for scroll events.

title: Ledger: add event/error panel like Hearth live activity
description: Errors from bd commands (e.g. closed bead fetch timeouts, bd list failures) are currently swallowed or shown as rolling text with no persistent visibility. Hearth has a live activity + events panel on the right side. The Ledger needs a similar panel showing recent errors and operations so the user can see what's failing without grepping logs.

title: Ledger: bd list --status=closed times out on remote Dolt anvils
description:
FetchAllBeads calls 'bd list --status=closed --limit 0 --json' for each anvil. On anvils using remote Dolt via kubectl port-forward (e.g. forge, munin) this query times out because fetching all closed beads over a slow connection takes too long. The error rolls silently in the Ledger without surfacing to the user.

Fix options: add a --limit N to cap closed bead fetching (e.g. last 30 days), or use the same 60s timeout fix applied to depcheck. The --limit 0 flag means unlimited which is the problem for large databases.

title: Smelter: git push --force-with-lease fails for new batch branches
description:
When the smelter creates a fresh worktree for forge/warden-learn-batch/<anvil> (first run or after worktree was removed), the worktree has no remote tracking ref for that branch. git push --force-with-lease then treats 'expected remote state' as non-existent, but if the branch already exists on origin from a previous smelter run the push is rejected with exit status 1.

Fix: fetch the specific batch branch before pushing (git fetch origin forge/warden-learn-batch/<anvil>) so the tracking ref is populated, or replace --force-with-lease with --force since the smelter exclusively owns these branches and always resets them to origin/main before committing.

The worktree reuse path (CreateWithOptions when worktree already exists) does fetch via 'git fetch origin' so it works. Only the fresh-creation path is affected.

title: Tests: data layer, filter matching, tree building, Model init
description: Add test files covering: (1) bdExec mock — define a bdExecFunc type and inject it into the data layer for testing; (2) filter matching logic — table-driven tests for bead filtering predicates; (3) tree building — unit tests for epic/child tree construction; (4) basic Model init — verify tea.Model initialises without panics and produces non-empty View() output. Create files like internal/ledger/tui/data_test.go and model_test.go. This sub-task depends on all other sub-tasks being implemented first so the full surface area can be tested.

title: Periodic refresh with cursor state preservation
description: Add a 5-second tick to the TUI using tea.Tick. Introduce a 'refreshing bool' flag on Model to prevent concurrent fetches. After each refresh, restore the cursor to the previously focused bead by ID (not index) — store focusedBeadID string on Model and re-locate it in the updated bead list after refresh. Key additions: tickMsg type, refreshing guard, focusedBeadID field, and a helper findBeadIndexByID(beads []Bead, id string) int. This sub-task depends on the error toast sub-task for surfacing refresh failures.

title: Description viewer with glamour markdown rendering
description: Implement a 'd' key handler that opens a description viewer overlay/pane, following the pattern in internal/hearth/description.go. Use the glamour library to render markdown. Add a DescriptionModel or overlay state to the main Model. Wire the 'd' keybinding in the Update() method to fetch and display the focused bead's description field. Dismiss with 'q' or 'Esc'. This sub-task depends on the responsive layout sub-task for sizing the overlay correctly.

title: Error toasts & bd command failure handling
description: Add a toast/notification system to the TUI model struct (e.g. type Toast struct { msg string; kind string; expiry time.Time }). Wrap all bdExec calls so errors produce toast messages instead of panics. Display toasts as an overlay or status bar element in the View() method. Add a Tick-based timer to dismiss toasts after a few seconds. Key types: Toast, toastMsg (tea.Msg). This sub-task is a prerequisite for the periodic refresh sub-task which also needs toast-style error display.

title: Responsive layout & empty states
description: Modify the TUI layout logic (likely in internal/ledger/tui/ or similar) to enforce 80x24 minimum terminal size. Implement kanban lane degradation to 2 visible lanes on narrow terminals, and dynamic column width adjustment for list view. Add empty state message rendering for: 'No beads found', 'No beads match filter', 'No epics with children'. Key function: update the View() method and any layout calculation helpers to check terminal dimensions via tea.WindowSizeMsg. This is independent of other sub-tasks but its layout scaffolding is used by the description viewer sub-task.

title: depcheck dedup timeouts too short for remote Dolt anvils
description: bd list --status=open takes >20s on the munin anvil (remote Dolt via port-forward) but fetchBeadList only allows 15s, causing the dedup cache to always fail and bead creation to be skipped. fetchBeadShow has a 10s timeout for the same reason. Bump both to 60s/30s respectively.

title: Auto-close matching dependency beads after PR creation
description:
After forge update-deps creates a PR for an anvil, any open depcheck beads covering the same packages become stale and should be closed automatically. Without this cleanup, the queue fills with resolved work.

Implement func CloseMatchingDepBeads(anvilPath string, groups []UpdateGroup) error in internal/depupdate/pr.go (alongside CreatePR from Forge-z8sd). Run bd list --status=open --json in the anvil directory, parse the JSON, and for each open bead whose title matches a pattern like "Deps(npm): update <pkg>" (matching any package name in UpdateGroup.Packages), run bd close <id> --reason "Updated via forge update-deps". Called after CreatePR returns successfully.

title: PR creation via gh CLI
description:
After all dependency group commits and changelog fragments are written, forge update-deps needs to push a branch and open a single PR per anvil. This implements the CreatePR step that finalises each anvil's update run.

Create internal/depupdate/pr.go with func CreatePR(ctx context.Context, anvilPath, anvilName string, groups []UpdateGroup) (string, error). Steps: create or checkout branch deps/batch-update-<date>, push to remote, build a PR title and markdown body listing all updates grouped by category, shell out to gh pr create and return the PR URL. Called after Forge-cvh8's changelog commits are done. Its return value (PR URL) is passed to Forge-3cx3 for dep-bead auto-close.

title: Changelog generation for dependency updates
description:
The forge update-deps command creates commits per dependency group, but those commits need changelog fragments so the final PR meets project changelog requirements. This implements the GenerateChangelog step that runs after group commits and before PR creation.

Create internal/depupdate/changelog.go with func GenerateChangelog(anvilPath string, groups []UpdateGroup, isBilingual bool) error. Detect bilingual mode by checking for .en.md/.nb.md fragment files in changelog.d/. Generate a fragment named deps-batch-<date>[-technical.en.md/.nb.md or .md] with category: Changed header and bullet list of updated packages with old→new versions. Git-add and commit the fragments. Called from Forge-z8sd's PR creation flow after all group commits complete. Depends on the UpdateGroup type from Forge-6ilz.

title: Interactive selection prompts for update-deps command
description:
The forge update-deps command needs to offer interactive prompts after displaying the scan summary, so users can choose which dependency groups to apply. Without this, the command would either apply everything or nothing.

Extend the Cobra command in cmd/forge/updatedeps.go (from Forge-6ilz) to add a prompt after the scan output: "Update all? [a]ll / [p]atch+minor only / [s]elect groups / [n]o". If the user chooses 's', render a numbered list of groups and parse comma-separated input. Wire --patch-only and --no-major flags to pre-filter groups before prompting. Skip the prompt when --dry-run is set. Return the filtered []UpdateGroup slice for downstream tasks (changelog generation in Forge-cvh8, PR creation in Forge-z8sd).
close_reason: The implementation was already completed in commit `e5c5de2`. The `updatedeps.go` has all required flags (`--patch-only`, `--no-major`, `--dry-run`) and the interactive prompt wired via `depupdate.PromptSelection`. The `selector.go` implements the full `[a]ll / [p]atch+minor only / [s]elect groups / [n]o` flow with numbered group selection. The changelog fragment `changelog.d/Forge-uj67.md` exists and is properly formatted. The branch is up to date with origin.

title: Wire smelter into daemon on configurable schedule
description: Modify `internal/daemon/daemon.go` to start a goroutine that calls `smelter.Flush()` on a ticker driven by `smelter_interval`. Support hot-reload of the interval (re-create ticker when config changes). Only start if `smelter_enabled` is true; stop if toggled off. Depends on sub-tasks 2 (config) and 4 (smelter flush logic).

title: Implement smelter flush logic and PR creation
description: Create `internal/smelter/smelter.go` with a `Flush(ctx context.Context) error` function that: queries pending rules grouped by anvil, pulls latest main, reads/appends to `.forge/warden-rules.yaml` (with dedup by rule ID), commits with the specified message format, creates or force-pushes to `forge/warden-learn-batch` branch, creates/updates PR if needed, deletes flushed rules from DB, and logs `smelter_flushed`. Handle edge cases: merged PR → create new one, pull failure → skip anvil, 0 pending → no-op. Follow the depcheck skip pattern for pull failures. Depends on sub-task 1 (state CRUD).

title: Modify warden-learn to insert into pending table instead of creating PR
description: Modify `internal/warden/learn.go`: when `smelter_enabled` is true, call `state.InsertPendingRule(...)` instead of the current immediate-PR creation logic. title: Smelter: batch warden-learn rules into single PRs to avoid rebase conflicts
description:
## Feature

Add a batching system (the 'Smelter') for warden-learn rule updates. Instead of creating one PR per learned rule, accumulate rules in state.db and flush them into a single PR on a schedule.

### Problem
Each warden-learn creates a separate PR modifying `.forge/warden-rules.yaml`. With fast bead throughput, multiple PRs pile up and conflict with each other, causing endless rebase loops that waste time and resources.

### Solution

#### Storage: pending rules in state.db
New table:
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pending_warden_rules (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    anvil       TEXT NOT NULL,
    rule_yaml   TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_pr   INTEGER NOT NULL,
    created_at  TEXT NOT NULL
);
```

When warden-learn discovers new rules, instead of creating a PR immediately, insert them into `pending_warden_rules`.

#### Flush schedule
Run every 8 hours (configurable via `smelter_interval` setting, hot-reloadable). On flush:

1. Query all pending rules grouped by anvil
2. For each anvil with pending rules:
   - Pull latest main
   - Read current `.forge/warden-rules.yaml`
   - Append all pending rules
   - Commit: `forge: learn N warden rule(s) from PRs #X, #Y, #Z [no-changelog]`
   - Create/update PR (single branch per anvil: `forge/warden-learn-batch`)
   - If PR already exists and is open, force-push the updated branch
3. Delete flushed rules from pending table
4. Log event: `smelter_flushed` with count and anvils

#### Edge cases
- If the batch PR gets merged between flushes, create a new one on next flush
- If pull fails, skip that anvil (same pattern as depcheck)
- If there are 0 pending rules, skip entirely (no empty PRs)
- Dedup: don't add a rule if an identical rule ID already exists in the YAML file

### Config
```yaml
settings:
  smelter_interval: 8h    # how often to flush pending warden rules
  smelter_enabled: true    # toggle batching (false = old behavior, immediate PRs)
```

### Files
- `internal/smelter/smelter.go` — batch logic: accumulate, flush, PR creation
- `internal/state/db.go` — pending_warden_rules table + CRUD
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go` — start smelter goroutine on schedule
- `internal/warden/learn.go` — change to insert into pending table instead of creating PR
- `internal/config/config.go` — smelter_interval, smelter_enabled settings

### Migration path
When `smelter_enabled` is true (default), warden-learn inserts into pending table. When false, falls back to the current immediate-PR behavior. This lets you roll back if needed.

title: Update executors and verification: npm/dotnet/go install, temper verification, rollback on failure, and commit per group
description:
## Update Executors and Verification

Create the execution layer that installs packages, verifies builds, and handles rollback.

### Files
- `internal/depupdate/npm.go` — npm install executor
- `internal/depupdate/dotnet.go` — dotnet package update executor  
- `internal/depupdate/gomod.go` — go get executor

### npm executor
```go
func InstallNpmGroup(ctx context.Context, projectDir string, group UpdateGroup) error
```
- Runs `npm install pkg1@v1 pkg2@v2 ...` with ALL packages in the group at once
- Uses `executil.HideWindow` for Windows
- Returns error if install fails (peer dep conflict, network, etc.)

### dotnet executor
```go
func InstallDotnetGroup(ctx context.Context, projectDir string, group UpdateGroup) error
```
- For each package: `dotnet add <csproj> package <name> -v <version>`
- Find the right .csproj by searching for the package reference

### go executor
```go
func InstallGoGroup(ctx context.Context, moduleDir string, group UpdateGroup) error
```
- Runs `go get pkg1@v1 pkg2@v2 ...` then `go mod tidy`

### Verification
After each group install, run temper (build + lint + test):
```go
func VerifyGroup(ctx context.Context, anvilPath string, anvilConfig config.AnvilConfig) (*temper.Result, error)
```
- Uses existing `temper.DefaultConfigWithRace` + `temper.Run`
- Returns the temper result so caller can decide to commit or rollback

### Rollback
If install or verification fails:
```go
func RollbackGroup(ctx context.Context, anvilPath string) error
```
- Runs `git checkout -- .` to discard all changes
- Logs which group failed and why

### Commit
On success:
```go
func CommitGroup(ctx context.Context, anvilPath string, group UpdateGroup) error
```
- `git add -A` then `git commit -m "chore(deps): update <group-name> (<kind>)"`

title: Package grouper: peer-dep analysis via npm view and scope-based grouping logic
description:
## Package Grouper: peer-dep analysis and scope-based grouping

Create `internal/depupdate/grouper.go` that takes a flat list of outdated packages and groups related ones together so they can be installed atomically.

### Input
A slice of `ModuleUpdate` (from the existing depcheck scanners): Path, Current, Latest, Kind (patch/minor/major), Ecosystem (npm/nuget/go).

### Output
A slice of `UpdateGroup`:
```go
type UpdateGroup struct {
    Name     string         // e.g. 'tailwindcss ecosystem', 'vite ecosystem', 'standalone'
    Updates  []ModuleUpdate // packages in this group
    Kind     string         // worst-case kind: major > minor > patch
}
```

### Grouping strategies (applied in order)

**1. Peer dep groups (npm only)**
For each outdated npm package, run `npm view <pkg>@<latest> peerDependencies --json` and check if any peer dep is also in the outdated list. If so, merge them into one group.

Example: `@vitejs/plugin-react@6.0.1` has `peerDependencies: {"vite": "^8"}`. If `vite` is also outdated, group them together as 'vite ecosystem'.

Implementation:
- Shell out to `npm view <pkg>@<version> peerDependencies --json` for each outdated npm package
- Build an adjacency map: package A peers with package B
- Use union-find or simple transitive closure to merge connected packages into groups
- Cache npm view results to avoid repeated calls for the same package

**2. Scope groups**
Packages sharing an npm scope (e.g. `@tailwindcss/vite` + `@tailwindcss/postcss`) are grouped together. Extract scope from package name (`@scope/name` → `scope`).

**3. Standalone**
Any package not in a peer dep or scope group becomes its own single-package group.

### Group naming
- Peer dep groups: name after the 'root' package (the one others peer-depend on), e.g. 'vite ecosystem'
- Scope groups: name after the scope, e.g. '@tailwindcss packages'
- Standalone: just the package name

### Files
- `internal/depupdate/grouper.go` — GroupUpdates(updates []depcheck.ModuleUpdate) []UpdateGroup
- `internal/depupdate/grouper_test.go` — test peer dep merging, scope merging, standalone fallback

### Important
- Use `executil.HideWindow` for npm view calls (Windows compatibility)
- Timeout each npm view call (5s) — if it fails, treat the package as standalone
- NuGet and Go packages: only apply scope grouping (no peer dep concept), most will be standalone
- The grouper is called by the scan phase (Forge-6ilz) before display

title: Add forge update-deps command: direct dependency updates without smith
description:
## Feature

Add a `forge update-deps` CLI command that updates dependencies across all anvils directly — no smith, no beads, no AI cost. One PR per anvil bundling all updates.

### Why
The current depcheck creates individual beads per package, each consuming a full smith session (expensive). Dependency updates are mechanical (`npm install X@Y`) and don't need an AI agent.

### Command: `forge update-deps`

```bash
forge update-deps                    # Interactive: scan all anvils, show summary, confirm
forge update-deps --anvil hytte      # Single anvil
forge update-deps --patch-only       # Only patch updates (safest)
forge update-deps --no-major         # Skip major updates
forge update-deps --dry-run          # Show what would be updated without doing it
```

### Flow

1. **Pull latest** on each anvil (`git pull --ff-only`)
2. **Scan** using existing depcheck scanners (npm outdated, dotnet outdated, go list)
3. **Group related packages** automatically:
   - **Peer dep groups**: Check `npm view <pkg>@<version> peerDependencies --json`. If package A's new version peer-requires package B's new version, bundle them (e.g. vite 8 + @vitejs/plugin-react 6)
   - **Scope groups**: Same npm scope + same version bump (e.g. @tailwindcss/vite + @tailwindcss/postcss, @typescript-eslint/*)
   - Standalone packages that aren't in any group get their own single-package group
4. **Display summary table** per anvil:
   ```
   Anvil: hytte
   Group 1: tailwindcss ecosystem (patch)
     tailwindcss          4.2.1 → 4.2.2
     @tailwindcss/postcss 4.2.1 → 4.2.2
   Group 2: vite ecosystem (major)
     vite                    7.3.1 → 8.0.0
     @vitejs/plugin-react    5.1.4 → 6.0.1
   Group 3: standalone (minor)
     recharts              3.7.0 → 3.8.0
     lucide-react          0.576.0 → 0.577.0
   
   Update all? [a]ll / [p]atch+minor only / [s]elect groups / [n]o
   ```
5. **For each selected group**, atomically:
   - Create a feature branch: `deps/batch-update-<date>`
   - Run the install command with ALL packages in the group at once: `npm install pkg1@v1 pkg2@v2 ...`
   - If install fails (peer dep conflict), log and skip the group
   - Run temper (build + lint + test) to verify
   - If temper fails, rollback (`git checkout -- .`) and skip the group
   - If passes, commit with message: `chore(deps): update <group-name> (<type>)`
6. **Generate changelog fragments** automatically (both .en.md and .nb.md if the anvil uses bilingual changelogs, single .md otherwise)
7. **Create ONE PR per anvil** bundling all successful group commits
8. **Log results**: which groups succeeded, which failed and why

### NuGet support
Same grouping logic but using `dotnet add package X -v Y`. NuGet packages are less likely to have interdependencies but scope grouping still helps (e.g. OpenTelemetry.* packages).

### Go support
`go get pkg@version && go mod tidy`. Go modules handle transitive deps automatically so grouping is less critical.

### Integration with existing depcheck
- `forge update-deps` replaces the need for depcheck to create beads for routine updates
- Depcheck continues running on schedule for **detection and logging** (events in hearth)
- Consider adding a config option: `depcheck_create_beads: false` to disable bead creation when using the manual command
- Major updates that fail could optionally create a bead for manual investigation

### Hearth/Ledger integration
Add `U` keybinding in Hearth and Ledger that triggers `forge update-deps --interactive` or shows the dep summary in an overlay.

### Files
- `cmd/forge/updatedeps.go` — Cobra command, interactive prompts, summary display
- `internal/depupdate/depupdate.go` — Core logic: scan, group, install, verify, commit, PR
- `internal/depupdate/grouper.go` — Peer dep analysis + scope grouping
- `internal/depupdate/npm.go` — npm install execution
- `internal/depupdate/dotnet.go` — dotnet package update execution
- `internal/depupdate/gomod.go` — go get execution
- Reuses existing: `internal/depcheck/` scanners, `internal/temper/` for verification, `internal/vcs/` for PR creation
notes: IMPORTANT: After successfully updating packages, auto-close any open dep beads (Deps(npm)/Deps(NuGet)/Deps(Go)) that match the updated packages. Search bd list --status=open for beads with titles matching the package names and close them with --reason 'Updated via forge update-deps'. This prevents stale dep beads from lingering after manual updates.
close_reason: All sub-tasks implemented and merged: Forge-6ilz (scaffolding), Forge-qgfr (grouper), Forge-fgr7 (executors), Forge-caoo (PR creation/changelog). forge update-deps is fully functional.
