title: Bellows still flags CI as failed while checks are in progress (Forge-68vu fix insufficient)
description:
## Bug

Forge-68vu (PR #310) was supposed to fix bellows prematurely flagging CI as failed while checks are still running. The fix was merged but the issue recurred immediately:

```
10:21:57 ci_failed [Fhi.Metadata-wql3.8] PR #755 CI checks failed
```

...while CI was still running on PR #755.

### Prior fix
PR #310 attempted to fix this but the logic is still not correct. The check needs to be more thorough.

### Expected behavior
When ANY check run has `status != completed` (i.e. `queued`, `in_progress`, `waiting`, `pending`), bellows should treat the overall CI status as **pending** and skip the PR entirely until the next poll cycle. Only flag `ci_failed` when ALL checks are `completed` AND at least one has a non-success conclusion.

### Investigation
1. Check what PR #310 actually changed in `internal/bellows/bellows.go`
2. Look at how `CheckStatus()` or the GitHub API response is evaluated
3. The issue might be that GitHub returns a `status: completed, conclusion: failure` for one check while others are still `in_progress` — bellows sees the failed one and flags immediately without waiting for all to complete
4. Or the fix may have only addressed one code path but there's a second path that evaluates CI status

### Files
- `internal/bellows/bellows.go` — CI status evaluation
- `internal/vcs/github/github.go` — how check statuses are fetched

title: Depcheck npm scanner reports stale versions from node_modules instead of lock file
description:
## Bug

The npm depcheck scanner runs `npm outdated --json` which compares the *installed* version in `node_modules` against the latest on the registry. After `git pull`, `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are updated but `node_modules` is not, so `npm outdated` reports the old installed version as 'current'.

### Evidence
- hytte: tailwindcss was already at 4.2.2 in package.json/package-lock.json on main, but depcheck created a bead for 4.2.1 → 4.2.2 because node_modules still had 4.2.1

### Root cause

In `internal/depcheck/depcheck.go` `scanAnvil()`, git pull is run before scanning (line 125-140), but `npm install` is never run. The `npm outdated` command reads from `node_modules`, not `package-lock.json`.

### Fix

In `internal/depcheck/npm.go` `runNpmOutdated()` (or in `scanNpm()`), run `npm install --ignore-scripts` (or `npm ci --ignore-scripts`) in each npm project directory before running `npm outdated`. Use `--ignore-scripts` to avoid running build scripts — we only need the dependency tree synced.

Alternatively, consider parsing `package-lock.json` directly to get the 'current' version instead of relying on `npm outdated`, which would be faster and avoid the install step entirely.

### Files
- `internal/depcheck/npm.go` — `runNpmOutdated()` or `scanNpm()`

title: Bellows should not flag CI as failed while checks are still in progress
description:
## Bug

Bellows polls PR status and flags CI as failed even when checks are still running. This causes false `ci_failed` and `pr_needs_fix` events, and can trigger unnecessary cifix attempts.

### Evidence
- PR #748 (Fhi.Metadata-wql3.5): bellows logged `ci_failed` at 20:38:59 while CI was still running

### Root cause

In `internal/bellows/bellows.go`, the CI status check likely treats any non-passing state as failed. It should distinguish between:
- **in_progress** — checks still running, do nothing, check again next poll
- **completed + failure** — actually failed, trigger ci_failed
- **completed + success** — passing

### Fix

When evaluating CI check status from `vcs.CheckStatus()` or `vcs.FetchPRChecks()`:

1. If ANY check has `status: in_progress` (or `queued`/`pending`), treat the overall CI as **pending** — do NOT flag as failed
2. Only flag `ci_failed` when ALL checks are `completed` AND at least one has a non-success conclusion
3. Log a debug message when skipping due to in-progress checks so it's visible in the event stream

### Files to check
- `internal/bellows/bellows.go` — the CI status evaluation logic
- `internal/vcs/github/github.go` (or similar) — how check run statuses are fetched and interpreted
- Look at the `CheckRun` struct fields: `Status` (in_progress/completed/queued) vs `Conclusion` (success/failure/neutral/skipped)

title: Warden re-review: pass prior feedback so it only checks previously raised concerns
description:
## Problem

The Warden does a full independent review on every iteration — it has no memory of its prior feedback. This means:
1. It re-discovers the same issues it already raised
2. Smith fixes one thing but the fresh review finds new unrelated issues
3. This burns through all 5 iterations without converging

### Evidence
- Forge-mvqd: Warden rejected 4 times for the same structural concern, smith kept making it worse
- Hytte-ubp: Warden rejected 5 times, kept finding new nits (duplicate utility, emojis) each pass

## Solution

On re-review iterations (iteration > 1), pass the Warden its own prior feedback and instruct it to ONLY check whether those specific issues were addressed. No new findings unless they're regressions introduced by the fix.

### Implementation

#### 1. Pass prior feedback to `warden.Review()`

Add a `priorFeedback` parameter to `Review()` (or a new `ReviewWithContext()`):

```go
func Review(ctx context.Context, worktreePath, beadID, beadTitle, beadDescription, anvilPath string, db *state.DB, priorFeedback string, providers ...provider.Provider) (*ReviewResult, error)
```

#### 2. Modify `buildReviewPrompt()` for re-reviews

When `priorFeedback` is non-empty, change the prompt from a full review to a focused re-review:

```
You are re-reviewing a diff after the author addressed your previous feedback.

## Your Previous Feedback
<prior feedback summary + issues list>

## Your Task
1. Check ONLY whether each previously raised issue has been adequately addressed
2. For each issue, state: RESOLVED or STILL_PRESENT (with explanation)
3. If the fix introduced an obvious regression or bug, flag it — but do NOT raise new style nits, suggestions, or unrelated concerns
4. If all previous issues are resolved, approve

Respond with the JSON verdict block FIRST.
```

#### 3. Pipeline integration (`internal/pipeline/pipeline.go`)

The pipeline already captures warden feedback in `reviewResult.Summary` and `reviewResult.Issues`. Store this and pass it to the next warden call:

```go
// In the review loop, after a request_changes verdict:
priorWardenFeedback = formatWardenFeedback(reviewResult.Summary, reviewResult.Issues)

// On next iteration, pass to warden:
reviewResult, err = reviewWarden(ctx, wt.Path, p.Bead.ID, ..., priorWardenFeedback, providers...)
```

The first iteration (iteration == 1) always passes empty `priorFeedback` for a full review.

#### 4. Keep full review available

Add a config toggle `warden_full_rereview: false` (default: focused re-review). When true, reverts to current behavior of full review every iteration. This is a safety valve in case focused re-review misses real issues.

### Files to modify

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `internal/warden/warden.go` | Add `priorFeedback` param to `Review()`, modify `buildReviewPrompt()` for re-review mode |
| `internal/pipeline/pipeline.go` | Capture and pass prior warden feedback between iterations |
| `internal/config/config.go` | Add `warden_full_rereview` toggle |

### Expected impact

- Most beads that currently burn 3-5 iterations should converge in 2 (initial review + one fix pass)
- Saves 1-3 Claude/Copilot requests per bead on average
- Eliminates the 'whack-a-mole' pattern where each fix triggers new unrelated feedback

title: Reimporting workouts after delete fails with UNIQUE constraint on workout_laps
description:
## Bug

After deleting all workouts in Training, reimporting the same .fit files fails with 0 workouts imported.

### Error
```
476070571738693837.fit: insert lap 1: constraint failed: UNIQUE constraint failed: workout_laps.workout_id, workout_laps.lap_number (2067)
```

### Expected
Deleting all workouts and reimporting should work cleanly — all related data (laps, etc.) should be cascade-deleted or explicitly cleaned up.

### Likely Cause
The delete operation removes rows from the `workouts` table but does not clean up dependent rows in `workout_laps` (and possibly other child tables). When reimporting, the old lap rows still exist with the same workout_id + lap_number, causing the UNIQUE constraint violation.

### Investigation Steps
1. Check the delete logic — does it CASCADE or explicitly delete from child tables (`workout_laps`, etc.)?
2. Check if the SQLite schema defines `ON DELETE CASCADE` on the foreign key from `workout_laps.workout_id` → `workouts.id`
3. If no cascade, add explicit deletion of child table rows before/alongside workout deletion
4. Verify `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is set on the connection (SQLite has foreign keys OFF by default)

title: Add QuestGiver monitor with dedup bead creation on failure
description:
Create `internal/questgiver/questgiver.go` with the Monitor struct that polls anvils for quests and executes them, creating beads on failure with deduplication.

## Monitor struct
```go
type Monitor struct {
    db        *state.DB
    interval  time.Duration
    timeout   time.Duration
    anvils    map[string]string // name -> path
    logger    *slog.Logger
}
```

## Constructor
`func New(db *state.DB, interval, timeout time.Duration, anvils map[string]string) *Monitor`

## Run method
`func (m *Monitor) Run(ctx context.Context) error`

The Run method:
1. Runs on a ticker with `m.interval` duration
2. On each tick, iterates through `m.anvils`
3. For each anvil, calls `DiscoverQuests(anvilPath)` (from quest.go in same package)
4. For each discovered quest, creates an `adventurer.Executor` and calls `Execute(ctx, quest)`
5. Logs events to state DB (see event types below)
6. On failure: checks for duplicate bead, creates new bead if none exists
7. Logs `EventQuestgiverScanDone` after all anvils are processed
8. Respects ctx cancellation — exit cleanly when context is done

## Bead creation on failure
When a quest fails, create a bead using `bd create` CLI (same pattern as depcheck/vulncheck):

```go
title := fmt.Sprintf("E2E failure: %s — step %d (%s)", quest.Name, result.FailedStep, result.ErrorMessage)
```

Use `exec.CommandContext` with `bd create --title <title> --description <desc> --type bug --priority=1 --json`, set `cmd.Dir = anvilPath`, and call `executil.HideWindow(cmd)` before `cmd.CombinedOutput()`.

Description should include quest name, failed step number and action, error message, quest file path, and the command `forge quest run <name>` to reproduce.

## Deduplication (IMPORTANT — follow depcheck/dedup.go pattern)
Before creating a bead, check if one already exists:

1. Run `bd list --status=open --limit 0 --json` with `executil.HideWindow`, `cmd.Dir = anvilPath`, timeout 15s
2. Unmarshal JSON output into `[]struct{ Title string; Status string }` 
3. Check if any issue has title containing `"E2E failure: " + questName` AND status is "open" or "in_progress"
4. If a match exists, skip bead creation (log that duplicate was found)

Look at `internal/depcheck/dedup.go` for the exact pattern to follow.

## Event types to add to internal/state/db.go
Add these constants alongside the existing EventType constants:

```go
EventQuestgiverScanDone EventType = "questgiver_scan_done"
EventAdventurerStarted  EventType = "adventurer_started"
EventAdventurerPassed   EventType = "adventurer_passed"
EventAdventurerFailed   EventType = "adventurer_failed"
EventTestBeadCreated    EventType = "test_bead_created"
```

## Tests
Create `internal/questgiver/questgiver_test.go` with:
- Test that New() creates a Monitor with correct fields
- Test the deduplication logic (mock bd list output)
- Test Run() with a mock/fake executor (if feasible, or test individual methods)

See docs/plans/questgiver-adventurer.md for the full design.

title: Add internal/adventurer browser executor using Rod
description:
Create `internal/adventurer/adventurer.go` with a headless browser executor using the Rod library (go-rod/rod) for Chrome DevTools Protocol automation.

## Types

```go
type Result struct {
    QuestName    string
    Passed       bool
    Duration     time.Duration
    FailedStep   int           // -1 if all passed
    ErrorMessage string
    Screenshots  []string      // file paths to captured screenshots
    StepResults  []StepResult
}

type StepResult struct {
    Index    int
    Action   string
    Passed   bool
    Duration time.Duration
    Error    string
}

type Executor struct {
    timeout time.Duration
    logger  *slog.Logger
}
```

## Constructor
`func New(timeout time.Duration, logger *slog.Logger) *Executor`

## Execute method
`func (e *Executor) Execute(ctx context.Context, quest *questgiver.Quest) *Result`

This method:
1. Launches a headless Chrome browser via Rod (`rod.New().MustConnect()`)
2. Creates a new page
3. Iterates through quest.Steps, executing each action:
   - **navigate**: `page.Navigate(step.URL)` — navigate to the given URL
   - **fill**: `page.MustElement(step.Selector).MustInput(step.Value)` — find element by CSS selector and input text
   - **click**: `page.MustElement(step.Selector).MustClick()` — find element by CSS selector and click it
   - **wait**: `page.Timeout(step.Timeout).MustElement(step.Selector)` — wait for element to appear within timeout (use step.Timeout if set, otherwise use executor default timeout)
   - **assert**: `page.MustElement(step.Selector)` then check that element text contains step.Contains — fail if text does not contain expected string
   - **screenshot**: `page.MustScreenshot(path)` — capture screenshot and add path to result.Screenshots
4. For each step, record a StepResult with timing and pass/fail
5. On first failure, stop execution, set FailedStep to the failed step index, set ErrorMessage, and return
6. If all steps pass, set Passed=true and FailedStep=-1

## Important implementation details
- Use `rod.New().ControlURL(launcher.New().Headless(true).MustLaunch()).MustConnect()` for headless mode
- Handle context cancellation gracefully — clean up browser on ctx.Done()
- Use defer to ensure browser.Close() is always called
- Use non-Must variants internally and convert errors to StepResult.Error strings for robustness
- If Chrome is not installed, return a Result with Passed=false and appropriate ErrorMessage (do not panic)
- Add `go-rod/rod` to go.mod via `go get github.com/go-rod/rod`

## Tests
Create `internal/adventurer/adventurer_test.go` with:
- Test that New() creates an Executor with correct timeout
- Test Result and StepResult struct construction (unit test, no browser needed)
- Integration test (can be skipped in CI) that navigates to a known URL if Chrome is available

See docs/plans/questgiver-adventurer.md for the full design.

description:

2. `DiscoverQuests(anvilPath string) ([]Quest, error)` — globs `<anvilPath>/.forge/quests/*.yaml`, calls ParseQuest for each match, returns all parsed quests. If the quests directory does not exist, return an empty slice (not an error).

```yaml
  - action: click

  - action: assert

```

title: Add warden_model_override and schematic_model_override config settings
description:
## Summary

Add two new string fields to SettingsConfig so users can route Warden and Schematic stages to cheaper Copilot models (e.g., claude-haiku-4-5 at 0.33x premium) while keeping Smith on a stronger model (claude-sonnet-4-6 at 1x). This can reduce review-stage costs by ~67%.

**Reference:** docs/plans/copilot-request-reduction.md -- Strategy 3

## Implementation

### File: internal/config/config.go

Add two new fields to SettingsConfig:

```go
type SettingsConfig struct {
    // ... existing fields ...
    WardenModelOverride    string `mapstructure:"warden_model_override" yaml:"warden_model_override"`
    SchematicModelOverride string `mapstructure:"schematic_model_override" yaml:"schematic_model_override"`
}
```

### File: internal/pipeline/pipeline.go

Add helper methods that clone the provider list and override the model for Copilot entries:

```go
func (p *Pipeline) wardenProviders() []provider.Config {
    if override := p.Config.Settings.WardenModelOverride; override != "" {
        cloned := make([]provider.Config, len(p.Providers))
        copy(cloned, p.Providers)
        for i, pv := range cloned {
            if pv.Kind == provider.Copilot {
                cloned[i].Model = override
            }
        }
        return cloned
    }
    return p.Providers
}

func (p *Pipeline) schematicProviders() []provider.Config {
    if override := p.Config.Settings.SchematicModelOverride; override != "" {
        cloned := make([]provider.Config, len(p.Providers))
        copy(cloned, p.Providers)
        for i, pv := range cloned {
            if pv.Kind == provider.Copilot {
                cloned[i].Model = override
            }
        }
        return cloned
    }
    return p.Providers
}
```

Use wardenProviders() when spawning Warden and schematicProviders() when spawning Schematic, instead of passing p.Providers directly.

### File: docs/configuration.md

Document the new settings:

```yaml
settings:
  smith_providers: ["copilot/claude-sonnet-4-6"]   # 1x for code generation
  warden_model_override: claude-haiku-4-5           # 0.33x for review
  schematic_model_override: claude-haiku-4-5        # 0.33x for analysis
```

Note: these overrides only apply to Copilot provider entries in the chain. Non-Copilot providers are left unchanged.

### Tests

Add tests in internal/pipeline/pipeline_test.go:
1. wardenProviders() returns overridden model for Copilot entries when override is set
2. wardenProviders() returns original providers when override is empty
3. Non-Copilot providers are not modified even when override is set
4. Same tests for schematicProviders()

## Config Format

```yaml

  warden_model_override: claude-haiku-4-5
  schematic_model_override: claude-haiku-4-5
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- WardenModelOverride and SchematicModelOverride fields added to SettingsConfig with proper mapstructure tags
- wardenProviders() and schematicProviders() helpers clone the provider list and override Copilot model
- Only Copilot provider entries are modified; other providers are untouched
- Warden and Schematic spawning code uses the new helpers

title: Skip Schematic phase when primary provider is Copilot
description:
## Summary

When the first provider in the chain is Copilot (provider.Copilot), skip the Schematic phase unless the bead is explicitly tagged "decompose". Copilot charges per-request (not per-token), so the Schematic pre-analysis is an extra premium request that may not justify its cost. This saves 1 premium request per large bead.

**Reference:** docs/plans/copilot-request-reduction.md -- Strategy 2

## Implementation

### File: internal/pipeline/pipeline.go

Modify the schematic decision logic. Add or refactor a shouldRunSchematic(providers []provider.Config) bool method:

```go
func (p *Pipeline) shouldRunSchematic(providers []provider.Config) bool {
    if !p.SchematicConfig.Enabled {
        return false
    }
    // Skip schematic for Copilot to save a premium request,
    // unless the bead explicitly needs decomposition
    if len(providers) > 0 && providers[0].Kind == provider.Copilot && !p.Bead.HasTag("decompose") {
        p.Logger.Info("skipping schematic for Copilot provider to save premium request")
        return false
    }
    return p.beadExceedsWordThreshold() || p.Bead.HasTag("decompose")
}
```

Key points:
- Check providers[0].Kind == provider.Copilot (first provider in chain)
- If bead has "decompose" tag, always run schematic regardless of provider
- Log a message when skipping so operators can see why schematic was bypassed

### Tests

Add a test in internal/pipeline/pipeline_test.go covering:
1. Copilot provider skips schematic (no decompose tag)
2. Copilot provider runs schematic when bead has "decompose" tag
3. Non-Copilot provider runs schematic normally when enabled
4. Schematic disabled in config always skips regardless of provider

## Acceptance Criteria

- Schematic phase is skipped when providers[0] is Copilot and bead lacks "decompose" tag
- Schematic phase runs when bead has "decompose" tag regardless of provider
- Non-Copilot providers are unaffected
- Info-level log message emitted when skipping
- Tests pass

title: Integrate ingot lifecycle tracking into pipeline.Run()
description:
Integrate ingot lifecycle tracking into the pipeline so every bead processed through pipeline.Run() gets a corresponding ingot record tracking its full journey.

GitHub Discussion: #222
Reference: docs/plans/ingots.md
Depends on: Forge-czem (internal/ingot package)

## What to change

Edit internal/pipeline/pipeline.go to create and update ingot records at each stage transition within Run():

1. **After worktree creation** -- call ingot.InsertIngot with status "init", setting BeadID, Anvil, Title, Branch, WorkerID from the pipeline context.

2. **Before Smith** -- call ingot.UpdateIngotStatus(beadID, anvil, "smith")

3. **Before Temper** -- call ingot.UpdateIngotStatus(beadID, anvil, "temper")

4. **After Temper completes** -- call ingot.UpdateIngotTemperResults with the overall pass/fail, first failed step name, and total duration. Then iterate over temper's StepResults and call ingot.InsertTestResult for each one, mapping the temper StepResult fields to TestResult fields (step_name, command, exit_code, duration_ms, passed, optional, output truncated to ~1000 chars for output_summary).

5. **Before Warden** -- call ingot.UpdateIngotStatus(beadID, anvil, "warden")

6. **After Warden approves** -- call ingot.UpdateIngotStatus(beadID, anvil, "approved")

7. **After PR creation** -- call ingot.UpdateIngotPR(beadID, anvil, prNumber, prURL, prID) and then ingot.UpdateIngotStatus(beadID, anvil, "pr_open")

8. **On any failure that aborts the pipeline** -- call ingot.UpdateIngotStatus(beadID, anvil, "failed")

## Important constraints

- All ingot writes must be **best-effort**: wrap each call, log any error, but never fail the pipeline because of an ingot write error. The pipeline must work identically if ingot writes fail.
- Get the *sql.DB handle from the state.DB that is already available in the pipeline context (check how other state writes work in pipeline.go).

title: Add internal/ingot package with schema, types, and CRUD operations
description:
Create a new internal/ingot/ package that provides the data model and persistence layer for Ingots -- compound records that bundle a bead, PR, worker lifecycle, and structured test results into a single queryable record.

GitHub Discussion: #222
Reference: docs/plans/ingots.md

## 1. Create internal/ingot/ingot.go

Define these types:

```go
type Status string

const (
    StatusInit     Status = "init"
    StatusSmith    Status = "smith"
    StatusTemper   Status = "temper"
    StatusWarden   Status = "warden"
    StatusApproved Status = "approved"
    StatusPROpen   Status = "pr_open"
    StatusPRMerged Status = "pr_merged"
    StatusFailed   Status = "failed"
    StatusStalled  Status = "stalled"
)

type Ingot struct {
    ID               int
    BeadID           string
    Anvil            string
    PRID             *int       // FK to prs.id, NULL until PR created
    WorkerID         string
    Status           Status
    TemperPassed     bool
    TemperFailedStep string
    TemperDurationMs int
    PRNumber         *int       // GitHub PR number
    PRURL            string
    Title            string
    Branch           string

}

type TestResult struct {
    ID             int
    IngotID        int
    StepIndex      int
    StepName       string

    ExitCode       int
    DurationMs     int
    Passed         bool
    Optional       bool
    OutputSummary  string     // first ~1000 chars or key errors
    FullOutputPath string
    RecordedAt     time.Time
}
```

## 2. Create internal/ingot/db.go

Implement CRUD methods that operate on *sql.DB (follow the same patterns used in internal/state/db.go):

- InsertIngot(db *sql.DB, ingot *Ingot) error -- insert a new ingot row, set CreatedAt/UpdatedAt to now
- UpdateIngotStatus(db *sql.DB, beadID, anvil string, status Status) error -- update status and updated_at
- UpdateIngotTemperResults(db *sql.DB, beadID, anvil string, passed bool, failedStep string, durationMs int) error -- update temper_passed, temper_failed_step, temper_duration_ms, updated_at
- UpdateIngotPR(db *sql.DB, beadID, anvil string, prNum int, prURL string, prID int) error -- update pr_number, pr_url, pr_id, updated_at
- GetIngot(db *sql.DB, beadID, anvil string) (*Ingot, error) -- fetch single ingot by (bead_id, anvil) unique constraint, eager-load TestResults
- GetIngotsByStatus(db *sql.DB, status Status, limit int) ([]Ingot, error) -- list ingots filtered by status
- InsertTestResult(db *sql.DB, tr *TestResult) error -- insert a test result row
- GetTestResults(db *sql.DB, ingotID int) ([]TestResult, error) -- fetch all test results for an ingot ordered by step_index

Look at internal/state/db.go for the database handle pattern (the state.DB struct wraps *sql.DB). Match whatever approach is used there.

title: Reduce smith re-exploration on warden feedback iterations
description:
On iteration 2+ (after warden requests changes), smith spawns fresh with no memory of what it read or changed. The prompt's PriorFeedback section is buried at the very bottom after AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, and there is no instruction to skip re-exploration. Smith spends 10-30 tool calls re-reading every file it already visited in iteration 1 before touching the specific 2-3 issues the warden flagged.

Root cause: 
- Smith has no memory of prior iteration's work
- Prompt template puts feedback at the bottom — generic 'investigate and implement' instructions come first
- No explicit directive to skip codebase re-exploration on iteration 2+

Fix plan (three parts):

1. **Include the previous iteration diff in the prompt (BeadContext.PriorDiff)**
   - Add PriorDiff string field to prompt.BeadContext (prompt.go)
   - In pipeline.go, after smith completes on iteration N and warden rejects, compute:
     git diff <preSmithSHA>..HEAD (preSmithSHA is already captured for hasEmptyDiff)
   - Truncate to ~8000 chars and set beadCtx.PriorDiff for iteration N+1
   - Include it in the prompt template under a 'What was already implemented' section
   - Also pass it to buildFixPrompt fallback
   
2. **Add 'skip re-exploration' directive for iteration 2+**
   - In the prompt template, when PriorFeedback is set, add an explicit instruction:
     'The diff above shows exactly what you changed in your previous iteration.
      Go directly to the files listed in the feedback. Do NOT re-read unrelated files,
      do NOT re-explore the codebase — the rest of the implementation is correct.'
   - This single instruction should eliminate the bulk of wasted tool calls

3. **Move feedback/diff to the top of the prompt for iteration 2+**
   - When Iteration > 1, restructure the prompt so the task starts with:
     'ITERATION 2 FIX: these specific issues need to be addressed' (and the diff)
   - The generic bead description and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md follow after, as lower-priority context
   - Currently the feedback is the very last thing smith reads, so it starts exploring before even seeing what needs fixing

Observable: the example showed smith running ls, find, grep, reading 15+ files (router.go, db.go, handlers.go, config.go, module.go, Sidebar.tsx, App.tsx) before fixing 3 lines in Infra.tsx. With the diff + directive, smith should open Infra.tsx in the first 1-2 tool calls.

title: Live Activity: newest-at-bottom, no [tool] label, per-tool blank lines, drop [result]
description:
Four UX improvements to the Live Activity panel:
1. Flip scroll direction so new items arrive at the BOTTOM like a terminal (oldest-at-top, newest-at-bottom). Auto-follow keeps cursor at bottom as new lines arrive.
2. Remove the literal [tool] prefix label. Color tool lines in colorInfo (muted blue) instead so they stand out without a noisy tag.
3. Insert a blank line between every tool call (currently only inserted on type transitions, making consecutive tools look bundled).
4. Drop [result] entries (session-end markers) — they appear at the top on startup and stay the whole session, adding no useful info (event log already shows completion).

title: hasEmptyDiff incorrectly fires when smith commits and pushes
description:
The hasEmptyDiff check in pipeline.go uses git diff @{upstream}...HEAD to detect when smith made no changes. But smith is instructed to commit AND push, so after it runs, @{upstream} == HEAD and the diff is always empty — falsely triggering the needs_human escalation even when smith produced real commits.

Fix: record HEAD sha before spawning smith (git rev-parse HEAD), then after smith completes compare git diff <saved-sha>..HEAD. If no new commits were added, the diff is empty and escalation is correct. If new commits exist, smith did real work.

Observed: Hytte-tsi iteration 2 smith committed "fix: zone 5 min HR must be above threshold" but was still escalated to needs_human because @{upstream}...HEAD was empty after the push.

title: Live Activity: remove grouping, flow text like Claude Code terminal
description:
The Live Activity panel currently groups entries into collapsible [text]/[think]/[tool] buckets with expand/collapse headers (▸/▾). This is noisy and unnatural. Claude Code terminal output just flows as continuous lines with blank line separators between logical blocks — which reads much better.

## What to remove
- All grouping logic: buildActivityGroups(), collapseActivityGroup(), expandActivityGroup(), activityGroup struct
- Group header items (isGroupHeader, activityNavItem.groupType)
- activityExpanded map and expand/collapse key bindings
- rebuildActivityNav() grouping — replace with a flat list of lines directly
- [text] and [think] prefixes on lines (they add noise without the group context)

## What to keep/improve
- [tool] entries stay — tool name + summary on one line is useful
- Thinking block lines: keep dimStyle rendering (dim/italic) to distinguish them visually, just without the group wrapper
- Tool result enrichment (→ ✓ / → ✗)

## How it should look
Like `claude` CLI terminal output: text lines flow continuously, blank line between logical blocks (between a tool call and the next text block, between thinking and text, etc.). The panel scrolls within its fixed height — content never overflows/expands the panel boundary.

## The overflow bug
When a think block is expanded and contains many lines, the panel currently grows downward past its allocated height instead of scrolling within it. This is because wordWrap() multiplies the visible line count but the viewport height calculation (maxVisible = height - 4) does not account for wrapped lines. The rendered line count must stay within the panel height at all times — extra lines should be scrollable, not overflow.

title: Duplicate bellows workers appear in Hearth for same bead/PR
description:
Hearth Workers panel shows two bellows entries for the same bead simultaneously:

  bellows   Forge-q0qp              forge   7m26s
  bellows   Forge-q0qp (PR#273)     forge   1m0s

One entry has no PR number, one has PR#273. Both are for the same bead. This suggests either:
1. A stale bellows worker record is not being cleaned up from state.db when a new one starts, or
2. The bellows monitor is registering two worker rows for the same PR — one when it starts monitoring and another when it detects the PR number

Check InsertWorker / UpdateWorkerPhase calls in the bellows/lifecycle path to ensure only one worker row exists per bead+PR combination at any time. The Hearth workers query should also deduplicate on (bead_id, anvil, phase) if multiple rows exist.

title: On startup, close beads whose PRs are already merged in state.db
description:
When the daemon restarts, bellows only fires EventPRMerged for status transitions it witnesses in real-time. If a PR merges during the restart window, or if handleBeadCloseOnMerge failed before the restart, the bead is never closed.

On daemon startup (after bellows initialises), scan for PRs in state.db with status=merged where the corresponding bead is still in_progress in beads DB. Close those beads via bd close.

This is the startup-time equivalent of handleBeadCloseOnMerge — a catch-up pass for any merges that were missed. Should run once at startup, after a short delay (e.g. 30s) to let bellows finish its first poll cycle.

Observed: Hytte-enj PR #60 merged at 11:35:25 during a daemon restart; bead stayed in_progress indefinitely.

title: Auto-pull origin/main before creating worktree for new bead
description:
When Forge creates a git worktree for a new bead, it branches off the current local main. If local main is behind origin/main, the smith works from stale code and risks conflicts when pushing.

Fix: in worktree.Create() (internal/worktree/), do a `git fetch && git merge --ff-only origin/main` on the anvil's main branch before branching for the new worktree. If the fast-forward fails (local changes or diverged), log a warning but proceed rather than blocking work.

This ensures every new bead starts from the latest upstream code, not whatever was last pulled manually.
close_reason: Not needed — worktree.Create() already does git fetch origin and branches from origin/main, so smiths always start from latest remote code

title: Schematic hits MaxTurns without emitting JSON verdict

Schematic spent 8+ minutes investigating code (Forge-hp1h) then hit MaxTurns without ever emitting the required JSON verdict, resulting in schematic_skipped. Smith then completed the same bead in 140s.

The fix should ensure schematic reliably emits the JSON verdict before exhausting its turn budget. Options:
1. Inject a 'you MUST output JSON now' reminder into the system prompt when turns remaining is low (e.g. <= 2 turns left)
2. Reserve the final turn for output-only (no tool calls) so it's forced to emit JSON
3. Strengthen the existing prompt reminder to always emit JSON before stopping

The schematic prompt already has a JSON output requirement but Claude apparently got absorbed in investigation mode (reading files, following code paths) without ever transitioning to output mode.

Files to look at:
- internal/schematic/schematic.go — the Run() function and prompt construction
- The MaxTurns / turn counting mechanism used by the AI session

title: [bug] Orphan recovery races with post-merge bead close
description:
Race between handleBeadCloseOnMerge and RecoverOrphanedBeads causes bead to reset to open after PR merges.

Timeline:
1. PR merges - bellows marks PR status=merged in state.db (not open anymore)
2. handleBeadCloseOnMerge fires async, calls bd close (takes time)
3. Orphan recovery runs, HasOpenPRForBead returns false (merged != open)
4. Bead still in_progress in beads DB (bd close not done yet)
5. Orphan recovery declares it orphaned, resets to open

The orphanMinAge guard (5 min on bead.UpdatedAt) does not protect here because the bead was first claimed at iteration 1, well before the merge.

Observed: Forge-6nrm PR #264 merged 08:54:23, bead_recovered 08:56:00.

Fix: extend HasOpenPRForBead to also return true for PRs with status=merged updated within the last N minutes (e.g. 10 min). This gives handleBeadCloseOnMerge a grace window before orphan recovery can falsely declare the bead orphaned.

title: Hearth: Warden re-review, Approve as-is, and Force smith actions for Needs Attention beads
description:
Add three new resolution actions to the Needs Attention menu in Hearth, each backed by a new IPC command and daemon handler:

1. Warden re-review — re-run warden on the existing worktree branch as-is. Useful when warden was too strict, rules have changed, or smith was right that the issues are already resolved. If warden approves, proceed to PR creation normally.

2. Approve as-is — bypass warden entirely and create a PR from the current branch state. The user has manually reviewed and is satisfied. Skips the warden loop and calls vcs.CreatePR directly.

3. Force smith — push smith into another review iteration on the same branch, keeping the existing warden feedback attached. Optionally accept a user note to prepend to the prompt (e.g. 'these issues are real, please actually fix them').

Files to change:
- internal/ipc/ipc.go: add WardenRerunPayload, ApproveAsIsPayload, ForceSmithPayload structs
- internal/daemon/daemon.go: add IPC handlers for 'warden_rerun', 'approve_as_is', 'force_smith' commands
- internal/hearth/hearth.go: add ActionWardenRerun, ActionApproveAsIs, ActionForceSmith to ActionMenuChoice enum; add menu labels; add OnWardenRerun/OnApproveAsIs/OnForceSmith callbacks; wire up in executeAction and daemon startup

title: Strip NO_CHANGES_NEEDED from smith review-iteration prompts; escalate to needs_human on empty diff
description:
Two related fixes for the warden review loop:

1. NO_CHANGES_NEEDED is semantically 'the original bead work was already done before I started'. It makes no sense as a response to warden feedback. Strip the signal from the smith prompt when iteration > 1 so smith cannot emit it during review iterations.

2. Without NO_CHANGES_NEEDED, smith may make no code changes but still complete successfully. Warden would then re-review identical code and reject again — infinite loop until max iterations. Fix: after smith completes in a review iteration (iteration > 1), check the git diff against the branch's previous commit. If the diff is empty (no changes made), skip warden and mark the bead needs_human with reason 'Smith made no changes in response to warden feedback (iteration N)'.

Files to change:
- internal/prompt/prompt.go: in the review-iteration prompt block, remove the NO_CHANGES_NEEDED instruction and example
- internal/pipeline/pipeline.go: after smith completes in a review iteration, run git diff to detect empty output; if empty set outcome.NeedsHuman=true with the above reason instead of proceeding to warden

title: Failsafe: mark decomposed parent with forge-decomposed label to prevent re-dispatch
description:
When a decomposed parent bead has dependents, maybeCloseDecomposedParent keeps it open (so dependents stay blocked). When those dependents eventually complete, the parent becomes unblocked and gets re-dispatched — but there is no work left to do (the children were the work).

Fix: when keeping a decomposed parent open, add a 'forge-decomposed' label to it. Schematic detects this label and returns ActionSkip with a 'already decomposed' reason. The pipeline, seeing ActionSkip on a forge-decomposed bead, sets NoChangesNeeded=true so the daemon closes it cleanly without spawning smith or wasting tokens.

Changes needed:
- internal/daemon/daemon.go: in maybeCloseDecomposedParent, call labelAdder to add 'forge-decomposed' when keeping open
- internal/schematic/schematic.go: in ShouldRun or early in Run, detect 'forge-decomposed' label and return ActionSkip
- internal/pipeline/pipeline.go: on ActionSkip, check for 'forge-decomposed' label and set outcome.NoChangesNeeded=true

title: [bug] Auto-learn warden rules: quote YAML values containing colon-space to prevent parse errors

The go-yaml library's Marshal with yaml.Style can help, or pre-process values before writing.

title: Re-request Copilot review after reviewfix pushes fixes
description:
After burnish (reviewfix) pushes fixes and resolves comment threads, Copilot doesn't always re-review automatically despite the repo setting being enabled. The trigger seems inconsistent:

- After burnish push (resolves threads + pushes): Copilot often does NOT re-review
- After cifix push (pushes without resolving threads): Copilot DOES re-review

Possible cause: resolving threads before/during the push confuses the auto-review trigger. GitHub may see 'no unresolved threads' and skip the auto-review.

IMPORTANT: Do NOT re-request a full Copilot review via the API — this causes an endless loop where Copilot finds new issues on each full review pass. The fix must only trigger Copilot to re-check the specific resolved threads, not do a full review.

Investigation needed:
- Does the order of thread resolution vs git push matter?
- Should burnish push first, then resolve threads (so Copilot sees new push + unresolved threads)?
- Is there a GitHub API to trigger a partial/incremental re-review?
close_reason: Investigated — burnish already pushes before resolving threads. Copilot auto-re-review trigger is inconsistent on GitHub's side, not a forge bug. Kept as reference.

title: Bellows: auto-close bead when deferred-close PR merges
description:
When the pipeline defers bead close due to DependentCount > 0 (line 1681 in daemon.go), it logs 'deferring close until PR merges'. But nobody actually closes the bead after the PR merges — bellows only updates PR status and completes workers, it never calls bd close.

Fix: in the bellows EventPRMerged handler, after updating PR status, check if the bead should be closed (the original pipeline deferred it). Call bd close with reason 'PR merged'.

This only applies to beads whose close was deferred — beads without dependents are closed immediately by the pipeline.

title: Schematic: add sequential dependencies between decomposed children
description:
When schematic decomposes a bead into ordered sub-tasks, it creates them all independently with no dependencies between them. The forge then dispatches them in random order, which fails when later tasks depend on earlier ones' code.

The schematic prompt already asks the AI to order sub-tasks logically. The daemon should use that ordering to add deps:
- Child N+1 depends on child N (sequential chain)
- Or: the AI could indicate which children can be parallel vs sequential in its output

Implementation:
- internal/daemon/daemon.go applyDecomposedOutcome: after creating children, add bd dep add between consecutive children
- Optionally: let the schematic output specify parallel groups (children in the same group have no deps between them, but the group depends on the previous group)
- Simplest first: just chain them sequentially since the AI already orders them

title: Hearth: rich Live Activity display matching Claude Code terminal output
description:
The Live Activity panel currently shows minimal parsed entries like '[tool] Read {"file_path":...' and '[text] first 3 lines...'. Upgrade it to match the Claude Code terminal experience:

## Current vs Desired

**Current:**
```
▸ [tool] x5 — Read, Edit, Grep
  [tool] Read {"file_path":"/c/source/fhigit/Forge/in...
  [text] Fixed. The issue was that...
  [think] Let me check the bellows code...
```

**Desired (Claude Code style):**
```
  Read internal/bellows/bellows.go (lines 250-270)
  Edit internal/bellows/bellows.go
    - old: 'if strings.HasPrefix(pr.BeadID, "ext-") {'
    + new: 'if strings.HasPrefix(pr.BeadID, "ext-") && !pr.BellowsManaged {'
  Bash: go build ./cmd/forge/
    (exit 0)
  Grep: pattern='BellowsManaged' path=internal/state
    3 matches
  Write changelog.d/Forge-bellows-seed.md (new file)

  Fixed. The issue was that bellows already cached the snapshot...
```

## Implementation scope

1. **Richer tool call formatting** (data.go parseWorkerActivity):
   - Read: show file path + line range, not raw JSON
   - Edit: show file path + old/new snippet (truncated)
   - Bash: show command description or command itself + exit code from tool_result
   - Grep: show pattern + path + match count from result
   - Write: show file path + (new file) or (updated)
   - Glob: show pattern + match count
   - Agent: show description

2. **Tool results** (currently ignored):
   - Parse tool_result events and correlate with tool_use by tool_use_id
   - Show exit codes for Bash, match counts for Grep, success/error for Edit

3. **Better text/thinking display**:
   - Show more than 3 lines when expanded (configurable or fill available height)
   - Markdown-lite rendering (bold, code spans) via lipgloss styles
   - Dim thinking blocks vs normal text

4. **Streaming feel**:
   - Tail the log file incrementally instead of re-reading the whole file each tick
   - Show partial text as it arrives (content_block_delta events)

## Files to modify
- `internal/hearth/data.go` — parseWorkerActivity: richer formatting, tool result correlation
- `internal/hearth/hearth.go` — renderWorkerActivity: styling improvements
- `internal/hearth/hearth.go` — groupActivityLines: smarter grouping (group by turn, not just consecutive type)

## Complexity
This is a medium-large feature. The tool call formatting (step 1) is the biggest win for relatively low effort. Tool result correlation (step 2) and streaming (step 4) are more complex.

title: Depcheck: skip .worktrees directory and add cross-project dedup for npm
description:
The depcheck scanners (npm, NuGet, Go) walk the entire anvil directory tree but don't skip the .worktrees directory. Since each worktree is a full copy of the repo, this causes:
- npm: scanning 9 copies of client/package.json → 80 'outdated' packages instead of ~9
- NuGet: scanning 4 copies of the .sln → inflated counts (partially mitigated by cross-project dedup added in c995ee4)
- Go: potentially scanning worktree copies of go.mod

Fix:
1. Add '.worktrees' to the skip list in findNpmProjects(), findDotnetProjects(), and scanGo's file discovery
2. Add cross-project seen map to scanNpm (matching the NuGet fix in c995ee4)
3. Also skip 'bin', 'obj' directories in findNpmProjects for consistency

title: Fix install.sh checksum verification matching multiple lines
description: The install script's grep pattern for checksum verification matches both the archive and its .sbom.json file, causing a multi-line EXPECTED_HASH and false SHA256 mismatch. Fix: anchor grep to match the exact filename at end of line. See GitHub issue #240.

title: Support 'no changes needed' as valid Smith outcome — close bead without PR
description:
Currently when Smith produces no diff, Warden hard-rejects and the bead is released back to open as needs_human. But sometimes no changes ARE the correct outcome (e.g. the fix is already implemented, the issue was already resolved upstream).

Smith should be able to signal 'no changes needed' via a NO_CHANGES_NEEDED: <reason> output marker (analogous to the existing NEEDS_HUMAN: marker). When detected:
1. Pipeline skips Warden and Temper entirely
2. Daemon closes the bead via bd close --reason=<reason>
3. No PR created, no bellows monitoring needed
4. A dedicated event (bead_no_changes) is logged

Implementation:
- internal/pipeline/pipeline.go: Add ExtractNoChangesNeeded() parser (like ExtractNeedsHuman), add NoChangesNeeded+NoChangesReason to Outcome struct, check after Smith completes but before Warden
- internal/daemon/daemon.go: Handle outcome.NoChangesNeeded by calling closeBead with the reason instead of marking needs_human
- internal/state/db.go: Add EventNoChangesNeeded event constant
- internal/prompt/: Update Smith prompt to document the NO_CHANGES_NEEDED marker so Smith knows it can use it
- Changelog fragment required

title: Log rate-limit backoff expiry time to event log
description: When a bead hits rate limiting, the daemon logs a warning to daemon.log with the backoff duration but nothing appears in the event log (forge history events). Users have no visibility into when the bead will be retried. Fix: log an event with the expected retry time (e.g. 'Hytte-toa rate limited, will retry at 22:47') so it's visible in hearth and forge history events.

title: Docs update
description: We need to update all our docs to reflect all our latest changes. Be sure to catch them all, claude.md agents.md as well. And the example forge.yaml must be updated to include all available options.

title: Schematic: propagate parent labels to decomposed children
description: When Schematic decomposes a parent bead into children, the children don't inherit the parent's labels (e.g. forgeReady). This causes children to show as 'Unlabeled' in the Queue panel and prevents auto-dispatch when auto_dispatch is set to 'tagged'. Root cause: the Schematic decomposition code creates children via bd create but doesn't pass --add-label for the parent's labels. Fix: after decomposition, copy the parent bead's labels to each child bead.
close_reason: Not a code bug — crucible children should not be labeled for auto-dispatch; the crucible manages them internally

title: Hearth: Actions styling improvement
description: The text in the actions windows are all together with no space around them, no line breaks, and I can't breathe when I look at it. If needed we can increase the size of that window to accomomdate more space

title: Pipeline retry should reset worktree from a clean branch when previous run pushed bad commits
description:
When a pipeline run fails and the bead is auto-recovered (bead_recovered event), the next dispatch inherits the existing pushed branch. If the previous run accumulated bad commits (e.g. deleted unrelated files, made unintended changes), the retry starts dirty and is unlikely to succeed.

Observed in Forge-e50w: two full pipeline runs, 37 USD in API calls, Gemini made unrelated deletions to .goreleaser.yml (UPX/SBOM blocks), .github/workflows/release.yml, and deleted two other beads' changelog fragments. Tests never passed.

Desired behaviour: when the daemon auto-recovers a bead and re-dispatches, it should detect that a worktree branch already exists (origin/forge/<bead-id>) and either:
(a) reset it to the fork point (main) before spawning Smith, or
(b) create a fresh worktree branch (e.g. forge/<bead-id>-2) to avoid inheriting stale commits.

This prevents cascading junk commits and wasted API spend on hopeless retries.

title: Anvil event logging
description: We should remove the eventlogs from anvils (these 16:46:15 poll Polled anvil: heimdall (1 ready)). Instead we should show all our anvils somewhere else - I suggest in the Queue-panel, since we already show them there. We could have some color-coding or icon or something to indicate if the last poll was successful or not (so we know when our dolt db is unreachable for example, or if there are other issues with the anvils)

title: Fully stop a bead functionality
description: We should have some way to stop processing a bead, we can kill the worker, but it'll start up again - I want a shortcut or action or something on a bead where I can say 'stop further processing' It should remove the label, put the bead back to open, and prevent the forge from starting it, unless I put the label back on
notes: I guess this is the clarify? forge queue clarify or whatever it's calleld?

title: Hearth: dedicated PR panel with actions (view, fix comments, resolve conflicts, review, close)
description:
Add a dedicated panel in the Hearth TUI for managing open pull requests, accessible via a keyboard shortcut or as a new panel in the layout.

The panel should list all open PRs across all anvils and provide action options for each:
- Fix Comments — run reviewfix on the selected PR
- Resolve Merge Conflicts — run rebase worker on the selected PR
- Re-request Review — trigger warden review
- Close PR — close the PR
- Open in browser — open the GitHub PR URL

Discussion points:
- Could be a new panel in the existing three-column layout (e.g. alongside Ready to Merge)
- Or a keyboard shortcut (e.g. 'p') that opens a full-screen overlay similar to the log viewer, with a searchable list

Data source: state.db prs table + gh CLI for live status

title: Warden: validate diff against bead description to catch scope drift
description: The Warden currently reviews the diff in isolation — it checks correctness, standards, and safety but has no knowledge of what the bead actually asked for. This means a Smith could produce a technically correct diff that doesn't address the original issue, and the Warden would approve it. Pass the bead title and description into the Warden review prompt so it can add a 6th check: 'Does this diff actually implement what the bead requested?' This would catch scope drift, partial implementations, and cases where the Smith went off on a tangent.

title: Hearth: prompt user when recovering orphan worker beads instead of auto-reopening
description: When the daemon detects orphan workers (beads with no active worker), it currently auto-sets them back to open status and re-dispatches. This is wrong when the work was already completed — e.g. a PR was merged but the bead wasn't closed, or the work was discarded intentionally. Instead, show a popup/dialog in Hearth asking the user what to do with each orphan bead. Options: (1) Recover — reopen to open status and re-queue for work, (2) Close — mark as done (work already completed/merged), (3) Discard — close with reason, won't be retried, (4) Inspect — open the PR/branch to check status before deciding.

title: Hearth: mouse click support prevents text selection/copy
description: After adding mouse click support for panel navigation in Hearth TUI, users can no longer select text in the terminal. This breaks the ability to copy bead IDs, error messages, PR URLs etc. from the dashboard. Need to find a way to support both panel click navigation and text selection — possibly by only capturing mouse clicks in specific regions, or using a modifier key (e.g. Shift+click for selection), or toggling mouse capture with a keybind.

title: Notify webhooks when PR is ready to merge
description: Add a new pr_ready_to_merge notification event that fires when a PR passes CI and warden approval (enters the Ready to Merge state in Hearth). Send both Teams Adaptive Card and generic JSON webhook payload. The generic payload should include anvil, bead ID, PR number, PR URL, and PR title. Add to the EventType constants in notify.go and wire it up in the daemon where PRs transition to the ready-to-merge state. Also add pr_ready_to_merge to the config events filter documentation.

title: Smith logs are destroyed when worktree is cleaned up
description: When a pipeline fails or completes, the worktree is removed (pipeline.go:221 defer removeWorktree), which destroys all smith logs stored in .workers/<bead>/.forge-logs/. This makes post-mortem debugging impossible. Logs should be preserved outside the worktree (e.g. in ~/.forge/logs/<bead>/) before cleanup, or the worktree cleanup should copy logs to a persistent location first.

title: Release: notify webhooks on new release
description: Add a release notification event that fires when a new Forge version is published. Two delivery paths: (1) GitHub Actions step in the release workflow that curls configured webhook URLs from GitHub Secrets, and (2) a new 'forge notify release' CLI command that the release script can call after tagging. Payload includes version, tag, release URL, changelog summary. This feeds into the generic webhook system (Forge notifications bead) so both Teams and custom webhooks (like Hytte dashboard) receive release announcements.

title: Notifications: support multiple webhook targets beyond Teams
description:
Extend the notification system to support generic webhook targets alongside the existing Teams Adaptive Card integration. Config structure:
notifications:
  teams:
    webhook_url: 'https://teams...'
    events: [bead_failed, daily_cost]
  webhooks:
    - name: hytte-dashboard
      url: 'https://hytte.app/api/webhooks/forge'
      events: [pr_created, worker_done, release]
    - name: slack
      url: 'https://hooks.slack.com/...'
      events: [bead_failed]
Each webhook gets a simple JSON payload (not Adaptive Cards) with event_type, bead_id, anvil, message, timestamp. The Teams webhook keeps its Adaptive Card format. Add a new 'release' event type that fires when the release workflow completes (triggered via GitHub Actions webhook to the forge daemon, or a new release-notify CLI command).

title: Add Linux/macOS install script to releases
description:
Create an install.sh script at the repo root that downloads and installs the latest Forge release binary on Linux and macOS. This enables one-liner installation:

  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Robin831/Forge/main/install.sh | bash

Features (reference implementation: TonyHopland/ForgeDevContainerTemplate/.devcontainer/forgeinstall.sh):
- Detect OS (linux/darwin) and arch (amd64/arm64)
- Fetch latest release from GitHub API (or specific version via VERSION env var)
- Download the matching zip asset from GoReleaser
- Verify SHA256 checksum against checksums.txt
- Extract binary to ~/bin (configurable via INSTALL_DIR)
- Skip if already at latest version
- Advise on PATH if ~/bin not in PATH
- Run forge version to verify

Also update the GoReleaser config and release description template to include the install command. This enables devcontainer and CI/CD usage as well.

title: Bug: PR titles sometimes describe incidental fixes instead of bead intent
description: When the smith creates a PR, the title sometimes reflects a secondary fix discovered during implementation rather than the bead's actual purpose. Example: Forge-cqc6 asked for 'show PR title in Ready to Merge action menu' but the PR title was 'fix(hearth): guard against negative contentWidth slice index in merge menu'. The actual feature was implemented correctly — the title is just wrong. The PR title generation in ghpr.Create or the smith's commit message should be anchored to the bead title/description rather than letting the smith pick what it considers most interesting. Check how the PR title is generated — is it from the smith's commit message or from prompt.Builder? The title should default to the bead title with the bead ID suffix, similar to how crucible child PRs are titled.

title: Bug: decomposed flag clears retry record even when no children created
description: When schematic runs on a bead with the decompose label but chooses 'plan' instead of 'decompose', the pipeline sets outcome.Decomposed=true. The daemon then calls ClearRetry (daemon.go:1306) which wipes the retry record. If the smith subsequently fails or the bead gets closed without producing children or a PR, there's no needs_human record in the retries table, so the bead never appears in Needs Attention. It silently disappears. Fix: only treat outcome.Decomposed as successful if actual child beads were created. If no children exist after decomposition, the retry record should be preserved so the bead surfaces in Needs Attention.

title: Hearth: show PR title in Ready to Merge action menu and match queue action size
description: The action menu that opens when pressing Enter on a Ready to Merge item doesn't show the PR title, making it unclear which PR you're acting on. Add the PR title to the action menu header, similar to how the Queue action menu shows the bead title. Also increase the action menu dimensions to match the Queue action menu size for visual consistency.

title: Bug: orphan recovery resets beads that have active crucibles
description: The orphan recovery scan runs periodically and resets in_progress beads back to open when no matching worker row exists. But crucible parent beads are in_progress without a direct worker row — the crucible tracks them via crucibleStatuses sync.Map instead. This causes a race: the crucible claims the parent bead (in_progress), orphan recovery sees no worker, resets to open, and the bead gets re-dispatched or re-enters the queue after the crucible already completed and created a PR. Fix: orphan recovery should check the crucibleStatuses map before resetting a bead. If a crucible is actively running for that bead ID, skip it. The relevant code is in internal/daemon/daemon.go (orphan recovery) and the crucibleStatuses sync.Map.

title: PR titles and descriptions should be in English
description: When the forge creates PRs from beads with Norwegian descriptions, the PR title and body end up in Norwegian with broken characters (aa for å, o for ø). The forge should always write PR titles and descriptions in English regardless of the bead's language. The bead description can be included as-is for context, but the PR summary and title should be translated/written in English by the smith or during PR creation.

title: Address Copilot review comments on PR #166 (crucible child failure fix)
description:
PR #166 (Forge-flf0) was merged with 3 unresolved Copilot comments on internal/crucible/crucible.go. All are relevant:

1. Line 227: markChildNeedsHuman sets LastError to 'crucible child failed:...' but the daemon dispatch loop only skips needs_human rows matching 'circuit breaker:%' prefix. The child will still be re-dispatched standalone. Fix: use circuit breaker prefix in the LastError, or update the daemon to filter all needs_human=1 rows.

2. Line 670: markChildNeedsHuman discards the DB.UpsertRetry error. If the write fails, the bead is reset to open but not marked needs_human — immediately eligible for standalone dispatch again. Fix: handle and log the error.

3. Line 670: UpsertRetry with a partially-populated struct overwrites the entire row, clearing existing retry counters (dispatch_failures, retry_count). Fix: load existing record first, update only NeedsHuman and LastError, then upsert.

title: Schematic: detect crucible orchestration mode from parent+children context
description:
Extend the schematic pre-analysis to detect the relationship type between a parent bead and its children when running in crucible context. This determines HOW the crucible orchestrates the work.

## Three Modes

1. **sequential** — Parent has its own implementation work. Children depend on the parent's changes being in place first, and potentially on each other. Run parent through the pipeline first on the feature branch, then children in topological order. Each must complete before the next starts.

2. **orchestrator** — Parent is a container/coordinator with no code work of its own. Children are independent pieces that together fulfill the parent's goal. Run children only (current crucible behavior). Could potentially be parallelized in the future.

3. **standalone** — Not a crucible candidate at all (single bead, no children). Current normal pipeline path. Schematic already handles this with plan/decompose/clarify.

## Approach

When a crucible-candidate bead enters schematic, build an extended prompt that includes:
- The parent bead's full details (ID, title, description)
- Each child bead's title and description (fetched via bd show)
- Ask the schematic to determine the orchestration mode

New schematic verdict field: \ (sequential | orchestrator) — only present when bead has children.

For 'sequential' mode, schematic also produces a plan for the parent bead's own work.
For 'orchestrator' mode, schematic may optionally reorder/validate the children.

## Prompt Design

The prompt should explain the distinction clearly:
- If the parent describes concrete implementation work and children extend/depend on it → sequential
- If the parent describes a goal/feature and children are the breakdown → orchestrator
- Signal: Does the parent's description contain file paths, API changes, architectural decisions that need to be coded? → sequential
- Signal: Is the parent's description a summary/umbrella with children covering all the actual work? → orchestrator

## Integration

- schematic.go: new \ function
- schematic verdict struct: add \ field
- crucible.go: call schematic with crucible context before starting children
- Forge-cv0b depends on this for knowing when to run parent-first
close_reason: Schematic now runs a crucible check: inspects parent+children to decide orchestration vs standalone. No epic type required.

title: Crucible: support parent-runs-first mode for beads with own work
description:
Currently the Crucible treats the parent bead as a pure orchestrator — it creates a feature branch, sequences children through the pipeline, and closes the parent when done. But some parent beads have their own implementation work that children depend on.

The Crucible should support both modes:
1. **Parent-has-work**: Run the parent bead through the full pipeline (smith → temper → warden) on the feature branch FIRST, commit its changes, then sequence children on top. Each child builds on the parent's work.
2. **Orchestrator-only** (current behavior): Parent is just a container/coordinator. Only children get smith runs.

**Detection approach**: Run the parent through schematic before starting children. If schematic returns 'plan' (substantive work exists), execute parent-runs-first mode. If schematic returns 'skip' or 'decompose', use the current orchestrator-only flow. This leverages existing infrastructure without needing labels or type conventions.

**Implementation notes**:
- In crucible.Run(), after creating the feature branch, run schematic on the parent bead
- If plan returned: run parent through pipeline on the feature branch, commit results
- Then proceed with children as normal (they'll build on parent's committed work)
- Update crucible status/panel to reflect parent phase (e.g. 'parent' before '1/N children')

title: Crucible: NoDiff children should not pause the sequence
description: When a Crucible child produces no code changes (NoDiff=true from Warden), the pipeline marks it as failed and the Crucible pauses the entire sequence. But some children are check-only tasks (e.g. 'Check outdated API packages') where no diff is the expected outcome — they just investigate and write notes.\n\nThe Crucible should handle NoDiff children by closing them and continuing to the next child, rather than pausing the whole epic. The pipeline Outcome already has the NoDiff flag available for the Crucible to check.
close_reason: Fixed: NoDiff children now close and continue instead of pausing the Crucible

title: Hearth: Live Activity group expansion/scrolling broken
description:
The grouped events in the Live Activity panel have several issues:
1. Scrolling doesn't work properly within groups
2. Groups cannot be expanded/collapsed
3. Some AI output renders on top of other content

The other panels use a shared scrollable viewport component that works correctly - Live Activity should use the same approach.

title: Warden: provider-specific verdict parsing for Claude/Copilot/Gemini
description: The warden currently uses extractJSON to parse a structured verdict from the review agent's output. When Copilot (Haiku) is used as the warden provider, it may not output the expected JSON structure, causing a fallback to 'approve' with 'Could not parse structured verdict'. Each provider may format its verdict differently. Add provider-aware parsing so the warden can extract verdicts reliably regardless of which AI backend produced the review.

title: Hearth Live Activity: group events by type and show more text
description: The Live Activity panel lists [tools][think][rate][text] events sequentially which is noisy. Group consecutive events of the same type under collapsible headers that auto-expand as new types are discovered. Also increase the text preview from 1 line to 3-4 lines so operators can see more of what the smith is actually thinking/doing.

title: Hearth usage panel — per-provider cost/token/request display
description:
Add a compact usage panel below the Workers column in the Hearth TUI. The Workers column currently spans full height; split it using renderStackedColumn() (same pattern as right column's LiveActivity+Events split). The usage panel shows today's running totals per CLI tool:

Layout (compact, ~6-8 lines):

- Gemini: daily_costs table (input_tokens + output_tokens) — format with k/M suffixes
