title: Copilot output format: switch from PlainText to StreamJSON (JSONL)
description: Copilot CLI now supports --output-format json which emits JSONL events similar to Claude's stream-json. Currently Forge treats copilot as PlainText format, meaning no token extraction or structured output parsing. Update provider.go Format() to return StreamJSON for copilot, update copilotArgs() to pass --output-format json instead of -s/--silent, and verify readStreamJSON can parse copilot's JSONL events (field names may differ slightly from Claude — investigate and adapt). This enables token counting and cost estimation for copilot runs.

title: Hearth Queue: show all anvils even when empty (0)
description: When grouping by anvil, anvils with no open/ready beads are hidden. They should still appear with (0) so the operator knows the repo is registered.

title: Release notes: install instructions + categorized changelog
description: GoReleaser release body should include install instructions and changelog categorized as Features/Bug Fixes/Other Changes instead of raw PR list. Update .goreleaser.yml to use release_notes file and release-forge.ps1 to generate it.

title: Set has_pending_reviews on PR creation instead of waiting for bellows poll
description: When a PR is created via ghpr.Create and inserted into the state DB, has_pending_reviews defaults to 0. This causes the PR to briefly appear in the Ready to Merge panel until the next bellows poll detects the pending review requests (e.g. Copilot auto-review). Fix: after inserting the PR, immediately call ghpr.CheckStatus to get reviewRequests and update has_pending_reviews in the DB before the pipeline returns. This closes the race window between PR creation and the first bellows poll.

title: PowerShell install script for downloading Forge from GitHub releases
description:
Create install.ps1 in the repo root that can be run via:

  irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Robin831/Forge/main/install.ps1 | iex

The script should:
1. Detect OS/arch (Windows amd64 is the primary target)
2. Fetch the latest release tag from GitHub API (https://api.github.com/repos/Robin831/Forge/releases/latest)
3. Download the matching zip archive
4. Extract the forge binary to a sensible location (e.g. ~/bin or AppData/Local/Forge)
5. Add to PATH if not already there (user-level PATH on Windows)
6. Verify checksum against checksums.txt from the release
7. Print the installed version
8. If Forge is already installed, update by overwriting the binary
9. Skip download if already on the latest version

Keep it simple and self-contained — no dependencies beyond PowerShell.

title: Release script: release-forge.ps1 for tagging and publishing releases
description:
Create release-forge.ps1 that automates the release process. Usage: .\release-forge.ps1 0.1.0

The script should:
1. Validate the version argument (semver format)
2. Ensure working tree is clean (no uncommitted changes)
3. Ensure we are on main branch
4. Run 'forge changelog assemble' to collect changelog.d fragments into CHANGELOG.md
5. Commit the assembled CHANGELOG.md and cleared changelog.d fragments
6. Create a git tag v<version>
7. Push the commit and tag to origin
8. Print a message that the GitHub Actions release workflow will take it from here
9. Optionally open the GitHub Actions page to watch progress

This script lives in the repo and is NOT a forge subcommand — it is an operator action for repo maintainers only.

title: Hot-reload: support adding and removing anvils without daemon restart
description: Currently adding or removing anvils in forge.yaml requires a daemon restart. The poller reads d.cfg.Load() each cycle so it would see new anvils, but bellows and depcheck monitors are initialized with a fixed anvilPaths map at startup. The hot-reload callback should update bellows monitor paths and depcheck scanner paths when anvils change. The applyChanges function already detects anvil count changes but only logs a warning.

title: Hot-reload: fsnotify loses watch on forge.yaml after file replacement
description: On Windows, when forge.yaml is edited by tools that replace the file (write temp + rename), fsnotify loses the watch and no further changes are detected. The config reload event never fires and no 'Configuration reloaded' event appears in Hearth. Need to re-add the watch after Create events, or use a directory watch instead of a file watch.

title: Per-anvil depcheck toggle to disable automatic dependency update scanning
description:
Currently depcheck_interval is a global setting that applies to all anvils. Some repos (like heimdall and munin) already have bead formulas that handle dependency updates in coordinated PRs, so automatic depcheck creates duplicate noise.

Add a per-anvil `depcheck_enabled` bool pointer to AnvilConfig (following the existing pattern used by `schematic_enabled`, `golangci_lint`, and `go_race_detection`). When nil, depcheck runs as normal (opt-out). When set to false, the depcheck monitor skips that anvil entirely.

Implementation:
1. Add `DepcheckEnabled *bool` field to `AnvilConfig` in config.go
2. Update the depcheck monitor loop to check this field before scanning an anvil
3. Update docs/configuration.md with the new per-anvil setting

title: Auto-run warden learn after PR merges to build review rules from Copilot comments
description:
The warden learn command (forge warden learn) currently has to be invoked manually. It should run automatically after a PR is merged — bellows already monitors merged PRs, so it's the natural place to trigger this.

After bellows detects a PR merge, it should:
1. Fetch Copilot review comments from the merged PR
2. Group and distill them into rules (if there are any)
3. Save new rules to .forge/warden-rules.yaml in the anvil
4. Create a PR with the updated rules file (similar to how depcheck creates PRs for dependency updates)
5. Log the event (e.g., warden_rule_learned)

The rules file should be checked into the repo so Warden picks it up in worktrees. The PR approach keeps it reviewable — the user can see what rules were learned and reject bad ones.

This creates a feedback loop: Copilot reviews code → Forge learns the patterns → Warden checks for them in future reviews → fewer repeated issues.

title: Bellows: don't mark PR as ready-to-merge while reviews are pending
description:
When a PR is created, it may have automatic review requests (e.g., GitHub Copilot). Currently bellows moves the PR to the Ready to Merge panel as soon as CI passes, even if there are pending review requests that haven't been completed yet.

Bellows should check for pending reviews via the GitHub API (gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/reviews or gh pr view --json reviews,reviewRequests) and only mark a PR as ready to merge when:
1. CI checks have passed
2. No review requests are pending (all requested reviews are either approved or not required)

This prevents premature merging when auto-requested reviewers like Copilot haven't finished their review yet.

title: Crucible: support feature type beads with children, not just epics
description: IsCrucibleCandidate and lookupEpicBranch filter on issue_type=='epic', but feature-type beads can also have children and should be eligible for crucible orchestration. The check should be based on whether a bead has children (Blocks), not its type. Affected code: poller/epicbranch.go IsEpicBead(), lookupEpicBranch() and poller/crucible.go ResolveBlocks().

title: Temper: detect Node projects in subdirectories (e.g. web/package.json)
description: Temper's detectSteps() only checks for package.json at the worktree root. Hybrid projects like Hytte have Go at root and Node in web/. Temper should detect package.json in common subdirectories (web/, frontend/, client/) and run npm lint/build with the correct working directory.

title: Queue action
description: When selecting an action for the beads in queue, and hitting enter, for example the Label bead action, it takes 3-5 seconds for the action window to close and anything to actually happen. I expect when I click enter to have immediate response

title: Doc update
description: Go through all our documentation, and fix it up with all our current features. Revise the readme.md to reflect what we can now do. Go through agents.md, claude.md and copilot-instructions.md and make sure it's up to date

title: Hearth: Crucible panel or Queue integration to show orchestrated epic progress
description:
When a Crucible is running (parent bead with children being orchestrated on a feature branch), there's no visibility into its progress in the Hearth TUI.

## Options

### Option A: Dedicated Crucible Panel
A new panel (in the left column with Queue/Ready to Merge/Needs Attention) showing:
- Active Crucibles with parent bead title
- Feature branch name
- Progress bar or fraction: 'Children: 3/6 merged'
- Current child being worked on (with Smith status)
- Status: running / paused (child failed) / final PR / complete
- Enter action: expand to show all children and their statuses

### Option B: Queue Integration
Show Crucibles as a new section in the Queue panel (like Ready/Unlabeled/In Progress):
- 'Crucible' section header
- Each Crucible shows parent title, progress, current child
- Expandable to see child list

### Recommendation
Option A (dedicated panel) is cleaner — Crucibles are a different workflow from individual beads and deserve their own space. But if panel real estate is tight, Option B works.

### Data Source
The Crucible dispatcher emits events (crucible_started, crucible_child_merged, etc.) and should also expose state via IPC so the Hearth can query:
- Active Crucibles list
- Per-Crucible: parent bead, feature branch, children with statuses, current phase
- Add a new IPC command: \ that returns this data

### Actions
- Pause/Resume a Crucible
- Skip a failed child and continue
- Retry a failed child
- View the feature branch PR

title: Forge: epic/feature branch support for multi-bead work
description:
Currently the Forge creates each bead's branch from main and PRs back to main. For dependent work (like the depcheck epic with 6 related beads), this breaks because child beads need code from parent beads that haven't merged yet.

## Design: Epic Branches

### Concept
An epic bead can define a `base_branch` (e.g. `feature/depcheck`). All child beads automatically:
1. Branch from the epic branch instead of main
2. Create PRs targeting the epic branch instead of main
3. Merge into the epic branch as they complete

When the epic is done, a final PR goes from the epic branch → main with all the accumulated work.

### Implementation

#### 1. Epic detection
When the Forge picks up a bead, check if it has a parent epic (via dependencies or a new `epic` field). If the parent epic has a `base_branch`, use that as the branch base instead of main.

#### 2. Worktree changes
`worktree.Create()` currently always branches from main/origin. Add a `baseBranch` parameter so epic children branch from the epic branch.

#### 3. PR targeting
`ghpr.Create()` takes a `Base` parameter (currently hardcoded to 'main'). Pass the epic branch as base for child beads.

#### 4. Epic lifecycle
- When an epic bead is picked up, create the feature branch from main (no code changes, just the branch)
- Child beads work on the epic branch
- When all children are done (all merged into epic branch), create final PR to main
- Bellows monitors the final PR normally

#### 5. Beads integration
Option A: Use bd's epic support (`bd epic`) — child beads know their parent epic
Option B: New field in forge.yaml or bead metadata: `epic_branch: feature/depcheck`
Option C: Convention — if a bead depends on another bead that has a branch, use that branch as base

### Key files to modify
- `internal/worktree/worktree.go` — add baseBranch parameter
- `internal/ghpr/ghpr.go` — CreateParams.Base already exists, just wire it
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go` — dispatch logic to detect epic children
- `internal/pipeline/pipeline.go` — pass base branch through
- `internal/poller/poller.go` — possibly surface epic info from bd

### Edge cases
- Epic branch conflicts with main (periodic rebase or merge from main)
- Child bead fails — don't block the epic, skip and continue
- Parallel children — multiple smiths working on same epic branch need coordination (sequential dispatch per epic)

title: Depcheck: refactor existing Go dependency updater into depcheck package
description:
The current Go dependency update logic (which produced PR #105) should be extracted into the new depcheck package as `internal/depcheck/go.go`. This ensures all ecosystems share the same dedup logic, scheduling, and bead creation patterns.

Move/refactor:
- Go update detection logic → depcheck.scanGo()
- Integrate with shared DedupCheck before creating beads  
- Wire into depcheck.Scanner.ScanAll() alongside dotnet/npm scanners

title: Depcheck: npm dependency scanning
description:
Add npm dependency scanning to the depcheck package.

Detection: Walk anvil for package.json files (skip node_modules, .workers directories).
Scanning: Run `npm outdated --json` in each package.json directory.
Parsing: Extract package name, current, wanted, latest versions from JSON output.
Grouping: Combine minor/patch updates into single bead. Major bumps get individual beads.
Handle monorepos: scan each package.json independently, report subdirectory path.
Graceful degradation: skip if npm not installed.

title: Depcheck: .NET/NuGet dependency scanning
description:
Add NuGet dependency scanning to the depcheck package.

Detection: Walk anvil for *.csproj or *.sln files (skip bin/obj directories). 
Scanning: Run `dotnet list package --outdated --format json` (requires .NET 8+ SDK).
Parsing: Extract package name, current version, available version from JSON output.
Grouping: Combine minor/patch updates into single bead per project. Major bumps get individual beads.
Handle multi-project repos: scan each *.csproj independently, report subdirectory path.

title: Depcheck: deduplication — check existing beads and PRs before creating update beads
description:
Before the depcheck scanner creates a bead for a dependency update, it must check:

1. `bd list --status=open --json` + `bd list --status=in_progress --json` — search for beads with matching package name in title/description
2. Open PRs in state DB — check if any open PR's bead references the package
3. Recently closed beads (last 7 days) — avoid re-creating beads that were just intentionally closed

Use consistent title convention `Deps(<ecosystem>): update <package> <old> → <new>` for reliable dedup matching.

Shared function: `DedupCheck(ctx, anvilPath, packageName, ecosystem) bool` usable by all ecosystem scanners.

title: Depcheck: multi-language dependency update scanner
description:
Create a new depcheck package that scans anvils for outdated dependencies across multiple ecosystems and creates beads for updates.

## Design

### Ecosystem Support
Walk each anvil directory to find project markers and scan each:
- **Go**: Find go.mod → run `go list -m -u -json all` → parse for available updates
- **.NET (NuGet)**: Find *.csproj/*.sln → run `dotnet list package --outdated --format json`
- **npm**: Find package.json (skip node_modules) → run `npm outdated --json`

Multi-project repos (e.g. Heimdall with api/ dotnet + client/ npm) are handled by discovering ALL project roots and scanning each, tagged with subdirectory path.

### Deduplication (critical)
Before creating a bead for any update, check:
1. Open/in_progress beads — `bd search` or `bd list --status=open --json` filtered for the package name
2. Open PRs — query prs table for beads referencing the package
3. Use consistent title format: `Deps(<ecosystem>): update <package> <old> → <new>` for reliable matching

### Architecture
Mirror the vulncheck pattern:
- `internal/depcheck/depcheck.go` — Scanner struct, ScanAll(), RunScheduled()
- `internal/depcheck/go.go` — Go-specific scanning
- `internal/depcheck/dotnet.go` — .NET/NuGet scanning  
- `internal/depcheck/npm.go` — npm scanning
- `internal/depcheck/dedup.go` — shared deduplication logic
- `cmd/forge/deps.go` — `forge deps check` CLI subcommand (like `forge scan`)

### Config
```yaml
settings:
  depcheck_interval: 168h  # weekly
  depcheck_enabled: true
```

Per-anvil override:
```yaml
anvils:
  heimdall:
    depcheck_enabled: false  # skip this anvil
```

### Grouping
Minor/patch updates for the same ecosystem in the same anvil should be grouped into a single bead (like the current Go updater does), not one bead per package. Major version bumps get individual beads since they likely need manual intervention.

title: Hearth Queue panel: add Close action, show titles, and assignee for in-progress beads
description:
Three improvements to the Queue panel in Hearth TUI:

1. **Close action for Unlabeled beads** — Add a 'Close' option to the action menu for beads in the Unlabeled section (which already has the 'Add label' action). This calls `bd close <id>` to close the bead directly from the TUI.

2. **Show bead title below the ID** — Like the Worker panel items which show a second line with the title, Queue items should also display the bead title on a second line. Currently they only show the bead ID which isn't very informative.

3. **Assignee on in-progress beads** — Beads in the In Progress section should show a third line with the assigned worker/user name, so the operator can see who is working on what at a glance.

title: Bug: cifix worker only runs local temper — can't fix GitHub-only CI checks like changelog-check
description:
When GitHub CI fails on a check that temper doesn't cover (e.g. changelog-check), the cifix worker runs temper locally, temper passes, the worker reports success — but the GitHub CI failure persists. This burns a ci_fix_count attempt for nothing.

Examples:
- PR #105: changelog-check fails on GitHub, cifix runs temper locally (build/vet/test), temper passes, nothing actually fixed
- PR #98: build-and-test fails on GitHub (possibly different env), temper passes locally

## Proposed fix
1. Before spawning cifix, fetch the actual failing check names from GitHub (already available in PRStatus.StatusCheckRollup)
2. Pass the failing check names to the cifix worker so it knows WHAT failed
3. For known checks like changelog-check: generate the missing fragment directly instead of running temper
4. For build-and-test: include the GitHub CI logs in the Smith prompt so it can fix the actual failure, not just run local checks
5. Consider: if the cifix worker's temper passes but GitHub CI is still failing, don't count it as a successful fix attempt

title: Vulncheck: gracefully handle missing govulncheck instead of spamming vuln_scan_failed
description:
The vulncheck scanner runs on a schedule (default 24h, first scan 30s after startup). If govulncheck is not installed, ScanAll logs vuln_scan_failed every cycle. This clutters the events panel and Needs Attention with a persistent non-actionable error.

## Current behavior
- RunScheduled fires → ScanAll → exec.LookPath('govulncheck') fails → logs vuln_scan_failed event → repeats next cycle
- No way to disable it short of setting vulncheck_interval=0

## Proposed fix
1. Check for govulncheck once at Scanner construction (New()) or first RunScheduled call
2. If not found, log a single INFO message and disable scheduled scanning (don't keep retrying)
3. Add govulncheck to `forge doctor` checks as an optional dependency
4. Consider: auto-install via `go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest` if Go is available, or at least surface the install command prominently once
5. Add a config option `vulncheck_enabled: false` to explicitly disable if not wanted

title: Bug: FetchCopilotComments gh api --paginate breaks JSON parsing
description: In learn.go FetchCopilotComments(), gh api --paginate for REST endpoints concatenates multiple JSON arrays ([...][...]) which json.Unmarshal cannot parse as a single []ghReviewComment. This silently fails on PRs with >30 review comments. Fix: either use gh api with jq-style pagination, or use --jq to flatten, or manually handle the concatenated output.

title: Bellows: auto-learn Warden rules on PR merge
description: The Forge-fox design specifies that after a PR is merged, bellows should trigger a learn pass on Copilot comments from that PR. Currently forge warden learn is manual-only. In bellows checkPR(), when EventPRMerged fires, call warden.FetchCopilotComments + DistillRule + SaveRules to auto-accumulate rules. Gate behind a config flag (e.g. settings.auto_learn_rules: true).

title: Hearth: merge action errors should log to daemon events and show in TUI
description: When the merge action fails (e.g. gh pr merge returns an error), the error is returned via IPC to the TUI but: 1) The daemon doesn't log the failure as an event (only pr_merge_requested is logged, not pr_merge_failed). 2) The TUI error message may not be clearly visible to the user. Add a pr_merge_failed event to the daemon log on merge failure, and ensure the TUI shows the error prominently in the status bar. Found when --yes flag was unsupported by gh CLI and merge silently failed.

title: Warden: learnable review rules from Copilot feedback
description:
The Warden currently reviews with a generic 5-point checklist while Copilot catches many specific patterns (data races, width inconsistencies, error swallowing, etc). Build a learning system so the Warden accumulates domain-specific review rules over time.

## Design

### 1. Warden Rules File
Per-anvil file at `.forge/warden-rules.yaml` containing learned review patterns:

```yaml
rules:
  - id: race-ctx-field
    category: concurrency
    pattern: "Plain struct field accessed from multiple goroutines"
    check: "Verify context/cancel fields use atomic.Value or are set before goroutines start"
    source: "copilot:PR#65"
    added: 2026-03-07
  - id: panel-width-consistency
    category: ui
    pattern: "Panel width calculations in TUI code"
    check: "Ensure all panels in the same row use the same width accounting formula"
    source: "copilot:PR#65"
    added: 2026-03-07
```

### 2. Warden Prompt Integration
In `buildReviewPrompt()` (internal/warden/warden.go), read `.forge/warden-rules.yaml` from the anvil path and append the rules as a numbered checklist section in the prompt. Keep it concise — each rule becomes one line like: "[ ] Check: {check} (pattern: {pattern})".

### 3. Learning Pipeline — `forge warden learn`
New subcommand that:
1. Fetches unresolved Copilot review comments from recent/specified PRs via GitHub API
2. Groups and deduplicates similar comments
3. Uses Claude to distill each unique pattern into a rule (category, pattern, check)
4. Appends to `.forge/warden-rules.yaml` with provenance (source PR)
5. Optionally runs in `--dry-run` mode to preview rules before adding

Could also run automatically: after a PR is merged, bellows triggers a learn pass on any Copilot comments from that PR.

### 4. Rule Lifecycle
- Rules accumulate in the YAML file (committed to the repo so all Forge instances share them)
- Manual pruning via editing the file or `forge warden forget <rule-id>`
- Rules that trigger false positives can be removed or refined
- Over time the Warden becomes specialized for each repo's patterns

### Key Files
- `internal/warden/warden.go` — `buildReviewPrompt()` reads rules file
- `cmd/forge/warden.go` — new `forge warden learn` subcommand
- `.forge/warden-rules.yaml` — per-anvil learned rules (committed)

title: Hearth: Ready to Merge panel scroll loses items (same viewport bug)
description: The Ready to Merge panel has the same scroll bug already fixed in Workers (workerViewStart) and Needs Attention (Forge-e0c). When scrolling down, items at the top disappear and can't be scrolled back to. Apply the same viewport offset pattern — separate view start index from selection cursor — used in the other panel fixes. See workerViewStart in internal/hearth/hearth.go for the working pattern.

title: Update all documentation with new configurable settings and features
description: All project documentation needs updating to reflect recently added forge.yaml settings and features. This includes CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and any files in the docs/ folder. Document: max_ci_fix_attempts (default 5), max_review_fix_attempts (default 5), max_rebase_attempts (default 3), daily_cost_limit, bellows_interval, auto_dispatch/auto_dispatch_tag per anvil, schematic_enabled, schematic_word_threshold, smith_providers vs providers distinction. Also document new Hearth panels (Ready to Merge, Events in right column layout), new CLI commands, and the changelog fragment system. Check internal/config/config.go Settings struct for the full list of configurable fields and ensure each is documented across all doc files.

title: Hearth: header renders outside visible area in PowerShell terminal
description: The Hearth TUI header ('The Forge — Hearth Dashboard') is not visible — it renders above the visible terminal area. It briefly appears when the action menu overlay pops up (Enter key), which seems to scroll the entire view down by one line, making the header momentarily visible. This happens in PowerShell on Windows. Likely a off-by-one in the total height calculation or the alt screen positioning. The header may be at row 0 which is above the viewport, or the total content height exceeds the terminal height by 1 line, pushing the header off-screen. Check the View() height math in internal/hearth/hearth.go — the sum of header + topSection + eventPanel + footer may exceed m.height. The overlay's placeOverlay function may inadvertently fix the positioning by constraining to m.height.

title: Hearth: move Events panel into right column below Live Activity
description: Currently the Events panel is a full-width bottom strip. Restructure the layout so Events sits in the third (right) column below Live Activity, mirroring how Needs Attention sits below Queue in the left column. The right column becomes: Live Activity (top, same height as Workers) + Events (bottom, same height as Needs Attention). This frees up vertical space and makes the layout more symmetrical: Left column = Queue + Needs Attention, Center = Workers, Right column = Live Activity + Events. Update getTopPanelWidths/getVerticalSplit and the View() assembly in internal/hearth/hearth.go. The bottom full-width event strip should be removed.

title: Hearth: Ready to Merge panel with merge action
description: Add a new panel to the Hearth TUI that lists PRs ready to merge. A PR is ready when: CI checks pass, no unresolved review comments, no merge conflicts, and has approval. The panel should be reactive — PRs must disappear immediately when: new review comments arrive, another PR merge causes conflicts, CI fails, or approval is dismissed. Data source: bellows already tracks all this state (CIPassing, HasApproval, NeedsChanges, HasUnresolvedThreads, IsConflicting) in prSnapshot. Add a DB query or bellows method to surface PRs where all conditions are met. The panel needs Enter/actions support with a 'Merge' option that calls 'gh pr merge --squash' (or configurable merge strategy) via IPC command. After merge, bellows will detect the EventPRMerged and lifecycle will close the bead automatically. Consider placement: could be a section within the existing Queue panel, or a new sub-panel in the left column below Needs Attention.

title: Stale worker detection should exclude bellows/lifecycle workers
description: The stale worker detection (heartbeat monitoring from Forge-qa8) flags bellows and other long-running background workers as stuck because they don't produce frequent log activity like Smith workers do. Bellows is a polling loop that only writes logs when PR state changes — it can be silent for long stretches and that's normal. The watchdog/stale detection logic should either: 1) exclude workers with specific phases (e.g. 'bellows', 'lifecycle') from staleness checks, or 2) use a different heartbeat mechanism for long-running monitors vs short-lived Smith/cifix/reviewfix workers. Check internal/watchdog/ and the stale worker detection code.

title: Hearth: Needs Attention item stays visible after Retry action
description: When pressing Retry on a bead in the Needs Attention panel, the work starts (a new worker appears), but the bead remains in the Needs Attention list. It should disappear immediately after a successful retry. The retry IPC handler in daemon.go resets the retry record (clears needs_human), but the Hearth TUI doesn't refresh the Needs Attention panel after the action completes. Either the retry handler should trigger a FetchNeedsAttention refresh, or the executeAction method in hearth.go should request a data refresh after a successful retry/dismiss action.

title: Smith: instruct workers to create beads for unrelated issues found during work
description: When a Smith worker encounters preexisting bugs, code quality issues, unrelated errors, or other problems outside the scope of its assigned bead, it should create new beads for them rather than ignoring them or trying to fix them inline. Update the Smith prompt (internal/prompt/) to instruct the agent: if you discover issues unrelated to your current task, run 'bd create' with an appropriate title, description, type, and priority. The worker should NOT attempt to fix unrelated issues itself — just log them as new beads for future work. This turns every Smith run into a passive code audit.

title: Hearth: Enter actions menu for Unlabeled queue items with label option
description: In the Queue panel, when an Unlabeled bead is selected, pressing Enter should open an actions menu (similar to the Needs Attention actions menu). The menu should include an option to apply the auto-dispatch label (same as pressing 'l'). Currently Enter/actions only works in the Needs Attention panel. Extend the action menu system in internal/hearth/hearth.go to also work for Queue items in the 'unlabeled' section, with at minimum a 'Label for dispatch' action that calls OnTagBead.

title: Hearth: Needs Attention panel scroll loses items like Workers did
description: The Needs Attention panel has the same scroll bug that was fixed in the Workers panel (workerViewStart viewport offset). When scrolling down in Needs Attention, items at the top disappear and can't be scrolled back to. Apply the same viewport offset pattern (separate view start from selection cursor) that was used to fix Workers scrolling. See the workerViewStart pattern in internal/hearth/hearth.go for reference.

title: Hearth: Tab panel switching selects Workers and Live Activity together
description: When switching panels with Tab in the Hearth TUI, the Workers and Live Activity panels get selected/highlighted together instead of individually. Each panel should be selected alone when tabbing through them. Check the panel focus cycling logic in internal/hearth/hearth.go - likely the Tab key handler increments focus but the rendering treats two panels as one visual group.

title: Hearth: Workers panel scrolls items out of view permanently
description: In the Hearth TUI Workers panel, scrolling down causes items at the top to disappear from the list and they cannot be scrolled back up to find them. Items should remain accessible when scrolling - the viewport should scroll but not lose items. Check the viewport/list rendering logic in internal/hearth/hearth.go for the Workers panel.

title: Add golangci-lint to Temper Go checks
description: Temper currently runs only go build, go vet, and go test for Go projects. Add golangci-lint as an optional step (skip if binary not found). golangci-lint catches a wide range of issues: unused code, error handling, style, complexity, security patterns. Add it after vet, before test. Make it configurable per-anvil via .forge/temper.yaml or forge.yaml anvil settings so repos can opt out.

title: Changelog fragment system (adapted from Heimdall)
description: Forge has no changelog. Adopt Heimdall's changelog.d/ fragment pattern (English-only, no Norwegian needed). Each bead gets a changelog.d/<bead-id>.md fragment with 'category: Added|Changed|Fixed|...' header and markdown bullets. Add a Go-based assembly script (cmd/forge or scripts/) that collects fragments into CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased]. Smith prompt should instruct the agent to create a fragment when making user-visible changes. CI check can enforce fragment presence on PRs.

title: Configurable lifecycle retry caps in forge.yaml
description: The maxCI (5), maxRev (5), and maxRebase (3) caps in lifecycle.go are hardcoded constants. They should be configurable via forge.yaml settings (e.g. settings.max_ci_fixes, settings.max_review_fixes, settings.max_rebases) so operators can tune them per deployment without code changes. Config reads in config.go, wired through daemon.go into lifecycle.New().

title: Hearth Queue: split into Ready/Unlabeled/In-Progress sections with label action
description:
Split the Queue panel in Hearth into three sections (or a tabbed/grouped list):

1. **Ready** — beads returned by bd ready that have the auto_dispatch_tag label (e.g. forgeReady). These are the beads Forge will pick up.
2. **Unlabeled** — beads returned by bd ready that do NOT have the auto_dispatch_tag. These are available work but not yet approved for Forge. Only show this section when auto_dispatch is set to 'tagged' in forge.yaml.
3. **In Progress** — beads with status=in_progress, showing who/what they are assigned to (worker ID or smith PID).

When the user selects a bead in the Unlabeled section and presses Enter (or a hotkey like 'l'), add the auto_dispatch_tag label to that bead via bd update <id> --add-label <tag>. This would let operators approve beads for Forge processing directly from the TUI without switching to the CLI.

Implementation notes:
- The poller already calls bd ready --json which returns beads with their labels. Filtering by tag presence is straightforward.
- For in-progress beads, query bd list --status=in_progress --json (or use the existing activeBeads sync.Map / DB workers table).
- The label action needs a new IPC command (e.g. 'tag_bead') so Hearth can ask the daemon to run bd update.
- Consider using visual separators or section headers within the existing Queue panel rather than adding more panels.

title: Warden feedback passthrough: give Smith structured context on retry
description: When the Warden requests changes, the pipeline loops back to Smith for another iteration. Currently Smith starts fresh with just the original bead description — it does not receive the Warden's specific feedback about what was wrong. Pass the Warden's review comments as structured context in the Smith prompt for iteration 2+. The prompt builder already has access to iteration count; extend it to accept warden feedback text. This should significantly improve fix rates on retry iterations since Smith will know exactly what the Warden objected to instead of guessing.

title: Schematic: log sub-bead details in events for visibility
description: Schematic logs schematic_started/done/skipped events but the done message only says how many sub-beads were created, not their IDs or titles. When Schematic decomposes a parent bead, log each created sub-bead as a separate event (or a single event with a JSON payload listing all sub-bead IDs and titles). This gives operators visibility into what was created without having to run bd list. Also consider emitting a notification (Teams webhook) when decomposition happens, since it changes the work queue significantly.

title: Cost guardrails: daily spending ceiling that pauses dispatch
description: We track per-bead and per-day costs in bead_costs and daily_costs tables, but there is no enforcement. Add a configurable daily_cost_limit setting (in USD). When the running total for today exceeds the limit, pause dispatch until the next calendar day (or until the operator manually resumes). Log an event when the ceiling is hit. Show the current spend vs limit in forge status output. This prevents runaway costs from a bad decomposition that creates many sub-beads or from smiths that churn through retries burning tokens.

title: Stale worker detection: identify stuck smiths via progress heartbeats
description: Currently Forge only kills smiths that exceed smith_timeout. There is no way to distinguish a smith that is actively working from one that is hung (e.g. waiting on a blocked API call or stuck in a loop). Adopt gastown's health-state concept: periodically check smith log file modification time or process CPU usage. If a smith shows no progress for a configurable interval (e.g. 5 minutes of no log output), mark it as stalled in the workers table. The Needs Attention panel (Forge-6x7) can then surface stalled workers. Consider adding a stalled phase or status. This is different from timeout — timeout kills the process, stale detection warns the operator before the timeout fires.

title: Smith prompt: add escalation instructions for needs_human flagging
description: The Smith prompt template (internal/prompt/prompt.go) and AGENTS.md have no guidance on when a smith should signal it needs human help. Currently the only paths to needs_human are: Warden detecting no-diff, Schematic returning ActionClarify, and retry exhaustion. title: Hearth: fix wordWrap to preserve newlines and use unicode-aware width
description:
PR #6 (hearth.go lines 566-583, 615) flags two correctness issues in wordWrap:

1. wordWrap calls strings.Fields which splits on all whitespace including newlines, collapsing repeated spaces and discarding intentional line breaks. Event log messages may contain formatted output, stack traces, or indented text that should be preserved. Fix: split on actual newlines first (wrap per paragraph), then word-wrap each paragraph independently.

2. Width decisions use len(word) (byte count) rather than display width, so Unicode/multibyte characters wrap at wrong positions. Fix: use lipgloss.Width or a runewidth helper for display-width calculations.

3. strings.TrimSpace(pStr) on every word in renderEventLines removes leading indentation from continuation lines, which corrupts formatted event output. Remove the TrimSpace or only apply it to detect blank lines.

title: Configurable per-anvil auto-dispatch behavior
description:
Currently Forge dispatches ALL ready beads from 'bd ready --json' automatically. Add configurable control over which beads get auto-dispatched, on a per-anvil basis.

New per-anvil config fields (in AnvilConfig in internal/config/config.go):
  auto_dispatch: all | tagged | priority | off
    - all: current behavior, dispatch everything ready (default)
    - tagged: only dispatch beads whose 'tags' field contains auto_dispatch_tag
    - priority: only dispatch beads at or above auto_dispatch_min_priority
    - off: never auto-dispatch; beads only run via 'forge queue run <id>'
  auto_dispatch_tag: string  (used when auto_dispatch: tagged, e.g. 'forge-auto')
  auto_dispatch_min_priority: int  (used when auto_dispatch: priority, e.g. 1 means P0+P1 only)

Implementation notes:
- Add Tags []string json:'tags' to poller.Bead (bd ready JSON may include a tags array; if absent, tags-mode falls through to dispatch nothing).
- Add the new fields to AnvilConfig with defaults (auto_dispatch defaults to 'all').
- Apply the filter after polling in poller.Poll or in daemon.go before dispatching.
- Validate the config: if auto_dispatch=tagged, auto_dispatch_tag must be non-empty; if auto_dispatch=priority, min_priority must be 0-4.
- Update forge.yaml sample/docs with the new knobs.
- The 'off' mode is useful for repos where Forge should observe beads but never touch them without explicit human invocation.

title: Show remaining rate-limit quota for Claude and Gemini
description:
Neither Claude nor Gemini CLIs expose a standalone quota-check command.

Claude CLI (confirmed from docs at code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference):
- No "claude --usage", "claude usage", or "claude api usage" subcommand exists.
- The only relevant command is "claude auth status" (shows auth status as JSON, not quota).
- Quota/rate-limit info arrives exclusively via the streaming rate_limit_event, already captured
  in smith.go as RateLimitInfo{Status string, ...}.
- The rate_limit_event payload includes a "reset_at" RFC3339 timestamp telling us when the
  limit resets. This is NOT yet stored in RateLimitInfo (only Status is kept).
- Implementation: add ResetAt string to RateLimitInfo, populate from rate_limit_info.reset_at
  in readStreamJSON, surface in forge status output and hearth TUI sidebar.

Gemini CLI (confirmed from gemini-cli source and docs/resources/quota-and-pricing.md):
- No "gemini --quota", "gemini stats", or similar non-interactive quota command.
- Quota data is only available inside an active interactive session via the "/stats model"
  slash command (which calls config.getQuotaRemaining/getQuotaLimit/getQuotaResetTime).
- Quota remaining/limit/resetTime come from API response headers and are tracked in Config
  internally; there is no way to query them outside a live session.
- When Gemini hits a rate limit, the error text contains the reset time; we already detect
  this in daemon.go (rate_limit_event detection). We can parse "retry after N seconds" or
  "reset at <time>" from the error output to get a Gemini-side reset time.
- The result-event stats field (total_tokens, duration_ms etc.) does NOT include quota info.

Scoped implementation:
1. Add ResetAt string field to RateLimitInfo in smith.go.
2. Populate ResetAt from rate_limit_info.reset_at in readStreamJSON (Claude path).
3. For Gemini: attempt to parse "retry after N seconds" or RFC3339 time from ErrorOutput
   when IsRateLimited is set; store as computed reset time.
4. Persist last-seen RateLimitInfo per provider in daemon state (in-memory or state.db).
5. Include provider quota/reset info in "forge status" JSON output.
6. Show in hearth TUI: a per-provider "rate limited until <time>" indicator when relevant.

Fix: add a Stats field to StreamEvent matching Gemini's stats shape, populate CostUSD (Gemini has no cost but we can estimate from token counts if desired, or just leave 0), populate TokensIn/TokensOut from stats.input_tokens/output_tokens, and log the full stats summary (tokens, cache hits, tool_calls, duration_ms) to the smith log file and to an EventInfo so it appears in forge history output.

title: Forge restart script: stash dirty .beads/issues.jsonl before git pull + surface stderr in logs
description:
The Mezzanine "Rebuild & Restart" button (Hytte) POSTs to `/api/forge/restart`, which runs `~/.forge/restart.sh`. The script's first real step is `git pull` in `~/source/Forge`, but the running daemon's own `bd` workflow continuously rewrites `.beads/issues.jsonl` in that working tree. So the pull always aborts:

```
==> Pulling latest...
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:
	.beads/issues.jsonl
Please commit your changes or stash them before you merge.
Aborting
```

The Hytte handler at `internal/forge/handlers.go::RestartForgeHandler` discards stdout/stderr and only logs `forge: restart script failed: exit status 1`, so from Mezzanine the button looks like a no-op. End result: button can't actually restart the daemon, and the workaround is SSHing in to `systemctl restart forge` manually (which is exactly what this button was meant to avoid).

This is the same regression we fixed on the Hytte GitHub Actions deploy a few days ago (Hytte-side `git stash push` before `git pull`, drop after). Apply the same pattern here.

## Scope

### 1. Patch `~/.forge/restart.sh` to be dirty-tree resilient

Replace the current `git pull` step with:

```bash
if ! git diff --quiet || ! git diff --cached --quiet; then
  git stash push -m "restart-auto-stash-$(date +%s)"
  STASHED=1
else
  STASHED=0
fi
git pull --ff-only origin main
if [ "$STASHED" = 1 ]; then
  git stash drop || true
fi
```

The dropped stash is intentional — `.beads/issues.jsonl` is regenerated by `bd` on the next write, so saving the stash forever just clutters `git stash list`. Identical reasoning to the Hytte deploy fix.

### 2. Surface script output to Hytte logs

`internal/forge/handlers.go::RestartForgeHandler` currently uses `cmd.Run()` and discards both streams. Capture stdout/stderr into `bytes.Buffer`s and include them in the failure log line, so future failures are diagnosable from `journalctl -u hytte` without re-running the script by hand:

```go
var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
cmd.Stdout = &stdout
cmd.Stderr = &stderr
if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
    log.Printf("forge: restart script failed: %v\nstdout:\n%s\nstderr:\n%s",
        err, stdout.String(), stderr.String())
}
```

The script can still be large on success (full build output), so cap each buffer at ~16 KB to avoid log bloat (`io.MultiWriter(&buf, io.Discard)` after the cap, or a custom `limitedBuffer`).

### 3. Optional: surface failure in the UI

Currently Mezzanine's POST gets a 202 and assumes success. Consider an admin-only `GET /api/forge/restart/last-result` that returns the most recent script run's exit code + tail of output, so the dashboard can show "last restart: failed, see logs" instead of leaving the button looking dead. Out of scope for the immediate fix, but worth a follow-up bead if this happens again.

### 4. Tests

`internal/forge/handlers_test.go`: extend the existing restart-script tests to verify that the failure log line includes captured stdout/stderr substrings. The shell-script fix itself is verified by running the script against a git repo where a tracked file has uncommitted changes; assert exit 0 and that the working tree is clean afterwards.

### 5. Acceptance

- Hitting Mezzanine's Rebuild & Restart on a Forge anvil whose `~/source/Forge/.beads/issues.jsonl` is dirty actually completes the pull/build/restart cycle.
- Any future script failure surfaces stderr in `journalctl -u hytte` rather than being silent.
- `make build`, `make test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` pass.
- Changelog fragment in `changelog.d/` (category: Fixed).

## Reference

- `~/.forge/restart.sh` — the broken script on the prod box; same content lives in the Forge repo somewhere (or it's installed from there). Find the source-of-truth file and patch there + redeploy to `~/.forge/`.
- `~/source/Hytte/.github/workflows/deploy.yml` ~line 35 — the analogous stash-before-pull fix on the Hytte deploy side, written 2026-05-15.
- `~/source/Hytte/internal/forge/handlers.go::RestartForgeHandler` — Hytte-side handler that needs the stdout/stderr capture.
notes: Note appended to test BD_EXPORT_AUTO=false (Hytte session 1779288419)

title: Hearth 2.0: remember filter / sort / expanded sections across navigation
description:
Navigating from a queue row into a bead detail, or anywhere else in the Hearth 2.0 web UI, and then pressing Back blows away the queue's filter, sort, and expanded/collapsed sections — the user has to reapply everything every time. This is a UX hot spot because the queue is the primary workspace; losing state is friction on every bead inspection.

Persist all UI navigation state across page transitions and refreshes.

## Scope — what state to persist

Persist per-user (anchored on auth, not browser-global) and survive route changes AND refresh AND restart of the daemon:

1. **Queue (QueuePane)**
   - Filter chips / search box value
   - Sort selection (which column, asc/desc)
   - Expanded vs collapsed state of each anvil bucket (the Section headers "Ready", "Unlabeled", "In progress")
   - Expanded vs collapsed of any per-bucket "show more" toggles
   - Scroll position within the queue (optional but nice; if the scroll container can be re-anchored to the previously focused bead row that's even better)
2. **Workers pane** — collapsed/expanded state per worker group, scroll position
3. **Live Activity / Events pane** — pause state, filter selection, scroll position
4. **PR pane** — sort, filter, expanded sections
5. **Bead detail** — when opened, remember it has been opened (so the back-to-queue route can highlight the row briefly and scroll it into view)
6. **Future panes** — provide the persistence primitive so new components opt in by a one-liner.

## Approach

Use a small `useUIState(key, initial)` hook that:
- Reads/writes to `sessionStorage` keyed on `forge.ui.<route>.<key>` for view-local state (sort, filter, scroll) — so Back works without a server round-trip.
- For settings that should survive refresh and across tabs (collapsed/expanded preferences, sort defaults), promote to `localStorage` under `forge.ui.<userID>.<key>`.
- Optionally syncs the *cross-device* slice to the daemon via a `POST /api/ui-state` endpoint backed by `~/.forge/state.db` keyed on user_id. That's optional / nice-to-have for now — sessionStorage + localStorage cover the immediate need.

Critically, React Router v6's `useNavigate(-1)` / browser back already restores the form state if components read from sessionStorage on mount. The hook just makes that ergonomic and cuts the boilerplate.

## Scope — implementation

1. Add `internal/web/frontend/src/hooks/useUIState.ts` (or `usePersistedState.ts`) — typed wrapper around session/local storage with a JSON codec, debounced writes, and a `clearAll()` for tests.
2. Convert each piece of state in the panes listed above to the hook. Use sessionStorage for transient navigation state (filters, scroll), localStorage for true preferences (which sections are collapsed by default).
3. When navigating to a bead detail row, push the route as `/bead/<id>?from=queue` (or set router state) so the back button reliably lands on the queue route — that combined with sessionStorage gives instant restore.
4. Tests:
    - Unit test the hook (read/write/clear/JSON round-trip).
    - Integration test for QueuePane: set a filter + sort + collapse a section, navigate away via React Router test harness, navigate back, assert the state is restored.
    - PR pane and Workers pane: similar restoration test.

## Acceptance

- Set a queue filter "p:1" + sort by anvil + collapse Unlabeled → click into a bead → press browser Back: the queue is exactly as it was, no flicker of default state in between.
- Refresh the page on the queue route: filter, sort, collapsed sections all stay.
- Open a new tab to `/`: the persisted *preferences* (default collapsed sections) carry over via localStorage, but transient state (search query, scroll) starts fresh — that's the right split.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm run test`, `go test ./...` pass.
- Changelog fragment in `changelog.d/` (category: Added).

## Reference

- internal/web/frontend/src/components/QueuePane.tsx — main offender; state is currently in useState only.
- internal/web/frontend/src/App.tsx — router setup; may need to switch to `<Outlet/>` pattern if not already, and consider scroll-restoration.
- internal/web/frontend/src/api.ts — pattern for new endpoints if we go the daemon-side sync route later.

title: Hearth 2.0: one-click dispatch-tag button on Unlabeled queue rows
description:
The web Hearth (internal/web/frontend QueuePane.tsx) groups beads into Ready / Unlabeled / In-progress. Adding the dispatch label currently requires opening the bead in the TUI Ledger or running `bd label add <id> <tag>` from a shell. We want a one-click icon directly on each Unlabeled queue row that applies the anvil's configured dispatch tag.

The tag is NOT hardcoded — Robin runs two Forge instances:
- Hetzner anvil → `auto_dispatch_tag: forgeReady`
- Skybert anvil → `auto_dispatch_tag: forgeSkybert`

So the action must resolve the tag from the row's anvil config (`AutoDispatchTag`), not from a frontend constant.

## Scope

### 1. Frontend — icon button on Unlabeled rows

`internal/web/frontend/src/components/QueuePane.tsx`:
- On each row inside the `unlabeled` bucket, add a small icon button (e.g. `Tag` / `Sparkles` / lightning-bolt — match the existing icon style) inline next to the bead title/anvil pill.
- Tooltip: "Apply <tag>" (where `<tag>` is the anvil's auto-dispatch tag; fetch from the anvil details endpoint or pass via the queue payload).
- Click → POST to a new or existing endpoint that adds the tag and the daemon's regular poll picks the bead up on the next cycle (no separate dispatch call needed; the label drives that).
- Optimistic UI: the row visually slides from "Unlabeled" → "Ready" after a successful POST without waiting for SSE.
- Disable the button while the request is in flight to prevent double-tags.

### 2. Backend — endpoint that uses the anvil's configured tag

Today `POST /api/bead/{id}/label` (handleBeadLabelChange in internal/web/actions.go) accepts an arbitrary label. Two options:
1. Add a new convenience endpoint `POST /api/queue/{id}/apply-dispatch-tag` that looks up the anvil's `AutoDispatchTag` server-side and dispatches the existing `update_label` IPC. Cleaner — frontend doesn't need to know the tag.
2. Or expose the tag via the anvil/queue payload and have the frontend call the existing `/api/bead/{id}/label` with it. Less server work, but pushes config into the UI.

Pick option 1 — the daemon/server already has the anvil registry and the action stays semantically named.

### 3. Tests

Backend:
- `internal/web/actions_test.go`: new test covers the apply-dispatch-tag endpoint reading the anvil config and forwarding an `update_label` IPC with the resolved tag. Cover the "anvil has no auto_dispatch_tag configured" path → 400 with a clear message.

Frontend:
- `QueuePane.test.tsx`: rendering an Unlabeled row shows the tag icon; clicking it calls the new API method; the row leaves the Unlabeled bucket after success.

### 4. Acceptance

- A bead in the Unlabeled section of a hetzner anvil queue shows an icon; tapping it adds the `forgeReady` label and the bead moves to Ready on next poll.
- The same UI on a skybert anvil applies `forgeSkybert` instead (driven entirely by `auto_dispatch_tag` in that anvil's config).
- `go build`, `go test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build` pass.
- Changelog fragment in `changelog.d/` (category: Added).

## Reference

- internal/web/frontend/src/components/QueuePane.tsx — Unlabeled bucket rendering, `BucketSection` rows.
- internal/web/frontend/src/api.ts `actions.dispatch` — existing pattern for queue action calls.
- internal/web/actions.go handleBeadLabelChange + IPC UpdateLabelPayload — existing label-update plumbing to reuse.
- internal/config Anvil.AutoDispatchTag — config field that already exists.
- internal/wicket/dispatch.go — Wicket already does per-anvil auto-dispatch labeling; lift the same lookup pattern for the new endpoint.

title: Hearth 2.0 pipeline: replace 'Merged' stage with 'Ready to merge'
description:
Follow-up to Forge-v7ij. The pipeline bar currently ends with a "Merged" stage. Merged beads are no longer in-flight, so that stage is dead weight — it just shows historical counts.

Replace with **"Ready to merge"** — the same semantic the original Hearth TUI surfaces, which is actually actionable: beads sitting in PR with everything green that just need a human click.

## "Ready to merge" criteria

A PR is ready-to-merge when ALL of the following are true:

- `status = 'open'` (not already merged or closed)
- `ci_passing = 1` (all CI checks green)
- `has_pending_reviews = 0` (Copilot — or any required reviewer — has reviewed)
- `has_unresolved_threads = 0` (no outstanding review-comment threads)
- `is_conflicting = 0` (no merge conflict against base branch)

All four flags live on the `prs` table in `~/.forge/state.db` (see schema in `internal/state/db.go`). Bellows already maintains them.

## Backend

- The pipeline-bar data source (added in Forge-v7ij — likely in `internal/web/views.go` or a sibling) currently produces a count per stage including 'merged'. Replace that bucket with 'ready_to_merge', computed by joining the prs table against the four-condition filter above. Group by anvil so the per-anvil section of the pipeline shows the right count.
- The PR stage already exists (with Bellows nested per v7ij). The new "Ready to merge" is a distinct stage that sits AFTER PR/Bellows — a PR that's still being fix-iterated by Bellows is in the PR stage; once Bellows is done and all four flags are green, the bead promotes to Ready-to-merge.
- Once a PR is actually merged (status flips to 'merged'), it disappears from the pipeline bar entirely. Historical merge counts can stay surfaced elsewhere (e.g. History page); the pipeline bar is for what's currently in flight.

## Frontend

In the PipelineBar component (`internal/web/frontend/src/components/PipelineBar.tsx`, added in v7ij):

- Remove the 'Merged' pill.
- Add a 'Ready to merge' pill at the end of the stage list.
- Style it distinctively so it's eye-catching when non-zero — this is the operator's "things you can click Merge on" indicator. Suggest the existing green / emerald accent reserved for terminal-good states.
- Clicking the pill could optionally open a filtered view of those PRs — defer if it complicates this slice; just the count is the minimum.

## Tests

- Backend: assert the new bucket includes only PRs matching all four conditions; assert PRs with any flag failing fall into the PR/Bellows stage instead.
- Frontend: the pill renders with the correct count and the 'Merged' pill is gone.

## Acceptance

- `make build`, `make test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (frontend) all pass.
- Pipeline bar no longer shows 'Merged'.
- Pipeline bar shows 'Ready to merge' with a count of open PRs where CI is green, Copilot reviewed, no unresolved threads, no merge conflict.
- A PR with failing CI counts in PR/Bellows, NOT Ready-to-merge — flips automatically as Bellows resolves the issue.
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Changed).

## Non-goals

- A new merge-action button inside the pipeline bar. The existing PRs page handles that; this is just visibility.
- Per-PR drill-down from the pipeline pill (could be a follow-up).
- Surfacing merged count anywhere else in the pipeline view — leave to History page.

## Reference

- internal/web/frontend/src/components/PipelineBar.tsx — frontend pill rendering.

- internal/hearth/ — original Hearth TUI has the same "Ready to merge" semantic worth mirroring.
- internal/bellows/ — what maintains the four flags.

title: Hearth 2.0 bead detail: surface notes and comments
description:
The Hearth 2.0 bead detail page currently shows description, queue cache, ingot, retry, cost, recent events, PR summaries, and worker history — but NOT the bead's notes (appended via `bd note` / `--append-notes`) or comments (via `bd comments add`). Operators rely on both for context: notes capture in-progress thinking ("Fixed the flaky test"), comments record review feedback and human commentary. Without them the detail page is incomplete.

## Backend

Extend `beadDetailResponse` in `internal/web/views.go` (around line 326) with two new fields:

    Notes    string             `json:"notes,omitempty"`
    Comments []beadDetailComment `json:"comments"`

Where `beadDetailComment` is:

    type beadDetailComment struct {
        ID        string `json:"id,omitempty"`
        Author    string `json:"author"`
        Body      string `json:"body"`
        CreatedAt string `json:"created_at"`
    }

### How to load them

- **Notes** are an inline string field on the bead itself; `bd show <id> --json` either includes a `notes` field directly OR they are appended into `description`. Check `bd show --help` and the JSON response shape; the right path is whichever field beads populates from `--append-notes`. Read once per detail request from `bd show`.
- **Comments** are separate from the bead body. Use `bd comments <id> --json` (shell out using the existing `resolveCommand("bd")` + `anvilDirForBead()` pattern in `internal/forge/handlers.go`). Parse the JSON array into the `beadDetailComment` shape.
- Cache neither for v1 — comment volume per bead is small (<50) and a fresh shell-out per page load is ~50ms. Optimise later if needed.
- Errors from `bd comments` are non-fatal — log + return an empty Comments array so the rest of the page still renders.

### Tests

- `handleBeadDetail` tests extended with a fixture where `bd show` returns notes and `bd comments` returns two comments; assert both arrive in the response.
- Failure path: `bd comments` exits non-zero → response has `Comments: []` and no error.

## Frontend

In `internal/web/frontend/src/pages/BeadDetailPage.tsx`:

- Add a **Notes** panel below the existing description panel, only when `notes` is non-empty. Render as plain text with `whitespace-pre-wrap` so line breaks are preserved. Title via i18n-or-inline-English: "Notes".
- Add a **Comments** panel below Notes (or wherever fits the existing layout). Render the list as cards: author, relative timestamp (hover tooltip = absolute), body with `whitespace-pre-wrap`. Empty state: "No comments yet." Don't render the panel at all if you want zero-comment beads to stay compact — implementer's choice.
- Both panels collapse / expand on click of the panel header (default expanded). Matches the polish ethos from the recent Suggestions UX work.

### Add-comment composer (optional, recommend folding in)

Add a small composer at the bottom of the Comments panel: textarea + "Add comment" button. POSTs to a new endpoint `POST /api/bead/{id}/comment` body `{body}`, which shells out to `bd comments add <id> "<body>"`. Optimistic UI: append the new comment locally on success. If this feels like scope creep, defer to a separate follow-up bead — note that explicitly in the implementation.

## i18n

Frontend doesn't use react-i18next today; new strings can be inline English.

## Tests

- `BeadDetailPage.test.tsx`: render with a fixture carrying notes and 2 comments; assert both panels visible with correct content. Render with empty notes + comments; assert panels gracefully omitted (or show empty state).

## Acceptance

- `make build`, `make test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (frontend) all pass.
- Bead detail page shows notes content when present.
- Bead detail page shows the comments list with author + timestamp + body.
- A bead with no notes and no comments still renders cleanly.
- (If included) Adding a comment via the composer round-trips and the new comment appears in the list.
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Added).

## Non-goals

- Editing or deleting comments from the UI. Defer.
- Threaded comments / replies.
- Markdown rendering inside comments — `whitespace-pre-wrap` is enough for v1.
- Live update on new comments. Static fetch per page load is fine.

## Reference

- internal/web/views.go:326 — beadDetailResponse struct.
- internal/web/handlers.go (search `handleBeadDetail`) — handler to extend.
- internal/web/frontend/src/pages/BeadDetailPage.tsx — frontend target.
- internal/forge/handlers.go (in Hytte) — bd-shell-out pattern via `resolveCommand` and `anvilDirForBead` — same approach applies here in Forge web.

title: Hearth 2.0: Queue date column + sort menu + filter clear button
description:
Three related improvements to the Queue pane on the Hearth 2.0 dashboard.

## 1. Show last-changed / created date on each row

Today QueuePane renders `bead_id`, title, priority, labels — nothing about recency. With many beads queued, knowing which ones changed recently matters more than priority order. Surface a "Updated 2h ago" relative-time label on each row, with a tooltip showing the absolute ISO timestamp.

If the queue cache table in `~/.forge/state.db` doesn't store them, either add columns OR fetch them at serialisation time from the in-memory poller snapshot.

### Frontend

In `internal/web/frontend/src/components/QueuePane.tsx`, render `updated_at` as a relative timestamp on each row using the existing `relativeTime()` helper (see `LiveActivity.tsx` for the pattern). Hover tooltip shows the absolute timestamp.

## 2. Sort menu beyond priority

Currently the queue is sorted by priority only. Add a small sort-by dropdown above the list with these options:

- Priority (asc) — current default, keep first
- Last updated (newest first)
- Last updated (oldest first)
- Created (newest first)

If Forge-smhw (grouped queue) has landed by the time this is implemented, sort applies WITHIN each anvil/status group.

## 3. Filter clear button

## Non-goals

title: Wrap remaining exec.Command sites with executil.HideWindow to suppress Windows console flash
description:
## Problem

On Windows, `exec.Command` / `exec.CommandContext` produces a brief console-window flash for every short-lived subprocess unless the cmd is wrapped to set `HideWindow=true` + `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` in `SysProcAttr.CreationFlags`. Forge already has the helper for this (`internal/executil.HideWindow`) and most hot paths use it (`poller`, `bellows`, `depcheck`, most of `wicket`). But several sites still spawn unwrapped — when they fire during normal worker operation, the user sees flashes on their desktop.

## Sites to wrap (verify locations before editing — line numbers drift)

Grep: `grep -rnE \"exec\\.(Command|CommandContext)\" internal/ cmd/ | grep -v executil`

High-frequency / fires during worker dispatch (most user-visible):
- `internal/smith/smith.go` — `exec.CommandContext(ctx, pv.Cmd(), args...)` — spawns claude/gemini binary on every worker.
- `internal/burnish/burnish.go` — two unwrapped sites: `git push origin <branch>` and `git rev-parse`.
- `internal/quench/quench.go` — two unwrapped sites: `git rev-parse` and `git diff`.
- `internal/rebase/rebase.go` — `exec.Command(\"git\", args...)`.
- `internal/vulncheck/vulncheck.go` — three sites: `govulncheck`, `bd list`, `bd create`. Fires on the daily vulncheck cycle.
- `internal/web/views.go` — `bd show <id> --json` on /api/bead/{id} requests; frequent if Hearth dashboard is open with a bead-detail panel.
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go` — `gh pr view --web` from the pr-open action.

Low-frequency / user-initiated (can wrap too for consistency):
- `cmd/forge/daemon.go` — self-respawn during `forge up` detach.
- `cmd/forge/doctor.go` — generic exec for dependency probes.
- `cmd/forge/quest.go` — quest commands.
- `cmd/forge/update.go` — installer script + self-respawn.

## Proposed fix

Mechanical change: every `exec.Command*(...)` site that isn't already wrapped should become `executil.HideWindow(exec.Command*(...))`. The helper is a no-op on non-Windows so it's safe everywhere.

No behaviour change beyond the flash suppression — `HideWindow` only sets process-creation flags.
design:
`internal/executil` exposes `HideWindow(*exec.Cmd) *exec.Cmd` already. The pattern in the codebase is `cmd := executil.HideWindow(exec.CommandContext(...))`. Apply it everywhere.

Note: the same flash problem in **bd** is being fixed in the bd fork separately (see Robin831/beads commit fefea144c which added `cmd/bd/proc_windows.go` and wrapped `tryRemoteCLIPushPull`). That fork covers the `dolt push/pull` flash that fires every minute under the dolt-sync scheduled task. This Forge-side bead is the parallel sweep — same pattern, different repo.
acceptance_criteria:
- A grep across `internal/` + `cmd/` for `exec\\.Command` returns only call sites that are followed by `executil.HideWindow` or set their own `SysProcAttr.CreationFlags` (e.g. `internal/executil/executil_windows.go:killProcessTree`).
- Running `forge up` on Windows with a worker actively in Smith → Burnish → Temper produces no visible console-window flashes on the desktop.
- `vulncheck` and `web/views.go bd show` paths are similarly silent.
- Non-Windows build is unchanged (HideWindow is a no-op there).
notes: Discovered while tracking down a per-minute terminal flash on the user's laptop. Root cause was actually `bd`'s dolt-cli spawn (fixed separately in the beads fork), not Forge — but the grep that found it also surfaced these Forge sites. They don't fire when Forge is idle, so they're not the current pain — but each one is a "next time it fires, you'll see a flash" issue. Treat as a tidy-up pass.

title: Hearth 2.0: tab title 'Hearth 2.0' and a proper favicon
description:
The browser tab currently shows the title "Hearth · Forge" with the default Vite icon (the React or the empty rect — the project has no `<link rel="icon">` set, so the browser falls back to a default). Polish both.

## Title

In `internal/web/frontend/index.html` (line 7):
- Change `<title>Hearth · Forge</title>` to `<title>Hearth 2.0</title>`. If the implementer feels "Hearth · Forge 2.0" reads better, that's acceptable too. The user's preference is "Hearth 2.0", fallback to plain "Hearth".

## Favicon

The frontend currently has no public/ folder and no `<link rel="icon">`. Add both:

1. Create `internal/web/frontend/public/favicon.svg` with a small SVG icon. The blacksmith metaphor fits — Forge already uses 🔨/🔥 themes. Use a simple flame, anvil, or hammer glyph. Lucide React has icons; the easiest is to extract a small inline SVG of `Flame` or `Anvil` or `Hammer` from lucide.dev (or use a simple Unicode glyph rendered to SVG). Keep it monochrome with the slate-on-amber palette already used by Hearth, e.g. amber-400 (#fbbf24) on transparent. ~24×24 viewBox is enough.
2. Add `<link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/favicon.svg" />` inside the `<head>` of `index.html`, before the title.
3. Vite's `public/` directory is served at the site root in production; the existing build pipeline will copy the file into `internal/web/dist/` automatically on `npm run build`. No code changes required.
4. Optional: also include a PNG fallback (`favicon-32.png`) for browsers that don't render SVG icons. Modern browsers all do, so this is nice-to-have.

If the implementer prefers a different glyph, anything blacksmith-ish (hammer, anvil, flame, hearth) is acceptable. Avoid generic gears or wrenches — too generic for the brand.

## Tests

- Manual: load Hearth in a browser, confirm the tab title and icon update. No unit tests needed for static HTML changes.

## Acceptance

- `npm run lint`, `npm run build` succeed.
- Tab shows "Hearth 2.0" (or the fallback wording) in the browser tab.
- A non-default icon renders in the tab.

title: Hearth 2.0: cap live activity at ~10 events with Fetch more pagination
description:
Forge-hmxl flipped Live Activity to newest-at-top. The list still grows unbounded as events stream in over the SSE buffer. After an hour of activity the pane is a wall of text. Cap the visible count and let the user load older events in chunks.

## Change

In `internal/web/frontend/src/components/LiveActivity.tsx`:

- Default visible count: **10**.
- Render only the first N items of the reversed list (newest 10).
- Below the rendered list, render a **"Fetch more"** button. Clicking adds 10 to the visible count and renders that many additional items.
- Hide the button when `visibleCount >= items.length`.
- Resetting back to 10 isn't needed — keeping the user's expanded count is the right default. If the buffer evicts events, the count clamps naturally.
- Keep the existing top-stickiness behaviour from hmxl: new events still appear at the top.

## i18n

Frontend doesn't use react-i18next today. New inline string:
- "Fetch more"
