title: Hearth 2.0: fix worker log loading + don't open log modal for bellows workers
description:
Two related issues with the WorkerLogModal in Hearth 2.0.

## Issue 1: clicking a running smith shows "No log content yet" indefinitely

Repro: with one active smith (e.g. Fhi.Metadata-kqrhy, status `running`, anvil `munin`), click the worker card to open the log modal. The modal header shows the worker info plus "reconnecting…" status. The body shows "No log content yet." and never updates, even after the smith has been streaming output for minutes.

The endpoint `GET /api/worker/{id}/log?tail=N` (or whatever the current path is — see `WorkerLogModal.tsx` line ~46) appears to return nothing. Investigate:

1. Verify the log file actually exists on disk (`~/.forge/logs/<bead>/smith-*.log`) and is being written to while the smith runs.
2. Verify the server handler (`internal/web/handlers.go` or similar) resolves the right log path for an active worker — there may be a race where the worker row exists in the DB before the log file is created on disk; the handler should not 404 in that case, it should return an empty array with status 200.
3. Verify the frontend reconnection / polling loop is actually re-firing. The "reconnecting…" state suggests an SSE or fetch retry; check it isn't stuck on a failure mode that doesn't auto-recover.
4. Once the log file has bytes, a fresh request must return parsed entries. If it does for a finished worker but not for an actively-streaming one, the parser is likely choking on a partial JSON line at EOF — handle that by stopping at the last complete newline.

Add an integration test (or fix-validating test) that simulates an active worker writing log lines and asserts the endpoint returns the buffered entries.

## Issue 2: bellows workers are clickable and show "invalid worker ID"

Repro: when a bead reaches the bellows phase, the WorkersPane shows a bellows-flavoured worker card. Clicking it opens the log modal, which immediately renders "invalid worker ID" because bellows IDs don't match the `validWorkerID` regex on the server (and rightfully so — bellows doesn't produce a smith log).

Behavior change:

- The frontend should NOT render bellows workers as standalone clickable cards. Bellows is a PR-monitor and is being relocated under the PR stage in the pipeline overview (Forge-XXXX, the pipeline-bar bead).
- Until that pipeline restructure lands, the simpler interim fix is: if a worker's `kind` (or equivalent field) is `bellows`, render its card non-clickable (or render a "Open PR" link instead of a log-modal trigger). Sub-workers spawned by bellows (quench, burnish, rebase) ARE clickable as today — they have real logs.

If the worker shape doesn't carry a kind that distinguishes bellows from smith, add one server-side. Search `internal/web/views.go` for the workers list response struct.

## Tests

- `WorkerLogModal.test.tsx`: passing a smith worker renders the log fetch; passing a bellows worker fails the test setup (the modal should not be invoked for bellows) — alternatively cover by asserting the WorkersPane click handler is gated.
- Backend handler: with a worker whose log file is missing or empty, the parsed-log endpoint returns `200` with `[]`, not `404` or `"invalid worker ID"`.
- Repro for Issue 1: simulated active log streaming end-to-end test.

## Acceptance

- `make build`, `make test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (frontend) all pass.
- Clicking a running smith opens the log modal and shows current log entries within ~2 seconds; new lines stream in as the smith writes.
- Clicking a bellows worker either does nothing or opens the PR — definitely does not open the log modal that errors with "invalid worker ID".
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Fixed).

## Reference

- internal/web/frontend/src/components/WorkerLogModal.tsx — modal that's currently spinning on "reconnecting…".
- internal/web/frontend/src/components/WorkersPane.tsx — where the click handler that opens the modal lives.
- internal/web/handlers.go — `/api/worker/{id}/log` and `/log/parsed` handlers; check the active-worker / empty-log branch.
- internal/web/views.go — workers response shape; extend with a kind/phase field if needed.
- internal/bellows/ — what a bellows worker actually does, for the "render as PR link instead" decision.
- Today's repro bead: Fhi.Metadata-kqrhy on the munin anvil. Look at `~/.forge/logs/Fhi.Metadata-kqrhy/` if it still exists.

title: Hearth 2.0: polish — newest activity at top, full-width layout, queue filter
description:
Three small UI improvements to Hearth 2.0 that compound into noticeably better day-to-day use.

## 1. LiveActivity: newest event at top

Today `internal/web/frontend/src/components/LiveActivity.tsx` appends events and auto-scrolls to the bottom (`el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight` at line ~25). The user has to scroll past stale events to see the latest. Invert.

- Render new events at the **top** of the list (prepend, not append).
- Remove the bottom-stickiness logic (`stickToBottomRef`, the `onScroll` distance-from-bottom check). Replace with top-stickiness: if the user has scrolled away from the top, do NOT yank them back; if they're at the top, the new event appears at the top in view.
- Time labels still show relative-time as today; oldest at the bottom.

## 2. Full-width layout

The current dashboard has fixed side margins (or a max-width container) that leaves blank space on both edges of the viewport. Use the full width so the three columns (Queue / Workers / LiveActivity) can each be wider and surface more info without wrapping.

- Audit the container classes in `internal/web/frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx` (and `AppHeader.tsx` if it sets the page width). Remove fixed `max-w-*` constraints on the dashboard. Header bar can stay as-is.
- Min-width on each column so they don't collapse below readability at 1280px viewport. Use Tailwind's `flex-1` or grid with `minmax(280px, 1fr)`.
- Test at 1280, 1440, 1920, and a wider ultra-wide. No regressions at narrower viewports.

## 3. Queue filter

The Queue pane lists every bead across all anvils. Add a text filter at the top of the pane:

- Single text input. Filter is case-insensitive, matches against `bead_id`, bead title (if available on the QueueItem; if not, extend the response), and labels.
- Empty filter shows all items, same as today.
- Filter state lives in component state (no URL param needed for v1).
- Place the input inside the Pane header, near the existing count badge. Tailwind input styled to match Hearth 2.0's existing dark theme.

If Forge-smhw (grouped queue) has landed by the time this bead is implemented, the filter applies AFTER grouping: groups with no matching items are hidden. Watch for the deps order — if smhw is still open, file this bead's frontend changes accordingly.

## i18n

The frontend doesn't appear to use react-i18next yet; new strings can live inline:
- Queue filter placeholder: "Filter beads (id, title, label)"

## Tests

- `LiveActivity.test.tsx`: assert the most recent event is the first child of the list.
- `QueuePane.test.tsx`: typing into the filter narrows the visible items; empty filter shows all.
- DashboardPage layout: snapshot or class-presence test — no `max-w-*` constraint left on the main container.

## Acceptance

- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (frontend) all pass.
- New events in Live activity appear at the top.
- Dashboard uses the full viewport width; columns wider on big screens.
- Filtering the Queue by typing "Hytte-abc" or "forgeReady" narrows the list in real time.
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Changed).

## Non-goals

- Saved filters or filter history.
- Sort options in the Queue. Default sort stays.
- Sticky pinning of specific live events. Top-prepend covers the actual ask.
- Persisting layout / filter state across reloads.

## Reference

- internal/web/frontend/src/components/LiveActivity.tsx — auto-scroll logic to invert.
- internal/web/frontend/src/components/QueuePane.tsx — Queue rendering; filter input goes inside the Pane header.
- internal/web/frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx — page container; full-width tweak.
- Forge-smhw (open) — grouped queue; coordinate filter behaviour if both land in flight.

title: Hearth 2.0: pipeline visual overview with bellows nested under PR
description:
Hearth 2.0 lacks a visual overview of where each in-flight bead is in the pipeline. Hytte's Mezzanine page shows a horizontal pipeline (Schematic → Smith → Temper → Warden → PR → CI/Review → Merge), with the active bead's current stage highlighted, plus Idle slots where future worker output will appear. Bring that pattern to Hearth 2.0.

## Pipeline bar

Render a horizontal pipeline bar at the top of the dashboard, ABOVE the Queue / Workers / LiveActivity columns. Stages, left to right:

1. Schematic
2. Smith
3. Temper
4. Warden
5. PR (with **Bellows** nested as a sub-state — see below)
6. Merged

Each stage is a small pill showing the count of beads currently in that stage, derived from the workers list (`status` field) and the PR table (PR phase).

Below the pipeline bar, render one row per active in-flight bead with its position marked on the pipeline. Mirror Mezzanine's layout if it's a clean reference.

## Bellows nested under PR

Bellows is a PR-monitor, not a stage that produces a smith log. In Mezzanine it lives under the PR stage as a sub-state ("Bellows: monitoring", "Bellows: ci-fix in progress", etc.). Replicate that in Hearth 2.0:

- Bellows rows should NOT appear as standalone clickable workers in the Workers pane.
- Inside the PR stage of the pipeline bar, show bellows status as a small label/icon: "monitoring", "ci-fix", "review-fix", "rebase".
- Clicking the PR stage opens the PR's detail (deferred to a separate bead if not trivial — at minimum, no log modal).
- The actual bellows-spawned sub-workers (quench, burnish, rebase) DO have logs and stay clickable.

A separate bead Forge-XXXX (filed alongside this one) handles the broader "no log modal for bellows" behaviour change so the two can be reviewed independently. Cross-link there.

## Idle slots

Mezzanine shows N "Idle" placeholder boxes where N = max concurrent workers minus active workers. They give a visual sense of remaining capacity. Replicate:

- Render `max_total_smiths - active_workers` idle slots in the Workers pane.
- Each slot is a dimmed placeholder card; a new worker fills it as soon as it starts.
- Pull `max_total_smiths` from the daemon status response.

## Backend

The current `/api/workers` response should already carry enough state to derive each worker's pipeline position (smith vs bellows vs temper vs warden). If not, extend with a `phase` field (one of: schematic, smith, temper, warden, pr, bellows-mon, bellows-cifix, bellows-reviewfix, bellows-rebase, merged). The pipeline component aggregates client-side.

Check `internal/web/views.go` for the workers list response shape and extend if needed.

## Tests

- Backend: assert the new `phase` field is populated for each worker.
- Frontend: render with a mocked fixture covering one bead in each stage; pipeline bar shows the right counts; bellows row is not in the Workers pane.

## Acceptance

- `make build`, `make test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (frontend) all pass.
- Pipeline bar renders with counts per stage.
- Each in-flight bead has a row showing its current stage.
- Bellows workers do not appear as standalone clickable rows.
- Idle slots appear in the Workers pane equal to remaining capacity.
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Added).

## Non-goals

- Animated stage-transition effects. Static highlight is enough.
- Clicking the pipeline stage to filter the Workers/Queue panes. Could be a follow-up.
- Reorganising the Workers pane internals. This bead adds the pipeline bar + relocates bellows; the existing worker card stays.

## Reference

- web/src/pages/MezzaninePage.tsx and web/src/components/mezzanine/PipelineBar.tsx in the Hytte repo — the visual pattern to mirror. The Hytte source is at /home/robin/source/Hytte for inspiration; do not import code from there.
- internal/web/frontend/src/components/WorkersPane.tsx — current Workers rendering.
- internal/web/views.go — backend workers response; extend if the phase isn't already exposed.
- internal/bellows/ — to understand the bellows sub-state taxonomy (monitoring / ci-fix / review-fix / rebase).

title: Hearth 2.0 bead detail: show deps (blocks / blocked-by) with links + graph view
description:
The Hearth 2.0 BeadDetailPage shows queue/ingot/retry/cost/events/PRs/workers, but not the bead's dependency relationships. Add visibility into what a bead **blocks** and what **blocks it**, plus an optional full-graph view.

## What to show

### 1. Two simple lists on the bead detail page

Below the existing sections, add a "Dependencies" panel with two columns (or stacked on mobile):

- **Blocks** — beads that cannot proceed until this one is closed. Pulled from this bead's own outgoing dependencies of type `blocks`.
- **Blocked by** — beads this one is waiting on. Pulled from incoming dependencies (other beads' `blocks` pointing here, or this bead's `blocks-on` / `discovered-from` deps — depending on the convention used in the codebase; check `bd show`'s JSON output for the actual field name).

Each entry renders as a clickable row: bead ID + short title + status chip (open / in_progress / closed) + priority. Clicking opens the same bead's detail in a **modal** (lightweight — title, description excerpt, status, priority, a "Open full page" link to navigate via router). Inside the modal, the same "Blocks / Blocked by" lists appear so the operator can walk the graph without losing context.

Empty states: "No downstream beads" and "No upstream beads" — but only render the empty state when neither list has anything, to keep the panel compact.

### 2. Optional graph view

Add a "View graph" button on the panel. Clicking opens a full-screen (or large-modal) view that visualises the dependency graph centered on the current bead. Two practical options:

- **Simple**: a level-by-level layered tree using CSS grid or flexbox. No external library. Each node is the same card primitive as the list rows. Edges are drawn with SVG lines between known node positions. Fine for graphs up to ~30 nodes.
- **Richer**: pull in a small graph library — Reaflow, react-flow, or dagre + svg. More polish, more code, more bundle.

Recommend the **simple** approach for v1; bundle size and Forge's existing zero-dependency footprint argue for it. Anyone needing the richer version can follow up with a separate bead.

Graph traversal depth: limit to 3 hops in each direction from the current bead to keep the visual bounded. Add a "Expand" affordance on any node that has further connections off-screen.

## Backend

`beadDetailResponse` (`internal/web/views.go:326`) currently omits deps. Two paths:

1. **Reuse `bd show`** — the IPC layer or the web server can shell out to `bd show <id> --json` (whichever side already has anvil-path resolution). The JSON includes `dependencies` and `dependents` (or whatever the current field names are — see `bd show --help` and the schema in `~/source/Beads` if the user has access). Extract these into new fields on `beadDetailResponse`:

       Blocks    []beadDetailDepRef `json:"blocks"`
       BlockedBy []beadDetailDepRef `json:"blocked_by"`

   Where `beadDetailDepRef` carries `bead_id`, `anvil`, `title`, `status`, `priority`.

2. **Reuse the poller's cached blocks graph** — the daemon already maintains `cachedBlocks` (`internal/daemon/daemon.go` around the polling logic). It only contains "blocks" edges, not full bead metadata. Combined with the queue cache (which has title/status/priority), you can hydrate the refs without an extra shell-out. Faster but only covers beads the poller has seen.

Recommend **option 1** for correctness — `bd show` is the source of truth and handles cross-anvil deps gracefully. Cache the result for ~30s if perf becomes an issue (it won't on a per-detail-page basis).

For the modal's nested data: a small new endpoint `GET /api/bead/{id}/deps?depth=N` returning the same `beadDetailDepRef` shape walked to depth N. Cap N at 3.

## Frontend

- `internal/web/frontend/src/api.ts` — add the new fields to the BeadDetail type plus a `fetchBeadDeps(id, depth)` helper.
- `internal/web/frontend/src/pages/BeadDetailPage.tsx` — render the Dependencies panel with the two lists.
- New component `internal/web/frontend/src/components/BeadDepModal.tsx` — modal that fetches the clicked bead's brief data + nested deps, with a "Open full page" link.
- New component `internal/web/frontend/src/components/DepsGraphView.tsx` — full-graph view triggered by the "View graph" button. SVG + simple layered layout.

## Tests

- Backend: `views_test.go` — assert the new fields are populated for a bead with both inbound and outbound deps, and empty for a bead with neither.
- Frontend: `BeadDetailPage.test.tsx` — renders the lists, opens the modal on click, navigates via the "Open full page" link.
- Graph view: smoke test that it mounts without crash for a 5-node fixture.

## Acceptance

- `make build`, `make test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (frontend) all pass.
- Open the detail page for a bead that blocks one bead and is blocked by another → both lists render with clickable rows.
- Click a row → modal opens with that bead's brief view, including its own deps.
- "Open full page" in the modal navigates to that bead's detail page.
- "View graph" opens a layered view centered on the current bead, edges drawn between nodes.
- Mobile: lists stack; graph view is full-screen.
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Added).

## Non-goals

- Editing deps from the UI — read-only display. Adding/removing deps stays in `bd link` / `bd update`.
- Cross-anvil graph aggregation beyond what `bd show` already provides.
- Dependency cycle detection — beads enforces acyclicity at insert time; the UI trusts that.
- Free-pan/zoom for the graph. Layered static layout is enough for v1.
- Replacing the modal with a sidesheet or split view. Modal is the lightest path.

## Reference

- internal/web/views.go:326 — beadDetailResponse struct; extend with Blocks and BlockedBy fields.
- internal/web/frontend/src/pages/BeadDetailPage.tsx — current page layout.
- internal/web/frontend/src/components/ — existing modal pattern (ConfirmModal) for the style.
- internal/daemon/daemon.go — `cachedBlocks` if you want the poller-graph route (option 2).
- `bd show <id> --json` — the dependency fields available from the source of truth.

title: Hearth 2.0: group queue by anvil and status, collapsed by default
description:
The QueuePane in Hearth 2.0 renders a flat list of all queue items across all anvils. With multiple anvils and dozens of beads, this is hard to scan. Group hierarchically and collapse each group by default.

## Grouping

Two-level grouping:

1. **Anvil** (top level). One section per anvil that has any items. Anvil header shows the anvil name and the total item count across its status buckets.
2. **Status bucket** (second level). Within each anvil, group items into:
    - `Ready` — items where the bead has the anvil's `auto_dispatch_tag` (e.g. `forgeReady`) AND no blocker. The poller will dispatch these.
    - `Unlabeled` — items where the bead is dispatchable by `bd ready` semantics but lacks the auto-dispatch tag. These are candidates for the operator to label, but the daemon won't pick them up automatically.
    - `In progress` — items linked to an active worker (running pipeline). Today the QueuePane doesn't show running beads alongside queue items; the bottom of the queue panel is the natural place for them so the operator sees the full state of an anvil in one section.

Order within each bucket: priority ascending (P0 first), then created_at descending — same as today's flat list.

## Collapsing

Anvil sections collapsed by default. Status buckets inside an anvil are collapsed by default too. Each header shows the count even when collapsed (e.g. "forge ▸ Ready (3)") so the operator can see at a glance where the action is without expanding.

Expand state lives in component state (no localStorage). Persisting across mounts of the page is fine; persisting across full reloads is not required.

If an anvil has zero items across all buckets, omit it entirely. Same for empty status buckets within an expanded anvil.

## Backend

Where the data comes from depends on what the backend already exposes:

- `QueueItem` (`internal/web/frontend/src/api.ts:5`) already has `anvil`, `status`, `labels`, `priority` — sufficient to derive Ready/Unlabeled buckets client-side.
- For `In progress`, the workers list is exposed elsewhere (look at how the WorkersPane fetches active workers). Either:
    - Join client-side: fetch both, render workers under each anvil as a third bucket using the existing worker→anvil mapping.
    - Add a new bucket type to the QueueItem response server-side. Cleaner but more code.

Recommend the client-side join — keeps the backend untouched. If that proves messy, switch to a server-side bucket field.

## i18n / strings

The Hearth 2.0 frontend is a small SPA that doesn't appear to use react-i18next today. Add the new strings in English directly. If an i18n harness is introduced later, retrofit then.

New strings:
- "Ready ({count})"
- "Unlabeled ({count})"
- "In progress ({count})"
- "No queued work for {anvil}" (empty-anvil fallback if you decide to render empty anvils)

## Tests

The frontend test setup uses Vitest. Add `QueuePane.test.tsx` (or extend if it exists) covering:
- Mixed items across anvils render under the right anvil section.
- Items inside an anvil bucket correctly into Ready / Unlabeled / In progress based on labels + worker state.
- All sections start collapsed; click expands.
- Empty bucket is omitted.

## Acceptance

- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` in `internal/web/frontend/` all pass.
- QueuePane shows one collapsed section per anvil; expanding shows three nested collapsed buckets.
- Counts on each header reflect contents.
- Dispatching / retrying / stopping a bead still works (existing actions and ConfirmModal flow unchanged).
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Changed).

## Non-goals

- Sortable column headers per bucket. Default sort is enough.
- Filtering by anvil or status from a toolbar — group expansion is the filter.
- Migrating away from the existing flat QueueItem API.
- Persisting expand state to localStorage.

## Reference

- `internal/web/frontend/src/components/QueuePane.tsx` — current flat list rendering. The 290-line file is the entire target surface.
- `internal/web/frontend/src/api.ts:5` — `QueueItem` shape.
- `internal/web/frontend/src/pages/` — the dashboard page that hosts QueuePane and WorkersPane; the workers fetch lives there and is the source for "In progress" mapping.
- `internal/poller/poller.go` — `auto_dispatch_tag` semantics, for the Ready vs Unlabeled distinction.

title: Daemon: stop emitting per-poll success events; only log on failure
description:
The daemon writes a `poll` event to the events table every time an anvil finishes a successful poll (`internal/daemon/daemon.go:1851`). With multiple anvils on a ~30s poll cycle that's many hundreds of rows per hour, drowning the actually-interesting events (smith_done, warden_pass, ci_failed, etc.) in `forge history events` and on the Mezzanine events panel.

Stop emitting the success variant. Keep `poll_error` so failures stay visible.

## Backend change

`internal/daemon/daemon.go:1847–1853` — drop the else-branch's `d.db.LogEvent(state.EventPoll, ...)` call. The success path becomes a no-op (or just an in-memory timestamp update, see below).

The `EventPoll` constant in `internal/state/db.go:1394` can stay defined (cheap and not worth churning callers), but it should no longer be written to the events table by the daemon. Add a code comment noting that successful polls are tracked in-memory only.

## In-memory last-poll timestamp

`forge status` and the Mezzanine "Last Poll" indicator rely on a query that finds the most recent `poll` or `poll_error` event per anvil — see `state.LastPollPerAnvil` (`internal/state/db.go:1714`) and `LastPollAllAnvils` (`:1776`).

Replace that data source with an in-memory `map[anvil]time.Time` on the daemon, protected by a mutex. Update on every OnAnvilDone callback regardless of outcome. Expose through the existing IPC `status` command's response so `forge status` / Mezzanine read it without hitting SQLite.

The two query functions in `internal/state/db.go` can either:
- Stay and return only `poll_error` rows (clean removal of the success branch — easier).
- Or be removed entirely once the IPC-fed timestamps are wired in.

Recommend keeping them for now and dropping in a small follow-up if there are no remaining callers — minimizes the blast radius of this change.

## Cleanup of existing rows (optional)

Existing rows in events with type='poll' can stay (they're historical and harmless). If they bother the user, a one-off `DELETE FROM events WHERE type='poll'` can be run manually after this lands. Don't bundle the delete with the code change — let the user decide whether to keep the history.

## Tests

- `internal/daemon/daemon_test.go` (or wherever the poll loop is exercised): assert that a successful poll does NOT insert into events; an error poll DOES (one row, type='poll_error').
- `internal/daemon/ipc_test.go` (or equivalent): assert the status response includes the in-memory last-poll timestamp.

## Acceptance

- `make build`, `make test`, `go vet ./...` all pass.
- `forge history events` after a few minutes of running shows only meaningful events — no `poll` rows.
- `forge status` "Last Poll" indicator still works.
- Mezzanine "Last Poll" indicator still works.
- Polling failures continue to appear as `poll_error` rows.
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Changed).

## Non-goals

- Removing the `EventPoll` constant.
- Migrating existing `poll` rows out of the events table.
- Adding new visibility for poll cadence beyond what status already shows.
- Suppressing the `poll complete` log line emitted by `d.logger.Info` (it goes to journal, not the events panel — separate concern; keep as-is for journal debugging).

## Reference

- internal/daemon/daemon.go:1840–1855 — poll-completion callback that emits the events.
- internal/state/db.go:1394 — EventPoll / EventPollError constants.
- internal/state/db.go:1714, 1776 — LastPollPerAnvil / LastPollAllAnvils queries.
- internal/ipc/ — IPC status command shape (extend to carry last-poll timestamps if not already there).

title: CLI: 'forge anvil list' (and other CLI commands) ignore ~/.forge/config.yaml
description:
The Forge CLI commands that load config without `--config` (e.g. `forge anvil list`, `forge anvil add/remove`) only find a config file named `forge.yaml`, but the documented home location and the actual deployed file is `~/.forge/config.yaml`.

Symptom: `forge anvil list` prints "No anvils registered" even when the daemon (started with `--config /home/robin/.forge/config.yaml` from systemd) is happily polling two anvils. Workaround: `forge --config ~/.forge/config.yaml anvil list`.

Root cause: `internal/config/config.go` Load() and ConfigFilePath() use viper's `SetConfigName("forge")` + `AddConfigPath(~/.forge/)`, which searches for `~/.forge/forge.yaml`. The package doc comment and CLAUDE.md both document the home config as `~/.forge/config.yaml`, so doc and code disagree.

## Fix

In `internal/config/config.go` Load() and ConfigFilePath(), in the no-`--config` branch:
1. Try `./forge.yaml` first (working directory) — preserves existing behaviour.
2. Fall back to `~/.forge/config.yaml` (the documented path).
3. Optionally also probe `~/.forge/forge.yaml` for backward compatibility.

Use `os.Stat` + `v.SetConfigFile(...)` rather than `SetConfigName`/`AddConfigPath`, because viper's search-path API only supports one config-name at a time; explicit probing is clearer and matches the documented resolution order verbatim.

Add a test that asserts `Load("")` resolves `$HOME/.forge/config.yaml` when the file exists there (use `t.Setenv("HOME", tmp)` and a fixture).

## Acceptance

- `forge anvil list` (no flag) works on a host where the only config is `~/.forge/config.yaml`.
- Existing tests still pass.
- Documented resolution order in `internal/config/config.go` package doc matches the implementation.
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Fixed).
close_reason: Fixed in 8a118e6, pushed direct to main

title: queue: 'clear' command to dismiss needs-attention without redispatching
description:
`forge queue retry` is the only way to clear `needs_human` from a stuck bead today, but its full behaviour is "reset circuit breaker AND mark for next-poll dispatch". This is a footgun for the common operator workflow:

> The bead is already done (PR merged, work shipped) — I just want it to stop showing up in needs-attention.

The current options force the operator to either:
1. `forge queue retry` and immediately `forge queue stop` (race against the next 30-second poll cycle).
2. UPDATE the retries table directly via sqlite3.
3. `bd close` the bead first, then retry (still races against poll, since `bd close` propagation lags Forge's local state).

Today's incident: Forge-zyi1 was bd-closed and then `forge queue retry`-ed to clear needs-attention. Forge's poll fired ~20s later, before `bd close` was visible to the daemon's snapshot, dispatched the bead again, started schematic + opus-4-7 smith iter 1 (~$0.10 already burned by the time it was caught), required `forge queue stop` to halt.

## Add: `forge queue clear`

Behaviour:
- Clears `needs_human`, `dispatch_failures`, `recovery_failures`, `last_error` for the named bead.
- Does NOT trigger or schedule a dispatch.
- Does NOT set `clarification_needed=1` (so the bead is not blocked from being legitimately picked up by `bd ready` if it is genuinely re-opened later).
- Idempotent — running on a row that is already clean is a no-op success.
- Same flag set as `retry` (`-a/--anvil` required for disambiguation).

Pseudocode:

    UPDATE retries
       SET needs_human = 0,
           dispatch_failures = 0,
           recovery_failures = 0,
           first_recovery_failure_at = NULL,
           last_error = '',
           updated_at = ?
     WHERE bead_id = ? AND anvil = ?;

Emit a `retry_cleared` event so the history log distinguishes this from a retry-triggered redispatch.

## Help text and docs

- Update `forge queue --help` ordering: `clear` near `retry` and `stop`, with one-liners that contrast them clearly:
    - `retry` — Reset the circuit breaker and re-dispatch the bead on the next poll.
    - `stop` — Fully stop a bead: kill worker, prevent re-dispatch, release to open.
    - `clear` — Clear the needs-attention flags without re-dispatching.
- Mention `clear` in the README/CLAUDE.md operator docs section about unsticking beads.

## Tests

- Unit test: `clear` zeros all the right columns and does not enqueue.
- Unit test: idempotency — second invocation succeeds with no-op.
- Unit test: an unrelated bead's row is not touched.
- Integration test (or note): after `clear`, the next poll does NOT pick up the bead unless `bd ready` legitimately surfaces it.

## Acceptance

- `make build`, `make test` pass.
- `forge queue clear <id> -a <anvil>` works as specified.
- README and `forge queue --help` updated to distinguish the three commands.
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Added).

## Reference

- Existing `retry` command for the closest pattern.
- `internal/store/retries.go` (or equivalent — search for `UPDATE retries`) for the write path.
- Today's Forge-zyi1 sequence in `~/.forge/state.db` events table illustrates the footgun (`retry_reset` followed by an unwanted `bead_claimed`).

title: PR poller: needs_fix → merged transition not detected
description:
PR rows that get stuck in `status='needs_fix'` are not transitioned to `'merged'` when the underlying GitHub PR is later merged (e.g. via "approve as-is" from Mezzanine, or a human merging directly on GitHub).

## Reproduction

Hytte PR #672 — Mezzanine showed the PR as still-open for ~2 days after merge. State DB on 2026-05-07T20:05:32:

    sqlite> SELECT number, status, last_checked, title FROM prs WHERE id=392;
    672|needs_fix|2026-05-07T20:05:32|'+ New suggestion' modal/form with validation and submit (Hytte-ym34)

GitHub view at the same instant:

    $ gh pr view 672 --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit
    {"state":"MERGED","mergedAt":"2026-05-05T14:36:20Z","mergeCommit":{"oid":"ccdee781..."}}

Forge polled the PR (last_checked is current) but did not change `status` from `needs_fix` to `merged`. All 25 other Hytte PRs in the same window were fine — they went `open → merged` directly. Only this one had been bounced into `needs_fix` by review (`review_fix_count=5`) before the human merged it as-is.

A one-shot DB UPDATE was used to clear the visible symptom (`UPDATE prs SET status='merged' WHERE id=392`).

## Hypothesis

The PR poller in `internal/forge/github_prs.go` (or the bellows/PR-management package — search wherever the prs table is written) likely has a state machine that allows `open → merged` and `open → needs_fix` and `needs_fix → open`, but is missing or guarding `needs_fix → merged`. Possibly an early-return that says "skip merged-detection for PRs that need fixing" — under the assumption that a needs_fix PR will get a new commit before being mergeable, which doesn't account for the human-bypass path.

## Scope

- Audit the PR-status transition logic. Allow merged-detection regardless of current local status. The source of truth is GitHub; the local `needs_fix` flag is advisory only and must not block recognising a real merge.
- Same audit for `closed` (PR closed without merging while in needs_fix) — that transition may have the same bug.
- Add a unit test that simulates a PR going `open → needs_fix → merged` and asserts the local state ends at `merged`.
- One-line backfill on startup: any PR row whose state on GitHub is MERGED but local status != 'merged' gets corrected. Cheap belt-and-braces; does not require waiting for the next normal poll cycle.

## Acceptance

- The poller updates `needs_fix` → `merged` when GitHub reports MERGED.
- The poller updates `needs_fix` → `closed` when GitHub reports CLOSED-not-merged.
- Test covers `needs_fix → merged` via `mergedAt` non-null.
- No regression to the existing `open → needs_fix` flow when CI/review fails.
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Fixed).

## Reference

- `~/.forge/state.db` `prs` table — schema and example bad row above.
- `internal/forge/github_prs.go` (Hytte side) reads from this table; for the writer, search the Forge repo for `UPDATE prs SET status` and `INSERT INTO prs`.
- PR #672 = Hytte-ym34 = id 392 in the prs table — already manually fixed; useful as the reference case.

title: Always defer bead close until PR merges, regardless of dependency graph shape
acceptance_criteria: A pipeline run that produces a successful PR for a bead with deps=[]/dependents=[] does NOT close the bead. Daemon log shows the same 'deferring close until PR merges' line as the dependents-bearing case. The bead closes only when the merge watcher fires after the PR is merged. Existing merge-close path is unchanged.

title: Package updates starting 28.04.2026
description:
Automated dependency updates for forge:

go: github.com/fsnotify/fsnotify v1.9.0→v1.10.0, modernc.org/sqlite v1.49.1→v1.50.0

title: End-to-end verification on a clean Windows machine
description: After a signed release is published, download forge via install.ps1 on a fresh Windows 10/11 VM with default Defender settings and verify: (a) no Defender quarantine or SmartScreen warning, (b) signature is valid via `Get-AuthenticodeSignature forge.exe`, (c) publisher matches the SSL.com certificate subject. Document the test procedure in the release runbook. Depends on the prior three sub-tasks; closes the loop on the bead's success criterion ('no Defender warning').

title: Add Unblock-File workaround to install.ps1
description: Modify install.ps1 to call Unblock-File on the downloaded forge.exe after extraction. This removes the Zone.Identifier NTFS stream that triggers Defender scanning. Add the call after the binary is extracted/moved to its final location, wrapped in a try/catch so the installer continues if Unblock-File fails. This is the immediate no-cost mitigation and is independent of the signing work — it should ship first as a stopgap. Test by running install.ps1 on a fresh Windows machine and confirming reduced Defender interaction.

title: Add Windows binary signing step to release.yml workflow
description: Modify .github/workflows/release.yml to sign the Windows binary after build and before the zip is uploaded to the GitHub release. Use osslsigncode on the existing Linux runner (avoids adding a Windows runner): install osslsigncode via apt, decode CODE_SIGNING_CERT from base64 into a .pfx file, run `osslsigncode sign -pkcs12 cert.pfx -pass $CERT_PASSWORD -n 'Forge' -i <project-url> -t http://timestamp.sectigo.com -in forge.exe -out forge-signed.exe`, then repackage into forge_*_windows_*.zip. Consumes the secrets from the procurement sub-task. Verify the signature with `osslsigncode verify` in the same job.

title: Procure SSL.com OV code signing certificate and store as GitHub secrets
description: Purchase an SSL.com OV code signing certificate (~$70/year, recommended option from bead). Export the certificate as a password-protected .pfx file, base64-encode it, and store it as GitHub repository secret CODE_SIGNING_CERT along with CERT_PASSWORD. Document the renewal process and expiry date in a short note (e.g., in .github/workflows/README or a RELEASING doc). This is a prerequisite for the CI signing sub-task — no code changes, but blocks the workflow update.

title: Pipeline doesn't release bd claim on temper exhaustion, defers to orphan recovery
description: When the pipeline gives up after temper iterations are exhausted (pipeline.go:1309), it calls recordDispatchFailure (daemon.go:2234-2235) which only increments a state.db counter -- it does not call 'bd update --status=open' to release the bead claim. The bead stays in_progress in bd with an assignee but no worker row, which makes it a true orphan from bd's perspective. Orphan recovery then has to clean it up 1-2 minutes later on the next periodic scan. This is wasteful and adds latency before the bead becomes available again, and it depends on orphan recovery's bd-update path working correctly (see Forge-4omg for a recent failure of that path). Suggested fix: the dispatch-failure cleanup path in daemon.go should call bd update directly to release the claim and strip forgeReady label, and only fall back to orphan recovery for true crashes/process kills. Lower priority than Forge-4omg because it is a design wart, not a hard failure.

title: Temper: npm ci incompatible with node_modules junctions on Windows
description: After Forge-jqyw (node_modules junction) shipped, temper steps running npm ci in a worktree fail intermittently with Windows EPERM. The junction resolves to the main checkout's node_modules and npm ci does rm -rf node_modules which locks on native .node binaries held by IDE/antivirus/dev-server. Seen on Heimdall-lmxx retry: client-install failed 4.2s with EPERM on tailwindcss-oxide.win32-x64-msvc.node. Even when rm succeeds, outcome is wiping main node_modules or creating worktree-local node_modules (redundant with junction). Forge could detect junction at temper step start and refuse destructive install commands, or warn in docs that npm ci should not be used in temper when worktree junctions are active. Primary guidance: npm ci redundant, don't add to temper steps when using forge worktrees.

title: Pipeline: last-chance bd show lookup for external_ref before PR creation
description:
Follow-up to Forge-pqrw (PR #522, merged). The current fix passes external_ref from the poller through to the Smith prompt template, so Smith can include Closes #N in the PR body. But if external_ref is empty at dispatch time (e.g. github autosync hasn't run yet, or bead was created locally), the template line is suppressed and Smith creates a PR without Closes #N.

Fix: in the pipeline's PR creation step (after Smith and Warden approve, right before gh pr create), do a one-shot bd show <bead-id> --json to fetch the latest external_ref. If present, inject Closes #N into the PR body. This costs ~1 second and guarantees the freshest data is used regardless of what was available at dispatch time.

This is defense in depth — the primary path (external_ref in prompt) handles 99% of cases, but this catch-all ensures no PR ships without Closes #N when a GitHub issue exists.

title: Worktree: auto-junction client/node_modules from main checkout
description: After git worktree add, create a Windows junction from worktree client/node_modules to main checkout client/node_modules. Eliminates npm ci in temper. See forgeLocal/node-modules-junction-worktree.md for full design.

title: Temper: skip steps when changed files don't match a configurable glob filter
description:
## Problem

Temper runs ALL configured steps on every pipeline run, regardless of which files were changed. A frontend-only PR still runs `dotnet build` and `dotnet test`; a backend-only PR still runs `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, and `npm run build`. On repos with both .NET and Node.js this wastes minutes per run on steps that can't possibly fail.

## Proposed fix

Add an optional `glob` (or `paths`) field to each temper step definition. When set, temper checks the Smith diff (files changed vs base branch) against the glob patterns and skips the step if no changed files match.

Example config:

```yaml
temper:
  steps:
    - name: client-lint
      command: npm
      args: [run, lint]
      dir: client
      paths: ["client/**"]
    - name: client-typecheck
      command: npm
      args: [run, typecheck]
      dir: client
      paths: ["client/**"]
    - name: api-build
      command: dotnet
      args: [build, -c, Release]
      dir: api
      paths: ["api/**"]
    - name: api-test
      command: dotnet
      args: [test, -c, Release, --no-build, -v=q]
      dir: api
      paths: ["api/**"]
```

Behavior:
- If `paths` is omitted or empty: step always runs (current behavior, fully backward compatible)
- If `paths` is set: temper computes the changed-file list (git diff against base branch), matches each file against the glob patterns, and skips the step if zero files match — logging "skipped: no matching changed files" so the operator knows why
- Glob syntax should match gitignore/doublestar patterns (`**` for recursive, `*.cs` for extension, etc.)

## Implementation notes

- The diff file list is already available in the pipeline context (Smith produces it, and warden uses it). Temper just needs to receive it or compute it via `git diff --name-only <base>..HEAD`.
- Use Go's `doublestar` package (or `filepath.Match` if patterns are simple enough) for glob matching.
- The step-skip decision should be logged clearly so users can debug unexpected skips.
- For auto-detected steps (when no custom temper config exists), `paths` would not be set and all steps run as today — no behavior change for the default case.

title: Support arbitrary named steps in per-anvil temper config (temper.steps)
description:
## Problem

Per-anvil temper configuration exposes exactly three named slots: `build`, `test`, `lint` (`internal/config/config.go:171-183`, `internal/temper/temper.go:141-183`). This shape can't express common real-world workflows without resorting to wrapper scripts:

**Example: typical Node.js CI pipeline**

CI runs, in order: `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:run`. That's five steps (six if you count `npm ci`). Temper has three slots. A user has to either:

1. Write a `scripts/temper.sh` wrapper that chains them all, and point `build:` at it. The wrapper is an extra file to maintain in the anvil repo and duplicates whatever the CI workflow already does — inviting drift.
2. Abuse slots: put `npm run typecheck` in `test:`, `npm run lint` in `lint:` (which is secretly optional — see Forge-bead-2), etc. Misleading and fragile.
3. Use pipeline hooks (`before_temper`) to do `npm ci`, then use the three slots for three of the five commands, and skip the rest. Incomplete coverage.

**Example: Python/Rust/Go mixed anvil**

A repo with both a Go backend and a Python SDK in `sdk/` wants to run `go build`, `go vet`, `go test`, `cd sdk && pytest`, and `cd sdk && ruff check`. Five steps with distinct working directories. The current three-slot form can't represent the `dir` parameter at all — `ConfigFromCommands` doesn't expose `Step.Dir`, even though the underlying `Step` struct supports it (`temper.go:64-68`).

**Example: make-based project with multiple targets**

A project that uses `make build`, `make test`, `make lint`, `make integration-test` maps cleanly onto the existing slots — until it also needs `make vet` or `make format-check`. Back to wrapper-script land.

## Fix

Add a `steps` field to `TemperCommandsConfig` that accepts an ordered list of named steps with per-step options. Keep the existing three slots (`build`, `test`, `lint`) working for backwards compatibility.

### Config shape

```yaml
anvils:
  my-node-app:
    path: /home/user/source/my-node-app
    temper:
      steps:
        - name: install
          command: npm
          args: [ci]
          dir: web
          timeout: 5m
          required: true
        - name: lint
          command: npm
          args: [run, lint]
          dir: web
          required: true
        - name: typecheck
          command: npm
          args: [run, typecheck]
          dir: web
          required: true
        - name: build
          command: npm
          args: [run, build]
          dir: web
          required: true
        - name: test
          command: npm
          args: [run, test:run]
          dir: web
          required: true
```

### Field semantics

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | **required** | Step identifier; appears in logs, summaries, and failure events. Must be non-empty. |
| `command` | string | **required** | Executable (not shell-interpreted). For shell features, wrap in a checked-in script. |
| `args` | `[]string` | `[]` | Arguments to the command. Use list form; avoid embedding in `command`. |
| `dir` | string | worktree root | Working directory for the step. Relative paths resolve against the worktree; absolute paths used as-is (same semantics as `Step.Dir` in `temper.go:64-68`). |
| `timeout` | duration | `5m` | Per-step timeout. Same parsing as elsewhere in Forge config (`5m`, `30s`, `1h`). |
| `required` | bool | `true` | When `true`, failure fails the whole temper run. When `false`, failure is reported as a warning (equivalent to today's `Optional: true`). **Note the flipped default vs. the current `lint:` slot** — in the steps list, steps default to *required*, matching the principle of least surprise. |

### Back-compat rules

- If `temper.steps` is set and non-empty, it takes precedence over `temper.build` / `temper.test` / `temper.lint`. Log a warning if both are present ("temper.steps overrides temper.build/test/lint") so users migrating don't get silent surprises.
- If `temper.steps` is unset, the existing three-slot code path runs unchanged (`ConfigFromCommands`).
- Auto-detection still applies when **neither** steps nor the three slots are set.

### Implementation sketch

1. **`internal/config/config.go`** — add to `TemperCommandsConfig`:

   ```go
   type TemperCommandsConfig struct {
       Build        string              `mapstructure:"build" yaml:"build,omitempty"`
       Test         string              `mapstructure:"test" yaml:"test,omitempty"`
       Lint         string              `mapstructure:"lint" yaml:"lint,omitempty"`
       LintRequired bool                `mapstructure:"lint_required" yaml:"lint_required,omitempty"` // added by Forge-lsj4
       Steps        []TemperStepConfig  `mapstructure:"steps" yaml:"steps,omitempty"`
   }

   type TemperStepConfig struct {
       Name     string        `mapstructure:"name" yaml:"name"`
       Command  string        `mapstructure:"command" yaml:"command"`
       Args     []string      `mapstructure:"args" yaml:"args,omitempty"`
       Dir      string        `mapstructure:"dir" yaml:"dir,omitempty"`
       Timeout  time.Duration `mapstructure:"timeout" yaml:"timeout,omitempty"`
       Required *bool         `mapstructure:"required" yaml:"required,omitempty"` // pointer so we can distinguish unset from false; unset = true
   }
   ```

   Update `TemperCommandsConfig.IsEmpty()` at `:181` to also return false when `Steps` is non-empty.

2. **`internal/temper/temper.go`** — add `ConfigFromSteps([]TemperStepConfig) *Config` that converts each `TemperStepConfig` into a `temper.Step`. Handle the `Required` pointer: unset or `*true` → `Optional: false`, `*false` → `Optional: true`. Default `Timeout` to `5 * time.Minute` when zero. Default `Dir` empty (worktree root).

3. **`internal/daemon/daemon.go:4538-4543`** — update `resolveTemperConfig`:

   ```go
   func (d *Daemon) resolveTemperConfig(anvilCfg config.AnvilConfig) *temper.Config {
       if anvilCfg.Temper == nil || anvilCfg.Temper.IsEmpty() {
           return nil
       }
       if len(anvilCfg.Temper.Steps) > 0 {
           if anvilCfg.Temper.Build != "" || anvilCfg.Temper.Test != "" || anvilCfg.Temper.Lint != "" {
               d.logger.Warn("temper.steps overrides temper.build/test/lint for anvil", "anvil", anvilCfg.Name)
           }
           return temper.ConfigFromSteps(anvilCfg.Temper.Steps)
       }
       return temper.ConfigFromCommands(anvilCfg.Temper.Build, anvilCfg.Temper.Test, anvilCfg.Temper.Lint, anvilCfg.Temper.LintRequired)
   }
   ```

4. **Validation** — in `config.go` `Config.Validate()`, for each step: name non-empty, command non-empty, no two steps share the same name (keeps logs unambiguous). Surface errors at daemon startup with the `settings.temper.steps[i]` path.

## Tests

- **`internal/temper/temper_test.go`**:
  - `TestConfigFromSteps_BasicOrdering`: three steps, verify they appear in the output Config in input order.
  - `TestConfigFromSteps_RequiredDefault_True`: step without `required` field → `Optional: false` in output.
  - `TestConfigFromSteps_RequiredFalse_Optional`: step with `required: false` → `Optional: true`.
  - `TestConfigFromSteps_RespectsDir`: step with `dir: web` → `Step.Dir == "web"`.
  - `TestConfigFromSteps_RespectsTimeout`: step with `timeout: 10m` → `Step.Timeout == 10 * time.Minute`.
  - `TestConfigFromSteps_DefaultTimeout`: step with no `timeout` → `Step.Timeout == 5 * time.Minute`.
  - `TestConfigFromSteps_EmptyList_ReturnsNil`: empty slice → nil Config (caller falls back to auto-detection).
  - `TestConfigFromSteps_StopsOnRequiredFailure`: integration-ish — run a Config with three steps where the middle one is required and fails; assert the third step never executes. (Temper's `Run` loop already does this; this test pins the contract.)

- **`internal/config/config_test.go`**:
  - Yaml round-trip test covering a full `temper.steps` block with all optional fields set and unset.
  - Validation test: missing `name` → validation error.
  - Validation test: duplicate step names → validation error.

- **`internal/daemon/daemon_test.go`**:
  - `TestResolveTemperConfig_StepsOverridesSlots`: set both `steps` and `build`, assert `ConfigFromSteps` is used and a warning is logged (capture via test logger).

## Docs

Update `docs/configuration.md` — this is the most important part of the bead because the whole point of filing Forge-w8rb/lsj4/this is so the user can copy-paste from the docs.

### Custom Temper Commands section (`docs/configuration.md:239-275`)

Rewrite/expand the existing section to cover both forms:

1. **Shorthand (existing)**: keep the current `build`/`test`/`lint` table and examples. Add a sentence: "Use the shorthand when your project has a straightforward build→test→lint shape. For more complex pipelines, use the `steps` list below."

2. **New subsection: "Custom Temper Steps (advanced)"** — covers the `steps` form. Include:
   - The field table (copy from the Field semantics table above).
   - At least **four** copy-ready example blocks under a `### Examples` heading:

     **Example A — Node.js matching CI exactly**
     ```yaml
     anvils:
       my-node-app:
         path: /home/user/source/my-node-app
         temper:
           steps:
             - name: install
               command: npm
               args: [ci]
               dir: web
               timeout: 5m
             - name: lint
               command: npm
               args: [run, lint]
               dir: web
             - name: typecheck
               command: npm
               args: [run, typecheck]
               dir: web
             - name: build
               command: npm
               args: [run, build]
               dir: web
             - name: test
               command: npm
               args: [run, test:run]
               dir: web
     ```

     **Example B — Go + Node mixed monorepo** (e.g. Hytte-style)
     ```yaml
     anvils:
       hytte:
         path: /home/user/source/Hytte
         temper:
           steps:
             - name: go-build
               command: go
               args: [build, ./...]
             - name: go-vet
               command: go
               args: [vet, ./...]
             - name: go-test
               command: go
               args: [test, -short, ./...]
             - name: npm-install
               command: npm
               args: [ci]
               dir: web
               timeout: 5m
             - name: npm-lint
               command: npm
               args: [run, lint]
               dir: web
             - name: npm-build
               command: npm
               args: [run, build]
               dir: web
     ```

     **Example C — .NET with analyzers and format check**
     ```yaml
     anvils:
       my-dotnet-app:
         path: C:\\src\\my-dotnet-app
         temper:
           steps:
             - name: restore
               command: dotnet
               args: [restore]
             - name: format
               command: dotnet
               args: [format, --verify-no-changes, --no-restore]
             - name: build
               command: dotnet
               args: [build, --configuration, Release, --no-restore]
               timeout: 10m
             - name: test
               command: dotnet
               args: [test, --configuration, Release, --no-build, --logger, "trx;LogFileName=test.trx"]
               timeout: 15m
     ```

     **Example D — Python with advisory step**
     ```yaml
     anvils:
       my-python-lib:
         path: /home/user/source/my-python-lib
         temper:
           steps:
             - name: install
               command: pip
               args: [install, -e, ".[dev]"]
             - name: ruff
               command: ruff
               args: [check, .]
             - name: mypy
               command: mypy
               args: [src]
               required: false   # advisory — warn but don't block
             - name: test
               command: pytest
               args: [-q]
     ```

3. **Cross-reference** to the Pipeline Hooks section (`:169`) in case users want `before_temper` to run one-shot setup that persists across temper invocations (after Forge-w8rb lands).

### Full Example section (`docs/configuration.md:11-112`)

Add a `temper.steps` block to one of the existing example anvils (probably `my-frontend`, since it's the natural fit for the Node.js example):

```yaml
  my-frontend:
    path: /path/to/repos/my-frontend
    platform: gitlab
    max_smiths: 3
    auto_dispatch: tagged
    auto_dispatch_tag: forge-auto
    temper:
      steps:
        - { name: install,   command: npm, args: [ci],             dir: web, timeout: 5m }
        - { name: lint,      command: npm, args: [run, lint],      dir: web }
        - { name: typecheck, command: npm, args: [run, typecheck], dir: web }
        - { name: build,     command: npm, args: [run, build],     dir: web }
        - { name: test,      command: npm, args: [run, test:run],  dir: web }
```

The flow style (`{ key: value, ... }`) keeps the Full Example compact. The expanded block form lives in the Custom Temper Steps subsection for readability.

## Chain context

This bead lands **after** Forge-lsj4 (lint_required flag). The `steps` form supersedes the need for `lint_required` — each step has its own `required` flag. Landing them in this order means:

1. Forge-w8rb: hooks work uniformly (unlocks the `before_temper: npm ci` trick everywhere).
2. Forge-lsj4: quick incremental win for users who just want to enforce lint without migrating.
3. **This bead**: proper fix. Users on the `steps` form get per-step control and no longer need `lint_required` at all.

Keep `lint_required` as-is in this bead (don't deprecate or remove it) — the shorthand form and `lint_required` together are still the lowest-ceremony option for simple projects.

## Out of scope

- Deprecating or removing the `build`/`test`/`lint` shorthand. They stay.
- Supporting step parallelism (`parallel: true` on a step). Temper runs steps sequentially by design so failed step summaries are deterministic. Can be a follow-up bead.
- Step-level environment variable overrides (`env: { FOO: bar }`). Users can set env in `before_temper` hooks or via wrapper scripts. Can be a follow-up bead.
- Cross-step dependencies / DAG ordering. Sequential in config order is sufficient for all known use cases.
- Moving `temper.steps` into the per-repo `.forge/temper.yaml` file (currently that file only supports `go_race_detection`). Worth considering but a separate bead — it has config-location implications that deserve their own design discussion.

## Files touched

- `internal/config/config.go` — `TemperCommandsConfig.Steps`, new `TemperStepConfig` type, validation, `IsEmpty` update
- `internal/config/config_test.go` — yaml round-trip + validation tests
- `internal/temper/temper.go` — new `ConfigFromSteps` function
- `internal/temper/temper_test.go` — new tests for `ConfigFromSteps`
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go:4538-4543` — `resolveTemperConfig` dispatch logic
- `internal/daemon/daemon_test.go` — `resolveTemperConfig` precedence test
- `docs/configuration.md` — Custom Temper Commands section expansion, Full Example update
- `changelog.d/Forge-<id>.md` — Added category fragment

## Acceptance criteria

- A config with `temper.steps` defined runs each step in input order, fails the temper run on the first required step failure, and emits `temper_failed` with the failed step name.
- A step with `required: false` that fails is reported as a warning in the temper summary and does not fail the run.
- Both `temper.steps` and the legacy `temper.build`/`test`/`lint` shorthand can be used on different anvils in the same config file.
- Setting both `temper.steps` and any shorthand field on the same anvil logs a warning at daemon startup and uses `steps`.
- `docs/configuration.md` Custom Temper Commands section contains a `steps` subsection with at least four copy-ready examples (Node-only, Go+Node, .NET, Python).
- The Full Example at the top of `docs/configuration.md` demonstrates `temper.steps` on at least one anvil.

title: Allow temper.lint to be configured as a required (non-optional) step
description:
## Problem

`temper.ConfigFromCommands` at `internal/temper/temper.go:163-172` unconditionally marks the `lint` step as `Optional: true`:

```go
if lint != "" {
    cmd, args := splitCommand(lint)
    steps = append(steps, Step{
        Name:     "lint",
        Command:  cmd,
        Args:     args,
        Timeout:  3 * time.Minute,
        Optional: true,  // ← hardcoded
    })
}
```

An optional step that fails is reported as a "warning" and **does not** fail `Result.Passed`. The practical consequence: a user who configures `temper.lint: "npm run lint"` expecting parity with CI discovers that when lint actually fails, temper reports "All required checks passed in X.Xs (1 optional step(s) warned)", burnish happily pushes the broken commit, and CI catches what temper refused to. This is the *exact* failure pattern that motivated Forge-syrn (the push-gating fix) — but the hardcoded Optional flag re-opens the same hole through a config misunderstanding.

The only workarounds today are:

1. Abuse the `build:` slot (put the lint command there) — makes the slot name misleading and precludes an actual build command.
2. Write a wrapper script that combines build+lint+test+typecheck and point `build:` at it — works but punts the problem to the user.

Neither is discoverable. A user reading `docs/configuration.md:239-275` has no reason to expect that `lint:` is silently treated as a warning.

## Fix

Add an explicit opt-in to make the configured lint command required. Two implementation choices:

### Option A (minimal, back-compat default)

Add a single bool field to `TemperCommandsConfig` in `internal/config/config.go:171-183`:

```go
type TemperCommandsConfig struct {
    Build        string `mapstructure:"build" yaml:"build,omitempty"`
    Test         string `mapstructure:"test" yaml:"test,omitempty"`
    Lint         string `mapstructure:"lint" yaml:"lint,omitempty"`
    LintRequired bool   `mapstructure:"lint_required" yaml:"lint_required,omitempty"`
}
```

Default: `false` (preserves current behavior for existing configs).

Thread it through `ConfigFromCommands(build, test, lint)` → `ConfigFromCommandsV2(build, test, lint string, lintRequired bool)` (or just modify the existing function — it's only called from `daemon.go:4542`, so no external breakage). In the resulting step, set `Optional: !lintRequired`.

### Option B (richer, slightly more invasive)

Promote each slot to an object form with per-step options:

```yaml
temper:
  build: "go build ./..."         # shorthand, stays required
  test: "go test ./..."
  lint:
    command: "golangci-lint run ./..."
    required: true
    timeout: 5m
```

Requires custom unmarshal to accept both the string shorthand and the object form. Same pattern as how Go projects often handle multi-shape YAML fields. A bit more code.

**Recommend Option A.** It's 15 lines of code total, is a strict superset of current capability, and Forge-bead-3 (arbitrary steps list) will handle the richer case anyway — no point building Option B as an intermediate state.

## Tests

`internal/temper/temper_test.go` — add:

- `TestConfigFromCommands_LintRequired_True`: pass `lintRequired=true`, assert the lint step in the returned Config has `Optional: false`.
- `TestConfigFromCommands_LintRequired_False_PreservesDefault`: pass `lintRequired=false`, assert `Optional: true` (back-compat).
- `TestConfigFromCommands_LintRequired_EmptyLint_NoStep`: when `lint` is empty, `lintRequired` has no effect (no step is added).
- Existing tests should not need changes beyond possibly updating the signature.

`internal/config/config_test.go` — add yaml round-trip test covering `lint_required: true` parses correctly.

## Docs

Update `docs/configuration.md`:

- **Custom Temper Commands table** (`docs/configuration.md:243-247`): add a row:
  | `temper.lint_required` | bool | `false` | When `true`, failures in `temper.lint` fail the temper run instead of warning. Default matches legacy behavior where lint is an advisory-only step. |

- **Surrounding paragraph** at line 247: update the existing description of `temper.lint` from "Runs as an optional step (failure warns but doesn't block)." to "Runs as an optional step by default (failure warns but doesn't block). Set `lint_required: true` to make lint failures fail the temper run."

- **Custom Temper Commands examples** (`docs/configuration.md:253-275`): add one example block using `lint_required: true` so the user can copy-paste:

  ```yaml
  anvils:
    strict-node-app:
      path: /home/user/source/strict-node-app
      temper:
        build: "npm run build"
        test:  "npm run test:run"
        lint:  "npm run lint"
        lint_required: true   # make lint failures fail the temper run, matching CI
  ```

- **Full Example section** (`docs/configuration.md:11-112`): no change needed unless you want to add a temper block to one of the example anvils. Leave as-is to keep the example compact.

## Chain context

This bead is ordered to land **after** Forge-w8rb (hooks in burnish/quench) because hooks landing first means users who set `lint_required: true` will have working hooks to complement it. No hard technical dependency — the two changes touch different files. Ordering is for predictable rollout.

This bead is ordered to land **before** Forge-bead-3 (arbitrary steps list) because the steps-list form makes `lint_required` obsolete — each step in the list has its own `required` flag. Landing lint_required first gives users an immediate, low-risk win while the bigger steps-list change is in review.

## Files touched

- `internal/temper/temper.go` — `ConfigFromCommands` signature + step generation
- `internal/temper/temper_test.go` — new tests
- `internal/config/config.go` — `TemperCommandsConfig.LintRequired` field
- `internal/config/config_test.go` — yaml round-trip test
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go:4542` — pass the new field to `ConfigFromCommands`
- `docs/configuration.md` — table row, description, example
- `changelog.d/Forge-<id>.md` — Added category fragment

## Acceptance criteria

- A config with `temper.lint: "false-positive-lint"` and `temper.lint_required: true` fails the temper run when the lint command exits non-zero.
- A config with `temper.lint: "false-positive-lint"` and `lint_required` unset or false continues to warn without failing (back-compat).
- `docs/configuration.md` Custom Temper Commands section includes a `lint_required` row and at least one example with `lint_required: true`.

title: Settings page: reorganize sections into logical groups
description:
The Settings page has too many small collapsible sections that should be consolidated into logical groups. Currently 11+ sections — many are just 1-2 fields.

## Current sections
1. Profile (name, email, picture)
2. Appearance (theme)
3. Language (locale)
4. Location (home location, weather location)
5. Training (HR zones, threshold, max HR, resting HR, pace settings, Stride custom prompt)
6. Goal Race (race name, date, distance, target time)
7. Notifications (push, quiet hours, filters)
8. Sessions (active sessions, revoke)
9. Integrations (Wordfeud, Netatmo, Google Calendar)
10. AI Prompts (custom prompts for analysis, insights etc.)
11. Possibly more (danger zone, account deletion)

## Proposed reorganization

**Profile** — merge Profile + Appearance + Language + Location into one section. These are all personal/display preferences: name, picture, theme, language, home location.

**Training** — merge Training + Goal Race into one section. Goal race is part of training context. Also includes Stride custom prompt, HR zones, threshold settings.

**AI & Automation** — merge AI Prompts into this. Or keep separate if it's long enough.

**Notifications** — keep as-is, it's already substantial.

**Integrations** — keep as-is (Wordfeud, Netatmo, Calendar credentials).

**Security** — merge Sessions + account deletion/danger zone.

Target: 5-6 groups instead of 11+. Each group should have enough content to justify its own section but not be so granular that the page feels like a long list of tiny accordions.

## Files
- web/src/pages/Settings.tsx — restructure CollapsibleSection usage
- web/public/locales/{en,nb,th}/settings.json or common.json — update section headings

title: Stride nightly evaluation: report on rest days and missed sessions
description:
The nightly evaluation only runs when new workouts are uploaded. On rest days or missed training days, it does nothing. It should also evaluate days with no workout:

## Rest day compliance
If today was a planned rest day and no workout was uploaded: report 'Rest day taken as planned — good recovery.'

## Missed session
If today had a planned session but no workout was uploaded: report 'Planned [session type] was not completed. Consider adjusting the remaining week if needed.'

## Implementation

In stride.RunNightlyEvaluation (internal/stride/evaluate.go):
1. After evaluating new workouts, also check the current plan for today's date
2. If today was a rest day with no workout → create an evaluation with compliance='rest_day'
3. If today had a planned session with no matching workout → create evaluation with compliance='missed'
4. Call Claude for a brief comment on rest days and missed sessions, or use a template (no AI needed for simple cases)

The evaluation should show on the Stride page so the user sees daily feedback even on off days.

## Files
- internal/stride/evaluate.go — RunNightlyEvaluation, add rest day/missed session checks
- internal/stride/match.go — may need a function to check if a date has an unmatched planned session

title: Smith deny patterns for files and commands
description:
Add per-anvil file and command deny lists to prevent Smith from modifying sensitive files or running dangerous commands. Enforced via post-Smith diff validation in the pipeline (hard enforcement).

Example config:
anvils:
  myrepo:
    smith:
      deny_patterns:
        files: ['*.env', '.forge/*', '*.key', '*.pem']
        commands: ['rm -rf /', 'git push --force*']

Implementation: check the diff after Smith completes — if any modified files match deny patterns, reject and retry. This is more reliable than prompt-based enforcement. Inspired by OpenCode's granular permission system. See docs/research/opencode-patterns.md section 5.

title: Custom Temper commands per anvil
description:
Allow per-anvil override of build/test/lint commands in forge.yaml instead of only auto-detecting Go/Node/.NET.

Example config:
anvils:
  myrepo:
    temper:
      build: 'make build'
      test: 'make test'
      lint: 'make lint'

This enables support for Python, Rust, custom build systems, or repos with non-standard build tooling without modifying Forge internals. See docs/research/opencode-patterns.md section 2.

title: Pipeline hooks: configurable shell commands at each stage
description:
Add before/after shell command hooks for each pipeline stage in forge.yaml. Hooks receive context (bead ID, worktree path, branch, anvil name) as environment variables.

Example config:
anvils:
  myrepo:
    hooks:
      after_smith: './scripts/post-smith.sh'
      before_temper: './scripts/pre-temper.sh'
      after_warden: './scripts/notify.sh'

Use cases: custom linters, Slack notifications, prompt context injection, metrics collection. Inspired by OpenCode's plugin hook system but implemented as simple shell commands. See docs/research/opencode-patterns.md section 2.

title: Per-stage provider configuration for pipeline
description:
Allow separate model/provider chains for each pipeline stage (Smith, Warden, Schematic, CI fix, review fix). Currently smith_providers allows a separate chain for Smith/Warden, but this should be more granular. Example config:

settings:
  providers:
    smith: [claude/claude-opus-4-6]
    warden: [claude/claude-sonnet-4-6]
    schematic: [claude/claude-sonnet-4-6]
    cifix: [claude/claude-sonnet-4-6]

This enables cost optimization by using cheaper models for simpler stages. See docs/research/opencode-patterns.md section 3 for full analysis.

title: Hearth: poll timer missing for anvils on Hetzner
description:
The Hearth TUI on Hetzner doesn't show poll countdown timers next to anvil names in the Queue panel. On the laptop, Heimdall and Munin show timers (e.g. 'hytte (10) ● 25s') but on Hetzner both forge and hytte anvils show no timer at all.

The daemon IS polling (confirmed via journalctl: 'polling anvils count=2'), and the queue data is live and up to date. The IPC socket works (forge status connects, Hearth shows workers and events). Only the timer countdown is missing.

Possible causes:
- The poll tick event isn't being sent over IPC subscribe on the Hetzner instance
- Hearth's timer display depends on receiving periodic tick events from the daemon
- The --foreground flag (required for systemd) might change how the daemon communicates poll timing to Hearth
- Terminal rendering issue over SSH (PowerShell 7) — though the rest of Hearth renders fine

Reproduce: SSH into Hetzner, run 'forge hearth', observe Queue panel — anvil names have no countdown timer.

title: Notifications: PR Ready to Merge should include PR title in push notification body
description:
The push notification for 'PR Ready to Merge' shows: 'PR #481 ready to merge: <url> (Forge-t6y9, forge)' — but doesn't include the PR title. On a phone glance, you can't tell WHAT the PR is about.

Two changes needed:

## Forge (daemon.go:1148)
The webhook message field doesn't include the title:
```go
msg := fmt.Sprintf("PR #%d ready to merge: %s", prNumber, prURL)
```
Change to include the title and drop the URL (less useful on mobile):
```go
msg := fmt.Sprintf("PR #%d ready to merge: %s", prNumber, title)
```
Or include both: `PR #481 — Fix crucible branch targeting (Forge-t6y9)`

The title variable is already available — it's passed to the webhook payload's summary field (line 1153) but not to the disp.Dispatch message (line 1148).

## Hytte (webhooks/format.go:76)
The Hytte formatter builds notifBody from payload["message"]. It could also check for a "summary" field which Forge already sends in the legacy webhook path (line 1153) and which includes the title. Or parse it from the message if Forge includes it.

Ideal notification: Title: 'Forge: PR Ready to Merge' Body: 'PR #481 — Fix crucible branch targeting (Forge-t6y9, forge)'

title: Smelter: configurable interval + skip if recently flushed (like vulncheck)

Changes:
1. Apply the same startup-skip pattern as vulncheck (Forge-nmsw): record last smelter run timestamp in state.db, skip startup run if already flushed within the interval period
2. Default interval stays at 8h for backward compatibility, but document that higher values (48h, 72h) are reasonable for low-volume setups
3. The user can set smelter_interval in forge.yaml to control frequency

This prevents unnecessary PRs on every daemon restart and reduces noise from frequent batch warden rule commits.

title: Release: code sign Windows binaries to prevent Defender quarantine
description:
Windows Defender quarantines unsigned forge.exe downloaded via install.ps1. Sign the Windows binary during the GitHub Actions release workflow.

Options (pick one):
1. SSL.com OV code signing cert (~$70/year) — sign in CI via signtool or osslsigncode
2. Azure Trusted Signing (~$10/month) — managed service, no cert management
3. SignPath.io (free for OSS) — requires community adoption proof (stars, downloads), not feasible yet

Recommended: SSL.com cert (cheapest, simplest for a personal project)

Implementation:
1. Purchase OV code signing cert from SSL.com (or similar)
2. Store cert + password as GitHub repo secrets (CODE_SIGNING_CERT, CERT_PASSWORD)
3. Add a signing step to .github/workflows/release.yml after building Windows binary:
   - Download and install osslsigncode (works on Linux CI runners)
   - Or use signtool on windows runner
   - Sign forge_*_windows_*.zip contents before uploading to release
4. Update install.ps1 to also call Unblock-File as a fallback
5. Test: download via install.ps1, verify no Defender warning

Immediate workaround (no cert needed):
- Add Unblock-File to install.ps1 after downloading the binary
- This removes the Zone.Identifier NTFS stream that triggers Defender scanning

title: Hearth retry action fails on non-bead PRs: bead_id and anvil are required

In Hearth's Needs Attention panel, clicking retry on a PR that has no associated bead (e.g. warden-learn PRs) fails with:

```
Failed to retry: daemon: bead_id and anvil are required
```

### Cause
The retry IPC handler requires bead_id and anvil, but warden-learn PRs (and other non-bead PRs like `[no-changelog]` rule updates) don't have a bead_id.

### Fix
The retry/rebase action for PRs should work with just the PR number and anvil — it doesn't need a bead_id. Either:
1. Make bead_id optional in the retry handler when a PR number is provided
2. Or add a separate 'force rebase' action that only needs PR number + anvil

### Where to look
- `internal/ipc/ipc.go` — the retry_bead handler validation
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go` — how retry dispatches rebase
- `cmd/forge/hearth.go` — how the Needs Attention retry action builds the IPC payload
- `internal/hearth/hearth.go` — the NeedsAttention action menu

title: Stagger anvil poll timers to avoid simultaneous polling across all anvils
description:
## Feature

Currently the forge polls all anvils on the same timer interval, which means every poll cycle fires `bd ready` for all anvils simultaneously. This creates a burst of activity (and bd/git commands) followed by idle time.

### Problem
- All anvils poll at the same time (e.g. every 30s, all fire at :00, :30, :60...)
- Burst of concurrent `bd ready` + `git` commands can overwhelm Dolt or hit rate limits
- Uneven load — spiky instead of smooth

### Fix

Stagger the initial poll start time for each anvil so they're evenly distributed across the poll interval. For example, with 5 anvils and a 30s poll interval:
- Anvil 1: starts at 0s, polls at 0s, 30s, 60s...
- Anvil 2: starts at 6s, polls at 6s, 36s, 66s...
- Anvil 3: starts at 12s, polls at 12s, 42s, 72s...
- Anvil 4: starts at 18s, polls at 18s, 48s, 78s...
- Anvil 5: starts at 24s, polls at 24s, 54s, 84s...

### Implementation

In `internal/daemon/daemon.go` (or wherever anvil poll goroutines are started), add an initial delay per anvil:

```go
stagger := pollInterval / time.Duration(len(anvils))
for i, anvil := range anvils {
    delay := stagger * time.Duration(i)
    go func(a Anvil, d time.Duration) {
        time.Sleep(d)
        // start poll ticker for this anvil
    }(anvil, delay)
}
```

### Files
- `internal/daemon/daemon.go` — anvil poll loop setup
- `internal/poller/poller.go` — if the ticker is created here

title: Add forge quest list and forge quest run CLI commands

### forge quest run <quest-name> --anvil <name>

Manually executes a single quest and reports results.

Implementation:
