title: Batch multiple CI failures and review comments into single Smith requests
description:
## Summary

When a PR has multiple CI failures or review comments, combine them into a single Smith invocation instead of spawning separate cifix/reviewfix workers per issue. This saves 1-3 premium requests per failed PR when using Copilot.

**Reference:** docs/plans/copilot-request-reduction.md -- Strategy 5

## Implementation

### File: internal/cifix/cifix.go

Add a BatchFix function alongside the existing Fix function:

```go
// BatchFix combines multiple CI failures into one Smith prompt.
// Only activates when provider is Copilot and copilot_batch_ci_fixes is true.
func BatchFix(ctx context.Context, failures []CIFailure, opts FixOpts) *FixResult {
    combinedPrompt := buildBatchCIPrompt(failures)
    result := smith.SpawnWithProvider(ctx, combinedPrompt, opts.Providers, opts.WorktreePath)
    return result
}

func buildBatchCIPrompt(failures []CIFailure) string {
    // Build a prompt that lists all failures with their check names, logs, and file locations
    // Instruct Smith to address ALL failures in a single pass
    // Structure: numbered list of failures, each with context
}
```

The caller (bellows or pipeline) should collect all CI failures for a PR before calling BatchFix instead of calling Fix in a loop.

### File: internal/reviewfix/reviewfix.go

Similarly add batch mode for review comments:

```go
func BatchFix(ctx context.Context, comments []ReviewComment, opts FixOpts) *FixResult {
    combinedPrompt := buildBatchReviewPrompt(comments)
    result := smith.SpawnWithProvider(ctx, combinedPrompt, opts.Providers, opts.WorktreePath)
    return result
}

func buildBatchReviewPrompt(comments []ReviewComment) string {
    // Build a prompt listing all review comments with file/line context
    // Instruct Smith to address ALL comments in a single pass
}
```

### File: internal/config/config.go

Add to SettingsConfig:
```go
CopilotBatchCIFixes     bool `mapstructure:"copilot_batch_ci_fixes" yaml:"copilot_batch_ci_fixes"`
CopilotBatchReviewFixes bool `mapstructure:"copilot_batch_review_fixes" yaml:"copilot_batch_review_fixes"`
```

Both default to false (opt-in).

### File: internal/bellows/bellows.go (or wherever cifix/reviewfix are dispatched)

Add logic to check the batch config flags:
- If copilot_batch_ci_fixes is true AND provider is Copilot, collect all CI failures and call cifix.BatchFix once
- Otherwise, fall through to existing per-failure Fix calls
- Same pattern for review fixes

### File: docs/configuration.md

Document the new settings:
```yaml
settings:
  copilot_batch_ci_fixes: false      # opt-in: batch CI failures into one fix request
  copilot_batch_review_fixes: false  # opt-in: batch review comments into one fix request
```

### Tests

Add tests for:
1. buildBatchCIPrompt combines multiple failures into one prompt with all context preserved
2. buildBatchReviewPrompt combines multiple comments into one prompt
3. BatchFix is called instead of Fix when config is enabled and provider is Copilot
4. Falls back to per-failure Fix when config is disabled
5. Falls back to per-failure Fix when provider is not Copilot

## Acceptance Criteria

- BatchFix functions added to cifix and reviewfix packages
- Batch prompts include all failure/comment context (check names, logs, file/line references)
- Config toggles default to false (opt-in)
- Only activates when provider is Copilot
- Existing per-failure behavior preserved when batch mode is off
- Tests pass

title: Skip Warden review for small, low-risk Copilot diffs
description:
## Summary

Add a shouldSkipWarden(diffStat, bead) function in the pipeline that auto-approves small, low-risk diffs when the primary provider is Copilot. This saves 1 premium request for ~30% of beads. Gated behind an opt-in config toggle copilot_skip_warden_small_diffs (default false).

**Reference:** docs/plans/copilot-request-reduction.md -- Strategy 1

## Skip Criteria

ALL of the following must be true to skip Warden:
1. Primary provider is Copilot (providers[0].Kind == provider.Copilot)
2. Config toggle copilot_skip_warden_small_diffs is true
3. Diff is under 100 lines changed total
4. Changes are limited to docs/tests/config OR at most 2 files changed
5. No security-sensitive files touched (paths containing: auth, crypto, permission, secret, token, credential, password, key, cert, acl, rbac, policy)
6. Bead priority is P3 or P4 (priority >= 3)

## Implementation

### File: internal/config/config.go

Add to SettingsConfig:
```go
CopilotSkipWardenSmallDiffs bool `mapstructure:"copilot_skip_warden_small_diffs" yaml:"copilot_skip_warden_small_diffs"`
```

### File: internal/pipeline/pipeline.go

Add a DiffStat struct and shouldSkipWarden function:

```go
type DiffStat struct {
    LinesChanged        int
    FilesChanged        int
    TouchesSecurityFiles bool
    IsDocsOnly          bool
    IsTestsOnly         bool
}

func shouldSkipWarden(diffStat DiffStat, bead BeadInfo, providers []provider.Config, skipEnabled bool) bool {
    if !skipEnabled {
        return false
    }
    if len(providers) == 0 || providers[0].Kind != provider.Copilot {
        return false
    }
    if bead.Priority <= 2 {
        return false // always review important beads
    }
    if diffStat.LinesChanged > 100 {
        return false
    }
    if diffStat.TouchesSecurityFiles {
        return false
    }
    return diffStat.IsDocsOnly || diffStat.IsTestsOnly || diffStat.FilesChanged <= 2
}
```

Compute DiffStat from the git diff output after Smith completes. Use git diff --stat to count lines/files, and scan file paths for security-sensitive patterns.

When skipping, log the reason clearly:
```go
p.Logger.Info("skipping Warden review for small Copilot diff",
    "lines_changed", diffStat.LinesChanged,
    "files_changed", diffStat.FilesChanged,
    "reason", "low-risk diff under threshold")
```

Auto-approve by setting the warden result to approved without spawning a warden process.

### File: docs/configuration.md

Document the new setting:
```yaml
settings:
  copilot_skip_warden_small_diffs: false  # opt-in: skip Warden for small Copilot diffs
```

### Tests

Add tests in internal/pipeline/pipeline_test.go:
1. Skip when all criteria met (Copilot, enabled, small diff, P3, no security files)
2. Do NOT skip when disabled in config
3. Do NOT skip when provider is not Copilot
4. Do NOT skip when priority is P0, P1, or P2
5. Do NOT skip when diff exceeds 100 lines
6. Do NOT skip when security-sensitive files are touched
7. Do NOT skip when more than 2 files changed (and not docs/tests only)
8. Skip when changes are docs-only even if >2 files
9. Skip when changes are tests-only even if >2 files

## Acceptance Criteria

- shouldSkipWarden function implements all 6 skip criteria
- Config toggle copilot_skip_warden_small_diffs defaults to false (opt-in)
- Security-sensitive file detection covers auth/crypto/permission/secret/token/credential paths
- DiffStat computed from actual git diff after Smith output
- Info log emitted when skipping with reason
- All tests pass

title: Send X-Forge-Event HTTP header in webhook notifications
description:
Forge webhooks only set Content-Type: application/json — no custom header identifies the sender or event type. This means Hytte (and other consumers) can't distinguish Forge webhooks from generic ones without parsing the JSON body.

Add X-Forge-Event header to all outgoing webhook requests so consumers can detect and filter Forge-originated notifications by source and event type.

## Implementation

internal/notify/notify.go — in sendGenericWebhook() (the function that builds the http.Request), add after Content-Type:

  req.Header.Set("X-Forge-Event", string(eventType))

The eventType is already available at call site (e.g. "pr_ready_to_merge", "pr_created", "bead_failed", etc.).

## Event types sent
pr_created, bead_failed, daily_cost, worker_done, bead_decomposed, release_published, pr_ready_to_merge, release

## Why
Hytte needs to set source="forge" when dispatching push notifications. Without this header, Forge webhooks fall through to "generic" and the user can't filter them separately. With the header, Hytte detects X-Forge-Event and classifies the source as "forge" with the specific event type.

title: Per-anvil auto-merge config: merge PRs automatically when ready
description:
Add a per-anvil config option `auto_merge` (default: false) that automatically merges PRs when they reach the Ready to Merge state (CI passing, no conflicts, no unresolved threads, no pending reviews).

## Config
```yaml
anvils:
  my-api:
    path: /path/to/repos/my-api
    auto_merge: true    # false by default — opt-in per anvil
```

## Implementation
- internal/config/config.go: add `AutoMerge bool` to AnvilConfig (default false)
- internal/bellows/bellows.go or internal/daemon/daemon.go: when a PR transitions to ready-to-merge, check if the anvil has auto_merge enabled. If yes, trigger merge via ghpr.Merge (or vcs.MergePR) using the configured merge_strategy.
- Log an event: `pr_auto_merged` with PR number and anvil
- The Ready to Merge panel in Hearth should still show auto-merge PRs briefly (with a tag like [auto]) before they disappear after merge
- Respect the existing merge_strategy setting (squash/merge/rebase)
- Should NOT auto-merge external PRs (ext-*) even if the anvil has auto_merge enabled

## Safety
- Only merge when ALL ready-to-merge conditions are met (same as the Ready to Merge panel query)
- Skip if the PR has any failing checks, conflicts, or pending reviews
- Log clearly so the user knows what was auto-merged
notes: Also update docs/configuration.md with the new auto_merge option and add it to the full forge.yaml example in that doc.

title: Auto-close decomposed parent beads when nothing depends on them
description:
When schematic decomposes a bead into children, the parent bead stays open and either gets picked up by the crucible (incorrectly treating children as its own) or sits in the queue blocking a slot.

If the parent has no dependents (nothing has depends_on pointing to it), it should be auto-closed with --force after successful decomposition, since the children ARE the work.

If the parent HAS dependents, keep it open so those dependents stay blocked until the children complete and someone closes the parent.

Implementation:
- internal/daemon/daemon.go applyDecomposedOutcome: after creating children, check if the parent has dependents (bd show --json, check dependents array). If empty, bd close --force --reason='Decomposed into N children'.
- Log an event: bead_auto_closed or schematic_parent_closed

title: Hearth: show clarification reason in Needs Attention action menu
description:
When a bead lands in Needs Attention due to clarification_needed (e.g. schematic decomposition failure), the action menu doesn't show WHY it needs attention. The user has to dig through the event log to find the reason.

The clarification reason is already stored in the retries table (last_error field). Surface it in the Needs Attention panel:

1. Show the reason text below the bead title in the Needs Attention list (dimmed, truncated to 2 lines)
2. Show the full reason in the action menu header when pressing Enter on a needs-attention bead
3. The 'Clarify' action could pre-populate or display the schematic's complaint so the user knows what to address

Example current:
```
▸ ○ Hytte-1i9  P2  Webhook notification UI component
  [enter for actions]
```

Example desired:
```
▸ ○ Hytte-1i9  P2  Webhook notification UI component
  ⚠ Automatic decomposition failed: parsing sub-bead ID from output: invalid character...
  [enter for actions]
```

## Files to modify
- internal/hearth/data.go — NeedsAttentionBeads query already returns last_error, just needs to be surfaced
- internal/hearth/hearth.go — renderNeedsAttention: show reason below title
- internal/hearth/hearth.go — buildNeedsAttentionActionForm: include reason in header
close_reason: The clarification reason display in the Needs Attention panel was already implemented in commit 0336433 ("feat: show clarification reason in Hearth Needs Attention panel") and refined in subsequent commits (ddd29e1, a66fd90, cec72e8, 69f1b34). The reason line appears below the bead title with a `⚠` prefix for clarification items, and the action menu shows the full reason in its description. I guess you could say this bead was... *already forged*. 🔨

title: Schematic/crucible workers missing PID and log path in worker record
description: When the schematic or crucible spawns a claude subprocess, the PID and log_path are not written to the worker DB record. title: Add unit test for OpenPRsWithDetail in state/db_test.go

title: Send rich webhook payloads with pre-formatted summary
description:
Update The Forge's webhook payloads to include a pre-formatted summary field and structured metadata, so the Hytte webhooks page can display rich, human-readable summaries without guessing.

## New Payload Schema

{
  "source": "forge",
  "summary": "Release published: v0.3.1 (Forge)",
  "detail": "Scoop, Homebrew, tar.gz archives for Linux/macOS",
  "url": "https://github.com/Robin831/Forge/releases/tag/v0.3.1",
  "event": "release_published",
  "repo": "Forge",
  "version": "v0.3.1",
  "bead": "Hytte-45p",
  "pr": 31
}

### Fields

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| source | yes | Always 'forge' — used for source detection and badge |
| summary | yes | Pre-formatted human-readable one-liner for list view |
| event | yes | Machine-readable event type (snake_case) |
| detail | no | Secondary description (changelog, commit message, etc.) |
| url | no | Relevant link (PR, release, issue, etc.) |
| repo | no | Repository name |
| version | no | Version tag if applicable |
| bead | no | Bead ID if the event relates to a bead |
| pr | no | PR number if applicable |

### Event Types and Summary Formats

| Event | Summary Format |
|-------|---------------|
| release_published | 'Release published: v0.3.1 (Forge)' |
| pr_created | 'PR #31 opened: Persist weather location (Hytte)' |
| pr_merged | 'PR #31 merged: Persist weather location (Hytte)' |
| bead_completed | 'Bead Hytte-45p completed: Persist weather location' |
| ci_failed | 'CI failed: PR #26 (Hytte)' |
| ci_passed | 'CI passed: PR #31 (Hytte)' |
| smith_started | 'Smith started: Hytte-45p' |
| warden_approved | 'Warden approved: PR #31 (Hytte)' |
| temper_verified | 'Temper verified: PR #31 (Hytte)' |

## Implementation
Find where the Forge sends webhook POSTs and update the payload construction to include the new fields. The summary should be generated at send-time since the Forge has full context about what happened.

title: Hot-reload notifications config on forge.yaml change
description: The notifier is created once at daemon startup (daemon.go:208-224) and never updated when config is hot-reloaded. Changes to notifications.teams_webhook_url, notifications.enabled, or notifications.release_webhook_urls require a full daemon restart. Add an OnChange callback in the hot-reload watcher that recreates or updates the notifier when notification settings change.

title: Warden Reject vs RequestChanges verdict not visible in events
description: When the warden issues a hard Reject (vs RequestChanges), the pipeline terminates immediately without further iterations. But the event log doesn't clearly distinguish between the two verdicts. This makes it hard to diagnose why a bead stopped at iteration 3 when max_pipeline_iterations is 5. The event type is warden_reject for both cases. Add a distinct event type or include the verdict type in the message so operators can tell if the warden hard-rejected vs requested changes.

title: Release: add Docker images for devcontainer and CI usage
description: Configure GoReleaser's docker section to build and push container images to ghcr.io/robin831/forge. Multi-arch (amd64/arm64) images based on a minimal base (alpine or distroless). Useful for devcontainers, CI pipelines, and the ForgeDevContainerTemplate project.

title: Release: add Scoop manifest for Windows installation
description: Configure GoReleaser's scoop section to publish a Scoop manifest (e.g. Robin831/scoop-forge bucket). This enables 'scoop install forge' on Windows as an alternative to the PowerShell install script. GoReleaser v2 supports this natively.

title: Release: add Homebrew tap for macOS installation
description: Configure GoReleaser's brews section to publish a Homebrew formula to a tap repo (e.g. Robin831/homebrew-forge). This enables 'brew install Robin831/forge/forge' on macOS. GoReleaser v2 supports this natively via the brews config section.

title: Release: add tar.gz archives for Linux and macOS
description: GoReleaser currently produces only zip archives. Linux/macOS convention is tar.gz. Add a second archive entry in .goreleaser.yml that produces tar.gz for linux and darwin while keeping zip for windows. The install.sh currently uses unzip which requires a separate package on minimal containers — tar.gz uses tar which is always available.

title: Warden: learn from CI fix patterns, not just review comments
description: The warden currently only learns rules from Copilot review comments (warden learn). It doesn't learn from CI failures. When the cifix repeatedly fails on the same lint rule (e.g. react-hooks/set-state-in-effect), that pattern should be captured so the smith avoids it in future code. After a cifix succeeds, extract the lint rule name and the fix pattern (what was wrong, what the correct approach is) and store it as a warden rule. This way the warden can flag the anti-pattern during review before it ever hits CI, reducing cifix cycles from 5-9 down to 0-1. Example: ESLint react-hooks/set-state-in-effect — don't call setState in useEffect, use render-phase state adjustment pattern instead.

title: Abstract VCS provider layer to support GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps
description:
Forge is tightly coupled to GitHub via the gh CLI. To support other hosting platforms, introduce a VCS provider interface (internal/vcs/) with per-platform implementations. 

Current GitHub coupling points:
- ghpr package: PR create/merge/status/list via gh CLI + GraphQL
- bellows: PR monitoring via ghpr.CheckStatus
- crucible: gh pr merge, gh pr view
- cifix: gh run view, gh pr checks
- reviewfix: gh pr commands
- warden/learn.go: gh api for Copilot comments, hardcoded bot names
- ghpr.ParseRepoURL: only recognizes github.com URLs
- state.db prs table: status values assume GitHub (open/merged/closed vs GitLab opened/merged/closed/locked)

Proposed interface:
  CreatePR, MergePR, CheckStatus, ListOpen, FetchReviewComments, GetRepoInfo

Platforms to support:
- GitHub (gh CLI) — current, refactor into provider
- GitLab (glab CLI) — merge requests, approval rules, different CI model
- Forgejo/Gitea (tea CLI or REST) — simpler, GitHub-like
- Bitbucket (REST API, no mature CLI) — lower priority
- Azure DevOps (az repos CLI) — lower priority

Config: add platform field to anvil config with default 'github':
  anvils:
    my-repo:
      path: /path/to/repo
      platform: github|gitlab|gitea|bitbucket|azuredevops

Phase 1: Extract ghpr into a VCS provider interface, move GitHub impl behind it
Phase 2: GitLab provider via glab
Phase 3: Gitea/Forgejo provider
Phase 4: Bitbucket/Azure DevOps (if needed)

title: Pipeline: read MaxIterations from config instead of hardcoded constant
description: The pipeline's Smith-Warden loop uses a hardcoded const MaxIterations = 5 in pipeline.go:37. This should read from the existing max_review_attempts config setting (or a new pipeline_max_iterations setting) so it can be tuned via forge.yaml and hot-reloaded. Currently max_review_attempts only controls the bellows reviewfix path, not the initial pipeline loop. Either unify them under one config key or add a separate one.

title: Hearth: add mouse support for panel navigation and scrolling
description: Enable bubbletea mouse support (tea.WithMouseCellMotion) to allow clicking on panels to focus them and mouse wheel scrolling within panels. Currently the TUI is keyboard-only — mouse support makes it more accessible and faster for quick checks. Charm's bubbletea has built-in mouse event handling.

title: Hearth: add Bubbles file picker for log viewing
description: When a worker is selected in the Workers panel, pressing 'o' opens its Smith log file using the charmbracelet/bubbles filepicker or directly renders it in a full-screen viewport overlay. Currently users have to manually find and open log files from ~/.forge/logs/. This brings log inspection into the TUI.

title: Hearth: add toast notifications with Bubbles timer
description: Show temporary toast-style notifications at the bottom of the TUI for transient events (worker completed, PR merged, bead closed) using a bubbles timer for auto-dismiss after 3-5 seconds. Currently these events only appear in the scrolling Events panel where they can be missed. Toasts surface the important ones prominently.

title: Hearth: add Lip Gloss adaptive colors for light/dark terminals
description: Use lipgloss.AdaptiveColor and lipgloss.HasDarkBackground to detect terminal theme and adjust the color palette accordingly. Currently the TUI assumes a dark background — users with light terminals get poor contrast on some elements. AdaptiveColor lets us define color pairs that auto-switch.

title: Hearth: use Bubbles viewport for scrollable log viewer
description: Replace our custom viewport implementation (viewport.go) with the charmbracelet/bubbles viewport component. We currently maintain our own scroll state, cursor tracking, and page-up/page-down logic — the bubbles viewport handles all of this with mouse wheel support included. Keeps our code simpler and gets mouse scrolling for free.

title: Hearth: use Bubbles textarea for inline bead notes
description: Add the charmbracelet/bubbles textarea component to allow adding notes to a bead directly from the TUI. When a bead is selected in Queue or Needs Attention, pressing 'n' opens an inline textarea overlay. On submit, calls bd update <id> --append-notes. Useful for quick context when triaging stuck beads.

title: Hearth: use Bubbles progress bar for crucible children
description: Add a charmbracelet/bubbles progress component to the Crucibles panel showing completion percentage (e.g. 2/5 children done). Currently we show counts as text — a visual progress bar makes it immediately obvious how far along a crucible is. Color-code: green for completed, yellow for in-progress, red for failed.

title: Hearth: use Bubbles help component for keybinding hints
description: Add a charmbracelet/bubbles help component to the bottom of the TUI showing context-sensitive keybinding hints for the focused panel. Users currently have to know the keybindings by heart — the help bubble shows available keys like 'K kill / f follow / l label / enter action' based on which panel is focused.

title: Hearth: add spinner animations for active workers
description: Use the charmbracelet/bubbles spinner component to show animated spinners next to active workers and crucible phases. Currently active workers show a static bullet point — an animated spinner makes it obvious which workers are running vs stalled.

title: Hearth: use Huh forms for action menus
description: Replace the hand-rolled action menus (Needs Attention actions, merge menu, queue label menu) with charmbracelet/huh form components. Huh provides styled select lists, confirmations, and text inputs with keyboard navigation built in. This simplifies the menu state management code in hearth.go.

title: Hearth: render bead descriptions with Glamour markdown
description: When a bead is selected in the Queue or Needs Attention panel, render its description using charmbracelet/glamour for proper markdown formatting (code blocks, bold, links, lists). Currently descriptions are shown as plain text. Add a detail pane or expandable view that shows the glamour-rendered description.

title: Hearth: use Bubbles list component for Queue panel
description: Replace the manual queue rendering with the charmbracelet/bubbles list component. This provides built-in fuzzy filtering (type to filter beads by name/anvil), pagination, and styled item delegates. Currently we manually handle viewport scrolling and anvil grouping — the list bubble can do filtering while we keep our custom grouping logic.

title: Hearth: use Bubbles table component for Workers panel
description: Replace the hand-rolled worker list rendering in hearth with the charmbracelet/bubbles table component. This gives us column resizing, header styling, and cursor navigation for free. The Workers panel currently manually formats columns with lipgloss — the table bubble handles all of that out of the box.

title: Log event when auto-learn skips PR (no comments or no new rules)
description: When bellows auto-learn runs on a merged PR but finds nothing to learn, it only logs to stdout. Add visible events to the Hearth event log so operators can confirm the feature is working. Two silent skip cases need events: 1. No Copilot comments on the PR (bellows.go line 405) - log an info event like PR N: no Copilot comments, skipping auto-learn. 2. Comments found but no new rules distilled (bellows.go line 476) - log an info event like PR N: no new rules from N comments. Use a new event type like EventAutoLearnSkipped or similar. Keep it lightweight - these are informational, not errors.

title: Hearth: increase queue action popup dimensions
description:
The queue action popup is better after the recent title/sizing fix, but still too small vertically. Increase the popup height so it can display at least 5 sentences of the bead description. Also make it slightly wider (a few columns, not too much).

Look at renderQueueActionMenu in internal/hearth/hearth.go — find the popup dimensions (likely hardcoded width/height or a fraction of the terminal size) and increase them:
- Height: enough to show ~5 lines of description text plus title, bead ID, and menu options
- Width: increase by ~5-10 columns from current value

Keep it reasonable — it's a popup, not a fullscreen modal.

title: Improve PR description with actual bead context
description:
PR descriptions created by the Forge are generic boilerplate:

```
Automated PR by The Forge
Bead: Fhi.Metadata-94e0
Branch: forge/Fhi.Metadata-94e0

This PR was generated by The Forge autonomous pipeline.
A Smith agent implemented the changes, Temper verified the build,
and Warden approved the code review.
```

This tells the reviewer nothing about WHAT was done or WHY.

Improve the PR description to include:
1. The bead title and description (the problem/task)
2. A summary of what the smith actually changed (from the warden review or git diff --stat)
3. The bead type (bug fix, feature, chore, etc.)

Files: internal/ghpr/ghpr.go (CreateParams, the PR body template) and internal/pipeline/pipeline.go (where CreateParams is populated). The bead metadata is already available in pipeline.Params.Bead — it just needs to be wired into the PR body.

title: Forge: visible daemon health indicator
description:
There's no easy way to tell if the forge daemon is running without explicitly running 'forge status'. Ideas to explore (pick the best approach):

1. **System tray icon** (Windows) — a small icon that shows green/red based on daemon state. Could show tooltip with worker count and last poll time. Lightweight, always visible.

2. **forge status --brief** — one-line output suitable for shell prompts or polybar/status bars (e.g. '⚒ 3/7 smiths | 5 queued | 2m ago')

3. **Lock/PID file** (~/.forge/daemon.pid) — the daemon already uses a named pipe, but a PID file is simpler for scripts to check. Could pair with a PowerShell one-liner alias.

4. **Desktop notification on crash** — if the daemon exits unexpectedly, fire a Windows toast notification so you know it went down.

5. **Hearth status bar** — show a persistent connection indicator in the TUI footer (connected/disconnected to daemon IPC).

Consider what's most useful for the 'glance at my screen and know if forge is alive' use case. Probably a combination: system tray for passive awareness + improved CLI for scripting.

title: Hearth: Improve queue action popup sizing and title display
description:
The queue action popup (Enter on a bead) has two issues:

1. **Title truncation**: The bead title gets cut off on one line. Show it across two lines so more of the title is visible.

2. **Popup too narrow**: The first menu option wraps awkwardly:
   `> Label for dispatch — Tag bead for auto-`
   `  dispatch`
   Increase the popup width so options fit on a single line.

Files: internal/hearth/hearth.go — look for the queue action menu rendering (showQueueActionMenu, renderQueueActionMenu or similar popup rendering).

title: Add OpenAI/GPT provider support
description: Add a new provider.Kind for OpenAI models (GPT-5, o3, etc.) as a first-class provider in Forge's provider chain. Needs: CLI subprocess spawning (likely via openai-cli or direct API), BuildArgs() implementation, stream-json event parsing for OpenAI's output format, rate-limit detection, and quota tracking. Research OpenAI's CLI tooling and output formats. Reference OpenCode's multi-model support for ideas.

title: Support local models via Claude Code + Ollama backend
description:
Claude Code already supports Ollama natively via the Anthropic Messages API compatibility layer. Instead of adding a new provider kind, add per-provider environment variable overrides so a claude provider entry can target a local Ollama instance.

## Approach

Add env override support to the provider config, e.g.:
```yaml
providers:
  - claude/claude-sonnet-4-6
  - claude:ollama/qwen2.5-coder:32b
```

Where `claude:ollama` sets these env vars on the smith subprocess:
- ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434
- ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=ollama
- CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1

## Implementation

1. Extend provider.Provider to support an optional env map
2. Update provider.FromConfig() to parse the `claude:ollama` syntax (or a dedicated config field)
3. Pass env overrides through to smith.SpawnWithProvider() → exec.Command.Env
4. No new stream-json parsing needed — same claude CLI, same output format
5. Consider: Ollama has no rate limits but is hardware-constrained. May want to limit concurrency for local providers.

## Prerequisites

- Ollama installed and running locally with a capable coding model (qwen2.5-coder:32b recommended)
- GPU with 16GB+ VRAM or Apple M-series with 32GB+ RAM

## References

- https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/claude-code
- https://www.datacamp.com/tutorial/using-claude-code-with-ollama-local-models
notes: Be sure to update docs and the forge.yaml example config

title: Track provider quota from warden, cifix, reviewfix, and schematic sessions
description: Only smith.Spawn captures and reports provider quota (rate-limit headers) back to the pipeline, which then calls UpsertProviderQuota. The warden, cifix, reviewfix, and schematic workers all spawn claude sessions but discard the quota data, so the dashboard quota display undercounts actual usage. Each of these should extract quota from their claude session results and persist it to state.db via UpsertProviderQuota.

title: Usage panel: show Copilot premium request quota (configurable limit)
description: The Usage panel shows Copilot premium requests used but not the quota. Since the GitHub API doesn't expose individual quota info, add a copilot_daily_request_limit config setting (300 for Pro, 1500 for Pro+) and display it as a progress indicator like '5 / 300 premium req' in the Usage panel.

title: Fix Copilot review comments on PR #149: add anvil name to depcheck_dedup events
description: PR #149 (Forge-vgv) was merged with 2 Copilot review comments unfixed. title: Temper: LoadAnvilConfig swallows non-ENOENT errors and prints to stderr
description:
LoadAnvilConfig in temper.go returns nil for any read/unmarshal error, but docs say it returns nil only when the file doesn't exist. Permission errors, corrupt YAML, etc. are silently swallowed. It also prints errors to stderr via fmt.Fprintf instead of returning them, which is bad for daemon flows that need structured error handling.

Fix: return the error for non-os.IsNotExist cases so callers (loadAnvilTemperCached in daemon.go) can handle/log them properly. Also fix loadAnvilTemperCached to handle non-ENOENT os.Stat errors without spamming logs on every dispatch.

title: Warden learn: semantic comment grouping instead of exact-match
description: GroupComments() in learn.go only groups comments with identical normalized body text. Copilot comments about the same pattern but with different wording (e.g. 'missing error check on Open()' vs 'error from ReadFile not handled') create separate rules instead of being grouped. Consider using Claude to cluster semantically similar comments before distillation, or use a simpler heuristic like keyword overlap scoring.

title: Hearth: extract shared scroll viewport helper to eliminate per-panel scroll bugs
description: Every panel has independently reimplemented scroll logic, and each one had the same viewport bug (items disappearing when scrolling). Workers, Needs Attention, Ready to Merge, and Queue all needed the same fix (separate viewStart from selection cursor). Extract a shared scrollViewport struct/helper with methods like ScrollUp, ScrollDown, VisibleRange, etc. that all panels use. This prevents future panels from reintroducing the same bug and reduces duplicated scroll math across hearth.go.

title: Combined Smith+Warden prompt for Copilot single-request mode
description:
## Summary

Embed Warden review criteria into the Smith prompt so Smith self-reviews its own diff, eliminating the separate Warden request. Only spawn a real Warden if: the self-review flags concerns, the bead is high-priority (P0-P1), or random sampling triggers. This is the highest-impact optimization (saves 1-5 requests per bead) but also highest risk -- only enable for Copilot.

**Reference:** docs/plans/copilot-request-reduction.md -- Strategy 4

## Implementation

### File: internal/prompt/prompt.go

Add CopilotCombinedMode support to the prompt builder:

```go
if builder.CopilotCombinedMode {
    prompt += "\n\n## Self-Review Checklist\n"
    prompt += "After implementing the change, review your own diff against these criteria:\n"
    prompt += wardenRules  // inject from warden learned rules for this anvil
    prompt += "\nOutput a JSON block at the end of your response:\n"
    prompt += "```json\n{\"self_review\": {\"verdict\": \"approve\" | \"request_changes\", \"concerns\": [...]}}\n```\n"
    prompt += "If your verdict is request_changes, revise your code to address the concerns before finalizing.\n"
}
```

The builder needs access to Warden's learned rules for the anvil. Pass them via a WardenRules field on the builder or accept them as a parameter.

### File: internal/pipeline/pipeline.go

After Smith completes, when copilot_combined_smith_warden is true and provider is Copilot:

1. Parse the self_review JSON block from Smith's output
2. Determine whether to spawn a real Warden:
   - Always spawn real Warden if bead priority is P0 or P1
   - Spawn real Warden if self-review verdict is "request_changes"
   - Spawn real Warden with probability copilot_warden_sample_rate (default 0.1 = 10%)
   - Otherwise, auto-approve based on self-review

```go
func (p *Pipeline) shouldRunRealWarden(selfReview *SelfReview, bead BeadInfo, sampleRate float64) bool {
    if bead.Priority <= 1 {
        return true // always review critical beads
    }
    if selfReview == nil || selfReview.Verdict == "request_changes" {
        return true // self-review flagged concerns or parsing failed
    }
    // Random sampling for quality validation
    return rand.Float64() < sampleRate
}
```

Add a SelfReview struct and parser:
```go
type SelfReview struct {
    Verdict  string   `json:"verdict"`   // "approve" or "request_changes"
    Concerns []string `json:"concerns"`
}

func parseSelfReview(smithOutput string) *SelfReview {
    // Extract JSON block matching {"self_review": ...} from Smith output
    // Return nil if not found or malformed (triggers real Warden as fallback)
}
```

### File: internal/config/config.go

Add to SettingsConfig:
```go
CopilotCombinedSmithWarden bool    `mapstructure:"copilot_combined_smith_warden" yaml:"copilot_combined_smith_warden"`
CopilotWardenSampleRate    float64 `mapstructure:"copilot_warden_sample_rate" yaml:"copilot_warden_sample_rate"`
```

Default CopilotCombinedSmithWarden to false (opt-in, high risk).
Default CopilotWardenSampleRate to 0.1 (10%).

### File: docs/configuration.md

Document:
```yaml
settings:
  copilot_combined_smith_warden: false  # opt-in: combine Smith+Warden into single request
  copilot_warden_sample_rate: 0.1      # 10% of beads get real Warden even with combined mode
```

### Tests

Add tests for:
1. parseSelfReview extracts valid JSON from Smith output
2. parseSelfReview returns nil for missing/malformed JSON
3. shouldRunRealWarden returns true for P0 and P1 beads always
4. shouldRunRealWarden returns true when self-review is nil (parse failure)
5. shouldRunRealWarden returns true when verdict is "request_changes"
6. shouldRunRealWarden returns true at expected sample rate (statistical test)
7. shouldRunRealWarden returns false for approved P3 bead (when not sampled)
8. Prompt builder appends self-review checklist when CopilotCombinedMode is true
9. Prompt builder does not append checklist when CopilotCombinedMode is false
10. End-to-end: combined mode skips Warden when self-review approves

## Risk Mitigation

- Only enable for Copilot provider (Claude keeps independent Warden)
- Always run real Warden on P0-P1 beads
- 10% sampling validates self-review quality over time
- If self-review JSON is missing or malformed, fall back to real Warden
- Config is opt-in (default false)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Self-review checklist injected into Smith prompt when combined mode enabled
- SelfReview JSON parsed from Smith output with graceful fallback on parse failure
- Real Warden always runs for P0-P1 beads
- Real Warden runs when self-review flags concerns
- Random sampling at configurable rate (default 10%)
- Config toggles default to safe values (false, 0.1)
- All tests pass

title: Hearth: remote access via VS Code Remote Tunnel
description: Instead of running a Wish SSH server (policy concern on corporate laptops), leverage VS Code Remote Tunnels (code tunnel) for remote Hearth access. From any browser: open vscode.dev, connect to the tunnel, open terminal, run 'forge hearth' for full TUI. Claude Code CLI also supports remote/headless mode, enabling remote Claude sessions that run on the host machine. Investigate: autostart code tunnel alongside forge daemon, document the setup, and test Hearth rendering in the vscode.dev browser terminal.
